author: reardan
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"reardan"} -->
_Requested by **Velentene** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_015R2ru18PtetEs9sDoPX4nr?thread=cmsg_015R2ru18PtetEs9sDoPX4nrDUpTSoGqi65YBZJ2YNPrtv)_

Before: the UI library had one flat right-click context menu, usable only with the mouse. There was no menu bar, no submenus, no check items, and no shortcuts. Ctrl+letter never reached a W program on X11, Win32 or macOS.

After: there is a full desktop-style menu kit, and the editor shell demo now has a File / Edit / View / Help bar that uses all of it (`demo.w --shell --menubar` pins View > Theme open for a screenshot; see `docs/images/ui_demo_shell_menubar.png`).

- **Menu bar** (`graphics/ui/widgets/menubar.w`, new). Menus open on press, and press-drag-release onto an item chooses it. Hovering another title switches menus. Alt plus the `&` mnemonic opens a menu from the keyboard, and Left/Right move between menus.
- **Nested submenus** (`ui_menu_begin_sub` / `ui_menu_end_sub`). They open beside their parent and flip left at the window edge. Parent and child both take input.
- **Check and radio items**, and `*_key` items that show their shortcut ("Ctrl+S") right-aligned.
- **Keyboard**: Up/Down/Home/End skip separators and disabled items. Right or Return opens a submenu, Left or Escape closes one level, and Return or Space chooses. Typing a `&` mnemonic chooses its item, and any other letter jumps to the next item starting with it.
- **Shortcuts** (`ui_shortcut`). A chord is declared once, on its item. It works while the bar's menus are closed because closed menus are walked without drawing on frames that carry a chord.

The existing context-menu API is unchanged, and its tests pass as they were.

How: one `ui_menu_state` is a whole chain (the root plus open submenus) and registers a single popup id, so every level stays interactive. Each level draws in its own popup bracket: the parent's bracket is left while a submenu draws, because the clip stack intersects. Sizes and keyboard masks come from the previous frame's walk, as before. Menus now reserve a fixed block of widget ids every frame, so opening one no longer shifts the ids of later widgets (which used to cost a focused field its focus).

Related fixes the menus needed:
- X11, Win32 and Cocoa now forward Ctrl+letter as its control code with the Ctrl bit. Cocoa also queues Command chords with the Super bit. The web host already sent the letter itself. `graphics/event.w` documents the contract.
- Text fields skip characters typed with Ctrl or Super held (but not with AltGr, which is Ctrl+Alt). Before this, the web host typed an `s` on Ctrl+S.
- Textbox, textarea and tree no longer take keys while a popup above them is open. They keep their focus. Before this, typing went into the editor behind an open context menu.

Testing:
- 12 new tests in `menu_test.w` and 9 in the new `menubar_test.w`.
- Every target `wtest changed` selects passes except `wasm_ui_test`. That one fails on `main` with the same "glyph-atlas uploads" error, already noted in §11.5.
- The darwin and win64 builds compile. The Cocoa input change was compile-checked only, not run on a Mac.

Design notes are in `docs/projects/ui_widgets.md` §12.

author: grauzone-dev
body:
<!-- review-base-original: d47afe46ce8eb028c4cbdaa9996f29761a6482d0 -->
<!-- review-base-current: 4cfff43124df72f1bfa50c7e8a961ef539d46905 -->

## Summary

`sandboxed-agents fingerprint NAME` prints the three host key fingerprints of a running sandbox for comparison with what a third-party UI shows. It needs no SSH setup and changes nothing on the host or in the sandbox.

```text
fingerprint NAME
  usage, valid name                  # step 1, no Podman call
  sandbox exists, has a container    # step 3, else "up NAME"
  owner of container and volumes     # step 4, else owner conflict
  no interrupted update              # step 5, else "update NAME"
  sandbox runs                       # step 6, else "start NAME"
  for ed25519, ecdsa, rsa
    podman exec --user=0:0 CONTAINER cat /etc/ssh/ssh_host_<type>_key.pub
    validate the public key against its expected type
  print all three lines, or none when one key fails
```

Each line is `KEY-TYPE SHA256:BASE64-DIGEST`, as recorded in #33: the SHA-256 hash of the decoded SSH wire blob in standard Base64 without padding, the digest OpenSSH shows by default. `docs/sandboxes.md` and `docs/host-prerequisites.md` describe the shipped command.

Closes #33

## Evidence

- **Before:** `TestFingerprintPrintsKnownHostKeysWithoutSSHSetup` failed on the `sandbox-host` and `windows` fixtures with `sandboxed-agents: unknown command "fingerprint"`.
  **After:** on the head `3a4285ac1cb6a763ea9e5a5ae95741d26ad82d1e`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `bash tests/test-mirror-issue.sh` pass locally; `git diff --check` is clean, and the Linux build and the Windows cross-build pass. Native CI passed on the same head in the [pull request run](https://github.com/grauzone-dev/sandboxed-agents/actions/runs/37201283586) (Linux, Windows, and compare-assets) and in the [push run](https://github.com/grauzone-dev/sandboxed-agents/actions/runs/37201280393).
- **RSA correction, before:** ten malformed RSA keys (one-byte zero, redundant sign padding, negative, exponent 1, even exponent, even modulus, modulus smaller than the exponent) printed three fingerprints with status 0.
  **After:** exponent and modulus must each be a canonical positive `mpint` (RFC 4251, section 5), the exponent odd and at least 3, the modulus odd and greater than the exponent. Twelve CLI cases on both fixtures now fail with no output.
- The expected fingerprints match what `ssh-keygen -lf` prints for the three fixture keys.
- **Rebase:** the branch is rebased onto `4cfff43124df72f1bfa50c7e8a961ef539d46905`. `git range-diff d47afe46..838beff 4cfff431..b3b34c11` carries over the four original patches: the three implementation and test patches are unchanged, and the docs patch differs only where the two command lists in `docs/sandboxes.md` keep every agent command that main added and `fingerprint`.
- **Review fix after the rebase:** CodeRabbit's review of `b3b34c11` found that `docs/sandboxes.md` described host key generation on the first start ambiguously. The docs-only commit `3a4285a` corrects it: an empty SSH server state volume gets all three keys, and a kept volume keeps its keys and gets only the missing ones. No runtime code changed.
- Two focused local reviews of this fix, against the repository standards and against #33, reported no findings.
- CodeRabbit reviewed the head `3a4285a` and reported [no actionable findings](https://github.com/grauzone-dev/sandboxed-agents/pull/94#issuecomment-5974960419).
- **Not verified:** no live Podman or SSH run was made; the evidence is offline, against fake Podman and fake SSH.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The change adds one command and touches no existing behavior beyond registering it. Users may come to rely on the output format, so a later change to it is visible, but nothing is stored.

**Blast Radius:** additive

A regression would be confined to `fingerprint`; a wrong digest would mislead a user who compares host keys by hand.

author: mgubi
body:
Part of #204: items 1-4 are fixed, item 5 is not reproduced (regression checks added), item 6 belongs to PR #97.

## Items
1. **C++ multi-line comments colored up to the end of the closing line** (`cpp_language.cpp` `in_cpp_comment`, `impl_language.cpp` `in_comment`). The end of a comment was searched from the column of the current token, in the line where the comment begins. So a comment closed on the current line colored the rest of that line, and in `a /* b */ c` the `*/` of a later comment made `c` a comment. Now `begin_comment` returns the position after the last `/*` at or before the token, `end_comment` the position after the first `*/` starting from there, and the token is in the comment when that `*/` ends after it. The same change is made to the two copies of these functions.
2. **`/* */` was a comment in every `prog_language_rep`** (`prog_language.cpp` `get_color`). The comment table now has `(multi_line "/*" "*/")` in `default-lang.scm`, which java, scala, javascript, dot, json and csv use. `customize_comment` sets `multi_line_comments` only for that feature, since `in_comment` only knows `/* */`. Python, julia and octave have their own comment tables without it, so `a /* b */ c` in Python now shows `/` and `*` as operators. A design note: json and csv keep `/* */`, as before, because they use the default table.
3. **Julia's multi-word declarations never matched** (`keyword_parser.cpp`). `put` records the keywords that contain a space, and `can_parse` tries them first (`can_parse_phrase`). A match needs a single space between the words and the end of a word after them: `mutable  struct` and `abstract types` do not match, and neither does `mutable` alone.
4. **R comments were not highlighted** (`r_language.cpp`): the constructor now gives the inline comment parser its start `#`, as `fortran_language` does.
5. **R `<-` split**: not reproduced on `wip_more_tests`. `x <- 1`, `x<-1`, `a <- b` and `x <<- 1` all show the assignment in dark green. `x <- 1` and `y <- "#" -> z` are added as regression checks.
6. **`$` in Julia red**: `$` is in the `operator_decoration` class, whose color is added by PR #97 (#44 item 3). Not redone here.

## Tests (`TeXmacs/progs/check/parse-test.scm`, `tests/Data/Parser/keyword_parser_test.cpp`)
- The two cpp FIXMEs are replaced by two cpp documents: `/* a` / `b */ x`, and `a /* b */ c` / `d` / `/* e */`.
- The python `/* */` FIXME is replaced by the python line `a /* b */ c`, plus a java line `x /* c */ y` that still has the comment. The table checks of `java` and `parse-test-nolang` now expect the `multi_line` feature.
- The julia FIXME is replaced by a group "highlight julia declarations": `abstract type T end` and `mutable  struct S; mutable = 1; types`.
- The R FIXMEs are replaced by `x = 1 # c` (brown comment) and the `<-` lines.
- `highlight` leaves out the glyphs of spaces, because a token can now contain one (`abstract type` is typeset as one string).
- New unit test `TestKeywordParser::test_phrase`.

**Without the fix**, these checks fail: the 2 cpp lines, R `x = 1 # c`, python `a /* b */ c`, and the 2 table checks. The julia check compares `abstract type` with the color of `struct`. On this base, `declare_type` is the invalid color `"0000c0"` (fixed by PR #97), so `struct` is black too and the julia check cannot tell the difference yet. With the julia color corrected locally as in #97, it fails without the fix (`abstract` black) and passes with it. **With the fix**, `parse` passes (470 checks), and so do `tests/scheme/check.sh all` (36 suites), `make -C tests` and `tests/documents/check.sh`.

## Overlap with PR #97
`cpp_language.cpp`, `prog_language.cpp` and the julia/python tables: #97's diff still applies cleanly on top of this branch (`git apply --check`). `keyword_parser.cpp` **will conflict** in `can_parse`: this PR inserts the line `if (can_parse_phrase (s, pos)) return true;` just above the lines that #97 rewrites. To resolve it, keep that line followed by #97's body. Once #97 is merged, the FIXME before `test-julia` (the `0000c0` colors) can go, and the julia check then discriminates by itself.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>prometheus/prometheus (prometheus/prometheus)</summary>

### [`v3.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/releases/tag/v3.15.0): 3.15.0 / 2026-09-24

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/compare/v3.14.0...v3.15.0)

- \[CHANGE] PromQL: A range query whose `end` was not aligned to `step` caused subqueries inside it to evaluate past the parent's last actual step, inflating `peakSamples` in the query stats and against the `query.max-samples` limit, and wasting storage I/O reading samples that were never used in the result. Add tests to prevent regression of the fix made in [#​18081](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18081). [#​18598](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18598)

author: sidkmenon
body:
Adds `diffr-grammars`, which links every Tree-sitter grammar statically but stores its tables of plain data as zstd bytes. The build finds those tables with `tree-sitter-c`, checks that each element type is plain data by resolving it through the grammar's `tree_sitter/parser.h`, and reads the bytes from an object file compiled for the target. A grammar's tables are unpacked into memory, in C, the first time diffr uses it. `diffr-core` takes every language from this crate and has no `unsafe` grammar code left.

- Release binary (aarch64 macOS): 108.07 MB on `main`, 58.00 MB here.
- Startup-bound commands are within 3 ms of `main`. On generalaction/emdash#2833 (5,273 files), time to the first file event and total time are within run-to-run noise.
- `debug --dump-ts` output is identical to `main` for all 223 files in `sample_files`.

Two commits: the first adds the crate unused, and the second switches `diffr-core` to it.

Not yet exercised: the release workflow, which runs only on tags or manual dispatch.

author: haoxuw
body:
## Why

The supplied 1200-in-1 cartridge could not load because the emulator rejected its cartridge controller (mapper 227). Its valid ROM header describes hardware we had not implemented. The live website reproduced the rejection; clearing browser storage cannot add the missing hardware.

## What changed

- Implement the base mapper 227 board's address-driven memory banking, mirroring, writable graphics memory protection and reset behavior.
- Support validated saves and restored peer checkpoints for this board through the existing state codec.
- Keep extended NES 2.0 submappers unsupported rather than silently treating different hardware as the base board.
- Record the vendored patch and update the current state-profile documentation. No ROM, default game, UI or separate loading path is added.

## Proof it worked

The user's unchanged ROM now reaches its 1200-in-1 menu, selects Bomberman and enters its playable stage through the normal host/load/ready/start journey. The compiled WASM also exports a running-game checkpoint, restores it and reproduces the same state and pixels after 120 frames of controller input. [Inspect the before/after images, paired gameplay result and save/replay proof](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/pull/226#issuecomment-5974994328). Final [CI37165193120](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/actions/runs/37165193120) passed in **218 seconds** after integrating accepted cleanup #225. Both CI attempts passed; 687 seconds elapsed from the first start to the final finish, including the integration interval.

## Details

The direct request is the governing bounded fix: make the supplied cartridge run through the existing emulator. The primary [mapper 227 hardware specification](https://www.nesdev.org/wiki/INES_Mapper_227) defines the address latch, six program-memory modes, graphics-memory protection, mirroring and reset. The battery flag distinguishes legacy multicarts from the writable graphics/RAM RPG board; there is no title/hash special case. [FCEUX's implementation](https://github.com/TASEmulators/fceux/blob/master/src/boards/addrlatch.cpp) independently corroborates that legacy distinction. Extended submappers 1/2 have extra hardware and remain explicitly rejected.

### Journey proof

Actor: host with an authorized local NES file. Entry: the normal website listing → Host a new game → Load NES game → Add NES file → Ready → Start. The unchanged user file is tested locally and is never committed or placed in the catalog. Baseline main rejected it with `unimplemented mapper 227`; candidate loads the menu and starts a selected game. Separate compiled-WASM proof covers save/restore and identical input replay. Current base is `18742834615a03a70ee3d449db23ceb10bdc0251`, head `ddce7fea8b2b302ad44970df7210c2df40056fd0`; Chrome, 1280×800, two independent browser contexts. The final merge contains only accepted obsolete-test cleanup; all affected product sources are byte-identical to the photographed predecessor. This does not claim exhaustive qualification of every game in the multicart or its extended board variants.

## Review evidence

### Problem validity

The supplied ROM has a valid iNES header selecting mapper 227; current main's mapper dispatch rejects it. The user's exact public error was reproduced. Implementing the missing hardware resolves this cause.

### Plan fidelity

The bounded scope follows the requested cartridge debugging and release goal. Existing host/join/play behavior and file admission are reused. No technical selection is exposed to players; unsupported extended hardware stays truthful.

### Implementation correctness

Three focused native board tests passed: 512 bank/mode combinations, CHR write protection and RPG RAM, reset/mirroring/state rebuild. An original generated mapper-227 fixture passes validated checkpoint restore/replay under NTSC, PAL and Dendy, rejects malformed latch/cartridge settings, and rejects extended submappers. Full preflight passed in 28.24 seconds (34 Rust, 24 Python, 234 Node tests; no skips). Final head `ddce7fea8b2b302ad44970df7210c2df40056fd0` incorporates accepted cleanup main `18742834615a03a70ee3d449db23ceb10bdc0251`; its private-target preflight passed in **27.25 seconds**, with the same 34 Rust/24 Python/234 Node results. [Prior CI](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/actions/runs/37164789853) passed in 242 seconds; [final CI](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/actions/runs/37165193120) passed in **218 seconds**, all seven substantive jobs; the inclusive elapsed time across both passing candidates and the intervening accepted-main integration was **687 seconds**, under 30 minutes. The [proof](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/pull/226#issuecomment-5974994328) retains one stale shared-cache failure and confirms a fresh private-target build produced the exact exercised core digest.

### Implementation simplicity

One board uses the existing mapper table and page maps. One small CHR write-permission primitive preserves read mapping; the existing codec validates one latch and one immutable board setting. No alternate emulator or ROM-header workaround is introduced.

### Clean codebase

The mapper table owns dispatch and stable serialization id 227. Banking is derived from the serialized latch by `update_banks`, including after restore. Searches covered mapper registration, cartridge naming, state admission, loader/UI callers and current profile documentation. Existing unsupported diagnostics and other boards are retained for their current responsibilities. Vendor provenance includes every changed and added file.

### User journey fidelity

The ordinary host/load/ready/start path now loads this cartridge, previews its menu and reaches the selected game's playable stage. [Published images and observed transitions](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/pull/226#issuecomment-5974994328) show the baseline rejection and both users paused at the same playable stage after controller input. The tested predecessor `1ddcd0d` and final `ddce7fe` have byte-identical core, adapter, client, coordinator and contracts; the final merge only imports accepted retired-test cleanup. Existing unrelated long-name/preview layout defects remain tracked separately.

author: vahidkaargar
body:
Stacked on #1. Merge that PR first, then this one rebases cleanly onto `main`.

## Problem
The admin route group in `routes/web.php` was declared with `middleware([])`. Any authenticated, verified user could open `/admin/users/{user}/settings` and `/fees` and change fee percentages, `is_active`, `can_place_order`, and `has_api` for any account, including their own.

## Changes
- `role:admin` (Laratrust) on the admin group.
- `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware([Laratrust\Middleware\Role::class])`, so the role check also runs on `/livewire/update` requests made by admin components.
- A migration that inserts the `admin` role, idempotent via `updateOrInsert`.
- `php artisan app:grant-admin-role {email} [--revoke]` to assign the role after deploy.
- The sidebar "Admin" group renders only for admins. `UserSeeder` gives the seeded user the admin role.
- Docs updated (`docs/business-logic.md`).

## Deploy note
After `php artisan migrate`, nobody holds the role yet. Run `php artisan app:grant-admin-role <owner email>`, or the admin area stays locked (403) for everyone.

## Verification
`php artisan test tests/Feature/AdminAccessTest.php` (PHP 8.5.9 + ext-mongodb 2.1.9 + MongoDB 8.0, local): 15 passed, 1 failed.
- Guests are redirected to login, non-admins get 403, admins get 200, nav visibility is correct, and the grant/revoke command works.
- The one failure is `admins can open admin pages (brands index)`. It is an environment gap: the brands page uses Flux Pro's `listbox` select, and Flux Pro can't be downloaded in my sandbox. It should pass in CI, where Flux Pro is installed.
- Full suite: no new failures besides that one. The other 14 local failures are the existing tests that need Flux Pro's `flux:chart`.

## Security impact
This closes a privilege escalation: any user could edit their own fees and enable API access. The diff contains no secrets.

_Requested by **fernando**_

**Antes:** el perfil de un negocio sin productos (Velazco) ofrecía "Explorá la Tienda", pero `/tienda` decía "Tienda no disponible", y la bio usaba un tercer criterio. El carrito se perdía al recargar y se vaciaba apenas se abría WhatsApp, aunque el pedido no se mandara. Los botones de la bio no eran links, y WhatsApp abría `wa.me` con el número local (sin 549), que no funciona.

**Después:** perfil, tienda y bio usan la misma regla para saber si hay tienda: el dueño no la apagó, el plan la incluye y hay al menos un producto activo. El carrito sobrevive a una recarga y solo se vacía cuando el cliente confirma "Sí, ya lo envié". Reservar, Tienda, WhatsApp y Ubicación son links reales, los íconos de redes tienen nombre y los números de WhatsApp se pasan a formato internacional.

**Cómo:**
- `src/utils/storeUtils.js`: `isStoreAvailable()` y `getActiveStoreProducts()`, usados en `BusinessStore.jsx`, `LinkBio.jsx` y `ProfileHighlightsAndStore.jsx`.
- `src/utils/whatsapp.js`: `buildWhatsAppUrl()` agrega el 549 a números argentinos locales (saca el 0 y el 15). Lo usan la tienda y la bio.
- `BusinessStore.jsx`: carrito en `sessionStorage` por negocio, confirmación de envío, búsqueda directa por slug (con la lista completa como respaldo) y sin la consulta a la tabla `store_products`, que no existe (los productos están en `metadata.store_products`).
- `LinkBio.jsx`: botones como `<a>`; los internos navegan dentro de la app al tocarlos.

**Para probar:** `/velazco-padel-club` y su bio sin tienda; `/lumore-nails/tienda` agregar algo, recargar, confirmar el pedido y el botón "Sí, ya lo envié"; en la bio de LuMore, mantener apretado un botón. `npm run build` pasa; el lint de estos archivos no suma errores nuevos (los que aparecen en `main` los baja a warnings el #3).

author: het415
body:
## Why
**Every `executor_degraded` row in the evals from 09-23 to 10-02 was a malformed tool call that three identical attempts couldn't get past.** That's the 3 frozen full-k3 discards (launch_006) and the 5 prompt-cache degradations. The failure is sticky: resending the same turn recovered 4 of 13 episodes on the 2nd attempt and 1 of 9 on the 3rd. The other 8 gave up and the run degraded. The logs only said `BadRequestError`, so nobody could see what the model had generated.

A capped probe replayed the eval's launch_006 executor state. `gpt-oss-safeguard-20b` (the executor's fallback after a rate limit) wrote this on 2 of 3 calls:

```
{"name": "price_history", "arguments": {""}"}
```

`price_history` takes no arguments, so the intended call is unambiguous. Groq rejects the turn because `{""}"` isn't JSON. Five of the executor's six tools take no arguments from the model. `gpt-oss-20b` handled the same state correctly (2 of 2).

## What changes (`backend/agent/nodes/executor.py` only)
- **`_salvage`** rebuilds the call from Groq's `failed_generation`, with no extra LLM call. It only rebuilds two cases:
  - a bound zero-argument tool that hasn't already been called;
  - `review_qa`, and only when its arguments parse and validate against the schema.

  Nothing is invented: a garbled question, an unknown tool, qwen's XML syntax or free text all go to the retry instead.
- **`_correction`**: if nothing can be rebuilt, attempts 2 and 3 no longer resend the identical turn. They append a note with what Groq rejected, the valid tools (and which take no arguments), and the option to finish in plain text. The note is per-call and never stored in graph state.
- **Logging**: the malformed-call line now carries Groq's message and the rejected generation, so the next unknown failure is visible.
- Unchanged: `TOOL_CALL_RETRIES = 3`; `_MalformedToolCalls` still doesn't fail over to other models; the degrade path; `backend/agent/prompts.py`, so the eval's prompt hash is the same.

## Checks
- `pytest tests/`: **467 passed**, 18 of them new in `tests/test_executor_tool_call_recovery.py`, with the network blocked and the Groq key blank. The new tests use the probe's generation verbatim. They cover what may and may not be rebuilt, the rebuilt call running through a LangGraph `ToolNode`, the correction on retry, and the unchanged degrade path.
- The ruff gate (F821, E9) passes.
- **Live check**, the same launch_006 state through the fixed executor node on `gpt-oss-safeguard-20b`: the model produced the same broken call **4 of 4** times, and every time it was rebuilt as `price_history({})` from that one call, with no retry and no degraded run.

## Not covered
- The correction path is tested offline only. Every live failure so far was the rebuildable kind.
- The prompt-cache branch's failures at the "finish" step didn't reproduce in the probe (6 of 6 ended cleanly), so their exact shape is still unseen. The new log line will show it next time.
- The synthesizer's malformed structured outputs (escaped quotes, curly closing quotes, a missing `summary`) recover today by failing over to another model, and are out of scope here.

It touches `backend/**`, so the keyed smoke eval will run.

author: santmun
body: ## Qué cambia El chat de `/demo` pide los mensajes con un cursor que sale del servidor (`GET /demo/poll?after=0` al cargar) y sigue sondeando 6 segundos después de la última burbuja. Apagado salvo `DEMO_MODE=on`. ## Por qué Ticket #F126BE. El visitante escribía, el bot contestaba y la respuesta quedaba en Conversaciones, pero el chat se veía muerto. Verificado en el cliente real del motor (instalaciones 1.0.73/1.0.76), no solo en el reporte: 1. **Reloj del navegador.** `send()` hacía `if(!since) since=Date.now()-1000` y ese número iba como `?after=` a `/demo/poll`, que filtra por `created_at` del servidor. Con el reloj del visitante adelantado, pedía mensajes de un momento que en el servidor todavía no llega y el poll volvía vacío. 2. **Burbujas siguientes.** `poll()` hacía `clearInterval` en cuanto llegaba el primer mensaje. Si la respuesta venía partida (`max_chunks`), las de después no se pintaban. Este repo (starter) no traía `src/demo.ts`. author: rwilliamspbg-ops
body:
## Summary

Turns Ghostlink's existing chat + MCP tool loop into a bounded, capability-gated
local assistant. Seven stacked commits, each compiling and testing on its own.

The invariant throughout: **the model is not the trust boundary, the server is.**
A system prompt telling the model to be careful is not enforcement. Every control
here is checked in Rust before the action happens.

## Commits (in order)

| # | Commit | What |
|---|--------|------|
| 1 | `ef1cf5b` | **Server-side capability boundary.** Classifies every tool call `read`/`write`/`exec` from a `(server, tool)` table, enforced in `invoke_mcp_tool` before dispatch. Fails **closed**: an unlisted tool defaults to `exec`. Session grants are keyed by `(workspace, server, tool)` and never cover `exec`. |
| 2 | `aa6c6eb` | **Durable per-workspace memory** (`crates/mcp-memory`). New internal stdio MCP server over SQLite: `memory_catalog`, `memory_search`, `memory_remember`, `memory_forget`. Scope is stamped server-side at dispatch, so a model-supplied `workspace_id` is discarded. |
| 3 | `48804b2` | **Turn traces with content exclusion enforced by type.** `TraceEvent` has no payload field and no free-form constructor, so prompts/completions/file bodies have nowhere to go. |
| 4 | `ce33716` | **Approval tray.** A gated call is queued as a pending action with a bounded preview and the model gets a handle — the turn finishes normally instead of erroring. GUI tray on the chat. |
| 5 | `07e4d3f` | **Bounded agent loop.** Three independent budgets (steps / tool calls / tokens) replacing a bare iteration counter, plus skills that can only *narrow* the boundary. |
| 6 | `b9ce392` | **Local schedule driver.** Recurring prompts that run as ordinary agent turns, so the same gate and approval queue apply. |

## Design decisions worth reviewing

- **Classification fails closed.** An unlisted tool is `exec`. A wrong `read`
  permits arbitrary command execution; a spurious `exec` costs one approval
  prompt. The asymmetry decides the default.
- **Rejection by absence of a field, not by convention.** `ActionSummary` (the
  approval list payload) has no `args`; `TraceEvent` has no payload; the memory
  catalog's `CatalogEntry` has no body. Adding a leaking field later is a
  deliberate, reviewable diff rather than a one-field-at-a-time erosion.
- **Previews read named fields, never the argument bag.** `build_preview` has no
  JSON-dump fallback, because the argument bag is exactly where a credential
  appears. Two tests pin it.
- **Cron rejects what it doesn't implement.** Without a new dependency a partial
  cron parser's failure mode is a job that silently never fires, so invalid
  specs are refused at *insert* time.

## Bugs the existing test suite caught

Recorded because each was a real defect, not a test artifact:

- **The pre-existing `test_mcp_tool_hashmap_lookup` failed.** The new gate queued
  an approval for a tool whose MCP server wasn't connected — unactionable, so the
  model would report "awaiting your approval" forever. Reachability is now checked
  *before* the gate.
- **Tests were writing to the production queue.** That test wrote real rows into
  `approvals.json` beside the binary, and `approvals.json` /
  `ghostlink_memory.db` / `schedules.json` were missing from `.gitignore` — so a
  queue holding pending actions' arguments could have been committed.

## Validation

Run after rebasing onto `origin/main` (`b16ffd4`):

```
cargo fmt --all --check                                        # clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings          # 0 errors
cargo test --workspace                                         # 688 passed, 0 failed
cargo audit                                                    # 0 vulnerabilities
cd ghostlink_gui_modern && npx tsc --noEmit                    # clean
cd ghostlink_gui_modern && npx eslint .                        # 0 errors
cd ghostlink_gui_modern && npx vitest run                      # 310 passed, 25 files
```

New tests: 23 (`approvals.rs`) + 31 (`agent.rs`, `skills.rs`) + 25
(`scheduler.rs`) + 7 trace/scope-stamping + 9 GUI (`ApprovalTray.test.tsx`).

`cargo audit` reports 5 warnings (`lru` ×2, `anyhow`, `paste`, `chacha20`). All
are **pre-existing** — verified identical at base commit `cf5eb14`, and none
involve `rusqlite`, `libsqlite3-sys`, `hashlink`, `vcpkg`, `fallible-*`, or
`ahash` from the new dependency. Bumping them is a separate change.

No benchmark numbers are claimed here. Nothing in this PR was measured against a
live model server.

## Known limitations

Stated rather than hidden; all are recorded in `docs/PLAN_LOCAL_ASSISTANT.md`:

- **A scheduled turn is offered no MCP tools.** Headless tool selection needs a
  persisted per-schedule tool list. This narrows what a schedule can do and never
  widens it.
- **`ACTIVE_TURN_ID` is process-global.** Two concurrent chats can interleave and
  mislabel an approval's `turn_id`. Correlation is display-only — workspace
  scoping and the approval itself don't depend on it.
- **`invoke_mcp_tool` emits structured logs, not durable traces**, because it
  holds no `BackendState`.
- **Skills are read once per process**; adding one needs a restart. Hot-reload
  would mean deciding what happens to a turn already mid-skill.

## Security

`docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md` is updated in this PR, not deferred to the end — the
classification table, per-workspace grants, approval scoping, and trace
redaction are new controls and the threat model changes with them.

Follows `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s PR expectations: focused commits, validation commands
in the body, and host-specific caveats called out. Closes the seven phases in
`docs/PLAN_LOCAL_ASSISTANT.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
## CI

All workflows green on `9cef07b`:

| | Workflow |
|---|---|
| ✅ Agentic Inference Tests |
| ✅ Benchmarks |
| ✅ CI |
| ✅ Distributed E2E (RPC Fabric) |
| ✅ Docs |
| ✅ Lint |
| ✅ MSRV Verification |
| ✅ Markdown Lint |
| ✅ Production Gate |
| ✅ Security |
| ✅ Tests |

The `Tests` workflow failed on the first push and the failure was real: the
scheduler driver was spawned in the function that constructs the Tokio runtime,
so the backend panicked at startup and never became healthy. Fixed in `9cef07b`
by spawning inside `rt.block_on`, matching where the existing host sampler is
started. Worth noting that the three-platform test matrix passed on the broken
commit — only the job that actually boots the binary found it, which is a good
argument for not treating "all tests green" as "the server starts".

## Follow-up: MCP tool classification audit

Audited the capability table against the *actual* tool set of every configured
server rather than against the table itself, and found six ordinary reads
unclassified — `git_diff_unstaged`, `git_diff_staged`, `sqlite.list_tables`,
`sqlite.describe_table`, `fetch.fetch`, and both `brave-search` tools. They fell
through to the `Exec` default, so looking at a diff or listing tables demanded an
approval. Fixed in `36f3935`, with a `REAL_TOOLS` test table so a tool added
upstream without classification now fails the build.

`fetch.fetch` was the instructive one: the table keys on `(server, tool)`, and
the old loop cross-filed `brave_web_search` under two servers while never filing
the tool that actually exists on the `fetch` server.

Verified against a live server with real connected MCP servers (calculator: 1
tool, memory: 4 tools), reporting the expected classes and approval flags.

**Scope limit worth stating plainly:** this verifies classification correctness.
It does *not* establish that all 14 configured servers connect — 9 cannot run on
this host (`uvx` is not installed, and the release-profile MCP binaries aren't
built). That's an environment gap, not a code defect.

## Follow-up: MCP server verification (all runnable servers)

Installed `uv` (provides `uvx`) and built the four release-profile MCP crates,
then connected **every server that can run

author: antoinetoussaint-byte
body:
## Summary

- **`Client.NotifyUser(ctx, UserNotice) (bool, error)`** calls `ModuleCapabilitiesService.NotifyUser` on the **authority endpoint** through `callAsModule`, the same way `NotifyOrgAdmins` does (#23). It sends the internal token and the module Work Context, and refreshes a rejected Work Context once.
  - The module names the recipient. The host checks they are a member of the tenant (PermissionDenied otherwise) and applies their category policy. The result says whether the notice was **delivered**, which is false when an optional category was switched off. That case is not an error.
  - A notice without a tenant, recipient, title or category is refused with `ErrInvalidNotice` before any call is made. A mint-only client answers `ErrNoAuthority`.
- `gen/` already carries the procedure, and the host serves it on the authority endpoint (`business.moduleAuthorityProcedures` in module-saas-starter). Nothing is regenerated.

First consumer: obin-ai/module-annotations#25. A reply or a resolution in a thread notifies the other people in it.

Classification: **fix**, a facade method on the existing seam. Without it, a module has to hand-roll the authority call: the transport, the two credentials, and refresh-once.

## Tests

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./moduleauthority/` and `gofmt` all pass. The new tests cover:

- the call reaches the authority endpoint as the module, carrying the internal token, the module Work Context and every notice field;
- a suppressed notice comes back as `delivered = false` with no error;
- an incomplete notice never reaches the host. I confirmed this test fails with the recipient check removed;
- the host's `InvalidArgument` (unknown type) and `PermissionDenied` (non-member) come back unchanged;
- a mint-only client refuses with `ErrNoAuthority`.

**Not verified:** a call against a real accounts service. The fake reproduces the authority endpoint's credential checks and the NotifyUser refusals it documents.

author: tomasz
body:
Closes #73

## What
Mechanical test-only change; no `contract` label. Cuts work from the unit suite that proved nothing new, and stops fixture catalogs from piling up in `build/`:

- `test/woff2.test.js`: the encoder round trip and the quality-11 check now run on two shipped files (the first TrueType and the first of the 11 CFF), not all 174. The header, padding, transform and payload checks still cover every file, but they only decode.
- `test/property.test.js`: the 500-seed determinism loop no longer runs brotli. The live-catalog budget test from #121 (3 largest files × 30 effects × both parameter ends) is kept unchanged and is the budget gate. Updated the stale header comment.
- `test/pick.test.js`: deleted the two 4k-seed loops (deny rules, role-set colours/ground). `property.test.js` already checks both over 10k fixture and 2k live seeds, using an independent checker. Fixed the stale "until WP-11 and WP-12" comment.
- `test/catalog.js`: `fixtureCatalog()` unlinks `build/fixture-catalog.<pid>.js` after importing it.

## Why
At d68cf89: `woff2.test.js:18-33` encoded 174 fonts at q11 (5.4 s here), `woff2.test.js:125-138` brotlied every font again at q5, `property.test.js:100-126` brotlied 500 renders of a 150 B stub font, `pick.test.js:123-129,146-154` repeated the property loops, and `catalog.js:21` left one file per worker per run (4 per run seen here).

## Proof
- check: pass (`pnpm run check`; 0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings in files outside this PR)
- goldens: unchanged (`git status --porcelain test/golden` empty)
- identity: n/a (tests only); pick golden vectors untouched and passing
- e2e: n/a (no e2e/, src/, effects/ or font change)
- budget: worst live response 11393 B brotli · `f:style-script.n-base-static p:wada1-271.1302 e:depth-long(a=135,d=20) l:stack-fit(g=6,a=center,side)`
- `vp test` wall time (vitest Duration, devcontainer on Colima, 4 CPUs, M-series host):
  - before (origin/main 78c6faa): 11.84 s, 10.04 s, 8.19 s
  - after: 8.03 s, 7.77 s, 7.20 s, 5.35 s, 6.59 s, 8.13 s, 7.79 s
  - `woff2.test.js` went from 6.2 s to 0.6 s, and the determinism loop from 4.7 s to 0.6 s.
- **The ≤ 2 s target is not reachable while the live budget test exists.** Run alone (`vp test test/property.test.js -t heaviest`), that test takes 2.93 s, and 4.4–6 s when the rest of the suite runs alongside it. It is the right gate, so this PR leaves it as it is. `test/fonts.test.js` (1.9 s, outside this row's Paths) is the next largest cost.
- `build/` after two consecutive `vp test` runs contains only `catalog.js`, with no `fixture-catalog.*` files.
- sheets: n/a

## Out of scope / follow-ups
- Making the live budget test cheaper (e.g. one brotli per effect on the single largest file, or a lower quality as a pre-filter) would change what the gate covers. That needs the owner's decision, not this row's.
- `test/fonts.test.js` at ~1.9 s is outside this row.
- Lowering `testTimeout` is left to K1 (owner file).

- 봉인된 재구매 최종 Test의 1회 평가 결과를 Validation과 구분해 기록하고, 사용자 노출·dev 연동의 운영 판단을 명시합니다.

author: vinicius-ssantos
body:
## Problem

The eleven questions of topic 7 had **no mechanical backing**, and they had resisted it the longest. A claim about modules is not true of a flat set of sources: whether `requires static` is resolved at run time, what `exports` permits that `opens` does not, whether a qualified export really excludes a third module — none of that can be shown by compiling files on the class path. Nine of the eleven needed a real module graph.

The pack goes from 124 to **135 of 150**, and topic 7 is complete.

## Solution

### Proved by running a module graph

| Question | What the program establishes |
|---|---|
| `requires static` | Declared at compile time, then **not resolved into the boot layer** although `optional` sits on the module path right next to the module that names it. `Class.forName("o.Flag")` fails. |
| `exports` / `opens` | A private field *and* a private method of an **opened** package read reflectively, while the same reflection on a merely **exported** package is refused with `InaccessibleObjectException`. |
| qualified exports | `isExported` answers `true` for the two modules the directive names and `false` for others; the unqualified export answers `true`. A third module really does read it. |
| `uses` / `provides` | A provider module that **nothing requires** is bound into the graph by service resolution, and `ServiceLoader` finds it. |
| `open module` | Declares **zero** `opens` directives, because being open covers every package, and still exports exactly one. |
| implicit `java.base` | A module declaring no `requires` has `java.base` as a *mandated* requirement, and can read it. |

### Proved by not compiling

| Question | Diagnostic |
|---|---|
| a package-private type in a fully exported package | `not.def.public.cant.access` |
| a named package reaching the unnamed one | `cant.resolve.location` |
| `import java.util.*` reaching `java.util.concurrent` | `cant.resolve.location` |

### Proved without a graph

- **automatic module** — a JAR with no `module-info.class`, built at run time and found through `ModuleFinder`: `isAutomatic=true`, with the name and version read off the file name and every package exported.
- **the launch form** — the launcher's own `jdk.module.main` and `jdk.module.main.class`. This question is proved *by how the harness runs it*: the harness launches a modular question with exactly the `--module-path <dir> --module <module>/<main class>` form the question asks about.

## Two expectations I had to strengthen

- `t07-unnamed-package-import` first attempted `import Helper;`, which fails as a **syntax** error (`compiler.err.expected: '.'`). Any typo anywhere in the file would satisfy that code, so the expectation would have been close to vacuous. It now references the type directly and pins `cant.resolve.location`.
- `t07-implicit-java-base` printed the whole `Requires` set, including java.base's recorded version (`@21`). That depends on the release the build compiles against rather than on anything the question claims, so it prints names and modifiers only.

## Two places I kept the program honest rather than tidy

- `t07-exports-and-opens` prints `qExported=true` for a package that is only **opened**. That is correct and documented — opening implies exporting — but it reads like a contradiction, so the program says why instead of hiding the line.
- `t07-open-module-semantics` proves **one half** of its question. That every package of an open module is open for deep reflection is shown by reading a private field of a package the module never exports. That `exports` still governs ordinary compile-time access **cannot be shown by the same program**, because a program that runs is not a program that fails to compile. That half is shown by `t07-export-does-not-make-type-public`, and the program says so rather than implying more than it establishes.

## Evidence

- [x] Unit tests — `ContentPackTest`: **153 tests, 0 failures** on JDK 25, the JDK the build pins. Two expectations were broken on purpose and the suite failed **exactly twice, on those two**; restored, 153 and 0.
- [ ] Integration tests — unchanged.
- [ ] End-to-end tests — unchanged.
- [x] Manual or visual demonstration — `docs/release/content-review-packet.md` regenerated, so each graph and its output are in the packet a reviewer reads.

## review.json untouched

All **20** human reviews still hold, **0** marked changed — checked by running `reviewStatusOf` over the pack. `t07-requires-transitive` is reviewed and was not modified.

## What this does not establish

The programs show what the module system does. They do not show that a question asks it well, that its options are unambiguous, or that it matches an exam objective. **130 questions remain unreviewed by a human.**

## Scope

- Included: 11 questions — 9 module graphs, 2 flat — the regenerated packet, a changelog entry.
- Not included: the remaining **15**, across topics 8 to 10. One of them, `t08-volatile-increment`, asserts that increments *can* be lost; I do not expect to prove a possibility deterministically, and I would rather leave it to the human reviewer than add a test that passes most of the time.

## Quality review

- [x] Acceptance criteria satisfied — partial progress on #84, which stays open.
- [x] Security and privacy impact reviewed — the graphs compile and run only in tests, never against learner input. `t07-automatic-module-jar` writes a JAR into a temp directory and deletes both.
- [x] Accessibility impact reviewed — not applicable.
- [x] Migration and rollback impact reviewed — content files only; nothing is published by this change.
- [x] Observability updated — not applicable.
- [x] Documentation and changelog updated — both.
- [ ] CI green — pending.

body:
Before: the agent could reach places but not use things. A chain like "turn on the PC > WITHDRAW > POTION" or "START > POKéMON > CUT" had to be guessed one Jev tick at a time. A wall the world tracker gave up on after three bumps stayed given up on, even after the player gained what opens it.

After: `anygame/chains.py` searches menu chains breadth first from a save state. Each pick is played out to the next decision, and the search returns the first chain whose outcome a test names, with the exact presses to replay it. In Pokemon Red, "Withdrew POTION." from Red's PC was found in 19 tries and replays exactly. In Aevilia, the search mapped the pause menu, which lists buttons rather than a cursor. A line that tells of a gain ("Received HM01") reopens the walls the tracker had given up on.

Gap 3 (numbers), which this PR first carried, is already on the base branch, so the diff is gap 4 only.

How:
- `chains.search(device, read_text, test)` opens with A or START. At each menu it tries the cursor places a direction reaches, each picked with A, plus B, SELECT and START. Only screens B backs out of are treated as menus, so the world's directions are never taken for a cursor. Tests: `says(words)` and `moves(pos, d)`. `Recorder`/`replay` record and play the chain.
- `chains.Gains(world).see(text)` and `reopen(world)`.
- `playout.py`: a play-out now ends with "waits" when neither A nor a direction changes the screen (a pause menu that lists buttons), instead of running to the cap.
- `tiletext.py`: a glyph whose character another glyph already holds needs two agreeing lines. The shared Pokemon book had trusted w as v from one reading.
- Docs: `docs/chains.md`, `docs/full-run-gaps.md`, `docs/playout.md`. Check script: `scripts/chains_check.py`. Tests: `test/test_chains.py` (4), plus one each in test_playout and test_tiletext. Full suite: 128 passed, 4 skipped.

No device, scanner, probe, grader or runner decision code changed. Call sites for the long-horizon branch are in `docs/chains.md`.

author: anyukhin
body:
## Что было

На 3D-доске темницы соломенные тюфяки, а в зале башни большой красный ковёр лежали белыми прямоугольниками и под светом выглядели засвеченными.

## Причина

Палитра доски читается из CSS-переменных темы через `getPropertyValue`, и значение приходит неразвёрнутым: `color-mix(in srgb, #ab9f91 80%, #1a120a)`. Холст такую строку понимает, а `THREE.Color` нет: он пишет `Unknown color` и оставляет `ffffff`. Процедурная заглушка ковра красит ткань в `floorAlt`, а кайму в `wall`, и в теме пещеры и базовой теме обе стороны становились белыми.

## Что изменилось

- **Палитра материалов.** `materialPalette` / `plainCssColor` в `src/board-render.ts` разбирают `color-mix(in srgb, …)` с вложенными смесями по CSS Color 5: доли, дополнение до ста, прозрачность при сумме меньше ста, предумноженная альфа. `createBoard3DScene` отдаёт развёрнутую палитру материалам three.js, а холстам пола — прежнюю.
- **2D не меняется намеренно.** Если развернуть палитру и для холстов, сетка на фактурах (`shade(palette.wall)`) в пещере становится тёмной на тёмном камне и пропадает. Сейчас она светлая, потому что `shade` не разбирал смесь и брал запасной цвет пола. Правка вида сетки — отдельное решение, в этот PR она не входит.
- **Плоские наклейки — штампом.** Ковры, шкуры, тюфяки и пятна набора детализации без своей модели (двойник `rug` или `floor_stain`, `isDetailFloorStamp`) ложатся на пол 3D своим 2D-штампом. Кадр вырезается из `detail-v1/prop-atlas.png` в ту же загрузку, что и GLB (`loadPropModelAssets` → `stamps`). Габарит и поворот считает `stampFit`, вынесенный из `drawStamp` и общий для обоих видов. Прозрачность — `PROP_DECAL_ALPHA`, как у декали в 2D. Наклейка не пишет глубину, поэтому сетка и туман ложатся поверх.
- Своя модель в выпуске или пакете стиля сильнее штампа. Пока атлас не пришёл или если он недоступен, лежит процедурная плашка двойника, теперь в цветах темы. После сбоя атлас запрашивается заново.
- Наклейки-растения и камни (камыш, галька, ритуальный круг) остаются объёмными процедурными моделями. Это записано в `docs/known-limitations.md`.

## Проверка

- `pnpm verify` локально: 5517 тестов (1 пропущен штатно), MVP 5/5, `typecheck:server`, `tsc` клиента, `vite build`.
- Новые тесты:
  - `test/board3d-scene.test.mjs` — `color-mix` темы не красит материалы белым, а холст получает строку темы.
  - `test/prop-model-assets.test.mjs` — габарит и поворот штампа совпадают с 2D; модель сильнее штампа; штамп получают только плоские наклейки; загрузка вырезает кадр из атласа, освобождает текстуру один раз и повторяет запрос после сбоя.
- Стенд новых локаций, кадры 2D и 3D до и после: в темнице тюфяки соломенные, в башне ковёр красный; 2D-сетка темницы не изменилась; снежная локация без регрессий.

author: nick-neely
body:
## Description

### What

The ADR 0221 household purge now writes a content-free Deletion Record (subject kind `household`) to the Recovery Journal before it deletes anything. A restore can no longer bring a purged household back. Recovery tooling can re-apply the record through the same erasure path.

### Why

[ADR 0250](docs/adr/0250-one-backup-window-bounds-recovery-and-the-deletion-tail.md) says every irreversible purge writes a Deletion Record before it deletes. #616 did this for account deletion. This change covers the household purge, and it unblocks the restore tooling in #623.

### How

- **Journal, then delete:** `runHouseholdPurgeSweep` takes a `RecoveryJournal`. It writes the household's Deletion Record after the last-safe-point eligibility check and before the erasure transaction opens. If the write fails, the household is counted as `failed` and left whole for the next pass. The cron wires in the Blob journal that account deletion already uses.
- **Record time:** the record is timed at the purge attempt, not at the recovery deadline. Deletion Record Retention ages a record from its time, so a back-dated record from a purge that ran weeks late could expire inside the Backup Window. As a result, a retry after a failed erasure writes a second record. That is harmless because re-application is idempotent.
- **Re-application:** `reapplyHouseholdDeletionRecord` erases the household through `eraseHousehold`, the same path the sweep uses, and leaves a tombstone. It returns `absent` when the household is already gone. It refuses a non-household record. It also refuses a household that was never dissolved, because such a household cannot have been purged inside the Backup Window, so it goes to the operator instead. It doesn't re-check the deadline and never writes to the journal. The restore tooling in #623 is its caller, so it is not added to the barrel yet.
- **Store:** `HouseholdPurgeStore` gains `findHousehold`, implemented in both the Drizzle store and the in-memory store.
- **Domain:** `DeletionSubjectKind` is now `"account" | "household"`.

## Related Issues

Closes #618

## User-visible impact

None. Purges behave the same; each one now also leaves a Deletion Record in the private Blob journal.

## Privacy-boundary impact

This strengthens the deletion promise: a purged household now stays purged across a point-in-time restore. The record is content-free, holding only the subject kind, the household id, and a time.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other

## Testing & Visuals

- [x] Linting passed (`pnpm lint`)
- [ ] Formatting passed (`pnpm format:check`)
- [x] Typecheck passed (`pnpm typecheck`)
- [x] Tests passed (`pnpm test`)
- [x] Build succeeded (`pnpm build`)
- [x] Manually verified

## Checks run

- `pnpm verify`
- `pnpm coverage:ci && FALLOW_AUDIT_BASE=origin/main pnpm fallow:ci`
- `pnpm --filter @tendnote/db db:purge:check` against the local Postgres. It now also checks that the record is journaled while the workspace row still exists, and that re-application purges a restored household exactly once.

## AI assistance (optional)

Implemented with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5).

  * Reapplying a deletion record safely removes restored household data and can be repeated without creating duplicate purge records.
* **Reliability**

body:
Budget Bloom becomes installable and launches in standalone mode. Budgets, groceries, and account pages continue to require the server. Going offline replaces the visible page with a generic message; navigations never return cached household data.

## Changed files

- `app.py`: public manifest and root `/sw.js` routes, explicit content types/root scope, content-derived cache versions, same-origin manifest/worker CSP, and `no-store, private` for dynamic HTML/JSON/redirect/error responses.
- `templates/pwa_head.html` and six user-facing templates: shared manifest, theme color, Apple metadata/icon, and registration include.
- `static/sw.js`: explicit CSS/JavaScript/icon/offline-file allowlist, credential-free installation, response type/redirect checks, obsolete-cache cleanup, and network-only navigation with a generic offline fallback. No runtime cache writes. APIs, authenticated responses, unknown static URLs, and Supabase are excluded.
- `static/pwa.js` and `static/app.js`: root registration, clearing private DOM on connectivity loss and page departure, revalidation after history restoration, and data-free auth notifications that refresh other tabs after login/logout.
- `static/icons/*.png`, `scripts/build_pwa_icons.py`: 192/512 PNGs, 512 maskable and 180 Apple icons, resized from the supplied repository sprout-and-coin logo without substitute artwork.
- `static/offline.html`, `static/layout-fixes.css`: English/Spanish offline message, mobile input sizing, keyboard-height dialog scrolling, larger close controls, grocery wrapping, and bottom safe-area spacing.
- `README.md`: Android/iPhone installation, internet requirement, cache/update behavior, reproducible checks, and HTTPS-domain acceptance steps.
- `tests/test_pwa.py`, `tests/pwa_worker.cjs`, `tests/pwa_browser.py`: route/header/icon checks, executable cache-policy tests, and real Chromium/FastAPI privacy checks with synthetic accounts and mocked database calls.

Budget calculations, Supabase schema, session/auth mechanisms, desktop styling, runtime requirements, and deployment configuration are preserved. No deployment was performed. No configured Supabase key/URL, session token, or real financial data was added to public assets or committed.

## Test results

All run in the prepared `budget-bloom` environment:

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'`: **17 passed**, including all 14 existing tests.
- `node tests/pwa_worker.cjs`: passed — allowlist, no private-navigation writes, offline fallback, old-cache cleanup, query/cross-origin/POST exclusions, redirected asset rejection.

author: hanthor
body:
Adds `StateSnapshot::diff(&other) -> Vec<(&StateKey, Option<&str>, Option<&str>)>`: every slot where two states disagree, in key order.

The walk descends both HAMTs in step and skips any subtree whose content hash matches, so two states of a large room that share history cost only the changed paths. Where the shapes differ at one level (leaf on one side, branch on the other), the two small subtrees are compared entry by entry.

Why now: the Synapse importer (#557, #563) runs the room version's resolver (v1 `state_res_v1`, v2 via ruma) at every fork whose parent states differ. In `!iMZEhwCvbfeAYUxAjZ:t2l.io` (104k events, about 100k state events, 8.6k merges) a full `for_each` per merge is the cost that matters. Live state resolution can use the same call to find the conflicted keys.

Pure and additive: no format, digest or key change.

Tests: `crates/spindle-core/tests/state_diff.rs` (a proptest against a full comparison over a shared base with diverging writes, unrelated states, and a 20,000-slot state that differs in two slots).

Closes #198. Closes #92.

Part of #75.

The second part of #92: the drive's labels popover (with its colour picker), the "New Credential" dialog and its five service forms, and the "Create Datalink" dialog with the datalink editor (`JSONSchemaInput`, `FilePathInput`). With it, no drive code calls `setModal` with a React element any more, and nothing in `src/cloud/` imports `#/`.

## What moved

| React (deleted) | Vue |
| --- | --- |
| `modals/ManageLabelsModal.tsx`, `components/ColorPicker.tsx` | `src/cloud/labels/` — `ManageLabelsModal.vue` (the popover, on the modal stack), `ManageLabelsForm.vue`, `NotFoundLabel.vue`, `ColorPicker.vue`, `labelChanges.ts` |
| `modals/CreateCredentialModal.tsx`, `data/serviceCredentials/*` | `src/cloud/credentials/` — `CreateCredentialModal.vue`, the Snowflake, Google, Strava, Microsoft 365 and Salesforce forms, `CredentialsFormFooter.vue`, `credentialInfos.ts` (over the existing recipes in `src/cloud/serviceCredentials/`) |
| `modals/UpsertDatalinkModal.tsx`, `components/JSONSchemaInput.tsx`, `components/FilePathInput.tsx`, `pages/dashboard/components/DatalinkInput.tsx` | `src/cloud/datalinks/` — `UpsertDatalinkModal.vue`, `JSONSchemaInput.vue` (+ `SchemaTextInput.vue`), `FilePathInput.vue` (mounts the project view's `FileBrowserWidget.vue` directly, no bridge), `DatalinkInput.vue`, `DatalinkFormInput.vue` (moved from `properties/`) |
| `cloud/properties/reactDatalinkInput.ts` + its `DASHBOARD_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST` entry | gone: the Properties tab uses the Vue editor |
| `modals/UpsertSecretModal.tsx` (its form only, left for the React `AssetProperties.tsx` that #190 deleted) + `upsertSecretFormParity.test.tsx` | gone (unused) |

Mount sites: the toolbar's New Credential / New Datalink and the labels column's two edit buttons were `Dialog.Trigger`s and now use `useVueModalTrigger` (keeping `aria-expanded`); the context menus' Label / New Credential / New Datalink use `setVueModal`. `labels` and `datalinks` join `CLOUD_AREAS`.

Primitives (additive where possible): `Popover.vue` gains `anchor` (Reka `PopoverAnchor` with a `reference`), `opener` (focus return without a trigger), `containerPadding` and a `closed` event; `focusReturn.ts` exports `returnFocus`; `Tooltip.vue` opens on focus only for keyboard focus (new `$/utils/inputModality`); `Dropdown.vue`'s list root is `contents`; `CheckboxControl.vue` names its input by its own text.

## Rulings (recorded as "Rulings from #198" in the foundations record)

1. One PR, logical commits; the leftover React secret form and `data/serviceCredentials/` go too.
2. All three are cloud areas: `labels/`, `credentials/`, `datalinks/`; `labels`/`datalinks` join `CLOUD_AREAS` (`credentials` can't: the core's `UpsertSecretPanel.vue` imports it).
3. A popover on the modal stack, anchored to the React element that opened it (`anchor`), returning focus to its opener.
4. **The Escape gap is fixed where contained**: the labels popover and its nested "Create Label" form each stop Escape and close only themselves (as #92's rename form does). `Popover.vue` itself does not stop the key — that would close popovers before their combo box / dropdown lists, changing #191's pinned order for every caller.
5. **Seven React quirks kept**, each a visible change for a separate decision (plus #92's three duplicate-dialog quirks, still open in #198): the context-menu popover sits at the window's top-left corner (React's anchor ref was cleared as the menu closed); "Next color" does nothing visible; Enter in the search resets the form; the pills show every label; labels written from the opening snapshot (two creations in a row keep only the second); an invalid secret's description shows twice; the `boolean` editor case is a plain checkbox (unreachable from the datalink schema).
6. Assistive technology: the `TagGroup` grid becomes a `list` (decision 1); the popover traps focus (#83); dialogs named by their titles (#156); each credential checkbox named by its own text ("Sheets", as React) instead of the whole group's.
7. Primitive fixes found by comparing the running app: keyboard-only tooltip on focus (a mouse-cancelled confirmation returned focus to the trash button and showed "Delete"); the dropdown's list is the grid item again, as in React; after deleting a label focus goes to the search field, as React's focus scope did.
8. `JSONSchemaInput.vue` keeps React's structure part for part, its classes, react-aria's keyboard-only focus ring and `anyOf` member choice.
9. Credential forms as React: `''` defaults, Microsoft 365 name "Microsoft365", Google shows failures in the form, the others toast.
10. No changelog entry (`CI: No changelog needed`).

## Parity numbers

- **Dashboard suite** (`integration-test/dashboard/`, WSL, CI settings: `CI=true`, 2 workers, `--retries=0`, production build, port 6419), fresh clones: **develop 5/5 runs, 440/440 test runs passed** (88 passed + 3 skipped per run); **branch 5/5 runs, 440/440 passed**. An extra axe scan of the ported overlays (labels popover, "Create Label", credential dialog, datalink dialog) gives identical violations on both branches (popover: `color-contrast` ×1; create form: `color-contrast` ×1, `label` ×10 — the unnamed colour radios, as React).

author: kushuh
body:
## Summary

First of the two follow-ups from #602 (HPKE is next, stacked on this). ECDH-ES and ECDH-ES+AES-KW only accepted X25519 keys, although the IANA registry marks ECDH-ES *Recommended+* and RFC 7518 expects it on P-256. They now run on X25519, P-256, P-384 and P-521, all through Go's `crypto/ecdh`.

- **Keys:** a new `jwk.ECDHPreset` binds an algorithm to a curve; `GenerateECDHKey` / `ConsumeECDHKey` take one. NIST keys serialize as `"kty":"EC"` with full-size coordinates (RFC 7518 §6.2), X25519 keys as `"OKP"`. Decoding rejects a `d` that does not match the public point, and `ConsumeECDHKey` rejects a key on another curve than the preset's.
- **Key agreement:** the ephemeral key follows the recipient's curve, and the `epk` names the matching key type. The stdlib validates every point on decode, which covers the rfc8725bis `epk` validation rule.
- **Why a preset keyed by `(alg, curve)`:** HPKE's DHKEM keys are the same Go type and use the same JWK mapping, so the HPKE PR adds its presets here instead of a parallel key family.

## Decisions to review

- `jwk.GenerateECDH()` / `ConsumeECDH()` are deprecated wrappers for `GenerateECDHKey(jwk.ECDHESX25519)`, not removed — this joins the unreleased v2.3.0 as a minor.

## Breaking changes

None. The deprecated functions keep their X25519 behavior; the v2.3.0 guide gains a section.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/test.sh` — 850 tests pass; each commit builds, vets and passes on its own
- [x] Known answers: RFC 7518 Appendix C decodes Bob's key + Alice's P-256 `epk` to the published CEK `VqqN6vgjbSBcIijNcacQGg`; Bob's key round-trips byte-for-byte
- [x] Producer→Recipient round trips for ECDH-ES on P-256 and ECDH-ES+KW on P-521, each with a fresh ephemeral key per token
- [x] `golangci-lint` (pinned) — 0 issues; prettier passes
- [ ] CI green

author: copilot
body:
P2 follow-up to the P0/P1 readiness fixes: a fully blank lead could be sent to the CRM, and a common phone-number format bypassed the pre-consent TCPA gate and leaked into the LLM conversation.

## Changes

- **Empty-handoff guard** (`src/ChatWidget.tsx`) — the summary panel is reachable with every intake question skipped, and the webhook accepts empty optional fields by design, so "Send summary securely" could deliver an empty record. `sendToProfessional` now requires at least one of name, email, or cell phone:

```ts
if (!state.fullName && !state.email && !state.cellPhone) {
  setHandoff('Please share at least your name, email, or cell phone before sending your summary.')
  return
}
```

- **Phone-gate coverage** (`src/useUnderwritingState.ts`) — `containsPhone()` only matched area-code-shaped numbers (`(555) 123-4567`, `5551234567`), so a pre-consent `555-123-4567` fell through to the LLM instead of the discard-and-disclose flow. Added a bare-format pattern to the gate:

```ts
const barePhonePattern = /(?:^|\D)(1?[\s.-]?\d{3}[\s.-]\d{4})(?:\D|$)/
export function containsPhone(text: string): boolean {
  return phonePattern.test(text) || barePhonePattern.test(text)
}
```

Capture into state is unchanged: numbers are still only stored via the original pattern after TCPA consent is granted.

author: daniel-c137
body:
Implements #22: the New meeting dialog can schedule a meeting with invitees picked from the workspace directory, and the host can invite or remove people.

## What
- `POST /meetings` takes `scheduled_start`, `duration_min` and `invitee_ids`. With a start time the meeting is `scheduled`; without one it is `live` now, as before. The start time must be timezone-aware, the duration must be 1 to 1440 minutes, and invitees must be members of the caller's team. Unknown ids get a 422 that lists them. The host is never stored as an invitee, and duplicate ids are dropped.
- Joining a scheduled meeting: when the host joins, the meeting starts (`start_meeting`, scheduled -> live, `started_at` set). Anyone else on the team who joins first gets a 409 saying "has not started yet" and the scheduled ISO time. Once the meeting is live, invitees and other teammates join by link as before, with no waiting room. Ended meetings still return 409.
- `GET /directory?q=&limit=` returns `list[Person]` from the caller's workspace through `search_members`. `limit` defaults to 20 and must be 1 to 100. The router is new: `brain/src/brain/api/directory.py`, registered in `api/__init__.py`.
- `POST /meetings/{id}/invitees` (`InviteRequest`) and `DELETE /meetings/{id}/invitees/{person_id}`: host only (403), other teams get 404, and the same members-only rule applies. Changing invitees on an ended meeting returns 409. Both return the meeting. Removing someone who isn't invited does nothing.
- `end_meeting` was a read followed by a write. It is now `transition_status(id, {"live"}, "processing")`. On `Conflict` it still returns the current meeting with a 200. It also records `ended_at`.
- `GET /meetings` is unchanged: it stays team-scoped and returns scheduled, live and past meetings in the store's order. New tests cover this.

## Interfaces for later issues
- `brain.api.meetings.end_live_meeting(store, meeting_id) -> tuple[Meeting, bool]`. The bool is True only for the call that made the live -> processing move. #24 should start the pipeline in `end_meeting` when it is True; a comment marks that spot.
- `brain.api.meetings.team_invitees(store, team_id, host_id, ids) -> list[str]`: dedupes the ids, drops the host, and raises a 422 that names anyone not on the team.

## Contract / Store
No changes to contracts or the `Store` protocol. Known limit: adding or removing an invitee reads the meeting and then calls `set_invitees` with the full list. Two overlapping invite edits by the same host could therefore lose one. Only the host makes these edits, so I kept the protocol as it is.

## TDD
- 040a209 Add failing tests for scheduled meetings, invitees and the directory (31 failed, 6 passed. The failures were 404s for the missing routes, missing validation (200 instead of 422), scheduled meetings created as live, and the `end_live_meeting` import.)
- 22c59d7 Implementation

## Checks
- `uv run pytest brain realtime`: 192 passed, 2 deselected
- `uv run ruff check .`: clean
- `uv run ruff format --check .`: clean
- No TS or board changes, so no typecheck.

## Live / unverified
This change makes no Gemini call, so there is no live test. Not verified: a real Supabase store (the tests use `InMemoryStore`) and the board UI path.

author: wieslawsoltes
body:
Follow-up of #1305 / #1307 (both closed): the two gaps an earlier pass reported - lambda return nullability and nullable annotations through generic instantiation.

## What is done
- **Lambdas and anonymous methods are checked against the delegate type they are converted to** (`nullable/walker-lambdas.js`). Before, the body was walked with no signature: nothing was reported for `Func<string> f = () => maybe;`, and the parameters of a lambda always counted as not null. Now a possibly null return for a non-nullable result is CS8603 (expression bodies, `return` statements, anonymous methods), and a parameter of an annotated type starts as possibly null (`Func<string?, int> g = x => x.Length;` is CS8602).
- **`Func<string>` and `Func<string?>` are told apart** (`symbols/annotated-instantiations.js`). The framework registry hands out one object per closed type, so the annotations of the type arguments were lost. For delegate types, an instantiation written with annotations is now a view of the shared object: the same members, the same equality, its own `typeArguments`; views are interned per annotation pattern. Other framework types keep the shared object.

## Limits
- Only delegate instantiations get a view: `List<string?>` and `List<string>` are still one object (their nested annotations are not compared in signatures, as stated on #3554).
- An async lambda (its result is wrapped in a task) and a lambda whose delegate type is oblivious are not checked.
- The natural type of a lambda (`var f = () => maybe;`) does not carry the null-state of its body: `string s = f();` has no CS8600.
- Local functions already had their own return check; nothing changed there.

## Verification (Roslyn 5.3.0.0 pins)
- New fixtures: `nullable-lambdas/cs8603-cs8602-against-the-delegate-type` (10 warnings, all matching) and the output fixture `nullable-lambdas/delegates-of-annotated-types-run` (prints what .NET prints on the bytecode and the CIL back end - delegates of annotated types still execute).
- `tests/compiler-nullable-lambdas.test.js` (4 tests).
- `node scripts/limited.js node --test tests/compiler-*.test.js`: 1529 pass, 0 fail.
- Differential corpus: 1205/1352 before, 1207/1354 after (warnings 1236 -> 1238, bytecode / CIL 388 -> 389 of 494), no regression; `run.test.js` 5/5.

The last end-to-end roots holding a symlink were still built path by path, so the one link each case turns on sat among `mkdir` and `write_text` calls, and nothing told the next test to do otherwise. They now declare their roots from workspace parts, and the test rules make that the way every end-to-end test writes a root.

- A link anywhere under the root is a part, and a skill lists the links in its own directory beside its references, so no test spells the skills layout to place one.
- Links are written after every file, so a link may dangle or lead to a directory the workspace wrote, and no file is written through one; a link at a path already taken fails the test, as a file does.
- A tree outside the repository, which a link leads to, is a second workspace written beside the root, which the write now creates when absent.
- A new `test-e2e` rule document states the end-to-end framework whole: the installed command run through `run_cli`, what it prints pinned by one plain-text snapshot per case with only per-machine values redacted, and the root written from a workspace that sets only the literals its case turns on, inline under `#: Given` unless several tests share it.


Closes #331

author: tellowss
body:
Improve shooting with confirmed equipment lifecycle feedback, layered spatial audio, in-play accountability story, twenty-map pressure progression and overall scene polish with grounded production-candidate props.

Address repetitive survival play with three operation rhythms and field tactics. Drawing design inspiration from CS2 objective/utility play, ARC Raiders extraction choices and Helldivers 2 support timing, reimplement these as offline site controls: finite 10-second control lines slow carts/gas without affecting workers, warning clocks or damage; finite support calls deliver existing recovery/radio pickups after 1.2 seconds at the locked call location; objective readiness now offers a choice instead of automatically ending the run. Request handoff after minimum patrol and actual boss/zone/response conditions, hold within 72 units for four seconds, cancel on movement or damage, or continue for star objectives. Preserve the 180-second fallback and once-only existing rewards/unlocks. Fix the old stretched ultimate wrapper blocking new mobile buttons.

Research selection is current popularity plus transfer suitability, not global rank 1–3. Source snapshots, official mechanic descriptions and implementation boundaries are in docs/survivors-shooter-three-reference-20261004.md. No original IP assets or online multiplayer added.

Validation: 210 test files / 1,125 tests pass (one opt-in calibration file/test skipped); typecheck/build pass. Six real Chromium early-gameplay cases cover keyboard/buttons at portrait/landscape/PC sizes, cooldowns, bounds, instructions and pause/resume; zero render errors. author: lalalalendia
body:
Follow-up to merged #1108.

The GUI walkthrough asserted that `operations().len()` must remain unchanged after Ctrl+Z. That contradicts the canonical `pub-editor` contract: `operations()` exposes the current undo/applied stack, and `EditorSession::undo()` pops exactly one operation from that stack and moves it to redo.

This PR changes only the acceptance invariant:
- before Ctrl+Z: N applied operations;
- after Ctrl+Z: N-1 applied operations and exact pre-edit geometry;
- after Ctrl+Y: N applied operations and exact edited geometry.

No production behavior changes.

## J-L · Ventanas por fecha, sin el día de hoy
- `gameMetrics` (metrics.js): la media de 7 días, el «7d», la tendencia y los días de evento de los últimos 30 cuentan los días **por fecha**, hacia atrás desde ayer (el último día cerrado). Antes contaba filas: con huecos comparaba con días de hace semanas (Lumber Tycoon 2 salía con «7d +561 %»).
