author: rostislavrotaru
body:
## Summary

Toolbar buttons are now 1.5rem high, as high as a tab's pill, and the grip follows them. The last button's fill is no longer cut off at the toolbar's edge.

**Why the last button was clipped.** A toolbar sizes itself from a hidden copy of its buttons and hides anything past that width. In the shown toolbar, each dropdown ("New from template", "Sort by week") has its menu host, `tr-place-menu`, placed just before it. That host has no size, but it was still a flex item, so it took the section's gap. As a result, the shown buttons were one gap wider per dropdown than the hidden copy. With two dropdowns, the content was about 4px wider than its box, and the last button lost its right edge and corners. More actions was cut the same way when it was last.

**The fix.** The place-menu host is now `display: contents`. It renders nothing itself (its menu is a template shown in an overlay), so it now generates no box and takes no gap. The shown buttons line up with the measured copy, and no widths are padded or forced. The dock strip had worked around the same gap with its own `display: none` rule. That rule is removed.

Also decided for this issue by the maintainer:
- Toolbar rows are 1.75rem high instead of 2rem (a button's 1.5rem with 0.125rem above and below), so the buttons of consecutive rows stand 0.25rem apart and the gap under the main menu shrinks.
- The drag drop line is as high as the buttons and centred on them, not the whole row. It was one pixel high before because of a negative block margin; that margin now applies only to the row-wide line.
- The grip's three dots are centred in the grip, 0.2rem apart, so they stand clear of its top and bottom. The dot size stays 0.125rem.

Changes:
- `toolbar-button` is 1.5rem and `toolbar-row` 1.75rem in the default theme. The grip's height follows the button, and the grips of stacked rows stand 0.25rem apart. A new `toolbar-grip-gap` token (0.2rem) sets the space between the dots, which the grip centres.
- `tr-place-menu` is `display: contents`, and the dock strip's own rule is gone.
- UI-STANDARDS: the Toolbar band, Toolbar grip and Toolbar button rows say so.
- The drag service spec expects the drop line at the toolbar's own top and height, with toolbars centred in taller rows.
- Toolbar component spec: a new test checks that the shown sections, dropdowns included, end where the measured copy's sections end. It fails without the place-menu change, with a 2px drift per dropdown.
- Toolbars UI workflow:
  - checks the 1.75rem rows, the 1.5rem button, the 0.25rem grip gap, the dots' 0.2rem spacing and that they are centred with space above and below, and that the drop line has the buttons' height and top;
  - checks that every item's box lies inside its toolbar's visible box, that the content doesn't scroll sideways, and that the last item's corners have the small radius;
  - runs these checks for the default toolbars and for a narrow window that shows More actions.

## Linked Issue

Closes #272

## Testing

- `npm test` natively on Linux (x64): 14 of 14 checks passed, including 984 Angular tests.
- UI workflows for the first commit (the 1.5rem buttons and the clipping fix), before merging `main`: natively on Linux (x64), toolbars, docking, menu bar, menus, module menus and window look passed (48 tests); natively on Windows 11 (x64), toolbars and docking passed (29 tests); natively on macOS, toolbars and docking passed (28 passed, 1 skipped: the toolbar-menu test that macOS skips by design).
- UI workflows for the row, drop line and grip commit: the toolbars workflow passed natively on Linux (x64), Windows 11 (x64) and macOS; natively on Linux (x64), `npm test` (14 of 14 checks) and toolbars, docking, window look and menu bar passed (37 tests).
- After merging `main`: `npm test` (14 of 14 checks) and the toolbars and document groups UI workflows passed natively on Linux (x64).
- Close-ups of the toolbars, before and after, light and dark, were taken natively on Linux, Windows and macOS and went to the maintainer.
  - Clipping before: the toolbar's content was 375px wide in a 371px box, and the "Sort by week" fill was cut at the edge. After: the content fits its box, and every button is 24px high with all four corners rounded.
  - Rows, grip and drop line, measured natively on Windows: the rows are 28px high, a button is 24px, the three dots lie at 37–39, 48–50 and 59–61px, and the button's fill spans 37–61px.
- After centring the dots and merging `main`: `npm test` natively on Linux (x64), 15 of 15 checks passed with coverage at 100%. The toolbars workflow passed natively on Linux (x64) and Windows 11 (x64) (9 tests each) and on macOS (8 passed, 1 skipped by design).
  - Measured in the toolbars screenshots on all three systems: the dots are 2px high at 43–44, 48–49 and 53–54px with 3px between them, centred on the button's fill (37–61px). Close-ups went to the maintainer.
- The window, startup and processes are unchanged, so the repeated native runs don't apply.

author: kaka11chen
body:
## Summary

The final local task-pool release currently waits for each idle worker to exit before closing the next one. Close these workers through the existing bounded concurrent cleanup helper and wait for every close before returning. Failed workers remain in both retirement ledgers, with their inventory counts held until cleanup succeeds.

This is an independent Python-only change against `feature/local-runtime`; it does not depend on #941. Shared-memory allocation overhead is tracked separately in #946.

## Related issue

close: #945

## Documentation impact

- [x] No user-facing documentation update is required.
- [ ] Documentation is updated in this PR or in a linked website PR.
- [ ] <!-- docs-follow-up --> A follow-up issue is required in
      `AstroVela/vane-website`.

No public API or configuration changes. The pool's final release continues to wait for physical worker cleanup and preserve failed cleanup owners.

## Validation

- Completed two consecutive manual static review passes before installation and tests. These were self-reviews, not independent reviewer approvals.
- Built and installed a non-editable Python wheel with the unchanged Release native library from the matching base; no C++ changes or native rebuild.
- `scripts/run_installed_pytest.sh tests/fast/test_udf_executor_lifecycle.py tests/fast/test_local_task_scheduling.py -m 'not real_ray and not gpu' -q --tb=short`: **403 passed**. Coverage includes overlapping shutdown, waiting for the last worker, shared-pool references, thread-launch failure, retained cleanup ownership, and real subprocess retirement fault injection.
- Applied the patch to #941 in a separate validation checkout: **14 focused lifecycle/retirement tests passed**.
- `scripts/format root --changed`, all applicable pre-commit hooks (including Ruff and mypy), and `python -I scripts/check_copyleft.py` passed.
- Per request, no full fast or Release suite was run.

Image diagnostic: 30,000 ImageNet images in one Parquet row group; no repartition; ResNet18, batch size 100; decoder `task_input_max_bytes=8192`; eight CPU cores with one GPU actor reserving one CPU and resource-admitted decoder tasks; 512 MiB local shared-memory budget. Linux x86-64, Xeon E5-2686 v4, RTX 2080 Ti, Python 3.12.14, PyArrow 25.0.1, Torch 2.7. Each measurement is one cold query, including binding/model load, processing, collection and Parquet write; initial imports and runner setup are excluded.

| Baseline | Pool shutdown before → after | Query + write before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `feature/local-runtime` (without #941) | 7.200 s → 1.524 s | 96.062 s → 94.883 s |
| #941 streaming output | 6.651 s → 1.355 s | 64.616 s → 59.197 s |

The non-streaming pair instantiated seven decoder processes before and eight after; both streaming runs instantiated seven. This is an additional end-to-end timing confounder in the non-streaming pair.

All four runs produced the same path/label multiset, 30,000 distinct paths, valid labels, and no nulls. Every profiled child process exited, and each query returned its shared-memory budget to zero.

The shutdown reduction is a query-tail improvement. A single end-to-end pair also includes variation in startup and image processing; this PR does not claim to eliminate the remaining local/Ray throughput gap.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and includes tests or a reason tests are unnecessary.
- [x] Public behavior and compatibility impact are documented.
- [x] New dependencies, copied code, model assets, and datasets have compatible
      licenses and are recorded where required.
- [x] No credentials, private endpoints, personal paths, generated data, model
      weights, or build artifacts are included.
- [x] Security implications of UDFs, serialization, remote code, network access,
      and untrusted input have been considered.
- [x] Native changes were compiled; Python-only, documentation, and workflow
      changes passed relevant checks.

No new dependencies or bundled assets; the existing process and IPC cleanup boundaries are retained.

author: chud-lori
body:
- `milog version` (also `--version`, `-V`) prints the bundle's build stamp and the version each installed companion binary reports; milog-web gains `--version`. Companions are run with a 3s cap on every OS, so an old binary that ignores the flag can't hang it.
- `milog update` installs the latest GitHub release over the running milog and its installed companions: SHA-256 checked against `checksums.txt`, each file staged next to its target and renamed into place, mode kept, companions that weren't installed are not added. milog itself is renamed last, so after a partial failure `--check` still reports an update and a rerun finishes it; failures say which files were and weren't updated.
- It refuses git checkouts, package-managed files (milog or any companion — prints the package-manager command) and unwritable directories (`run: sudo milog update`); it never calls sudo or restarts services, but prints the restart commands.
- `milog update --check` exits 10 when an update exists. Installs from releases with a mis-stamped bundle (`v0.3.0-…-g<sha>`) are recognised as up to date when the stamp's commit matches the latest tag.
- build.sh stamps with `git describe --tags`, so release bundles carry the real tag (same one-line change as in #91).

Both commands run with no apps configured. Tested by tests/smoke_version_update.sh against a fake release, no network.

author: cgfixit
body:
## Proposed changes
Addresses the execution-boundary findings in #1526. Run each verification command in a fresh Gitless copy and never copy its writes back. Linux requires bubblewrap filesystem/PID/network confinement; macOS uses Seatbelt. Child processes receive capability-specific environments. Fsconnect refuses broad/protected roots and FIFO reads; scheduled OpenTweet content receives injection/link screening.

**Invariant / Governance Impact:** I1-I5 graph, provider consent, audit convergence and human-gated Soul behavior remain unchanged. I6 separation remains intact through maintained subprocess bridges. Existing fsconnect write/audit/quota gates remain in place; these checks add refusals.

## Types of changes
- [x] Bugfix
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Invariant / Governance refinement

## Benefits / why
Verification cannot modify authoritative Git/config state or promote its output back into the workspace. Optional commands no longer inherit unrelated credentials. Unattended sync supports encrypted rclone configuration without exposing the password in argv; drafts remain available when scheduled content is refused.

## Risks to monitor
Windows verification now fails closed because Job Objects do not provide the required filesystem/network boundary; the gateway remains available. Linux runners need bubblewrap and compatible namespace policy. CI installs bubblewrap and requires native acceptance without weakening AppArmor/sysctl policy.

macOS detached descendants remain confined but are not claimed killed. Environment filtering is not same-user filesystem/process isolation. Scheduled URL/tag screening may reject benign posts. No live cloud transfer or social publication was exercised.

## Checklist
- [x] All six invariants and I6 preserved.
- [x] Maintained sandbox, sync, filesystem and channel docs updated.
- [x] Actual native/runtime and combined browser checks completed.
- [ ] Full sandbox/test suite run. User requested direct code execution instead of local suites.
- [x] Hosted Linux confinement at `9d8a0e3a`; the final descendant changes only core fixtures.
- [ ] Final-head broad matrix and native Windows refusal acceptance.

## Further comments
On this exact draft, native macOS execution denied writes to authoritative checkout, Git metadata and sibling state, denied a real loopback socket, allowed the disposable mirror, and preserved source bytes. A detached setsid descendant remained unable to write outside confinement. The maintained native acceptance script passed.

Actual hook, Numbat, ops, filesystem, scheduler and rclone child paths excluded unrelated synthetic credentials. Real rclone 1.75.1 refused missing/wrong config passwords, then copied and checked identical local bytes with encrypted configuration. FIFO/protected-path refusals and scheduled injection/link/tag refusals passed. Computer Use on the combined candidate confirmed Sync status and Soul metadata.

Python compilation/Ruff F/B/S, Actionlint, telemetry, documentation and diff checks passed. No local suites ran.

**Required predecessor:** #1547. This draft targets `codex/1526-core-security` at `937cdc8f` and contains only the incremental execution changes. Merge #1547 first, then retarget/revalidate this draft on main. Installation and CI publisher drafts are independent. All four trial-merged cleanly on main `5765ae1f`, preserving README #1545 and cleanup #1544. #1526 remains open for its close-out gates.

Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 rejected bubblewrap loopback setup with RTM_NEWADDR EPERM. Native Linux acceptance is pinned to supported Ubuntu 22.04 with stock host policy and the same mandatory filesystem/PID/network probe. [Hosted native acceptance and real-repository smoke passed at 9d8a0e3a](https://github.com/cgfixit/CyClaw/actions/runs/37176863365/job/111361228004). No AppArmor disabling or host-network fallback was introduced. macOS native confinement was rerun successfully on the updated branch. The filesystem fixture now intercepts only its synthetic path and forwards pathlib keyword arguments, repairing the hosted traceback/cleanup failure without changing production confinement.

author: landonreekstin
body:
Replaces #80. Blaney's Claude session reported the VPN wouldn't connect while working the MW2/IW4x runbook — this is why.

## Root cause

Blaney's VPN has been dead since **2026-08-02**, and the break is on our side, not his machine.

The firewall peer for `10.10.0.5` was re-keyed that day (openbsd-dotfiles `52c397b`, *"re-key blaney peer 10.10.0.5 for blaney-pc sops-managed NM client"*) to the key of a declarative NetworkManager client. That client only ever existed on #80, which never reached `main` — so the key Blaney was actually using was deleted from `hostname.wg0` and nothing replaced it.

Confirmed on the firewall: `wg show wg0` records **no endpoint and no handshake at all** for the peer, while every other active peer handshakes fine from the internet. UDP 51822, the router forward and pf are all healthy; the server simply never receives a packet it recognises as Blaney.

`docs/runbooks/blaney-sops-setup.md` was the plan that stalled. Parts A and B were done in August but landed on the feature branch instead of `main`, so Part C never ran.

## What this does

Rebases the #80 work onto current `main`:

- **`modules/nixos/services/wireguard-nm-client.nix`** — declares `customConfig.services.wireguard.nmClient`. A NetworkManager WireGuard profile, so it is toggleable from the desktop network applet, and the private key is injected via an `ensureProfiles` environment file from sops rather than sitting in the store or a plaintext keyfile. Distinct from the existing `wireguard.client`, which is a wg-quick/systemd interface.
- **`.sops.yaml`** — blaney-pc's real age key replaces `age1PLACEHOLDER_blaney-pc`.
- **`secrets/blaney-pc.yaml`** — `wg-nm-private-key`, encrypted to blaney-pc + lando.
- **`hosts/blaney-pc/networking.nix`** — the `nmClient` block, gated by `blaneyWgVpn`.

### Two deliberate changes from what #80 had

1. **No DNS.** #80 set `dns = "192.168.1.76"` with `ignore-auto-dns`. But pf does not rdr port 53 on the legacy alias for restricted peers (`docs/networking.md`), and this host only routes `192.168.1.76` into the tunnel — so that would have taken Blaney's DNS down for as long as the VPN was connected. Restricted peers reach homelab services by IP, so no DNS is set and `.lan` is not expected to resolve.
2. **Kept `airplay-receiver.nix` and `ios-device.nix`.** #80's `services/default.nix` predates both and would have removed them.

Docs updated: the MW2 runbook no longer says "KDE network applet" (blaney-pc runs XFCE too, and it's an NM profile either way) and no longer justifies the SMB warning with "no sops identity", which this PR makes false; the peers table records the re-key; the sops runbook is marked superseded with what actually happened.

## Verification

Eval-only — this can't be rebuilt anywhere but blaney-pc.

- All **12** configurations eval clean on a clean tree.
- The generated profile is correct: server key `Z1ZtZiXE…` (matches `wg show`), `allowed-ips 192.168.1.76/32;`, `autoconnect false`, `ipv4 = { address1 = "10.10.0.5/32"; method = "manual"; }` with no `dns`/`ignore-auto-dns`.
- Key stays out of the store: profile holds `$WG_PRIVATE_KEY`, `environmentFiles = [ "/run/secrets/rendered/homelab-vpn-wg.env" ]`, and the store copy of the secret is ciphertext only.
- Five unrelated hosts' drvPaths shift (optiplex, asus-m15, atl-mini-pc, vm-sandbox, vm-blaney). That is the known effect documented in `docs/architecture.md` — declaring a new `customConfig` option changes a host's `etc` derivation even where the feature is off. Fell back to the prescribed `customConfig` fixpoint check on optiplex and asus-m15: the **only** delta is the new option tree appearing with `enable = false` and everything else unset. No behaviour change.

## ⚠️ Before merging — check this first

The secret is encrypted to blaney-pc's age key as it was in August, derived from `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key`. That file was created **by hand** (the host runs `ssh.enable = false`, so NixOS never generates it). **If blaney-pc has been reinstalled since August, the key is different, sops can't decrypt, and his `rebuild` will fail.**

Have his session print:

```bash
sudo cat /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub | ssh-to-age
```

It must equal `age10zcfv4gcvlc42wqyp4cjt8ckym4rghuwfzrr9yf57gcesjn0napqykkk6y`. If it doesn't, re-encrypt per Part B of the sops runbook — that has to happen on asus-laptop or gaming-pc, since the admin age key isn't on the NAS.

If it does match: he runs `update` over the plain internet (no VPN needed), then toggles **homelab-vpn** in his network applet, and `curl -sI http://192.168.1.76/public/` should return `200`. `blaneyWgVpn = false` is the one-line rollback if anything goes wrong.

Then the MW2 runbook can proceed — port 80 to `.76` is already passed for restricted peers, so no firewall change is needed.

Closes #80.

author: phix33
body:
- [X] Mark this if you consider it ready to merge
- [X] I've added tests (optional)
- [ ] I wrote some lines in the [book](https://github.com/radareorg/radare2book) (optional)

**Description**

The m68k `link` instruction gets the wrong stack delta: `link.l` keeps only the low 16 bits of its displacement, and both forms leave out the 4 bytes of the pushed address register.

```
$ r2 -a m68k -e asm.cpu=68020 -qc 'e asm.bytes=false; e asm.stackptr=true; wx 480efffedcbb4e56fff04e75; pd 3' -
            0x00000000     0      link.l a6, 0xfffedcbb
            0x00000006  9029+     link.w a6, 0xfff0
            0x0000000a  9045+     rts
```

`link.l a6, #-0x12345` allocates 0x12345 bytes plus the pushed `a6`, so the depth after it is 74569, not 9029, and `link.w a6, #-16` adds 20, not 16. With this PR the column reads `0`, `74569`, `74589`.

- The displacement is sign-extended from 32 bits when capstone reports a long operand size (`link.l`), and from 16 bits otherwise, as before.
- The delta includes the 4-byte push of An that `link` does before moving sp.

The new case in `test/db/anal/m68k` fails if `link.l` is truncated to 16 bits again, if `link.w` is read as 32 bits, or if the push is dropped. The case also checks `afi~stackframe` for `link.w a6, #-16` (20, was 16). No existing golden moved. `asm.cpu` is set at startup because the plugin picks its capstone mode once, at load, so `e asm.cpu=68020` later does not enable `link.l`; the `invalid value '68020'` warning it prints at startup is the known load-order one and does not stop `link.l` decoding. Function frames only see the `link.l` part once the 8096-byte stack-delta limit in `fcn_stack_delta` is raised. The +4 applies already, and also moves `link.w` frames of 8092 to 8095 bytes onto that limit, which drops them until it is raised.

author: jsakkos
body:
## Why

Prefect and the pandas nightly flow were using far more resources than the work needed (measured on pve-docker, 2026-10-03):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Always-on RAM | prefect 606 MB + postgres 244 MB + app 15 MB | collector ~18 MB |
| Orchestrator disk | 7.9 GB Postgres (Prefect run history) | none |
| Per-minute collection | new Prefect process each minute, 16.6 s avg | one long-running stdlib loop |
| Nightly processing | 746 s on the server (188 s locally), 2+ GB RAM, recomputes all history, writes a 608 MB CSV | ~13 s incremental, 17 s full rebuild |

Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-pipeline-slimdown.md` (all phases) and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-duckdb-build.md` (phase 2).

## What changed

**Phase 1: collector** (deployed 2026-10-03 ~21:45 PT, running)
- `src/collector.py`: stdlib only, `INSERT OR IGNORE` against the existing unique index, writes timestamps in exactly the stored text format (verified by replaying real rows from Jan and Sep: 0 duplicates). No retries within a minute because 511 allows 60 req/h per key.
- Brings in production-only fixes that lived just in the server checkout: Postgres backend, asyncpg, pandas<3, `np.select` fix. Also found during the cutover: SQLAlchemy 2.1 broke Prefect's scheduler (pinned), and the prefect container never had `API_KEY` (it only worked through the old hardcoded fallback).

**Phase 2: `python -m src.pipeline.build`**
- `arrivals.py`: DuckDB reads `train_locations` straight from SQLite and keeps one row per arrival in `data/analytics.duckdb`. It recomputes only new days, the last two Pacific days, and days whose schedule version changed.
- `dashboard.py` / `incidents.py`: the same 10 website files with the same keys and rounding; route projection is vectorized.
- **Parity:** on the 4.33M-row snapshot, all 10 files the website reads match the legacy flow (including 25 incidents and trajectories). Checked with `scripts/compare_outputs.py`. Legacy quirks are kept on purpose and listed in the phase 2 plan.

**Phase 3: retire the stack**
- `docker-compose.yaml` runs only `collector`; every job is in `deploy/crontab.txt` (UTC, because Ubuntu's cron has no `CRON_TZ`).
- Removed: Prefect flows/deployments, FastAPI app, SQLAlchemy models, Alembic, `requirements*.txt`, old ad-hoc scripts. Dependencies now live only in `pyproject.toml`.
- `scripts/check_freshness.py` runs from cron every 15 min and can ping `HEALTHCHECK_URL`.

## Deployment (done)

Deployed to pve-docker on 2026-10-04 at 05:29 UTC. Only `collector` runs in Docker, and `deploy/crontab.txt` is installed (the old crontab is in `~/crontab-backup-2026-10-03.txt`). The first cron freshness check passed. On production data the new build matched the legacy output, apart from pings collected after the last Prefect run. A full rebuild takes 67 s with a 1.0 GB peak (DuckDB is capped at 1 GB and works in monthly batches); the nightly run takes 33 s.

Left for the owner:
- `docker volume rm caltrain-prefect_postgres_data caltrain-prefect_prefect_data` (7.9 GB of Prefect history; can't be undone)
- The server checkout shows `gtfs_data/` as modified and `gtfs_feeds/v20260922/` as untracked, because 511 published a new schedule tonight. Commit those to the repo so future `git pull`s stay clean.

## Notes

- The website links `plots/commute_delay.html`, but the pipeline has always written `commute_delays.html`, so that plot on the site is a stale committed file. Unchanged here.
- Known legacy scoring bug kept for parity: GTFS times ≥ 24:00 are scored on the ping's own date. The phase 2 plan has an optional follow-up to fix it.

## Testing

`uv run pytest`: 56 tests (collector, arrivals rules, dashboard numbers and plot weighting, incidents, build end to end, freshness check, comparer).

author: kingkillery
body:
## What

Lets the Colab model launcher serve GGUF LoRA adapters on top of a base GGUF with llama.cpp `--lora-scaled`.

- New `adapters` / `alias` launch options; `prepareModelCache` may return `{directory, adapters}`.
- `validateColabAdapters`: 1-4 adapters, plain `.gguf` basenames (no path, comma, colon, quote), sha256, size, scale in (0, 4]. Upstream llama.cpp runtime only. Adapters never download; they are read only from the staged cache directory.
- Remote script: the VM re-checks size and sha256 of every adapter before building argv, emits one `--lora-scaled PATH:SCALE` per adapter, and echoes `adapters` (file, sha256, scale) and `alias` in the READY payload. The host asserts the echo equals the validated request, or the bridge is never started.
- Reuse of a running server compares the ordered (path, scale) list and refuses any other `--lora*` form. It also requires a sidecar written by `start_server` (server pid + the adapters it verified at start), so a same-named adapter replaced after the server read it is never treated as served.
- No new `@measured` stage name. Base-only launches are unchanged (empty adapters, null alias).

## Tests

`test/colab-model-adapters.test.ts` (81 tests, runs the generated remote script against fakes) plus the existing colab suites: 192 pass, 0 fail across 7 files. biome clean. Three temporary mutants (dropping the reuse adapter check, alias matching, `server_args.extend`) each failed the new tests.

## Not validated yet

Nothing has run on a real Colab VM or llama-server b11064. Whether repeated `--lora-scaled` flags append (the first live test uses a single adapter) and whether scales survive float32 are untested.

## Merge order

Merge before mesh-inference `feat/gguf-lora-bucket`: that repo's `launch.ts` imports this launcher from `../oh-my-pk` and refuses an adapter setup if `validateColabAdapters` is missing.

author: guysuter
body:
Structural commits can now consume an explicitly resolved terminal resource bundle without reconstructing a secret-bearing grant request. The common gate checks the original package/grant checkpoints before resource verification and again immediately before structural mutation, so stale bundles cannot renew themselves or create a structural intent.

The recovered path verifies every selected/latest package receipt, joins only explicitly selected entry references, and privately requalifies the selected grant against genuine package expectations and the exact controller owner. It shares candidate validation with the live receipt path and reuses the existing exact structural retry ordering, including uncertain latest attempts, successful duplicate recommits, and older-operation rejection. Latest-only resources are not implicitly selected.

Validation on exact main399240b8b56268deba773d32fca4ee9699d4ff51 plus these five files:13 focused tests,388 full Core tests, and unsigned arm64 iOS Simulator compile passed. Controls include fresh store-instance recovery,15 structural failure boundaries, empty/nonempty/shared resources, old-selected/latest-extra separation, stale same/other-instance and same-tip checkpoint rejection before effects, and owner/reference/coverage/bounds failures. Parent reviewed every source delta and new test; five current/isolated/frozen source hashes, nine logs, and929 unaffected baseline files were verified. Initial fixture/cache failures remain in the evidence.

This is an internal unmounted commit API. No persistent-format, package/grant/structural store, caller, reset, wire, live Keychain, or runtime activation change. Production all-writer admission, explicit legacy conversion, and platform qualification remain separate prerequisites. Independent review and current-head CI are required before merge.

body:
## #️⃣ 연관된 이슈 - close #144
## 💻 작업 내용 ### 1. 진동 강도 설정을 내 기기 연결 상태에서만 표시 - 기기 카드가 뜨는 상태(`is_connected && is_active_user`)에서만 "진동 강도 설정" 섹션을 렌더링합니다. 미연결·로딩·에러·타 계정 활성 상태에서는 섹션 자체를 그리지 않습니다. - `useDeviceSection`에 묻혀 있던 첫 번째 기기 연결 판정을 `useDeviceConnection` 훅으로 분리해 `DeviceSection`과 `HapticSection`이 같은 판정식을 공유합니다. ### 2. 설정 페이지 QA 반영 (5건) | 심각도 | 증상 | 수정 | |---|---|---| | 높음 | 진동 세기가 화면과 서버에서 어긋남 (방향키 연타 시 PATCH 응답 순서 뒤섞임, 저장 실패 시 복구 없음) | `useHapticStrength` 훅 신설. 300ms 디바운스 + 요청 직렬화로 마지막 값만 전송, 실패 시 마지막 저장값으로 슬라이더 복구 및 안내 | | 높음 | 프로필 저장 실패 시 안내 없음, 처리되지 않은 예외 | try/catch 후 `AlertModal` 안내. 페이지·입력값 유지 | | 높음 | 기기 이름 수정·연결 해제 실패 시 안내 없음 | 이름 모달은 성공 시에만 닫히고 실패 시 모달 안에 안내. 연결 해제 실패는 카드 아래 인라인 안내 | | 중간 | 폴링 조회가 한 번 실패하면 기기 카드 전체가 오류 화면으로 교체 | 데이터가 전혀 없을 때만 오류 화면. 재조회 실패는 기존 데이터 유지(TanStack Query가 data를 보존) | | 낮음 | 연결 실패 시 5xx도 "전원·Wi-Fi 확인"으로 안내 | `getDeviceConnectErrorMessage` 유틸로 409만 전원·Wi-Fi, 그 외는 "연결 요청에 실패했어요". 온보딩 `HwConnectPage`도 동일 적용 | - 닉네임 10자 초과 입력 차단(낮음)은 입력은 허용하고 검증 메시지로 안내하는 기존 UX를 유지하기로 해 반영하지 않았습니다. ### 3. 닉네임 반응형 - 320px 폭에서 10글자 닉네임이 말줄임으로 잘리던 문제. `truncate` → `break-words line-clamp-2`로 바꿔 두 줄까지 전부 보여주고 그 이상만 말줄임합니다.
## 📸 스크린샷 (선택) - 미연결: "연결하기" 버튼만 보이고 진동 섹션 없음 / 연결됨: 기기 카드 아래 진동 섹션 표시 - 320px 한글 10자·영문 11자 닉네임 모두 두 줄로 전부 표시 확인
## 🌟 리뷰 요구사항 - `src/pages/setting/hooks/useHapticStrength.ts`의 저장 대기열 로직(`pendingStrengthRef` / `isSavingRef`)을 중점적으로 봐주세요. 요청 진행 중에 새 값이 들어오면 끝난 뒤 최신값 하나만 이어서 보내는 구조입니다. - `useDeviceConnection.ts`에서 `isError`를 `isFetchError && devices === undefined`로 좁힌 것이 의도와 맞는지 확인 부탁드립니다. - 검증: Playwright로 `GET /devices` 응답을 4가지 상태로 주입해 진동 섹션 표시 13건, QA 수정 30건, 닉네임 반응형 3건 시나리오 통과. `tsc -b` 통과. - 참고: `useProfileEditPage`의 초기값 주입 effect에 ESLint `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` 에러가 있는데, develop에서도 동일하게 발생하는 기존 이슈라 이번 범위에서는 손대지 않았습니다.
## 🔗 참고 자료 ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **새로운 기능** * 연결된 기기에서만 진동 강도를 조절할 수 있으며, 저장 실패 시 안내가 표시됩니다. * 기기 연결, 이름 변경, 연결 해제 및 프로필 저장에 실패하면 상황에 맞는 오류 안내가 표시됩니다. * 기기 이름 저장 중에는 진행 상태가 표시되고, 완료 후 모달이 닫힙니다. * **개선 사항** * 프로필 닉네임이 최대 두 줄까지 표시되며, 긴 영문 닉네임도 줄바꿈됩니다. * 진동 강도 슬라이더의 표시 조건이 API 문서에 명시되었습니다.

body:
## Events off by ~30 min in zones without DST (1880 LMT applied)

**Bug:** A 12:00 Moscow event created from macOS/iOS Calendar was stored at 09:29:43Z and displayed at 12:29 in the web UI.

**Root cause:** Apple ships a VTIMEZONE whose single STANDARD period carries the zone's 1880 Local Mean Time offset (+023017); installs without the bundled NGCards `TimeZones` resources couldn't resolve the TZID and applied the LMT offset verbatim.

### Before / After

```diff
- 12:00 Moscow → stored 09:29:43Z → displayed 12:29
+ 12:00 Moscow → stored 09:00:00Z → displayed 12:00
```

---

Fixes [#6042](https://bugs.sogo.nu/view.php?id=6042)

author: yetval
body:
Related: #136241

## What problem this solves

`openclaw completion --install` used `trimEnd()` on retained shell profile content, destroying a significant escaped trailing space. A final `export COMPLETION_PROOF=value\ ` silently changed from setting `value ` to setting `value`.

## Fix and impact

Retain yetval's fix: normalize terminal LF separators only, rather than trimming user command characters. Existing completion block recognition and reinstall behavior remain unchanged. Profiles damaged by an earlier installation still require manual restoration of the original command.

Thanks to @yetval for the fix and regression coverage. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Reproduced in a secretless Linux container through the built `openclaw.mjs --profile p164785base completion --install --shell bash` CLI with isolated HOME and state paths. The Bash profile ends in `export COMPLETION_PROOF=value\ ` followed by LF. A valid prewritten completion cache isolates profile installation from unrelated completion generation.

- Base: current main `7de09d5a2337f332a2e46f0831e2a818676a7d02` production owner, with the candidate regression test retained. `bash -ic 'printf "[%s]" "$COMPLETION_PROOF"'` changes from `[value ]` before installation to `[value]` afterward. The profile prefix is corrupted.
- Candidate: `06bc38c1f9169142d5599748858c6bf1283a2937`. The same real CLI invocation preserves `[value ]` and all original profile bytes before the appended completion block.
- Second install is byte-identical and leaves exactly one block in every case.
- Plain Bash profile, real Zsh and real Fish controls preserve their original profile prefixes and `[value]` output, on both base and candidate.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/completion-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: base **73 passed, 1 failed**, specifically the escaped-space assertion (`<value>` instead of `<value >`). Candidate **74 passed**, Vitest 2.09 s; wrapper wall time 2.96 s. Existing shell fixture extended without adding a process.
- Both CLI artifacts built using `pnpm openclaw --profile … --version`; candidate forced a rebuild after restoring the exact candidate owner.
- Exact-head real Gateway smoke: one `gpt-5-mini` Responses API call through a passive proxy, reasoning `low`, output budget 4096; HTTP 200 and exact requested `LIVE_GATE_OK_164785` reply.
- Hosted CI and exact-head ClawSweeper review run on the published head; no CI reruns requested.

Native Windows PowerShell and completion-cache generation were not exercised. No real operator profile or state was used. No changelog changes.

author: stingd85
body:
## Why
On the live KUT build, Batch Tag on `Kampala Uganda - Interior_v26_detached.rvt` ran for 99 s and reported **Tagged 0 of 3,121**. It printed a NOT WRITTEN block for every category and token, plus 100 `malformed tag '-------'` warnings. The cause was one line at the bottom of the report: Load Shared Parameters had never been run on that model, which the log confirms (`parameter is not reachable on the instance`).

## What
- `BatchTagCommand.ProbeTokenBindings` runs before the mode picker. It checks one element per category for each of the 8 token parameters. The check uses the same scope `SetString` writes through: an instance `LookupParameter` that is not read-only.
- `Core/TokenBindingPreflight` (Revit-free) gives one of four results:
  - **No category can hold a tag:** the run is refused in a single dialog: "run Load Shared Parameters on THIS model".
  - **Some categories cannot:** they are named in the picker status line and the log, largest first.
  - **Every category can:** the run starts with no extra message.
  - **Nothing was probed:** the run is not blocked.

- `TokenBindingPreflightTests` adds 6 tests. The wiring test **fails** against the old `BatchTagCommand.cs` and passes with the change.

body:
## Qué cambia

**F2 · Exterior de la torre** (spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-downcastle-f2-exterior-design.md`)
- **Proyección tipo Nebulus:** torre de 32 tiles de circunferencia. La torre gira bajo el jugador y deja cielo a los costados (radio 80 px), con estrellas, luna y montañas en parallax. Los compañeros que quedan detrás se ven como silueta de su color y la cuerda de atrás va punteada. Afuera no hay capa de oscuridad.
- **Anillos ASCII de 32×8** en `rings.js` (13), con metadatos y costos en `content.js` y asserts en `level.js`. `genExterior` los apila con un giro al azar y a veces espejados, entre la `ventana` rota del inicio y la `entrada` del FIN.
- **Secuencia del ciclo** (`CYCLE_SEQ`): T1, T2, **Afuera** (mini de 2–3 anillos, también en el primer ciclo), T3, T4, jefe, **Bajada por la torre** (4 + c anillos). Cada exterior termina con su pantalla de premios. La run pasa a guardarse como `{ c, s }`.
- **Mecánicas nuevas.** La bajada del ciclo 1 las presenta en orden, una por anillo:
  - viento: ráfagas con aviso que arrastran la posición; la mitad en el suelo y nada si estás anclado;
  - plataformas móviles: horizontales y ascensores; se cruzan desde abajo y llevan al que está parado o anclado;
  - gárgola: avisa y sopla; empuja sin dañar;
  - murciélago: se despierta, persigue en picados y vuelve a su percha.
- **Wrap:** la x de los jugadores **no se envuelve**. Solo dan la vuelta `tileAt`, `ropePath`, la alcanzabilidad y el campo de los bots. `rewrap` lleva criaturas, gemas, balas, flechas y plataformas a la vuelta más cercana al equipo en cada paso, así las comparaciones directas de x siguen valiendo y la red interpola sin saltos en la costura.
- **Red:** viento y plataformas son funciones puras del tiempo (`windAt`, `moverPos`), sin estado de red nuevo. La gárgola y el murciélago viajan en los flags de criatura.
- **Audio y voz:** ambiente de viento y sonidos nuevos procedurales. Afuera, los vivos se oyen en seco.
- **Herramientas:** `?ext=mini|bajada`, `goto(c, k, { ext })` y `__downcastle.tick(n)` (cuadros sin rAF; con el panel oculto no corre `requestAnimationFrame`). El visor `?ver=bloques` también muestra los anillos y `simrun.mjs` suma `--ext` y dos grupos a la suite.

**Arreglos pedidos**
- **Ancla flotando:** anclado sobre una plataforma que se derrumba, el jugador quedaba flotando. Pasaba porque el ancla se mantenía sin volver a mirar el apoyo y `move()` sale temprano. Ahora `hasSupport` revisa piso, pared o plataforma en cada paso.
- **«Sonido crujiente» más suave:** banda de 350–3000 Hz, compresor y saturación menores, bitcrusher a 8 kHz / 6 bits.
- Alto mínimo de 1 px del canvas con la ventana oculta (antes `drawImage` fallaba con alto 0).

## Verificación
- `node games/downcastle/tools/simrun.mjs`: todos los umbrales OK. Mini 100 %, bajada 98 % (umbral 85 %), sin cambios en los grupos de F1, paso ≤ 0,02 ms. Bajada con 4 bots: 98 %.
- `npm run build` sin errores; asserts de bloques y anillos en silencio.
- En el navegador:
  - la torre gira, la gárgola sopla y las siluetas se ven con 4 jugadores;
  - un ciclo completo pasa por mini → T3 → T4 → El Ojo → bajada → CICLO 2 · TRAMO 1;
  - anfitrión + invitado en la misma sala: posiciones iguales y plataformas en fase (iguales módulo 512 px).

## Para revisar
- **Desviaciones de la spec:** la re-envoltura reemplaza al `dxw` que proponía la spec, y las criaturas de atrás de la torre no se dibujan. Las dos ya están anotadas en la spec.
- **Sin probar:** con teléfonos ni con 2 personas, y los sonidos nuevos no se escucharon. La prueba real de un ciclo completo sigue pendiente; `downcastle.tel` ahora guarda `sub` y los anillos jugados.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds Storybook 10 to `frontend/`, so the components can be viewed one at a time and also as part of the full app. It also makes every story a UI test that runs in CI.

- **Stories for each component.** `CardTile`, `CardDetail`, `NewCardDialog`, `ActivityHeatmap` and `ActivityPanel` each have stories, with autodocs and controls.
- **Stories for whole pages.** `BoardPage`, `ReportPage`, `LoginPage` and the full `App` have stories covering signed out, board view, report view, admin, no teams, a teams error and not found.
- **Fake backend.** `src/lib/__mocks__/pocketbase.ts` replaces PocketBase through `sb.mock`, and the `api.*` calls are spies backed by an in-memory store in `src/stories/fakeBackend.ts`. Stories never touch the network, and actions like "Mark done" really refetch and update. Stories pick a signed-in user and a route with `parameters.auth` and `parameters.route`.
- **Tests.**
  - `@storybook/addon-vitest` renders every story in headless Chromium, so each one is a smoke test (38 tests).
  - Most stories also have `play` functions that check interactions, such as completing a card, creating a card, changing filters, signing in and sanitising unsafe HTML.
- **Two Vitest projects.** The test setup moves to `vitest.config.ts` with projects `unit` and `storybook`. `npm run test` is still jsdom-only (94 tests, unchanged), and the new `npm run test:storybook` runs the stories.
- **CI.** A new `storybook` job runs the story tests and builds the static Storybook. The `ci` gate waits for it.
  - The job's first step diffs the commit against its base. Unless something under `frontend/` (other than a `*.test.ts(x)` file), `.mise.toml` or `ci.yml` changed, the remaining steps are skipped and the job stays green.
  - The filter is at step level rather than a workflow `paths:` filter, so the required `CI` check still reports on backend-only PRs.
  - It installs only Playwright's headless shell (about 100 MB, a few seconds). `--with-deps` is added only under act, because the hosted runner already has Chromium's system libraries.
- **mise tasks.** New tasks are `frontend:storybook`, `frontend:storybook:build`, `frontend:storybook:test` and `frontend:storybook:browsers`. `test` and `check` include the story tests and the Storybook build.
- **Docs.** `docs/ci.md`, `docs/testing.md`, `docs/development.md` and `README.md` are updated.

### Changes to existing config
- **Dev proxy.** In `vite.config.ts` the key `'/_'` is now `'^/_(/|$)'`. The old prefix match also sent Vitest's `/__vitest_browser__` assets to the backend. The PocketBase dashboard at `/_/` is still proxied.
- **Playwright 1.63.0.** Playwright 1.56.1 hangs while unpacking Chromium on Node 26 (reproduced locally). That is what timed out the first CI run.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (94 passed)
- [x] `npm run test:storybook` (38 passed, headless shell only)
- [x] Deliberately breaking the "Mark done" text fails 3 story tests
- [x] `npm run build-storybook` writes to `frontend/storybook-static` and leaves `backend/pb_public` untouched
- [x] Change filter checked against real diffs (frontend changes run the job; backend, docs or unit-test-only changes skip it)
- [x] CI `storybook` job green on GitHub: about 30s in total, with 5s for the Chromium install, 7s for the story tests and 4s for the build

author: ogunjobisam
body:
Three more fixes from tonight's journey test on the live demonstration. One migration each, one commit each.

## 1. The demonstration has a price list (`20261005500000`)

- **Found:** the sales flow opens with "work out what this customer pays", and Find a price answered nothing for every product and customer. New quotations and requisitions said "No agreed price" under every line. The demo holds no row in `erp.item_price`.
- **Why:** it was built before price lists were. Its own trading types each price from the product's demo attributes (`list_minor`, `cost_minor`), so it never needed one.
- **Fix:** `erp.seed_demo_prices()` gives each demo product a sales list price at its `list_minor` and a purchase list price from its supplier at its `cost_minor`: the same figures its history trades at. It runs only in a demonstration, and never over a price somebody set. `erp.ensure_demo_configuration()` calls it, and the migration adds them to every demonstration there is today.
- **Checks:** `demo_prices_suite` 5/5. The demonstration catch-up suite, which trades a demo forward day by day, passes with the prices present (1,123 s locally, on a busy machine).

## 2. A press is given the time to finish (`20261005600000`)

- **Found:** writes a person presses once kept meeting the 8-second statement timeout on live. Picking an order never finished (6 tries). Raising a stock adjustment, receiving a notice, and creating, converting and moving a document were cancelled under load.
- **Fix:** those six doors get `statement_timeout = 30s`, the way `erp_accept_interview` has 55 s. Each does one bounded piece of work. No read is given more.
- **This is a stopgap.** The time goes on `erp.credit_position`: 1.6 s for one customer on the quiet live database, 2.3 s inside the pick's release check. The dunning worklist asks it of every overdue customer, which is why that read never finishes. That needs its own change.

## 3. A cancelled receipt gives its quantities back (`20261005800000`)

- **Found:** an order of 15 had 2 received. A second receipt for the other 13 was raised and cancelled as a draft. The order then said "Nothing is left to receive", and its lines read fully received.
- **Why:** `erp.refresh_order_line_progress()` counted every receipt whose `is_cancelled` flag is unset. A receipt cancelled by its lifecycle moves to the state `cancelled` and the flag stays as it was, so it counted for ever. Nothing refreshed the order's lines when a receipt was cancelled.
- **It also inflated "Received, not yet billed"** by the cancelled receipt's value, ahead of the ledger. The close's check (`erp.assert_grni_reconciles`) reads one against the other, so the demonstration's October close would have refused.
- **Fix:** the routine leaves out a receipt in the state `cancelled`, as `erp.receivable_lines()` and `erp.receive_against()` already do. A trigger on `erp.object_state` refreshes a receipt's order lines when it moves to cancelled. The migration re-reads every order line a cancelled receipt was raised against, in every organisation.
- **Not changed:** a draft receipt still counts as received. My first version counted posted receipts only; `procurement_controls_suite` holds that three-way matching reads a receipt before it posts, and refused it (17/24). So a draft receipt that is neither posted nor cancelled still puts the report ahead of the ledger. That's a decision for the owner.
- **Checks:** `cancelled_receipt_suite` 4/4. On a committed local copy of the live state, the order line reads 2 received after the migration. The procurement checks (controls, three-way match, receipts, returns, samples, prepayment, landed cost, freight, shipping notices, confirmations) pass 15/15.

## Checks across all three

- Applied in order (`400000`, `500000`, `600000`, `800000`) to a local database holding committed organisations: all apply.
- Preflight and the figures (all four places) pass.
- **Not run locally to the end:** the full catalogue; CI is the first full run. This replaces #373, which carried the first version of the receipt change.

author: mrgobert
body:
## What was wrong

Churn intelligence (the Customers page) counted every expired or cancelled user doc whose `expirationDate` fell in the window as churn. It divided that by every `"active"` doc. Neither number says who paid:
- **The base was mostly accounts that never paid.** The native app writes `"active"` for trials and promotional grants. Of 91 `"active"` docs, 50 have no payment in the ledger at all.
- **Unpaid trials counted as paid churn.** The July 2026 web trials carry no trial fields, so 32 of them counted.
- **The webhook's fields are missing too.** 26 of 39 paying accounts' docs carry none of them, so the revenue summary's provenance screen can't stand in.
- **The Cloud Function's `"canceled"` spelling was never read.** 3 of its 5 paid churners in the last 90 days have no `expirationDate`, so even a status scan wouldn't have counted them.

## Changes

**The churn rate comes from `subscription_ledger`.** `_paid_subscriptions` reads each account's paid subscription from the ledger:
- **A payment** is a production, non-promotional purchase or renewal with a price. Sandbox, trial, family-sharing and $0 events don't count.
- **A subscription** runs from a payment until the EXPIRATION after its last one. A refund ends it early, and billing grace ends it late (up to 31 days).
- **With no EXPIRATION,** it ends with its paid period once the grace has run out.
- **Paying again** after it ends starts a new subscription.

The rate is the paid subscriptions that ended in the window over the accounts paying at its start. As before, accounts that started paying inside the window are left out of the base.

**The churned list:**
- **Expired trials stay on the list as trials,** with the trial reasons. The ledger now knows they were trials.
- **Sandbox builds and promotional grants leave the list.**
- **Paid churn comes first, then trials,** newest first in each. The 100-row cap never drops a paid churner for a trial.
- **Paid churners the status scans don't return are read by id.** On prod that's 5 `"canceled"` docs for the 90-day window. A deleted account still counts in the rate; it just has no row.

**`LEDGER_LOOKBACK_DAYS` goes from 400 to 490.** One read then covers the yearly plans bought before the 90-day window that ended inside it. Without that, 2 of the 12 would have been missed.

**If the ledger can't be read,** the user doc's webhook fields decide, as in the revenue summary.

## Should `"canceled"` join the churn scans?

Not as a status scan. That's 457 docs × 3 windows on every 15-minute run, about 132k reads a day, and it would still miss the 3 paid churners with no `expirationDate`. Going through the ledger costs 5 reads per 90-day run.

The 102 other `"canceled"` docs in that window are trials that never paid: 97 web trials (the July batch), 4 App Store trials, and one web trial whose first charge failed. They don't change the rate. **I left them off the churned list:** listing them would cost about 30k reads a day until they leave the 90-day window, by December. Say if you want them listed.

## Measured on prod (read-only, one-off dyno, counts only, 2026-10-04)

I ran the deployed code (v76) side by side with this branch:

| | 7 days | 30 days | 90 days |
|---|---|---|---|
| Churn rate | 3.3% → **6.7%** | 5.6% → **9.1%** | 33.9% → **25.0%** |
| Counted as paid churn | 3 → 3 | 5 → 4 | 40 → 12 |
| Divided by | 91 → 45 | 89 → 44 | 118 → 48 |
| Churned list, paid / trial rows | 3 / 3 → 3 / 3 | 5 / 5 → 4 / 6 | 40 / 10 → 12 / 43 |
| User docs read by id | 0 | 0 | 5 (all `"canceled"`) |

**The paying base is 43 accounts:** 39 `"active"` or `"cancelled"` docs plus 4 whose doc reads `"canceled"` or has another status.
- 1, 3 and 7 of them started paying inside the 7-, 30- and 90-day windows.
- The at-risk count (80) and average tenure are unchanged.

**Reasons in the 90-day window:**
- **"No usage" 36 → 9.** The web trials now read as trials.
- **"Trial - no usage" 4 → 36.**
- **30 days:** one account that paid months earlier and later let a trial lapse moved from "Active user" to "Trial - did not convert".

**The revenue summary's churn rate isn't touched by this PR.** It reads 14.3 / 21.4 / 41.7% because it still screens by the webhook's fields: 12 subscribers instead of 43. More on that below.

## Read cost

- **The ledger read** grows from 1,312 to 1,610 events, every 6 hours per process.
- **Each 90-day run** adds 5 reads by id, plus usage and email-history reads for those 5 rows.
- **Total:** a few thousand reads a day, against about 132k for a `"canceled"` scan.

## Not changed

- **The revenue summary's subscriber count, MRR and churn rate** still require the webhook's fields on the user doc. It counts 12 subscribers and $69 MRR; the ledger shows 43 paying accounts, about $300 a month at their latest prices. Most of the gap is yearly App Store subscribers whose docs carry none of those fields. RevenueCat's overview metrics return nothing in prod, so the headline falls back to this figure. I'm flagging it as its own task.
- **The at-risk and engaged lists** still start from the status scans, `"active"` docs that never paid included.
- **The churn trend chart** keeps its old daily points, so the line steps at the deploy.

## Tests

`cd server && python3 -m unittest`: all 258 pass, 14 of them new.
- **`PaidSubscriptionTests` (7):**
  - a subscription runs to the EXPIRATION after its last payment;
  - a refund ends it early and billing grace ends it late;
  - a trial taken later doesn't stretch the paid period;
  - with no EXPIRATION, it ends once the grace has run out;
  - paying again starts a new subscription;
  - only a production sale someone paid for is a payment;
  - an unreadable ledger returns None.
- **`ChurnIntelligenceTests` (6):**
  - the rate is paid churn over the ledger's paying base;
  - trials stay on the list as trials, and accounts that never paid leave it;
  - a `"canceled"` doc is read by id and dated by the ledger;
  - paying again isn't churn;
  - held-out accounts never count;
  - an unreadable ledger falls back to the webhook's fields.
- **`ChurnReasonTests`:** the ledger can say a trial expired when the doc can't.
- **`LedgerReadTests`:** one read still serves every window, churn's included.

All 6 churn-intelligence tests and the new reason test fail against main.

This branch merges cleanly with MrGobert/chunk-analytics#10, and the combined tree passes all 267 tests.

Merging deploys cerebral-analytics. The next 15-minute snapshot picks it up.

body:
Adds the first storage-independent table consumer toward #1585: a bounded selected-column service for ordered SUM/MEAN. `SUM([i64::MAX, 1, 0.0])` fails at the integer prefix; it does not pre-promote the group. A later cell-access failure takes precedence over that potential overflow because all arguments are collected before folding.

Core now owns borrowed normalized cells and an immutable ordered schema; missing cells, invalid coordinates and opaque access failures remain distinct. Schema survives zero rows, text borrows its backing storage, and exact i64/float/temporal precision are retained. Selections must be strictly increasing row indices, preserving relation order without duplicates. The caller supplies the row budget; preflight precedes allocation and cell reads. No new dependencies.

Validation:
- 32 independently specified reduction cases replayed by Rust and the real Python aggregate evaluator, with exact float bits, signed zero, missingness, overflow and type/error order.
- Fake-table tests verify eager reads, opaque non-Clone errors, empty/filtered relations and no reads for invalid or over-budget selections; schema/borrow tests preserve exact data and temporal metadata.
- All 70 Rust tests pass in debug/release; 632 focused Python tests and 23 native tooling/architecture tests pass. Strict Clippy, formatting/lint and repository validation pass.

This is an internal bare-column reduction API. Aggregate grammar, grouping/filter evaluation, computed arguments, Arrow storage and installed table interchange remain next integration work; no dataset execution or default-backend change is claimed. CodeRabbit reviewed `5e9548e072b1c388eb638ec199c532f2508a5809`, with 100% documentation coverage and no actionable findings or retained architecture concerns. Its integration guidance is retained: derive future request budgets from trusted policy and validate storage snapshot guarantees. The TSV is excluded by the bot's default filter but replayed independently by both runners. All 19 hosted CI jobs plus CodeRabbit pass on this exact revision. Merged at `261a1c64fe593f118cb846501347d55ab7830753` under the user's autonomous merge authorization.

body:
## Why
The mobile app's Kilter **Generate** panel will tell you whether a generated climb **was in the model's training data**, or how close it is to the nearest training climb. That check needs the training split, which isn't published anywhere today.

## What
- **`scripts/build-climb-dataset.py --training-index <path>`** writes one row per climb: `[uuid, name, setter, split, frames, ascents, angle, grade]`.
  - `split` uses the trainer's own deterministic per-uuid hash (salt `kilter-gen-v1`).
  - The file is gzipped with mtime 0, so rebuilding from the same snapshot gives identical bytes.
- **`climb-generator/training-index.json.gz`** (~4.6 MB): 66,338 climbs (52,878 train / 6,600 val / 6,860 test).
  - Listed in `climb-generator/manifest.json` as `trainingIndex`.
  - Already excluded from the PWA precache (`**/climb-generator/**`).

## Verified exact

author: qian-ning
body:
## Why

`scripts/` ships three Python generators (`make-icon.py`, `make-dmg-background.py`,
`publish-screenshots.py`). Nothing in `.gitignore` covered what importing or
byte-compiling them leaves behind, so a `__pycache__` directory appears as
untracked noise in `git status` in every worktree.

```
$ git check-ignore -v scripts/__pycache__/x.cpython-311.pyc scripts/loose.pyc
.gitignore:62:__pycache__/  scripts/__pycache__/x.cpython-311.pyc
.gitignore:63:*.pyc          scripts/loose.pyc
```

Both paths are ignored; nothing else in the working tree is affected.

## Scope

One concern, two lines, no runtime effect. Deliberately **not** folded into the
DMG or CI pull requests — AGENTS.md §6 rules out drive-by cleanup inside an
unrelated change, and this is neither.

`.pi-desktop/` and `.pi-desktop-test/` are left as they are. They look like
rebrand residue, but nothing in the repository creates either directory: the
data-directory names are `~/.qianning-agent` and `~/.qianning-agent-dev`
(`apps/desktop/electron/main/data-paths.ts:29,32`), under `$HOME` rather than the
checkout, and every test and E2E harness uses an explicit temporary root. Removing
entries that might still match someone's local layout would expose directories in
their `git status` for no gain, so the stale-looking lines stay until there is a
reason to touch them.

author: grayom
body:
## 🔴 심는 방식 노드 23개가 정답을 거부하고 있었습니다

`traceLabels`는 **노드 이름**으로 키가 걸려 있는데, 흔적 발급 경로가 **번호**로 찾고 있었습니다.

```ts
if (!traceLabels[stage]) return json({ stage, token: null });   // stage는 숫자, 표는 이름 키
```

항상 `undefined`이므로 **모든 노드에서 `token: null`** 을 돌려주고, 그 줄에서 바로 반환하므로 **바로 아래의 진행도 검사는 한 번도 실행되지 않았습니다.**

`BLACK_TRACE_SECRET`이 설정된 상태에서는 브라우저가 `FLAG{label}`을 만들고 서버는 `FLAG{label_<토큰>}`을 기대합니다. 양쪽이 어긋나 **정답을 넣어도 거부됩니다.** 비밀값이 없을 때만 우연히 일치해서 동작합니다.

심는 노드에 도달한 사람이 없어 아무도 신고하지 않았습니다. 이 저장소에서 두 번째로 나온 "아직 아무도 밟지 않은 경로" 결함입니다.

## 단위 테스트 94건이 전부 통과하고 있었습니다

각 조각이 **스스로** 일관적인지만 보기 때문입니다. 그래서 검증 두 가지를 함께 넣습니다.

### 1. 플레이스루 — 50문제를 실제로 푼다

세 함수를 Node에서 띄우고 1번부터 50번까지 풉니다. 흔적은 정답표가 아니라 **조작자가 얻는 경로 그대로** 얻습니다. 정적 파일에서 읽고, 채널을 호출하고, 모의 응용프로그램을 조작합니다. 블라인드 노드는 `like`로 한 글자씩 좁혀 값을 복구한 뒤 제출하는 것까지 수행합니다.

```
푼 문제: 50 / 50          제약으로 거부된 단계: 없음
49개만 푼 상태 : issued=false, 남은 모듈 1
50개 전부     : issued=true, HG-WSF-2026-...
다시 요청     : 같은 코드 ✓
```

### 2. 브라우저 전수 검사 — 계기가 실제로 값을 심는지 본다

플레이스루도 **계기가 그 값을 화면 어디에 두는지**는 보지 않습니다. 심는 방식 23개를 전부 열어 확인합니다.

| | 흔적이 발견된 자리 |
| --- | --- |
| 1 Idle Tooltip | DOM 마크업 |
| 2 Wrong Destination | 주소창 |
| 3 Ghost Comment | DOM 마크업 (주석) |
| 4 Forgotten Field | 입력 칸 value |
| 5~7 | DOM 마크업 |
| 8 Shadow Root | shadow DOM |
| 9 Residual Trace | 쿠키 |
| 10 Local Memory | localStorage |
| 11 Until You Leave | sessionStorage |
| 12 Deeper Store | IndexedDB |
| 30~39 해독 | 평문 없음 + 되돌리면 평문이 됨 |
| 50 Fragmented Key | DOM 마크업 (조각) |

**23 / 23.** 화면에 그대로 보이는 노드는 없습니다.

해독 노드는 "평문이 없다"만 보면 빈 화면도 통과하므로, **되돌리면 평문이 되는 것**까지 함께 봅니다. 되돌리기는 세 겹까지 시도합니다 — 세 겹인 노드(`hex → base64 → rot13`)와 서명 자리에 흔적을 둔 노드가 실제로 그 깊이를 요구합니다.

## 운영 확인

배포된 `hg-black-trace`의 **15개 모드 전부**와 정적 파일 3개를 직접 호출해 흔적이 나오는 것을 확인했습니다. 상태 코드도 의도대로입니다 (302 / 206 / 204). `hg-range`는 세션 없는 호출을 막습니다.

## 회귀 테스트

1. 이름으로 키가 걸린 표를 **번호로 찾지 않을 것**
2. 진행도 검사가 흔적 발급보다 **앞에 있어 죽은 코드가 되지 않을 것**

일부러 되돌려 테스트가 실제로 잡는 것을 확인했습니다.

## 배포

**`hg-learning` 재배포만 필요합니다.** SQL 없음, 다른 함수 변경 없음.

이것을 배포하기 전까지 심는 방식 노드 23개는 정답을 넣어도 통과하지 않습니다.

La Mise en vers par syllabes laisse régler la mesure vers par vers, de deux façons.

- **Selon des mesures** : nouvelle coupe avec un champ « Mesures » (« 5 7 5 » par défaut). Chaque vers prend la mesure suivante, en boucle, sans la dépasser ; un mot plus long que sa mesure fait un vers à lui seul. Une suite sans nombre valable prend « Syllabes par vers ».
- **Modulation et verrous** : « Syllabes par vers » devient modulable et verrouillable. La valeur du premier mot d'un vers en donne la mesure (rang : vers de plus en plus longs ; lettres, syllabes, motif, rampe…).
- L'inspecteur ne propose un verrou que pour un paramètre visible : une Mise en vers coupée par mots n'en a pas.

Tests : `test/domain/layout-plugins.test.ts`, `test/ui/tracks/view-model.test.ts`. `npm test` vert (646 tests), couverture > 90 %. Vérifié dans la page sur l'exemple de Proust (5-7-5, puis modulation par rang).

body:
## Description

The E2E suite repeatedly initializes the full playground for checks that can run with smaller editor fixtures, and sometimes initializes it before discovering that a test is inapplicable.

This audit reduces that work while retaining playground integration coverage:

- Evaluate static mode/platform exclusions before page creation and playground setup.
- Move matching, formatting, indentation, serialization, and table-model checks into unit tests.
- Move focused native-input and selection coverage into real-browser tests, including Markdown shortcuts, navigation, code-block keyboard behavior, hashtags, emoticons, mutation recovery, character limits, and selected table/list regressions.
- Move 28 HTML copy/paste cases into browser fixtures using the playground’s CSS and relevant extensions/plugins. Retain eight cases that exercise playground integration.
- Retain E2E coverage for toolbar wiring, system clipboard behavior, collaboration, nested editors, and layout interactions.
- Reduce setup work through bulk fixture insertion, cached HTML formatting, fewer redundant waits, combined keyboard shortcuts, and narrower clipboard-lock scopes. Hold the clipboard lock until its async callback finishes.
- Address intermittent failures with DOM/model caret checkpoints, deterministic fixture setup, popup-creation checks, and controlled cross-origin video fixtures.
- Preserve Unicode code points during native typing, bound individual input actions, and stop pending input when its editor is removed. Keep typing within one Playwright command to avoid per-character Vitest round trips.
- Wait for collaboration editor readiness without blocking on unrelated page resources, with a regression covering an unfinished subresource.
- Add CI timing reports, retain failure artifacts, and split the two slow macOS WebKit projects into two shards each.

The normal 50 ms E2E action delay and debug views remain enabled.

## Test plan

### Before

E2E discovery: **884 tests in 102 files**.

CI exposed intermittent selection/setup failures, native-input timeouts, and input continuing after its fixture was removed.

### After

E2E discovery: **658 tests in 100 files** — **226 fewer full-playground cases** per discovered project.

The static-skip audit compared all 12 platform/editor-mode combinations across three browser projects. Test IDs, titles, and outcomes matched. A native skip-only run confirmed 173 skipped cases with zero playground initializations or Playwright browser API calls.

Full local Linux WebKit browser suite: **660 passed, 3 skipped, across 60 files**.

Native-input regressions cover Unicode input, targeting the requesting editor, and stopping after editor removal. A temporary slow-input probe verified continued progress beyond the former whole-string timeout.

CI is green on `33e5087`:

- [Core tests](https://github.com/facebook/lexical/actions/runs/37259280206).
- [Extended platform/browser matrix](https://github.com/facebook/lexical/actions/runs/37259280167).
- [Internal registry](https://github.com/facebook/lexical/actions/runs/37259279688).

All seven browser CI configurations passed across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, and `git diff --check` passed. Individual commits contain detailed validation results.

body:
Piglit exposed incorrect formats, shader outputs, clipping, depth/stencil copies, and per-attachment blending in the SVGA-to-Vulkan path. This change corrects those paths and preserves guest state through an opt-in Mesa 22.3.6 patch. It also adds reproducible guest-driver builds, actual loaded-module provenance, independent guest controls, and desktop session setup.

The renderer fixes include packed/alpha/luminance/sRGB formats, typed and shadow samplers, fragment depth, pretransformed vertices and point size, four render targets and masks, constant-alpha blending, two-sided stencil, packed depth/stencil copies, supported custom border colors, and volume textures. Native format capabilities follow the physical Vulkan device. Framebuffer self-copy draws sample preserved, budgeted snapshots that remain alive until descriptor references complete. Occlusion queries begin and end outside render passes.

The optional guest patch leaves legacy behavior available without `SVGA_VLKN_EXTENDED_STATE=1`; software references keep the unchanged system module. The optional Piglit patch accepts either applicable error for one invalid unsized cube-storage call. Raw test failures and skips remain recorded; no pixel checks are waived.

Validation:
- Exact 146-case final hardware replay: **140 pass, 1 API expectation failure, 5 skip, 0 timeout, 0 recovery**. Zero failed pixel probes. All 85 PR26 passes and all 118 intermediate passes retained.
- Fresh unchanged llvmpipe: **146/146 pass**. The one raw API failure reproduces with matched GL 2.1 software; the corrected expectation passes on both renderers.
- Additional paired 29-case framebuffer selection: **13 hardware pass, 16 unsupported skips, no failures**, with 154 passing hardware subtests. Software passes all 29 top-level cases.
- Full replay and expanded comparison: **zero Vulkan validation errors or warnings**. Independent asymmetric depth/stencil controls pass all four orientations and overlapping copies on hardware and software.
- All 14 real-Vulkan host suites, mock/preload checks, and renderer-source CI pass, including repeated attachment-copy pixels, a three-pixel point, and its exact nine-sample query.

Final performance was measured with validation off, full 33-scene glmark2 at 800×600, vblank off, 0.5-second warm-up per scene, and three one-second-per-scene runs. At a 1100 MHz GPU minimum and default CPU weight, medians are 231 with VM105 running and 465 briefly paused. CPU weight 1000 plus separate vCPU affinity gives **443 running / 463 paused**. An unrelated Jellyfin transcode remained active. The **500 target remains unmet**; historical 556 and intermediate 532 measurements lack matched background-load evidence and are not claimed as final-build results. VM105 was automatically protected during each brief pause, resumed, and confirmed running. Glmark validation reports 27 Success / 6 Unknown / zero Failure; terrain is unsupported.

See [the recorded comparison](https://github.com/sukar0972/vlkn4svga3d/blob/91f3650d9bf2debc8e51771b9010741b476a8d4c/docs/piglit-accuracy-20261004.md) for hashes, full profile tables, limitations, deployed settings, and local raw evidence locations. author: justinthenick
body:
## Summary

Adds a contained ACP execution boundary for coding-agent runtimes.

The host Broker now owns:

- managed-task authorization through executor-maintained task identity
- immutable ACP runtime image pinning
- hardened disposable Docker sandbox lifecycle
- fixed task-worktree mounting
- ACP stdio transport
- per-task/session coordination
- validated cleanup and failure handling

The caller cannot supply an image, host path, container name, Docker option, shell command, mount, or network override.

## Security boundary

The ACP sandbox enforces:

- exact managed task worktree as the only host bind mount
- task worktree read/write
- read-only root filesystem
- non-root UID/GID 1000
- `cap-drop ALL`
- `no-new-privileges`
- no Docker socket
- no host SSH/Codex credentials
- `network=none`
- PID, memory and CPU limits
- bounded private tmpfs for runtime state
- immutable runtime image ID
- exact OpenCode ACP command
- Docker object revalidation before lifecycle mutations

Task authorization is derived from the executor's existing managed-worktree evidence, including registered worktree identity, expected `agent/<task_id>` branch, approved repository, Git locks/operations and an identity fingerprint.

## ACP transport

Adds the operator-side entry point:

`coding-agent-acp --task <managed-task-id>`

The adapter:

- owns sandbox create/validate/start/remove
- binds transport to the immutable container ID
- forwards only ACP stdio
- preserves stdout/stderr separation
- applies bounded buffering/backpressure
- limits session duration and byte counts
- coordinates with maintenance and per-task locks
- performs validated cleanup on EOF, error, SIGINT or SIGTERM
- refuses cleanup if sandbox identity/policy has drifted

This is not a general Docker or shell interface and is not exposed as a new HTTP/MCP maintenance tool.

## Candidate evidence

Base:

`cb0d7177f35b759033e2d2671b174e9d8da6947a`

Contained ACP commit:

`b8aba880846c24ea1f3bded8d514a6218dab95b1`

Candidate executor:

`sha256:3d35507d0fe4c8fd93b97d3d352bd85175e04d03a2a3fbe261cfd8cc312d384b`

Pinned OpenCode 1.18.34 runtime:

`sha256:485b8145db51ff2b7b494f117b8409d1e3a68ffcb315fc9d814b1d5662d5a276`

Validated:

- real managed-task identity: PASS
- real Broker create → inspect → start → remove: PASS
- real ACP initialize over contained stdio: PASS
- protocol version 1 / OpenCode 1.18.34: PASS
- EOF cleanup: PASS
- SIGTERM cleanup: PASS
- active-session lifecycle exclusion: PASS
- held maintenance gate: PASS
- image override refusal: PASS
- focused ACP tests: PASS
- full host suite: 93 passed
- full executor suite: 119 passed
- `git diff --check`: PASS
- production/source checkout remained clean
- live executor was not replaced or modified
- temporary candidate containers and ACP sandboxes were removed

## Deliberately deferred

This PR does **not** claim or implement:

- OpenClaw/ACPX routed model-turn acceptance
- model/provider authentication
- provider network access from the sandbox
- production deployment of the contained ACP path

Those belong to the next integration phase after this execution boundary is reviewed.

body: ## Intent Keep the Basecamp skill focused on durable operating and safety rules instead of duplicating the CLI's command manual. The existing skill had grown to 89 KB / 1,565 lines. Loading it for a simple question such as “how many Basecamp accounts do I have?” added roughly 13,000 tokens of tool output before the command could run, even though the installed CLI already exposes structured, command-specific `--agent --help`. ## What changed - reduce the main skill to 8.3 KB / 235 lines (about 91% smaller) - make live `basecamp ... --agent --help` the source of truth for command syntax, flags, scope, and notes - retain cross-cutting rules for credentials, URLs and replies, output modes, project/account scope, stdin content, attachments, retries, authentication, and mutations - teach the eval harness to serve structured help from the locally built CLI - add an eval for the original account-count question - enforce a 16 KiB skill budget and discovery-first contract in Go tests - document deterministic checks and model-eval comparison workflows ## Why the eval harness changed A discovery-first skill cannot be evaluated faithfully if help calls receive the generic empty mock. The harness now executes only structured `--agent --help` requests against the local binary; normal Basecamp operations remain deterministic mocks. ## Verification - `GOWORK=off bin/ci` - eval patterns: 162 compiled across 30 cases - structured-help harness self-test - skill drift checks The hosted model eval was not run locally because `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not configured; the existing PR eval workflow can run it when the repository secret is available. --- ## Summary by cubic Slims the Basecamp skill from 89 KB / 1,565 lines to 8.3 KB / 235 lines by removing the embedded command manual and treating live `basecamp ... --agent --help` output as the source of truth for syntax, flags, and scope. body:
What changes for families: On the setup page, parents can now paste each Kid's MyClub calendar link, so club events reach the Brief without going through the chat.

Closes #93

The MyClub step lists each Kid known so far, with whether their link is saved. The link itself is never sent back to the page. An "Open MyClub" button opens MyClub's site. The server opens it, so the page itself names no outside site. Three pictures show where the link is: the Kid's calendar, Calendar subscription (Tilaa kalenteri), and the `webcal://` link to copy. The parent picks the Kid and pastes the link into the page's own password field (ADR 0007).

- **Checking and saving:** The chat's `setup myclub` and the page now share one function, `setup_steps.myclub_link`, so both give the same results: `saved`, `not-a-myclub-link`, `link-failed`, `not-a-calendar` and `save-failed`. Each result is explained in Finnish, English and Chinese. The download runs outside the page's save lock, so a slow MyClub holds up no other save. The link never reaches a response, the output, the logs, a command line or setup's progress.
- **Progress:** Once a link is saved, MyClub is done. Setup moves on by itself once every Kid has a link. Until then the parent can add the next Kid's link or press Continue (`api/myclub/done`).
- **Without Wilma:** A Household without Wilma adds its Kids on this step by the name it calls them, through `setup save`. A Household with Wilma gets its Kids from Wilma and can't add them here.
- **Skipping:** MyClub can still be skipped with the existing Skip button.
- **Cleanup:** Every Source now has its own step, so the "not on the page yet" placeholder and its text are removed. The "town saved" message now says Kids are added later in setup instead of naming the Check step.
- **Docs:** `SECURITY.md`, `docs/setup-internals.md` and `app/tests/README.md` describe the page's MyClub field.

Design choices to look at:

- **"If it has none yet":** I read this as "while Wilma isn't on". So a Household without Wilma can add more than one Kid, not only its first.
- **When MyClub counts as done:** MyClub turns done after the first saved link. Kids without a club are left without a link.

## Not verified

- The page wasn't opened in a browser. The tests drive the server's JSON API, and `page.js` was only syntax-checked with `node --check`. Per #84, people check the look and the flow, not browser automation. The new pictures, the Kid list and the add-Kid form haven't been seen rendered.

body:
Closes #122

## Summary

```diff
 ExclusiveRun(client, name, stale_after=..., heartbeat_every=...,
+              now=None)            # default: time.time (stamped) / time.monotonic (never stamped)
   _stamp      -> heartbeat = time.time()
+                 heartbeat = self._wall_clock()
   _age        -> time.time() / time.monotonic()
+                 self._wall_clock() / self._elapsed_clock()

 KnowledgeIndex(settings, gateway, client=None,
+                lock_clock=None)   # handed to every ExclusiveRun it builds (Corpus locks + index-wide)
```

Takeover tests:

```diff
-crashed = ExclusiveRun(client, "lock", stale_after=0.05, heartbeat_every=3600)
-holder.__enter__(); time.sleep(0.1)
+crashed_holder(ExclusiveRun(client, "lock", heartbeat_every=3600, now=clock))
+clock.advance(119)  -> still refused
+clock.advance(2)    -> taken over
```

`crashed_holder` also stops the "crashed" holder's heartbeat thread at teardown.

## Evidence

- **Before:** takeover tests used `stale_after` of 0.05-0.2 s plus `time.sleep`; the crashed-Corpus test asserted a refusal, ran a whole Sync of another Corpus, and relied on it finishing inside 0.2 s.
  **After:** no `time.sleep` in `tests/test_sync.py`; the same tests use the default 120 s `stale_after` and a `FakeClock`. New tests: lock still held at 119 s, and a never-stamped marker goes stale by the same clock.
  `pytest -q`: 781 passed, 1 skipped. `ruff` and `mypy src tests` clean.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** negligible

The new `now` / `lock_clock` parameters default to the real clocks, so production staleness decisions are unchanged. Stamped heartbeats are still wall-clock because other processes read them.

author: undeemed
body:
## What this PR does

This PR is a follow-up to https://github.com/ayaangazali/telly/pull/117, which merged before this commit was pushed. It fixes stale data when the selected person changes, for caretaker and older-person views (#13).

- **The bug:** `useApi` kept its last state when its path changed. After a switch in the person picker, the previous person's alerts, readings, and messages stayed on screen under the new person until the server answered.
- **The fix:** `useApi` now returns `loading` when its path changes, until the new path replies. All family reads go through `useApi`, so this fixes every screen at once. The dashboard body and the report sheet are keyed by `family.id`, so a shown alert, a picked report, or an error does not carry over. A "Mark as seen" error clears on a switch.

## Selection contract (published on https://github.com/ayaangazali/telly/issues/53)

- **Authorized:** the selected person is the selected family in `useFamily()`. The only choices come from `GET /api/families`, which lists the caller's memberships. A remembered id that is not listed falls back to the first family. The server returns 403 to a non-member on every `/api/families/:familyId/*` route.
- **No impersonation:** selection changes only the `:familyId` in the path. The token and `/api/me` stay the signed-in person, so acknowledgements, messages, and reports are recorded as that person.

## Checks

These all pass at `1e2de4c0` (after merging current main): `bun run check-types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run test` (123 pass, 27 skip, 0 fail), `bun run --filter web build`, `bun run check:quality`, and `bun run check:structure`.

## Runtime proof (real local stack: in-memory SpacetimeDB, test OIDC issuer, built server, vite dev)

- Alice is a member of "Smoke family" (1) and "Second person" (3). Carol owns family 2.
- A `MutationObserver` recorded every DOM state while the picker switched 1 → 3.
  - **Before** (old `useApi`, same stack): `OLD > OLD+LOADING > OLD > OLD+NEW > NEW`.
  - **After:** `OLD > LOADING > NEW`. No state shows the previous person's data.
- `GET /api/families/2` and `/api/families/2/alerts` with alice's token return 403 forbidden.

## Limits

- The switch check used a test-issuer token through the app's own `setSessionToken`, because the default browser tier does not keep `sessionStorage` across reloads. UI sign-in passed on the Chrome tier for https://github.com/ayaangazali/telly/pull/117.
- The fallback for a tampered remembered id was checked by reading the code, not in the browser.

Closes 42nights/telly#79
Refs 42nights/telly#13

ts 干净（适配文件在检查程序内）；lint:arch 0 违规；test:harness 377/377；ci:quality 1352/1352。

Switch eligible single-shot chat generation to the Pi provider path while preserving existing provider-specific routes and unsupported-history fallbacks.

- Route eligible single-shot generation requests through the Pi supply layer while preserving AI SDK handling for static-factory providers, ACP, Responses API, and unsupported message histories.

Tests:
- Add real HTTP boundary coverage for Pi routing, prompt and token-limit projection, usage mapping, and AI SDK fallback behavior.
