author: copilot
body:
The `Build and Publish` workflow fails in `announce` with "Resource not accessible by integration" when posting to the release monitor issue. The token lacks `pull-requests: write`, and the `issue_comment` trigger can also run in contexts where the token is restricted, such as fork or PR comments.

- **Permissions**
  - Add `pull-requests: write` to the workflow-level `permissions` block.

- **Comment guards (`announce`, `report-success`, `report-failure`)**
  - Each `github-script` comment step now has an `if` guard and `continue-on-error: true`.
  - The guard skips the step on forks, on comments made on pull requests, and when the head repo is a fork.
  - The guards sit on the steps, not the jobs. `announce` therefore still succeeds when it skips the comment, and `validate` and the installer jobs still run. Posting a comment can no longer fail a release.

```yaml
- name: Post run link
  if: >-
    github.event.repository.fork != true &&
    github.event.issue.pull_request == null &&
    github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork != true
  continue-on-error: true
  uses: actions/github-script@...
```

- **Unchanged**
  - `workflow_dispatch`, tag and `main` push triggers, and the owner `/release v3-build-1` comment trigger behave as before.
  - I haven't addressed the `context.sha` concern for `issue_comment` events, where the SHA is the default branch's. Only the comment body is affected.

Reviewer note: the guard also silently skips comments when the repo itself is a fork. This is intended, but tell me if you'd rather it surface a warning.

Gold was stored twice: as Parquet and as a 559 MB SQLite copy rebuilt with indexes and VACUUM on every run. DuckDB now queries the Parquet files in place through a single module (etl/common/warehouse.py), which the app, both model scripts and the tests share.

- run_gold: drop the SQLite export; Parquet is the only gold storage

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing clean-close receipts for quiescent agent databases when unrelated shutdown work remains unfinished, avoiding stale-lease recovery for those databases on the next start.

Related: #164670.

## User Impact

Settled databases publish their existing clean-close receipts independently. After drain grace, completed publication retention and unborrowed native handles retire before restart-marker waits. Active borrowers and unfinished writes retain their leases.

No schema, configuration, receipt-format, update, or rollback migration is required. Acceptance must name a predecessor build containing this change: installing it cannot change the old predecessor's cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle reuses per-path close operations under one root-wide admission fence, installed before reentrant revocation and held through every selected outcome. Fresh native opens and resource registrations use the same fence. The existing last-lease owner remains the sole receipt writer.

The process admission owner publishes the post-grace cleanup boundary. Worker stores release completed retained references there, and native handles reuse their existing idle-eviction callback at cleanup and after the final borrower releases. Accepted cleanup keeps its authority and can reopen through normal admission, which dirties the receipt again.

Production delta: **+88 LOC** (163 added / 75 removed, seven files). The required contracts account for the growth: root-wide exclusion across independent closes (+25), the reset-owned post-grace event and joined publication cleanup (+43), and ordinary idle eviction with listener disposal (+20). The global all-or-nothing native-close barrier and redundant rejection wrapping are removed.

Cold-reopen fixtures now join canonical asynchronous closure while preserving their cache resets, intentional revocation races, persisted-state assertions, and underlying cleanup failures. Native handle-loss fixtures evict only the cached native handle, preserving the accepted writer authority their scenarios require.

## Evidence

Current PR head: `85ab46fbac904c3cfb53f176895c274e02368f81`. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37189499704) with 95 successful jobs, 20 skipped, and no failures (572 s elapsed). The complete PR check rollup has 121 passing checks, 43 skipped, and no pending or failing checks. Across scoped Blacksmith runs, 733 focused tests in 31 files passed; independent reviews through P1 are clean.

**Process-rig source:** `76c760d915f949acaf886f66a5ab4c68a0cb2985`, compared with clean main `f28801628446a76a77fc856b01c87464fe7701a4`. All 37 changed source-file hashes were verified before and after the builds and rig.

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m42xgk4scmf4357mbnmvkvvz`, profile `openclaw-check`, Linux / Node 24.19.0, [provisioning run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37186331654): separate clean `pnpm build` runs and both assertion-driven process scenarios passed. Combined command time: **1,319.010 s**, exit 0.

The rig admits three real embedded turns stalled at a loopback provider, a real background exec session, and transcript/SQLite workers with attributed persisted leases. It warms a fourth, idle database through `sessions.create`, `chat.inject`, and `chat.history`. The explicit fault withholds one successful native restart-marker reply. SIGTERM uses a 45-second drain and an armed 90-second external SIGKILL ceiling; both predecessors exit at their own earlier deadline.

| Measurement after SIGTERM | Main | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Canonical written receipts | 0 | 1 |
| Idle database receipt | absent | **45.021 s** |
| Retained leases at predecessor exit | 7 | 6 |
| Successor stale database paths | 4 | 3, unfinished siblings only |
| Predecessor deadline exit | 85.120 s | 85.113 s |

The candidate's `receipt-ready` database has durable `clean_close=1`; its successor performs a real write without a stale-lease report for that path. The derived partial report names `main`, `blocked`, and `healthy` as unfinished, with two actual leases each and `clean_close=0`. This reads existing records and adds no receipt format. All three model requests aborted at 45.014 s on main and 45.024–45.025 s on the candidate.

Commands, through normal synced `crabbox run --id <id> --timing-json -- bash -c <script>`:

```text
pnpm build
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <shutdown-rig.mjs> --root <fresh-root> --port <19580-or-19582> --fault hold-marker-reply --idle-database --expect <baseline-or-candidate>
```

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m42t20wtwjb50acwzgb1k4ck`, same profile, [provisioning run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37183307301): **677 tests across 28 files passed in 367.67 s** with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <28 files> --maxWorkers=1`. Core types, all 27 test type graphs, ratchets, boundaries, formatting, dead-export scans, and changed-file lint passed. After correcting two test-only rebase naming issues, passing unchanged stages were reused; the affected resource gate and all 35 changed TypeScript files' lint passed. The original full command stopped at lint and is not represented as an exit-0 run. Independent reviews through P1 returned scoped-clean.

First PR CI exposed unjoined fixture closes and stale close-result assertions. Those were repaired; unrelated UI failures were inherited through rebase to their main fixes. Post-rig follow-ups include two fixture corrections from [the previous exact-head run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37187797920): archive pruning joins revoked cleanup before postcondition readback, and handle-loss scenarios use native eviction. No production bytes changed after the process rig. Both follow-up suites passed on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m42zjw7ycwvm7cz7xj6nxs4m`: `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-handle-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 17 tests (40 s wall), and `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-history-archive-pruning.admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 16 tests (32 s wall). Fresh independent review through P1 returned scoped-clean; follow-up `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --timed --base 76c760d915f949acaf886f66a5ab4c68a0cb2985 --head 76c760d915f949acaf886f66a5ab4c68a0cb2985 -- <the two fixture paths>` passed the affected test type graph, core graph boundary, lint, formatting, ratchets and dead-export checks. Full synced command: 324.453 s, exit 0. The lease was stopped before the next commit.

The preceding CI run on `f7f9682c9ed53f0043b28f74fb37d85c810adfbf` passed every selected test shard except one cold-storage rollback postcondition read. That fixture now joins path closure after preserving the immediate revocation, original rejection, actual worker exit, and close-latency assertions. On Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m430g369wmxcs9bxgysp62pf`, `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 23 tests (83 s wall); the file-scoped `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --timed --base f7f9682c9ed53f0043b28f74fb37d85c810adfbf --head f7f9682c9ed53f0043b28f74fb37d85c810adfbf -- src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.test.ts` passed all selected checks. Combined command: 330.996 s, exit 0; fresh independent review through P1 was scoped-clean. The existing suite exercises real archival, restore, rollback workers, and 34 MiB candidates; this adds no test or worker boot. The lease was stopped before committing.

The ordinary earlier stalled-model workload already wrote receipts on main. The injected marker stall remains distinct from the unconfirmed production cause: live reply claims still retain six leases in this comparison. Recovery marking revalidates live run/session authority, so moving cancellation ahead of it requires a separate ownership change. **Total production outage reduction remains unproven.**

author: saymon0123
body:
## O que mudou

Achado **por acaso**, conferindo o `cron.job` antes de inserir uma inscrição de
teste para o dono revisar o item 16: **nada chamava `expirar_reservas`.**

Nenhum dos sete jobs do cron, nenhuma tela, nenhuma edge, nenhum fluxo do n8n —
procurado nos quatro lugares. As únicas menções no banco eram a própria função e
um **comentário** dentro da `devolver_chamados_sem_resposta`.

E a história explica como passou: a `private.expirar_reservas` nasceu na **0192**,
a **0197** criou a fachada `public.expirar_reservas` **justamente para o n8n poder
chamá-la**, e o chamador nunca foi construído. Cada peça assumiu que a outra
ligaria o fio.

## O que estava quebrado — três coisas ao mesmo tempo

A `devolver_chamados_sem_resposta` reconhece quem não respondeu pela **ausência**
da reserva (`chamado` com `appointment_id` nulo, pela FK `on delete set null`).
Sem ninguém apagando:

1. quem fosse chamado e não respondesse ficaria `chamado` **para sempre** — nunca
   devolvido à fila, nunca chamado de novo, nunca encerrado;
2. a reserva ficaria `reservado` **para sempre**, e a `horarios_livres` **não olha
   `reservada_ate`** (conferido) — o horário ficaria bloqueado para **todo mundo**:
   agenda pública, agente e CRM;
3. e quem respondesse "Sim" depois do prazo levaria *"O prazo da reserva venceu"*
   — perdia a vaga, a vaga seguia bloqueada, e a pessoa seguia presa.

**O prazo de 30 minutos era decorativo: ninguém o fazia valer.**

Nada disso mordia hoje, porque o remetente está desligado e não havia reserva
viva. Mordia no dia em que fosse ligado — e esse dia é o dono apertar dois
interruptores.

## O conserto

`rodar_a_fila` ganhou a expiração como **primeiro** passo, e passou de três para
quatro. A ordem agora importa duas vezes: apagar a reserva **antes** de devolver
(é a ausência dela que sinaliza "não respondeu"), e devolver **antes** de chamar
(a que chama só enxerga `esperando`).

**Dentro do tique, e não num job novo, de propósito:** quem agenda o remetente
agenda tudo. Um job separado seria uma segunda coisa para alguém lembrar de
ligar — e foi exatamente esquecer de ligar que criou este defeito.

A `horarios_livres` **não** mudou. Ela é a régua que a agenda pública, o agente e
o CRM usam, e mexer nela para cobrir atraso de varredura seria tratar o sintoma
no lugar mais caro do sistema. Com o tique a cada 10 minutos, uma reserva fica no
máximo ~10 minutos vencida, e a trava de sobreposição continua sendo a palavra
final.

## Medido, não deduzido

O ensaio provou o defeito **e** o conserto na mesma transação:

```
SEM expirar:  a inscricao fica em "chamado" (presa) e a reserva existe=1
COM expirar:  reservas_expiradas=1 | reserva apagada | devolvidas=1 | chamada de novo
```

Migration aplicada em produção e o arquivo conferido contra `prosrc` por md5.
pgTAP do tique: **12 → 14 asserções**, e a segunda delas afirma que não sobra
reserva vencida depois do tique — que era o defeito.

---

# Adendo: mais dois defeitos, achados pelo dono na revisão

## 3. Cancelar uma vaga segurada era recusado (0212)

Ele tentou apagar a inscrição de teste pela tela do agendamento e levou **"Essa
operação não é permitida porque deixaria um dado inválido"** — o CHECK
`appointments_reserva_com_prazo` (0192). A tela faz `set status = 'cancelado'` e
mais nada. Medido: só com o status, **23514**; com os dois campos juntos, passa.

**E eu já sabia disso** — está escrito na 0207, onde a `confirmar_vaga_da_fila`
muda os dois na mesma instrução *"porque o CHECK exige o par"*. Tratei o caso da
fila e deixei os outros: cancelar (dois botões), faltar, concluir e remarcar, por
quatro portas.

O conserto **não foi na tela**: um gatilho `before insert or update` que zera
`reservada_ate` sempre que a linha não está em `reservado`. Caller por caller é a
forma de errar o próximo — e o próximo já existia sem ninguém ver, porque a fila
nunca tivera uma reserva viva numa tela de verdade. O CHECK segue sendo a
garantia; o gatilho é quem a cumpre.

Ensaio em produção com cinco pontos (reserva viva mantém o prazo; cancelar só com
o status passa; `faltou` passa; `agendado` passa; nascer com prazo é normalizado).
pgTAP da 0192: **10 → 13**.

## 4. "Dia inteiro" deixava as 23:59 abertas

> *"clico em dia todo e ainda assim é possível realizar um agendamento para
> aquele dia"*

A investigação primeiro **derrubou a hipótese óbvia**: `DIA_INTEIRO` está certo
(00:00–23:59), o modal usa a janela certa, e a trava de sobreposição do banco
**inclui** `bloqueio`. Então medi.

Com um bloqueio de dia inteiro num dia vazio, os horários livres caíram de **59
para 1** — não para zero. O que sobrava era exatamente o que **começa às 23:59**.

A causa é o intervalo ser `[início, fim)`: um bloqueio que **termina** às 23:59
não se sobrepõe a um horário que **começa** às 23:59. O dia inteiro passa a
terminar na meia-noite **seguinte**.

`fimDoDiaInteiro` foi para o módulo puro `janelaDeBloqueio.ts` — e não ficou
dentro do componente — para poder ser testada: **quatro testes**, com virada de
mês e de ano. Usa `setDate` e não soma de 24h: virada de fuso é com o calendário.

Nos campos da tela o fim continua 23:59. *"Termina à meia-noite do dia seguinte"*
é verdade de banco, não frase para quem marca uma folga.

## O que os dois têm em comum

Nenhum apareceu em teste automático, e os dois estavam em código que eu declarei

author: aschenrot
body:
Refs #23.

## Authority

Accepted RunenRender base:

```text
ac7a1049d688145d9c2e570889315e72f485435a
```

Previously reviewed RR23-E1 head:

```text
7bcd19c02fc6671896fde8a1fe09f371d10e5432
```

Corrective candidate:

```text
cdaddbc98de771c1287055a425c026b5ec9e125e
```

This is **RR23-E1b investigation evidence only**. It does not change production source, public API, root manifests/lockfiles, or durable architecture authority.

## Why this correction exists

Cold review found the accepted E1 comparative CPU ratios were not methodologically fair:

- Sparse Strips was forced to `Level::baseline()` while Lyon used its normal optimized implementation;
- timed Sparse-Strips iterations reused `StripGenerator` without the documented `reset(width, height)` used by Vello's own benchmark.

Those facts do not invalidate the E1 corpus, determinism, dependency isolation, structural support, or hosted execution provenance. They do invalidate treating the previous numerical Sparse/Lyon CPU ratios as acceptance-grade comparative performance evidence.

## Exact delta from reviewed E1

Only `.github/evaluations/rr23_path_realization.rs` changes:

- `Level::baseline()` -> `Level::new()` for Sparse-Strips verification/timing;
- reset the reused `StripGenerator` after each generation.

The existing neutral corpus, scales, fill/stroke semantics, changing/reused modes, batch size, raw samples, summary statistics, temporary-workspace isolation, and workflow remain unchanged.

## Required evidence

On this exact head:

- RR23 path realization evaluation;
- RunenRender repository validation;
- RunenRender Vulkan conformance.

The corrected run may replace the previous comparative CPU ratios. It still makes **no GPU-performance claim**.

This PR should remain unmerged; it is temporary investigation machinery. The accepted result belongs on #23 and later in the separately reviewed durable architecture-authority reconciliation.

## Final RR23-E1b evidence

Exact corrective head: `cdaddbc98de771c1287055a425c026b5ec9e125e`.

Exact-head hosted evidence:
- evaluation run `37179443844`, job `111368831112`: PASS;
- validation run `37179444112`, repository baseline job `111368831993`: PASS;
- validation run `37179444112`, Vulkan conformance job `111368831824`: PASS.

The corrected median reused Sparse/Lyon CPU preprocessing ratio across 40 case/scale pairs is ~3.44x; the earlier ~5.81x value is superseded. Sparse Strips is competitive on some complex paths and strongly favorable in the culling-heavy cases, while Lyon remains cheaper for simple geometry and the exercised stroke cases.

Disposition: Lyon remains the initial owner-compatible general-path baseline. Sparse Strips remains a deferred replaceable candidate, not a rejected approach. No GPU-performance conclusion is made.

The corrected disposition is recorded on #23. This investigation PR is intentionally not merged.

body:
Switching between Driving, Inventory sorting and other saved arrangements now supports keyboard actions, an unsaved Previous arrangement, selective restoration, startup restore and portable workspace files. This follows merged PR #4 and targets current main; the implementation is split into reviewable commits.

## Feature history: PRs #1–4
These are already inherited from main; the checklist below records what was added across the earlier PRs. PR #3 was brought into main through PR #4.

### [PR #1 — Assistant controls and visual viewport setup](https://github.com/DrCum/Folderstorm/pull/1)
- [x] Dedicated **Local assistant** preferences with Permissions/Setup tabs, concise help, readiness/activity status, configuration copying for Codex/Cursor/Claude Code and a bounded token-free connection check.
- [x] Stronger compound permissions for snapshot thumbnails and texture uploads; permission revocation cancels stale approvals/work and higher upload prices require approval.
- [x] Paginated approval reviews showing authoritative names, paths, counts, destinations, rename pairs, costs and consequences, with material scope revalidation.
- [x] Draggable viewport edges, monitor selection, numeric editing, immediate preview and Preferences Cancel rollback, including monitor-topology guards.
- [x] Verified replacement-link creation before submitting originals to Trash, with per-link outcomes, cancellation/deadline guards and protection against duplicate uncertain retries.

### [PR #2 — Permissions, workspaces, bulk Inventory and setup](https://github.com/DrCum/Folderstorm/pull/2)
- [x] **Read only / Ask before changes / Custom** permission presets, expandable individual permissions and session-only access/permissions.
- [x] Account-local named viewport/bar and supported utility-window workspaces: save, rename, delete and transactional preview/rollback; primary and workspace-owned extra Inventory support.
- [x] Bulk Inventory review/history from the gear menu and capability-gated MCP preview, execute, history and undo-preview tools; frozen targets, bounded session history, Stop/Clear, idempotent execution and submitted-versus-confirmed results.
- [x] Narrow undo for verified AIS completion with unchanged provenance; unconfirmed UDP results remain ineligible for undo.
- [x] Installation-owned Windows MCP configuration, stable verified Velopack launch paths and conservative ownership-checked legacy-link cleanup on uninstall.
- [x] Consolidated viewport/toolbar controls in **Layout**, removal of the empty redundant Viewport tab, unclipped profile/toolbar controls and corrected workspace scrolling.
- [x] Reported Windows strict-type fixes and absolute CMake source-path handling for junctioned build directories.

### [PR #3 — Quick switching, search and additional windows](https://github.com/DrCum/Folderstorm/pull/3)
- [x] Draggable **Workspaces** toolbar button and **World → Workspaces & Layouts…**, with account-local favorites and distinct workspace/layout entries.
- [x] Save the current arrangement from the switcher; exclude Preferences and workspace UI from capture and preserve pending Preferences edits.
- [x] Capture/restore up to 16 ordinary additional Inventory windows, reuse/create missing windows and hide extras absent from the arrangement, with Preview/Cancel recovery and attached-utility protection.
- [x] Move & View tab order: **Layout**, then **Workspaces**. Removed the included workspace Starting Arrangements.
- [x] Compatible chat restoration: Conversations geometry without changing conversations/open state; detached Nearby Chat visibility only when supported.
- [x] Settings search aliases for **MCP**, **dual monitor**, **workspace** and **undo**, selecting nested tabs and scrolling matches into view; clearing search restores prior navigation.
- [x] Local assistant **History** tab linking to Inventory history/undo review.

### [PR #4 — Favorites and optional Inventory folders](https://github.com/DrCum/Folderstorm/pull/4)
- [x] Optional workspace/layout favorites buttons with shortened labels, full tooltips, overflow/management and shared guarded switching. PR #5 moves these onto the existing landmark row.
- [x] Per-workspace **Remember Inventory folders** for primary, workspace-owned and ordinary additional Inventory windows, including single-folder roots and list/gallery/combination modes.
- [x] Graceful missing/filtered/unavailable-folder handling and live-only Preview/Cancel recovery of prior folder/navigation/selection state; folder references remain account-local and optional.

## Completed features added in PR #5
- [x] **Keyboard shortcuts:** assign direct workspace/layout switching, next/previous favorite and Return to previous arrangement through existing Controls. No default keys; existing text-input, focus and mode routing applies.
- [x] **Previous arrangement:** one session-only snapshot includes unsaved supported-window positions and toolbar/folder context. Returning swaps arrangements; account/session changes clear it.
- [x] **Optional snapping:** supported standalone utility windows snap to frame, viewport and neighboring edges; Shift bypasses.
- [x] **Alignment:** align selected supported windows to an edge or distribute horizontally/vertically, with Previous recovery.
- [x] **Startup restore:** account-local Off (default), named workspace or Last arrangement; waits for UI/Inventory readiness and cancels after a manual switch/session change.
- [x] **Active/modified indicators:** switcher and favorite buttons track the current definition and changes to included fields.
- [x] **Update current:** replacement confirmation captures the reviewed arrangement and preserves the workspace's folder, component and toolbar choices.
- [x] **Selective restoration:** independently include viewport/bars, Inventory/Received Items, maps and compatible chat. Excluded groups remain untouched; legacy saves retain their behavior.
- [x] **Optional toolbar button sets:** ordered registered commands and display modes for left/right/bottom toolbars, integrated with Preview/Cancel, Previous, Last and Update.
- [x] **Export/import:** native file pickers; portable export excludes folder references by default. Bounded validated imports review collisions and unavailable commands, keep existing names by default and require explicit replacement confirmation.
- [x] **Read-only diagram preview:** inspect saved arrangements before switching using the same fitted window geometry as loading, with included/omitted groups and adjustment counts.
- [x] **Shared favorites row:** workspace/layout favorites sit alongside landmarks after a `|` divider, using the active skin's landmark button styling. Removes group labels and the extra opaque row; each group retains overflow.
- [x] **Short-window usability:** switcher options scroll while its action footer remains accessible.

The shared controller handles captures, restoration and account/session guards. Supported-window limits, restrictions and Preferences OK/Cancel remain enforced. Named files do not capture conversation content, Inventory contents, search filters or item selections. Latest roadmap documentation from the plan-only commits is carried forward and marked complete.

author: yuto-trd
body:
## Description
- Hosted Git now authenticates with opaque, non-expiring access tokens scoped to one repository, so remotes can be written as `https://git:TOKEN@beutl.beditor.net/api/v3/git/ID.git` and work with stock Git and Git LFS without the desktop app refreshing one-hour tokens.
- Tokens are revocable. Only a SHA-256 of each token is stored; a token stops working when it is revoked, its repository is deleted, or the repository leaves the account that created it. Each repository allows up to 50 active tokens, and last use is recorded at most once an hour.
- The v3 API (`GET/POST /repos/:id/tokens`, `DELETE /repos/:id/tokens/:tokenId`) and the dashboard connect dialog list, create (name + read/write scope, secret shown once with an authenticated clone URL) and revoke tokens.
- Git and LFS accept Basic credentials (user name ignored) or Bearer. The 401 now sends a Basic challenge so Git uses the URL credentials. The LFS upload action reuses the client's own credential instead of a separate OID-scoped upload token.

Verification: full Vitest suite (3170 passed), workspace typecheck, `vp run build`, `opennextjs-cloudflare build` and `wrangler deploy --dry-run`.

## Breaking changes
- `POST /api/v3/repos/:id/token` is removed. Desktop clients must create a token with `POST /api/v3/repos/:id/tokens` and keep it.
- Previously issued JWT Git tokens stop working after deploy.
- Apply migration `20261004000000_add_git_access_tokens` to production before deploying. Git and LFS requests authenticate against its table.
- `BEUTL_GIT_TOKEN_SECRET` is no longer read and can be removed from the Worker secrets after deploy.

## Fixed issues
None

author: nicholasjconn
body:
## Summary

- `al upgrade` and `al upgrade plan` now list a customized file that a rename migration moves when its content differs from the target template, at the file's new path.
- Approving "overwrite all", or running `al upgrade --yes --apply-managed-updates`, no longer replaces that file with the template without showing it. Examples include `.agent-layer/instructions/02_memory.md` becoming `01_memory.md`, and skill directories such as `agent-dispatch` and `playwright-cli` moving to `dispatch-agent` and `playwright`.
- A moved file that already matches the template is still omitted. Deletes, skill-format migrations, and append migrations still hide their diffs, including when they overlap a rename.

## Key decisions

- Apply-time review coverage now excludes rename operations. Coverage is still computed before migrations run and still matches by path prefix, but only non-rename coverage hides a post-migration diff. Rename sources disappear with the move; the destination diff is the pending template overwrite.
- Plan detection follows the file through chained renames back to its current path, including a symlink, and compares those bytes with the destination template. The plan does not need the target manifest to rebuild that preview from the migration report.
- Template lookup for a destination does not depend on the destination already existing on disk. Other migration kinds still win when they cover the same path.

## Changes

- Split non-rename migration coverage from full coverage and use only the former to filter the managed overwrite-all review.
- Add post-migration path origins and detect template differences for renamed files in `BuildUpgradePlan` and `BuildUpgradePlanDiffPreviews`.
- Cover unified and non-unified apply previews, directory renames, plan updates, plan diffs, rename chains, symlinked sources, selective decline, template-equal moves, overlapping non-rename coverage, and error propagation.
- Record the fix under `Unreleased` › `Fixed` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/install/ -count=1 -timeout 240s -run 'Renamed|MovedFileUpdates_Renamed'` — pass

## Notes

- Renaming onto an occupied destination, snapshot and rollback behavior, ownership baselines across renames, and new files that appear only under a rename destination remain unchanged. A new file with no existing source stays hidden in both reviews.
- If an earlier upgrade already replaced one of these files, `al upgrade rollback --list` shows that upgrade's snapshot, and `al upgrade rollback <snapshot-id>` restores the files that upgrade changed.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Upgrade plans and overwrite-all reviews now show customized files moved by a rename at their new paths, with a diff against the destination template. Files that already match the template remain unlisted.
  * Upgrades can now recover customized files that were already replaced, helping preserve changes during rollback.

  - Added a pre-step that emits a notice and skips work when any required secret is missing.
  - Added an `if` condition on the action step so gist updates run only when all required secrets are non-empty.

- **Resulting behavior**
  - Missing-secret runs now no-op with a clear notice instead of failing the job.
  - Properly configured repos retain existing update behavior.

```yaml
- name: Skip when required secrets are missing
  if: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN == '' || secrets.GIST_ID == '' || secrets.WAKATIME_API_KEY == '' }}
  run: echo "::notice::Skipping gist update because GH_TOKEN, GIST_ID, or WAKATIME_API_KEY is not configured."

- name: Update gist
  if: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN != '' && secrets.GIST_ID != '' && secrets.WAKATIME_API_KEY != '' }}
  uses: quackclub/hacka-box@main
```

body:
Closes #12. Specified by Vonyx (DaxAvalon/Vonyx#131, `docs/ux/booth-visual-language.md` §2); the last of the six items that specification filed here, after #19–#23.

## What

A built-in **`booth`** theme (`themeName="booth"`, `boothTheme`): a recorder read from one to two metres away in a dark room.
- The dark theme's ground (`bg1` `#0a0a0a`) and accents, unchanged.
- Text tiers lifted — `text1` `#f0f0f0`, `text2` `#c8c8c8`, `text3` `#a0a0a0` — so every tier used for words measures **at least 7:1** on `bg1` and `bg2` (WCAG 1.4.6), asserted in a test with the repository's own `contrastRatio`; `border4` at 3:1 for focus and separators.
- The type scale raised for arm's-length reading: `fontMd` 18 px, `fontLg` 24, `fontXl` 32, `fontXxl` 40, `font3xl` 48 (small tiers 11–14); line height 1.4; zero radius.
- Wired like the other built-ins: `src/themes/booth.ts`, `THEME_NAMES`, provider and scope maps, root export, the `[data-vf-theme="booth"]` cascade block in `tokens.css` (the cascade test pins it to the token object), the dark `color-scheme` group, the breakpoint group, the testing helpers' name unions, the themes guide line, the llms summary (which now counts all seven themes; regenerated).

## Scope

No change to the token interface: the two reading-face tokens the Vonyx specification proposed (`fontBoothReadingFamily`, `fontBoothReading`) would add keys every theme must implement and are left as a follow-up; a consumer sets the reading face with a `ThemeScope` override meanwhile. The Figma export's theme map (dark, light, midnight, grey) is untouched, as it is for `soft` and `soft-light`. The values are a starting point for the maintainer to tune; Vonyx's usability plan tests them at the distance narrators actually sit.

## Verified (in the dev container)

- New `boothTheme.test.ts` (name registered, ground and accents kept, 7:1 text tiers, 3:1 border, raised scale); the theme cascade, provider, theme-script, phase-4 token, SSR, export-tokens and CSS-logical suites; `lint:css-colors`; `lint:voidframe`; typecheck; full suite passed (counts in the final check log).

No release — the maintainer cuts versions. The CHANGELOG's Unreleased section gains a bullet after `AudioLevelMeter`'s, as #20–#23 do.

「運用設定 > HuggingFace」で scheme なしのミラー（`hf-mirror.com`）を保存すると、backend を再起動するまで実行中の設定が `hf-mirror.com` のままになり、サービスの起動 / 再起動のときに parser へ `HF_ENDPOINT=hf-mirror.com` が渡ってモデルの DL が失敗する（`httpx.UnsupportedProtocol`）。`backend/.env` には書いた値で再起動後に直るため、実行中の値と `.env` の値が食い違っていた。

- `app/api/routes/settings.py` の `_huggingface_settings_candidate`: endpoint を `Settings.normalize_huggingface_endpoint`（起動時の読み込みと同じ規則）で正規化し、token は前後の空白を除いてから扱う（空白だけなら未入力 = 保存済みの token を保持）。

CI: `RAG / Backend` の全テスト・mypy は CI を参照。

- endpoint の形式（http / https 以外の scheme や空白を含む値）の検証は今回は足していない（今までどおり受け付ける）。

author: wenshao
body:
## What this PR does

Two Workspace-bound Hosted Sessions that share one mount used to race fatally: the Runtime Broker correctly serializes the mount's execution lease, but the second Session's turn surfaced the definite `workspace_busy` refusal as a terminal, unclassified `turn_error` (`hosted_turn_failed`) — indistinguishable from a genuine execution failure, and the coordinator would not redrive. With this change, a turn that meets a definite 409 `workspace_busy` while acquiring the mount during tool execution queues instead: it retries the acquisition on a short poll bounded by the turn's own cancellation and deadline, then continues once the holder's turn releases the mount. Queueing starts with a single stderr notice so operators can see a waiting turn. Behavior outside that case is unchanged on purpose: `workspace_unavailable` refusals and recovery acquisitions still end the turn with the fast, classified error, and everything after storage is claimed keeps recovery-blocking semantics. The reproduction test for the issue scenario is kept in the suite as the regression pin, unit tests pin the queue/cancel/ambiguity branches, and the design document's failure semantics are updated in both languages.

## Why it's needed

A second user (or a second tab/agent) on the same Workspace simply lost their turn before this change: the client could not tell "busy, retry later" from a real failure. Issue #13328 makes the fail-terminal shape a conscious decision — this PR picks the issue's queueing option so the second turn completes after the first instead of being lost.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Reproduced behavior (before): two Hosted Sessions bound to one mount, both prompts admitted `202`; the first turn acquires the mount's execution lease; the second turn's first acquisition is refused `409 workspace_busy` and the turn settles terminally with `turn_error` code `hosted_turn_failed`, logging `Hosted Harness turn … failed: Error: Runtime Broker returned HTTP 409 (workspace_busy)`. An independent reproduction run recorded `{ completedTurns: 1, failedTurns: 1, busyEvidence: true, crossTalk: false }`.
- Expected behavior (after): the second turn polls the acquisition, logs `Hosted Harness turn … waits for the Workspace mount held by another Session.` once, acquires once the first turn finishes, and settles `turn_complete`; both sessions' tools execute exactly once, with no cross-session text leakage. An independent verification run recorded the loser settling `turn_complete` with `failedTurns: 0` and all positives holding, plus adversarial probes: five consecutive busy refusals then release completes on 250 ms pacing with the notice logged exactly once; cancelling mid-queue rejects with the abort reason and releases nothing; a mount that stays busy across many polls keeps polling.
- Confirm the boundaries did not move: `workspace_unavailable` and the recovery/continuation acquisition paths still refuse fast with classified codes (the session may retry or reload), and an ambiguous acquisition failure (e.g. lost reply) keeps recovery-blocking even when the turn is being cancelled.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI change. Before/after summaries and probe outcomes are quoted above from the reproduction and verification reports; the harness-level regression test encodes both shapes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

<!-- ✅ tested · ⚠️ not tested · N/A -->

### Environment (optional)

Harness-level vitest suites over the real HTTP stack (express listener, local journal/resource stores, the Broker mocked at its HTTP boundary) against `node dist/cli.js`-equivalent sources; `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run bundle` all green. The full packaged-stack E2E runner's `--second-workspace-session` mode is not in the repository and was not run; the issue author is expected to re-run it, where the summary should flip to `{ completedTurns: 2, failedTurns: 0 }`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a queued turn waits without a built-in cap — it ends only when the mount frees, the turn is cancelled, or its prompt deadline fires. That is the deliberate queue semantics; a wedged mount holder remains the operator-recovery domain it already was.
- Not validated / out of scope: the packaged-stack runner mode mentioned above; the daemon-side workspace removal/agents `workspace_busy` routes (unchanged); MCP-profile session busy handling at session open (unchanged); extracting shared test scaffolding across the harness-session suites (noted as follow-up).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — the only behavior change is that a turn refused with definite `workspace_busy` now queues rather than settling as an error; clients that matched on `hosted_turn_failed` for this case will instead see the turn stay active and then complete.
- Design doc updated (both languages, kept in sync): docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.md and docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.zh-CN.md.

## Linked Issues

Closes #13328

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

共享一个挂卷的两个 Workspace 绑定 Hosted Session 此前会致命竞争：Runtime Broker 正确地串行化挂卷的执行租约，但第二个 Session 的回合把确定的 `workspace_busy` 拒绝以终态、不可归因的 `turn_error`（`hosted_turn_failed`）抛出——与真实执行失败无法区分，协调器也不会重驱。本改动后，回合在工具执行中获取挂卷时若遇到确定的 409 `workspace_busy` 拒绝，改为排队：以短轮询重试获取，仅以回合自身的取消与截止为界，持有者回合释放挂卷后继续执行。开始排队时打印一条 stderr 提示，便于运维观察等待中的回合。其余情形刻意保持不变：`workspace_unavailable` 拒绝与恢复路径获取仍以快速归类错误结束回合，占用存储之后的一切保持恢复阻断语义。issue 场景的复现测试作为回归钉桩保留在套件中，单元测试钉住排队/取消/歧义分支，设计文档的失败语义在中英双语中同步更新。

## 为什么需要

在此改动之前，同一 Workspace 上的第二个用户（或第二个标签页/agent）会直接丢失回合：客户端无法区分「忙，稍后重试」与真实失败。issue #13328 要求把终态失败这一形态变成有意识的选择——本 PR 采用 issue 的排队方案，使第二个回合在第一个之后完成而不是丢失。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

- 复现行为（修复前）：两个 Hosted Session 绑定一个挂卷，两个 prompt 均以 `202` 获准；第一个回合取得挂卷执行租约；第二个回合的首次获取被拒 `409 workspace_busy`，回合以 `turn_error`（code `hosted_turn_failed`）终态结算，日志为 `Hosted Harness turn … failed: Error: Runtime Broker returned HTTP 409 (workspace_busy)`。独立复现记录为 `{ completedTurns: 1, failedTurns: 1, busyEvidence: true, crossTalk: false }`。
- 期望行为（修复后）：第二个回合轮询获取，打印一次 `Hosted Harness turn … waits for the Workspace mount held by another Session.`，第一个回合结束后取得挂卷并以 `turn_complete` 结算；两个 Session 的工具各恰好执行一次，无跨 Session 文本泄漏。独立验证记录为败方以 `turn_complete` 结算、`failedTurns: 0`、全部正面性质保持，并附对抗探针：连续 5 次 busy 后释放按 250ms 节奏完成且提示恰好打印一次；排队中取消按中止原因拒绝且不释放任何资源；挂卷持续被占时持续轮询。
- 确认边界未移动：`workspace_unavailable` 与恢复/接续获取路径仍以归类错误快速拒绝（Session 可重试或 reload），歧义获取失败(如响应丢失)即使回合正被取消也保持恢复阻断。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A — 非 UI 改动。前后摘要与探针结果如上引自复现与验证报告；harness 级回归测试同时编码了两种形态。

### 测试环境

同上表：macOS ✅；Windows、Linux ⚠️ 未测。

### 运行环境（可选）

基于真实 HTTP 栈的 harness 级 vitest 套件(express 监听、本地 journal/资源存储、Broker 在其 HTTP 边界上 mock),源码与 `node dist/cli.js` 等价;`npm run build`、`npm run typecheck`、`npm run bundle` 全绿。完整打包栈 E2E runner 的 `--second-workspace-session` 模式不在仓库中、未运行；预计由 issue 作者重跑，届时摘要应翻转为 `{ completedTurns: 2, failedTurns: 0 }`。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：排队等待无内置上限——仅在挂卷释放、回合被取消或 prompt 截止触发时结束。这是刻意的排队语义；楔死的挂卷持有者仍属既有的运维恢复域。
- 未验证/范围外：上述打包栈 runner 模式；daemon 侧 workspace removal/agents 的 `workspace_busy` 路由(未改);MCP profile 会话开启时的 busy 处理(未改);跨 harness-session 套件抽取共享测试脚手架(已记为跟进项)。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明:无——唯一行为变化是被确定 `workspace_busy` 拒绝的回合现在排队而不是以错误结算;此前对该情形匹配 `hosted_turn_failed` 的客户端将改为看到回合保持活动随后完成。
- 设计文档已更新(双语同步):docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.md 与 docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.zh-CN.md。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #13328

body:
M3 had no explicit closure check for the remaining Test and Middleware reader boundaries. Add cross-consumer regressions proving that Graph and Plan Impact agree on supported root-route reachability, and document the shared readers and retained evidence policies in RFC 0032.

Nine integration cases cover literal/parameter shadowing, ALL-method precedence, conservative cross-module reachability, unmatched/dynamic requests, malformed TestApp source, absent/unreadable test directories, and registered/inline/unresolved middleware. Request files contain throwing top-level code to detect accidental execution. Static graph mode keeps Test identities and reports registered relations unavailable.

The existing readers already share discovery, request parsing and matching, so this PR changes tests and the RFC only. Plan's registrar authority and approval facts remain unchanged. The RFC records M3 completion within the supported source-reader scope and the generated-file-only boundary for M4.

Validation: clean full build, typecheck, lint, 175 related regression cases and all nine final boundary cases, dependency/core-first/docs audits, and git diff checks. Example apps pass (127 blog, 42 API, 35 agents), and the docs site passes (241 Vitest and 25 Bun cases).

The first full package run passed 11,264 cases but hit five 5-second timeouts and a subsequent dependent assertion failure in the existing publishing tests. All 16 publishing cases pass when rerun alone with the default timeout; no timeout settings or publishing code changed.

author: oskar-stachowski
body:
Daily demand history includes quantity revisions and publication times but lacks per-version quality flags. The branch now replays the pinned complete source under five durable pre-read reservations and exposes a private, context-bound version inventory. Only the exact latest observation supplies explicit quality evidence, usable from its own availability time; earlier versions remain unqualified.

The branch also includes frozen AI09 preparation, the compact TensorFlow development runner, bounded comparison storage, durable shared fit/outcome journals, chronological five-role key preparation, the physical label reader, and complete source-to-curated transform replay. The new version reader reuses one source replay, checks all version joins before the first public row, and releases its receipt only after immutable-parent/runtime checks and all audit completions.

Validation for this increment:
- 278 focused tests passed, including 52 new temporal-quality, inventory, lifetime, mutation, and audit-failure cases; no skips.
- Lint/format, Mypy across 358 files, documentation links, and all contract snapshots passed.
- Installed wheel has 283 byte-identical Python files; 46 consumer modules import from the installation, both v8 schemas match, and TensorFlow/Keras stay unimported. This is a static package proof, not native/wheel source-replay equivalence.
- Full Git and directory secret scans passed. Exact rule-scoped path/digest exceptions cover public membership hashes in concurrent AI08 Git history; negative controls still detect other keys in those files and the same hashes elsewhere.
- Parent commit 3b1ee7e1b11069400364d0497eb402c4687e0570 has successful Required CI178. This head requires its own Required CI; a current full local make ci-local run is not claimed.

Remaining acceptance: complete physical five-role feature/partition-to-outcome binding and export, frozen training/candidate artifacts and audited fits, source 1.1 integration, and the independent campaign. Measured native/wheel resource acceptance is blocked before execution because free disk is about 34 GiB below the preserved 50 GiB reserve. No larger profile was started and no guard was lowered.

The shared project journal remains byte-identical: four preparation plans, zero new project read reservations, and 64 remaining reads. This increment uses previously public smoke and controlled synthetic cases only. No new project-data fit, portfolio final-test opening, or promotion occurred. AI07/08 worktrees and processes were not modified. AI09 remains not_ready.

author: station-automation[bot]
body:
## User outcome

For OpenCode, the composer now knows whether the selected model can read images, instead of only that OpenCode as an engine accepts them. OpenCode answers "yes" for the engine and then swaps an image for an error text when the model lacks image input. Before this change, every OpenCode model got a "can't confirm this model can read them" note.

- **A model that reads images** shows no note.
- **A model that can't read images** refuses images before Send, naming the model.
- **A model OpenCode did not list, or a listing that failed or hasn't been read yet,** keeps the existing note. An unknown answer is never treated as "no".

Follow-up to #3108, where per-model image support for OpenCode was a NOT_VERIFIED row.

## Issue and closure condition

- Issue: none filed; follow-up recorded in #3108.
- Closure condition satisfied by this PR: the three cases above, covered by tests that reach the server listing and the composer's resolution.
- Cause classification: inherited gap. ACP reports image support per engine, not per model.

## Documentation impact

- Impact/catch-up report: `docs/guides/acp.md` and `docs/design/chat-composer.md` now describe the per-model source and the three outcomes. Reviews were recorded on the branch and carried through the path-only ledger migration (#3227); `docs:truth:gate` passes.
- Affected public docs and generated sources: the two documents above and `docs/learn/review-ledger/`.
- Architecture or behavior changes:
  - Contracts (changeset `opencode-model-image-input`, minor): optional `ModelOptionCapabilities.imageInput`.
  - New `src-server/services/acp/opencode-model-capabilities.ts`. After a successful ACP handshake it reads `opencode models --verbose` off the request path, using:
    - the connection's configured binary, with argv only and no shell;
    - an 8s timeout and a 2 MB output cap;
    - an owned child, so the whole process group is killed on timeout;
    - a per-connection cache, cleared on reconnect or removal and ignored when launch settings change;
    - the last good answer, kept when a refresh fails.
  - The runtime catalog publishes `capabilities.imageInput` per model.
  - `catalogModelImageSupport` in `src-ui/src/utils/execution.ts`: the engine's own per-model answer outranks the Bedrock-only catalog.
- Intentional NOT_VERIFIED platform/UI claims: see below.

## Evidence

### Exact commands and receipts

- **Original review.** The branch was written on the #3108 branch and independently reviewed, with a security focus on the spawned process: SHIP. That round's fixes were fault-injected by an independent verifier:
  - keep the last good answer;
  - own the listing process;
  - recheck launch settings on read.
- **Rebuild on `main`.** Rebuilt by cherry-picking its source commits unchanged, with no conflicts, then merged with current `main`.
- **`npm run test:focused`.** On the three new test files, 47 passed on the rebuilt branch and again after the merge:
  - `opencode-model-capabilities.test.ts`, with a fixture captured from real `opencode models --verbose` output;
  - `opencode-catalog-no-spawn.test.ts`;
  - `execution.catalogImageSupport.test.ts`.
- **Gates.** `npm run docs:truth:gate` passes. The pre-push gates ran on the pushed head, including the transfer gate, since `packages/contracts/src/tool.ts` changed.

### NOT_VERIFIED

| Claim or surface | Owner | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A real OpenCode install on a device | this PR | Exercised against a fixture captured from real output, not a live engine in this round. |
| Composer render of the per-model refusal | this PR | Covered by the resolution tests; not rendered in a browser in this round. |
| Per-file wall cost of the new tests | this PR | Measured together (47 tests), on a loaded host. |

## Personal or manual verification

I rebuilt the branch on `main`, checked that `main`'s later edits to `chat-composer.md` (#3126, #3144) are in other sections, and ran the suites and gate above.

### New code-health findings

None known; CI's code-health report is the receipt.

## Risk and rollback

- Risks: a child process per OpenCode connection after each handshake. It is bounded by the timeout, the output cap and process-group ownership, and runs off the request path.
- Rollback: revert the squash commit; the contract field is optional.

## AI-assisted work

- AI tool or tools used: Claude Code, with independent implementation, review and verification subagents.
- Material areas affected by AI-assisted work: all of the above.
- Personal inspection performed: as above.

author: barakserv2-cmd
body:
## Why
Saar asked for the arrival companion to send from גובגט's number. That's the official Meta / 360dialog number that interview reminders already go out from (`officialReminderAccount`). On this channel, free text only goes through within 24h of the candidate's last message. Outside that window, only a template approved by Meta goes through.

## What
- **Sending:** each touch first tries the full free-text message from the official number. If the 24h window is closed, it sends the matching approved template instead. The text that was actually sent is what gets saved in the chat. If no official number is configured, it falls back to the business number, same as before.
- **Replies:** replies to גובגט's number never reach the WhatsApp webhooks, because גובגט forwards them through `/api/bridge/from-machine`. That route now runs `applyArrivalSignals` on newly saved user messages only, so if the same payload is sent again it won't raise the flag a second time. `appendBridgeMessages` accepts an optional collector for the messages it actually saved, and its existing behaviour is unchanged.

## Templates to create and approve at 360dialog (he, Utility)
| name | body |
|---|---|
| `arrival_confirm` | היי {{1}}, כאן ברק שירותים. הראיון שלך באילת נקבע {{2}}. מגיע/ה לבד או עם חבר/ה? אם משהו משתנה, אפשר לכתוב לנו כאן. |
| `arrival_travel_check` | היי {{1}}, עוד יומיים הראיון שלך באילת. כבר יש כרטיס לאוטובוס? באיזו שעה יוצאים? אם צריך עזרה לפני הנסיעה, אפשר לכתוב לנו כאן. |
| `arrival_day_of` | בוקר טוב {{1}}, היום הראיון שלך באילת. בהצלחה! אם משהו השתנה בדרך, אפשר לכתוב לנו כאן. |
| `arrival_first_day` | היי {{1}}, כאן ברק שירותים. איך היה היום הראשון ב{{2}}? הכל בסדר עם המגורים והמשמרות? אם משהו לא מסתדר, כתבו לנו ונטפל בזה מהר. |

Until these are approved, any touch sent outside the 24h window fails and is recorded with Meta's error. The companion stays off unless `ARRIVAL_COMPANION_MODE` or `ARRIVAL_COMPANION_TEST_PHONES` is set.

## Verification
- `tsc` ✅, `vitest` 450/450 ✅ (new tests: template/param consistency, no empty params, the bridge collector ignores resent payloads), `next build` ✅, eslint 0 errors.
- Not tested against Meta or 360dialog from this environment.

author: hsoliwal
body:
## Purpose

Refresh the A3 complete-denominator packet from PR #83 onto the current M3JDK21 stack without rebasing or rewriting history.

This PR is intentionally stacked on the refreshed SourceFile-preserving OpenRewrite repair (#90).

## Denominator authority

A3 now plans the complete released evidence universe:

- **85 released JEP rows** from the merged release-authority catalogue;
- **14,948 released OpenJDK commits** across JDK 22..27 GA intervals;
- manually inspected JBS seed rows;
- community/capability rows;
- challenge/search taxonomy rows.

The exact released commit counts remain:

- JDK 22: 2,384
- JDK 23: 2,355
- JDK 24: 2,562
- JDK 25: 2,678
- JDK 26: 2,611
- JDK 27: 2,358
- total: 14,948

## Recipe first

Named recipe:

`com.m3.a3.CompleteDenominator`

Owner:

`com.m3.rewrite.a3.M3A3CompleteDenominatorRecipe`

Four exact A3 targets remain source-sealed:

- `m3/tooling/a3/pom.xml`
- `A3.java`
- `A3Plan.java`
- `A3PlanTest.java`

Current master still matched every sealed preimage byte-for-byte before replay.

## A3 plan families

A3 keeps evidence families distinct:

- `JEP`
- `JBS`
- `UPSTREAM`
- `CAP`
- `ALGO`

The exact upstream commit SHA is the identity for `UPSTREAM` rows.

## Challenge/search taxonomy

Adds `m3/backports/CHALLENGE_SEARCH_TAXONOMY.tsv`.

Serial evidence order is mechanically locked:

`LeetCode -> HackerRank -> GeeksForGeeks`

Challenge sites remain taxonomy/reference evidence only and carry no source-copy authority.

Implementation mechanics remain existing JDK/M3 owners or separately license-pinned donors such as OpenJDK, Apache Lucene and RE2J.

## Compatibility authority

A3 planning does **not** declare all 14,948 commits compatible.

It preserves the original inventory disposition and derives only an absorption lane. Compatibility still requires:

`dependency closure -> recipe/patch -> diff -> lint -> compile -> jtreg -> runtime/JNI/HotSpot parity -> benchmark when claimed -> serial promotion`

## CI consistency

The refreshed A3 workflow now requires:

- exactly **85 JEP rows**;
- exactly **14,948 UPSTREAM rows**;
- challenge review-order/source-copy invariants;
- recipe fixed point;
- Java 21 build of the tooling closure.

## Refresh semantics

The old #83 branch was based on the already-merged #80 branch and became 401 commits behind master. This refreshed stack:

1. recreates the prerequisite #90 repair on current master;
2. replays the unchanged source-sealed A3 packet on top;
3. merges only the A3-specific README additions into newer backport documentation;

author: jasagiri
body:
## Summary

Makes `tinylm.c` build and run on macOS / Apple Silicon (tested on an M2). Windows/x86 behaviour is unchanged.

- Win32-only headers and calls are now behind `_WIN32`, with POSIX equivalents elsewhere:
  - `direct.h` / `_mkdir` → `mkdir`
  - `_fseeki64` / `_ftelli64` → `fseeko` / `ftello`
  - `GetModuleFileNameA` → `_NSGetExecutablePath` (macOS) or `/proc/self/exe`
  - `K32GetProcessMemoryInfo` → `getrusage`
  - the `\` in model paths → `/`
- `immintrin.h` is only included on x86.
- arm64 gets NEON versions of `dot_i8_32`, `qdot_row` and `q4dot_row`. They use `sdot` when the CPU has dot-product (`__ARM_FEATURE_DOTPROD`) and widening multiply-accumulate otherwise.
- There is a portable scalar fallback for any other CPU. Building with `-DTINYLM_NO_SIMD` forces it.
- The decode pool's spin uses `yield` on arm64. `set_ftz` sets `FPCR.FZ` on arm64.
- README: macOS build commands, with and without Homebrew `libomp`.

## Testing

- **macOS 15 / M2, Apple clang 17**
  - `cc -O3 -mcpu=native -ffast-math` builds, with and without `-Xpreprocessor -fopenmp -lomp`.
  - `selftest` passes. `bench m3` runs and reports peak RAM.
  - `LS2.5-108M-A17M-Base-Q4_K_M.gguf` loads and generates.
- **Kernel test** (2,000 random rows of 24 blocks, plus an extreme-value case)
  - `dot_i8_32` must equal the scalar integer dot exactly. `qdot_row` and `q4dot_row` (with `g_q4=1`) must match a double-precision reference to 1e-5 relative.
  - Passes for:
    - arm64 NEON with `sdot`
    - arm64 NEON without `sdot` (`-march=armv8-a`)
    - x86-64 AVX2 under Rosetta 2
    - the scalar fallback on arm64 and on x86-64
- **`nll`** (16 windows × 256 tokens of wikitext-2 test, LS2.5 Base)
  - arm64 build: mean NLL 4.13403.
  - x86-64 AVX2 build under Rosetta: 4.13409.
- **Greedy `gen`** (4 prompts × 64 tokens)
  - For 2 prompts the arm64 output matches the x86 AVX2 output.
  - For the other 2, the outputs part after a few dozen tokens. The x86 AVX2 build alone also gives different text with and without `TINYLM_EXACT_GEMV=1` on those prompts, so this is float summation order on near-ties, not the port.
- **Windows (MinGW cross-compile)**
  - Built `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc 14` with the CI flags, minus `-fopenmp`: Homebrew's mingw has no libgomp.
  - Built before and after this change: same size, same DLL imports.
  - Disassembly with RIP-relative offsets normalized differs only in `model_path` (the `exe_dir` change), NOP padding and one switch-table label.
- **Not tested:** Linux (the `/proc/self/exe` and KiB `ru_maxrss` branches compile only on macOS here), and Windows on arm64.

The one compiler warning left (`blob=r.p` discards `const`) is in the existing code and appears on the Windows build too. I left it alone to keep this PR to portability only.

Correzioni preventive emerse dal beta test sui giorni 14-18 settembre (5 giorni, 10 annunci, più una ripetizione del 15/09).

## 1. Falso "nessun annuncio" (grave)
Il primo controllo del **15/09** ha registrato `success`, copertura completa e 0 annunci: la pagina 1 conteneva solo annunci più vecchi del 15/09, cioè il contenuto che normalmente è a pagina 2 (pochi minuti prima, la pagina 1 arrivava fino al 03/10). Ripetuto subito dopo, ha trovato l'annuncio 4630714 (Alessandria).

Dato che la ricerca si ferma alla prima pagina "tutta più vecchia", una pagina 1 sbagliata produce un elenco vuoto spacciato per completo. Ora:
- la **pagina 1 viene ricaricata** (fino a 2 volte, 3 s di attesa) se contiene solo annunci più vecchi della data cercata o se il suo annuncio più recente è più vecchio di quello visto nel controllo precedente (`coverage.site_newest_date` del `latest.json` precedente);
- se l'anomalia rispetto al controllo precedente persiste → avviso `first_page_older_than_previous_run`, stato `partial`;
- se le date non sono in ordine decrescente (nella pagina o tra pagine) → avviso `result_order_unexpected`, stato `partial`;
- `coverage.pages` registra per ogni pagina numero di annunci, data più recente/più vecchia, annunci senza data e ordine; il log riporta una riga per pagina.

Nel caso quotidiano senza annunci nuovi la pagina 1 è legittimamente "tutta più vecchia": viene ricaricata due volte (circa 10 s in più) ma resta `success`.

author: tezerports-dot
body:
Before: supervisors could not see how their members were doing. Nothing recorded when a member was online, nobody was told about an idle member, members saw nothing about their team, and a supervisor had no part in their member's disputes.

After: each member's Online switch is logged. Once a day, a member whose completed orders AND online time are both more than 25% below the team average (an admin setting) is flagged to the supervisor and the admin; the flag acts on nothing. A supervisor sees each member's activity today and over 7 days, a member's log (orders with no player detail, and their Online stretches), and the disputes on their teams, where they can write to the dispute manager. A member sees the team's totals and their own figures, never a teammate's row. The admin sees every flag and can edit the threshold.

There is no commission-farming flag. 2f built one; Vikram removed it on 2026-10-04 because the 90:10 deposit/reserve split and the 1% winnings fee already make farming lose money (in a ₹100 against ₹100 bet the winner gets 200 and pays 2, which is 1% from each side).

**How**
- `merchant_online_sessions` is written only by triggers on `merchants.is_online`: one open stretch per member, closed once, never edited, and switching off can no longer fail.
- `teamOversight.evaluateRedFlags` is the one writer of `team_red_flags`. Each IST day is claimed in the flags' own transaction (`team_red_flag_days`), and the hourly cron `team-red-flags` catches up the last 3 days. Completions are counted by `order_states.completed_at`, so sells settled by the hold sweep count.
- Supervisor reads are scoped to their own teams in the WHERE (trap 16). Only APPROVED members' logs open, and online time counts from when they joined. Order rows go through `SUPERVISOR_ORDER_FIELDS`, and free text through `hideForSupervisor` (mobiles, UPI handles, numbers of 9+ digits).
- A supervisor's dispute message has one path, `postSupervisorMessage`. Its INSERT checks DISPUTED, own team and a 50-message cap, under a share lock on the order (S6). A mobile in the message is refused by the row. The supervisor reads only their own, their member's and the dispute manager's messages.
- One mobile-number rule, held to one list in JS and SQL (`mobileInText.js`, `bb_text_has_a_mobile`, `mobileInTextPg`): any script's digits, up to two separators, 0/91/+91/091/0091. Merchant usernames and team names may not carry one.

**Security review**
- An independent review pass of the build found 8 issues, none high, all fixed in `e6006c0`: UPI handles, UTRs and account numbers reaching a supervisor in text; the player's messages and staff notices in the supervisor's thread; mobile spellings the rule missed (Indian-script digits, two separators, 091); mobiles in usernames and team names; the dispute post's checks not in one locked statement and uncapped; switching Online off able to fail; a merely proposed member's log opening; a team of two showing its totals.
- Removing the farming flag (`432b573`) was self-reviewed. It only removes surface: the admin card that listed player ids is gone, and each supervisor still sees only their own teams' flags (new mutation M423).
- No mobile number is exposed anywhere. The audit gate's exception list is unchanged (braces only).

**Verification (local, PostgreSQL 16)**
| What | Result |
|---|---|
| `test:unit` | 892/892 |
| `test:pg` | 1,582/1,582 (129 files) |
| admin panel | build OK, 176/176 |
| merchant panel | build OK, 102/102 |
| Gates | all 17 plus `audit:map -- --check` exit 0; `check:no-mongo`: "All checks report zero" |
| Mutations | 28 on the files and tests this change touched, all KILLED (M392–M393, M397–M400, M402–M423); earlier 72/72 on the build and fixes |

Not covered: `test:e2e` and the browser tiers were not run (they need a running server; planned for 2g). Not independently reviewed by a human.

- INSTRUMENT: route.test.ts (real handler; principal, access check and module mocked, module returning a deliberately WIDER row with staff fields) and athleteInjuries.pg.test.ts (real listFamilyInjuries against embedded Postgres).
- SUBJECT: 18fc61a109bc05f99a01f91c92c2bfc07535cf01 (branch lane/injury-record-c; f1cbee97cb1cbb7fa8bad2f763770a805c16c5a0 after it changes only the guardian page header copy and its test).

author: 33tu
body:
Alternating ordinary filters with back-buffer blend passes repeatedly removes a listener from Pixi's shared `Texture.EMPTY.source`. Cached graphics texture groups fill unused slots with that same source, so each removal scans a list that grows with previously prepared graphics.

Give each filter system a private empty back texture. Restore the original filter data after applying, including on exceptions, and release the private texture and its bindings when the system is destroyed. Real back-buffer textures remain unchanged.

Validation:
- `pnpm check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` pass: 394 unit tests and 88/88 player reference cases.
- Regression test covers alternating empty/real back textures, separate filter systems, exceptions, and destruction.
- Radeon RX 7900 XTX / ANGLE Vulkan benchmark: 64 alternating layer/overlay objects, 2,000 cached texture groups (62,001 shared-empty listeners), 20 warmup and 80 measured renders per variant. Median CPU render submission falls from 5.6 ms to 0.2 ms in both baseline/fixed/fixed/baseline comparisons; full-frame pixel readbacks are identical. With no accumulated groups both variants take 0.2 ms. This measures the isolated bottleneck, not end-to-end application performance.

The first full suite attempt hit a browser startup failure while the benchmark was also running. The affected case passed independently and the complete suite passed on rerun without concurrent benchmarking.

## 揺れの原因
- 同じビルド・同じ確認用インスタンスで `pc-1920x1080/my-archive-list.png` だけを新しいブラウザで 15 回撮ると、結果が 2〜3 通りに分かれた。
  - 差は 42 ピクセル（検索欄の右下・「検索」「条件をクリア」ボタン・「カード」ボタン・検索の枠と表の枠の左の角）か、6 ピクセル（検索の枠の右上の角）。#791・#793 で見た 6・48 ピクセルと同じ場所。
  - 違う画素は色の値が **1 だけ** 違う（例 243 と 244）。角のぼかし（アンチエイリアス）の画素だけが揺れている。
- 撮るたびに、入力欄・ボタン・選択欄の位置と大きさ（`getBoundingClientRect`）を小数点以下 4 桁まで出したが、毎回同じだった → レイアウトの揺れではない。
- `--disable-gpu` で起動しても同じように揺れた → GPU の描画の揺れでもない。
- 原因は Chromium の **partial raster**（すでに描いたタイルのうち、変わった範囲だけを描き直す仕組み）。一覧の画面は、検索欄の選択肢・件数・表が別々の通信で後から埋まるので、書き換えが何度も起きる。角の丸い枠を描き直す範囲で切り取って描くと、境目の画素のアンチエイリアスが全体を描いたときと 1 だけ違う値になる。どの範囲がいつ描き直されるかは通信と描画の間合いで毎回変わるので、結果が揺れていた。

## 止め方
- `shoot.cjs` で Chromium を `--disable-partial-raster` 付きで起動する（`CHROMIUM_ARGS`。iPhone を Chromium で撮るときも同じブラウザなので効く。WebKit には渡さない）。毎回タイル全体を描くので、同じ画面なら同じ画素になる。
- しきい値も、画像の一部を隠すことも使っていない。画面の CSS・HTML・JS は変えていない。
- 理由は `shoot.cjs` の `CHROMIUM_ARGS` のコメントに書いた。

## 注意（判断した点）
- この引数を付けると、角の画素が引数なしで撮った画像とも少し違う（一覧の画面で 60 ピクセル）。前後を比べるときは、両方をこの PR 以降の道具で撮る必要がある。PR のベースブランチがこの PR より前だと引数なしで撮られるので、このことを `CHROMIUM_ARGS` のコメントに書いた（`PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION` を上げたときと同じ扱い）。
- 本物のブラウザ（partial raster が有効）の描き方とは角の 1 段階の色だけ違うが、変更の前後を比べる目的には影響しない。

## 実行した確認
- 原因の切り分け（同じインスタンス、一覧の画面だけを毎回新しいブラウザで撮る）
  - 引数なし: 15 回中 5 回が 1 回目と 42 ピクセル違う
  - `--disable-gpu`: 15 回中 4 回が 42 ピクセル、1 回が 6 ピクセル違う
  - `--disable-partial-raster`: **20 回すべて 1 回目と差 0**
- 完了条件: 同じビルド・同じ確認用インスタンスで `UI_SNAPSHOT_IPHONE_ENGINE=chromium bin/ui-snapshot.sh shoot` を 5 回 → どの 2 回を比べても（10 組）`bin/ui-snapshot.sh diff` は「PC の画像 28 枚はすべて同じです」で終了コード 0。iPhone（Chromium）の 42 枚も 10 組すべて差 0。
- 確認用インスタンスを止めて `./gradlew clean build javadoc` → 起動し直した後に撮った画像も、その前に撮った画像と PC・iPhone とも差 0。
- 修正前の確認: 修正前の道具で 3 回撮った分は、たまたま 3 回とも差 0（揺れは 3〜4 回に 1 回ほど）。そのため上の 1 画面だけの繰り返しで切り分けた。
- AGENTS.md「終わったら」の共通確認
  - `./gradlew clean build javadoc`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL、コンパイル・javadoc の警告なし
  - `npx -y -p typescript tsc -p src/main/resources/static/jsconfig.json --noEmit`: エラー 0
  - `node --test src/test/js/*.test.cjs`: 42 件すべて成功
  - `SANDBOX_PORT=18382 bin/sandbox.sh start`（ほかの作業ツリーの 18180 と重ならないように）→ `bin/api.sh POST /api/monitor/check`: 応答あり（監視を止めた起動なので「今すぐチェックは行いません」・終了コード 22。想定どおり）、`bin/sandbox.sh cli channel list`: 動いた → `bin/sandbox.sh stop`
- WebKit はこの端末では起動できない（Smart App Control）ので、iPhone を WebKit で撮ったときの揺れは確かめていない。

body:
## Expected

When a model endpoint returns a non-permanent 401/403, Gym should preserve the provider's error body, fail that request once, and allow later requests on the same client.

## Actual

The auth classifier introduced in #3571 consumes the response stream and returns it. Downstream error handling reads EOF, so `ClientResponseError.response_content` becomes empty and provider details such as model-access denial are lost.

## Fix

Pass the already-read body to the existing `raise_for_status` helper in the auth branch. Permanent-key detection and retry policies stay unchanged. Replace the repeatable-read mock with a real HTTP regression covering 401/403, a 400 control, and successful recovery on the same client.

Validation: real-HTTP regression, 386 adjacent tests, core/sandbox suites (95.18% coverage), all-file pre-commit, and diff checks passed. Model rollouts are N/A for this shared error-propagation fix.

author: danielhanchen
body:
## Problem

On an AMD ROCm GPU, asking Studio for `attention_backend: "flash"` (or `"flash2"`) silently runs native SDPA. `select_attention_backend` treats every `flash*` alias as NVIDIA-only (`if not _is_cuda_nvidia(target): return None`), so only `aiter` is honored on ROCm.

DAO-AILab flash-attention has a ROCm build: Composable Kernel by default, or a Triton backend with `FLASH_ATTENTION_TRITON_AMD_ENABLE=TRUE`. diffusers' `flash` backend calls the same `flash_attn_func`. AMD's ROCm blog ("ComfyUI flash-attention backends") measures, on Strix Halo (gfx1151) for Wan2.2, the DAO CK build at +43% / +50% and the DAO Triton build at +36% / +47% throughput over AOTriton SDPA (T2V / I2V). A ROCm user who has built it cannot select it today.

There is also a trap on the install side: `_INSTALLABLE_BACKENDS` maps `flash` to the PyPI `flash-attn` package, which is the NVIDIA CUDA build. If the selection gate were simply opened, the on-demand installer would try to put that wheel next to a ROCm torch.

## Change

All in `diffusion_attention.py`:

- **When explicit `flash` is honored on ROCm:** `flash` / `flash2` on a ROCm target (CUDA device API, ROCm torch) is honored only when `flash_attn` imports and a per-device check passes.
  - The check is one `flash_attn_func` call on a small random (1, 128, 2, 64) input at the load dtype (bf16 when the load is not half precision). It must not raise and must be within 2e-2 max abs error of an fp32 reference attention.
  - The answer is cached per (device index, dtype). An unaskable check (OOM, device error) falls back to native and is retried on the next load.
  - Otherwise the result is `None` (native SDPA), exactly as before.
- **Unchanged backends:** `flash3`, `flash4`, `sage`, `cudnn` and `xformers` stay NVIDIA-only.
- **`auto` on ROCm:** unchanged (native). A module constant `ROCM_AUTO_FLASH = False` gates the one line that would let `auto` pick verified ROCm flash-attn under a speed profile. The runner numbers below do not justify turning it on.
- **Installer:** never pip installs `flash-attn` on a ROCm torch. It logs that the PyPI wheel is the CUDA build and names the DAO-AILab ROCm build (or `aiter`) instead. A missing `flash_attn` on an explicit ROCm request logs the same hint once per process.
- **NVIDIA:** every path returns what it returned before, and the new check never runs there.

## Results

Real AMD hardware: the Strix Halo CI runners, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), Linux. Studio is installed by `install.sh --local` (torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0). DAO-AILab flash-attention 2.8.4 is the Triton AMD backend (the CK build was not tried). Base (main) and head (main + this change) run in the same job, on the same runner, with the same prompts and seeds, at ComfyUI's template operating points.

Engagement, from a profiled 2-step render per cell:

- **Main drops the request:** `flash_attn_func` is called 0 times; native SDPA (AOTriton) runs.
- **This branch engages it:** Triton `attn_fwd` kernels run.

  | model | `flash_attn_func` calls | of all attention calls |
  |---|---|---|
  | FLUX.2-klein-4B | 50 | 87 |
  | FLUX.1-schnell | 114 | 127 |
  | Wan2.2-TI2V-5B | 240 | 408 |
  | Qwen-Image-2.1 | 32 | 133 |

  The rest, mostly text encoder and masked calls, stay on SDPA.
- **The check passes on gfx1151,** and diffusers accepts the ROCm build.

Speed on this branch, `attention_backend="flash"` vs default (native SDPA, AOTriton), seconds:

| model, size, steps | default s/out (s/step) | flash s/out (s/step) | per step | LPIPS vs default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLUX.2-klein-4B, 1024x1024, 4 | 8.71 (1.88) | 8.04 (1.71) | -9% | 0.010 |
| FLUX.1-schnell, 1024x1024, 4 | 18.87 (4.41) | 17.40 (4.03) | -9% | 0.039 |
| Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, 1280x704x21, 20 | 586.7 (7.75) | 567.1 (6.83) | -12% | 0.036 |
| Qwen-Image-2.1, 1024x1024, 25 | 98.7 (3.87) | 101.3 (3.99) | +3% | 0.001 |
| SDXL, 1024x1024, 25 | 21.66 (0.82) | 21.70 (0.82) | 0% | 0.000 |

- **SDXL:** the UNet does not route through the diffusers attention dispatcher, so nothing changes.
- **Qwen-Image-2.1:** most of its calls keep SDPA, so the change is within noise.
- **Attention alone, measured in the same job:**

  | kernel | 4096 tokens | 16384 tokens |
  |---|---|---|
  | AOTriton SDPA flash | 11.8 ms | 178 ms |
  | DAO flash-attn, Triton | 7.9 ms | 117 ms |

  Measured as one call, bf16, 24 heads of 128. Both are within 0.0017 max abs error of an fp32 reference. `TORCH_ROCM_FA_PREFER_CK=1` changes nothing (this torch has no CK SDPA kernels for gfx1151).
- **Without the AOTriton opt-in:** in a process where `TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL` is not set, native SDPA falls to the math backend and this option matters much more: FLUX.2-klein 28.2 -> 8.2 s, Z-Image-Turbo 125.1 -> 47.0 s. The opt-in itself is a separate PR.

## Tests

New `tests/test_diffusion_attention_rocm_flash.py` (CPU only, hermetic):

- **ROCm, passing check:** with `flash_attn` and a passing check, `flash`, `flash2` and `FLASH` return `flash`; the check is cached per (device, dtype).
- **ROCm, fallbacks:** without `flash_attn`, with a failing check, or with an unaskable check, the result is native (the unaskable case is not cached).
- **ROCm, unchanged paths:**
  - `auto` stays native with and without a speed profile.
  - `flash3` / `flash4` / `sage` / `cudnn` / `xformers` stay dropped.
  - Non-CUDA devices stay native.
- **NVIDIA:** every alias, with and without a speed profile, matches a frozen table of main's results, and the ROCm check is asserted never to run.
- **Installer:** on a ROCm torch `flash` installs nothing and records no attempt; on a CUDA torch it still installs `flash-attn`.
- **The check itself,** run on CPU against a fake `flash_attn_func`: a correct kernel passes, an output off by 0.1 fails, and a raising kernel fails, for bf16 / fp16 / fp32 loads.

Against main the same file gives 12 failed, 25 passed (the NVIDIA table and the unchanged paths pass on both); on this branch, 37 passed. The related suites (`test_diffusion_attention*.py`, `test_xformers_stub_diffusion_parity.py`, `test_video_backend.py`) pass: 608 passed, 2 skipped.

## Not covered

- **CK build:** the DAO-AILab CK flash-attention build was not built or measured; only the Triton AMD backend was.
- **Other AMD hardware:** only gfx1151 on Linux. Windows ROCm, RDNA3 discrete, RDNA4 and Instinct were not run.
- **Noise:** one or two renders per cell and no repeated-baseline run, so per-image differences under about 5% are within noise. The per-step deltas above come from a long-minus-short render pair on the same prompt.
- **`auto` stays native on ROCm:** the gain over AOTriton (9 to 12% per step on the DiTs that route through the dispatcher) is not large enough, or general enough, to change the default.

author: blairham
body:
Part of #5712.

Measured 2026-10-03 with `v1=é`, `v2=$'a\tbé'` and the stray `v3=$'\303'`, over `set` and `typeset -p`/`declare -p`:

| | `LC_ALL=C` | `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bash 5.3.20 | `v1=$'\303\251'` | `v1=é` |
| ksh93u+ | `v1=$'\xc3\xa9'` | `v1=é`, `$'a\tb\u[e9]'` |
| zsh 5.9.2 | `v1=é` | `v1=é` |

Before this change the engine listed the character in every locale. That was a stated choice, made because the character is what a terminal shows. It is still the answer in a UTF-8 locale. It is also the answer with no locale set when the dialect reads an unset locale as Unicode, which is bash's reading (`UnsetLocaleIsUnicodeAware`). A new axis, `ListedNonAsciiFollowsTheLocale` (bash and ksh Yes, others No), switches to the byte reading where the locale has no characters above ASCII. It is asked only of a value that contains such a byte. Real ksh93 run under `env -i` also spells the bytes out, which matches ksh reading an unset locale as C.

The existing ksh tests that pinned the character reading (`dialect/ksh/listednonascii_test.go`) were measured under `en_US.UTF-8`, and they now run under that locale explicitly. The comments in the bash preset and in `aliasquote.go` that described the old choice are updated.

Fixes `set/listed-value-with-a-byte-above-ascii` for bash and ksh: `oracle -recorded` gives 1/1 each. Across 48 corpus rows with non-ASCII bytes, no bash, ksh or zsh row fails anew. New tests in `dialect/bash` and `dialect/ksh` fail with the axis flipped.

Still different under `C` and outside this row's scope: `printf %q` and `${v@Q}` in bash, which have their own quoting path.

Effect 4.0 導入の3本目（chronoscroll #40・somewhere-now #59 に続く）。

本番の `daily-digest` は直近7回中2回 500 で落ちていたが、ログにはスタックしか残らず、どの段階で何が起きたか読めなかった。

- Supabase の各段階（`load_sources` / `save_raw` / `load_candidates` / `save_articles` / `save_digest` / `mark_processed`）の失敗を `DigestStepError` にし、段階名と PostgREST の code をメッセージに載せる。文字列化は既存の `describeError` を再利用
- Gemini は `GeminiError`（`filter` / `summarize`）。再試行は従来どおり 3 回・1s→2s 待ち。最後の失敗後に 4s 待っていた無駄をなくす
- RSS は `Effect.forEach` で並列取得。1 本の失敗は `error` 付きの結果にして全体を止めない（従来どおり。エラー文字列も同じ形）
- route は失敗の message を 1 行目に出す（`[cron] daily-digest failed: digest step save_raw failed: ... (code=57014)` の形）
- Gemini とフィード取得を `Context.Reference` にし、node:test で待ち時間を `TestClock` で検証（13 件追加）

## 検証
- `tsc` / `npm run lint`（既存の warning 1 件のみ）/ `test:lib` 33 件 / `test:coverage` 56 件 / `next build` / `opennextjs-cloudflare build`
- Worker バンドル gzip 2,164 → 2,211 KiB（+47 KiB・無料枠 3,072 KiB）
- 本番 Supabase への書き込みを伴うため、ローカルでの実行はしていない。マージ後の最初の cron（JST 06:00）で確認する

## 概要

利用先(CivilizationEvolutionSimulator)で PR #28 の版を試したところ、`dispatch-prompt-gen.ps1` が成功しても `exit 0` を呼ばないため、`$LASTEXITCODE` が空のまま残る問題が見つかりました。その修正です。

PowerShell のセッション内で `& .agents/workflow/scripts/<名前>.ps1` と直接呼ぶと、スクリプトが `exit` で終わらない限り `$LASTEXITCODE` は更新されません。そのため、直前の値や空のまま残り、skill の手順(「exit code で分岐する」)どおりに判定できません。

## 変更内容

- `dispatch-prompt-gen.ps1` / `state-sync.ps1` / `workflow-archive.ps1`: 末尾に `exit 0` を追加
- `dispatch-run.ps1`: 正常終了時は `exit 0`、ラッパー自体が異常終了した場合(crashed)は `exit 1` を返す。子の終了コードは、これまでどおり done マーカーに記録する
- `tests/test-exitcode.ps1`(新規)
  - 静的検査: 直接実行するスクリプト(dot-source される `tasklib.ps1` 以外)の最終行が `exit` になっているか
  - セッション内で `&` 呼び出しし、直前の `$LASTEXITCODE` を 99 にしておいて、成功後に 0 になるか
- README に exit code の扱いを追記

PR #28 とは独立しています(main から分岐)。ローカルで #28 のブランチと試しにマージしても衝突せず、`task-state.ps1` を含めて静的検査が通ることを確認しました。

## テスト計画

- [x] 修正前に `test-exitcode.ps1` が失敗し、`dispatch-prompt-gen` / `state-sync` で `$LASTEXITCODE` が 99 のまま残ることを確認(RED)

- [x] `tests/test-*.sh` 全5スイートが全件パス(sh 版は変更なし)
- [x] PR #28 のブランチと試しにマージしても衝突せず、`test-exitcode.ps1` がパス
- [ ] 利用先で、PowerShell セッション内から `dispatch-prompt-gen.ps1` を呼んだあとに `$LASTEXITCODE` が 0 になることを確認する
