author: dreampiler
body:
## Problem

Every source event the bounded task-status projector handles reloaded the task's launch queue. The wired loader reads the task row **and** the install-wide admitted-session population through `orchestratorSvc.CurrentSessionCeilingObservation` -> `ListAdmittedSessionIDs`.

`message.updated` is published once per tool-call status update (`task/service.UpdateToolCallMessageWithCreate`), so a single agent turn with hundreds of tool updates caused hundreds of task-row reads plus hundreds of full admitted-session scans, and almost all of them persisted nothing.

## Change

`Projector.handleEvent` now refreshes the launch queue only from sources that can change it:

- `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.state_changed` — a ceiling deferral is written on the task row and every such write publishes a task event (`orchestrator/ceiling_defer.go`).
- `task.session.state_changed` — the displayed capacity moves only when a session enters or leaves the admitted population; a release drains deferred launches and republishes the task row.
- `message.queue.status_changed` — keeps the existing missing-task deletion handling on the queue-status path.
- plus the existing first observation for a task with no persisted summary.

Any other source retains the last observation and reports no change. This mirrors the existing `isCompletionGateRefreshEvent` / `isTaskErrorRefreshEvent` predicates next to it. `session_ceiling.go`, `ListAdmittedSessionIDs` and the `backendapp` wiring are untouched.

Conversation receipt semantics are unchanged: `message.updated` is still published on every tool-call update; only the summary's *read* of launch-queue state is bound to real state changes.

## Files

- `apps/backend/internal/task/statussummary/projector_events.go` — `isLaunchQueueRefreshEvent`
- `apps/backend/internal/task/statussummary/projector.go` — refresh gate
- `docs/specs/platform/system-design/bounded-task-status-delivery.md` — one derivation-rule bullet recording the closed refresh set and the retain-on-skip rule

No permanent test file is added: the refresh-gating checks for this change were a one-off verification and were kept outside package collection (they ran through a Go overlay against this package and passed).

## Verification

- `go build ./...` (apps/backend) — exit 0
- `go test ./internal/task/statussummary/... -tags fts5 -p 2 -count=1` — ok
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/task/statussummary/... --new-from-rev=origin/main --timeout=5m` — 0 issues
- `python scripts/list-docs.py validate`, `python scripts/lint-spec-files.py --all` — pass
- Overlay run of the one-off checks (per-message traffic causes 0 extra launch-queue loads and retains the previous observation; each classified source reloads and projects; a deferral written during tool traffic is projected on the next `task.updated`; a task with no persisted summary still gets its one cold observation; the closed refresh set is pinned against every subscribed source) — all pass. Reverting the gate made the read-bound check fail with 7 extra loads for 7 events, so the check does bite.

`internal/backendapp` and `internal/task/service` have pre-existing failures on the Windows host used for development (console/temp-ownership, kubernetes/git/desktop-discovery); each was reproduced with this change stashed, and `internal/task/service` fails non-deterministically at baseline, so a clean full Go run needs a Linux/macOS runner.

Before: `ribbon.js` loaded `/static/ribbon-ia.js` (and ~13 other modules, workers and fetched files) from a fixed URL with no `?v=<hash>`, so a browser could keep a stale copy after a deploy.

After: every static script/style load carries the deploy hash, and a test fails if a new unversioned one appears.

How: the page templates include a new `_static_boot.html` that emits an import map (built from the files on disk, one entry per `.js`/`.mjs`) mapping each `/static/x.js` to `x.js?v=<hash>`. That versions every `import()` and relative import with no change to the importing code. Loads the browser makes itself (`new Worker`, `fetch` of the `.mpp` template and PDF font, the created ExcelJS `<script>`) go through a new `staticUrl()` helper (`static/static-url.js`), and the portfolio worker passes its own `?v=` on to its import. Tests are in `tests/test_static_cache_busting.py`.

Tests: `uv run pytest` and `npm run test:js` have the same failures as `main` (2 in `test_browser_excel_parity.py`, 17 JS), nothing new. Browser suites not run.

Not covered: modules imported inside vendored libraries by a worker (`pptx-export.js`'s own imports) stay unversioned; they are still served `Cache-Control: no-cache`.

author: aabuhijleh
body:
## Summary

1.0.0: Linux support, a frozen cross-platform event shape, safe hooks, prebuilds, and a staged-release pipeline.

```text
src/
├── index.js        # public wrapper: listen() subscriptions, fan-out, key translation
├── index.d.ts      # export = keylogger; KeyEvent { key, code, state, repeat }
├── keys/index.js   # ONE key table: CGKeyCode / Win32 VK / Linux KEY_* → { code, key }
├── macOS/keylogger.mm    # listen-only CGEventTap, blocking CFRunLoop, real modifier state
├── windows/keylogger.cc  # WH_KEYBOARD_LL, unhooks on exit, off-thread dispatch
└── linux/keylogger.cc    # NEW: read-only libevdev, no EVIOCGRAB, X11 + Wayland
```

```diff
 // 0.0.4
-keylogger.start((key, isKeyUp, keyCode) => ...)   // keyCode differs per OS
-keylogger.stop()                                  // leaks the hook/tap
 // 1.0.0
+const unlisten = keylogger.listen((event) => ...) // event = { key, code, state, repeat }
+unlisten()                                        // removes hook/tap/evdev reads
```

```text
OS callback (hook/tap/reader thread)
  copy event by value ──▶ tsfn.NonBlockingCall (queue 1024, drops counted)
                              │
JS thread                     ▼
  build { keyCode, extended, state, repeat, character } ──▶ wrapper ──▶ handlers
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** `npm test` did not exist; Space reported `"Spacebar"`; `start` printed to stderr on failure; Windows never called `UnhookWindowsHookEx`; Linux built an empty addon.
  **After:** `npm test` → 18/18 pass (key table, UI Events names, subscription lifecycle against a fake addon, fan-out, failure paths). Linux table verified programmatically against the kernel's `input-event-codes.h` (caught `KEY_KPEQUAL` off by one).
- **Linux, real run on this machine:** tests ran, and a live session works. Press and release are reported. Confirmed by the author.
- **Windows backend:** `g++ -fsyntax-only` clean against node-addon-api 8.9.2 + Node 24 headers.
- **macOS backend:** cannot compile on Linux — review-verified against `napi.h`; needs a real Mac (see Merge Danger).
- `npm pack --dry-run` ships only LICENSE, README, binding.gyp, src/ (+ prebuilds/ when present).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way for the code; **one-way for the publish**. Merging to `main` triggers semantic-release → `npm stage publish` of **1.0.0**. It becomes public only after a maintainer approves the stage with 2FA — but a staged version still burns the semver (a rejected 1.0.0 cannot be re-staged).

Before the release job can succeed, one-time npm setup is required (human, on npmjs.com): add a trusted publisher for this repo + `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, restricted to **stage-only** (`npm trust ... --allow-stage-publish`, publish disabled), and set package access to "Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens". Until then the release job fails at the staging step — CI itself is unaffected.

**Blast Radius:** public API break. 0.0.4's `start(cb)`/`stop()` with positional `(key, isKeyUp, keyCode)` is gone; first semantic-release run publishes 1.0.0 with the new `listen()` surface. No runtime effect on existing installs.

`b678eaae18a407603bb7eaf5a2deee2b9b8f59bb3e1d07c452688b48d921a458`

### Counterexample discipline

Each generated case has a deterministic seed derived from:

`SHA256(master_seed | property_id | case_index)`.

Failures are written to a replayable counterexample ledger. The frozen M2 suite produced none.

### Claim boundary

M2 is stronger than hand-picked examples but weaker than formal proof. It establishes only that no counterexample was found in the frozen 1500-case deterministic generated suite.

### Next phase

M3 deliberately mutates the governance/property machinery and requires the qualification harness to kill the mutants.

author: aryanjathar
body:
Public clip lookups accepted arbitrary titles and could rapidly consume the shared YouTube quota. This change requires expiring, signed recommendation claims, adds atomic Redis rate limits and an 8,000-unit daily quota budget, and caches/coalesces clip lookups. Recommendation workflows now have an overall deadline, bounded upstream work, cancellation, and bounded local capacity.

Next.js and its ESLint config are upgraded to 16.3.8, patched brace-expansion versions are enforced, and pages use an enforced nonce-based Content Security Policy. The README documents hardcoded demo data and deployment requirements.

Deployment requires UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN, and a shared SHORTS_SIGNING_SECRET. Live production recommendation APIs return 503 without the shared store; clip searches fall back to links when the required protection is unavailable. Nonce-based pages render dynamically.

Validation: production build, TypeScript, lint, nine mocked security regression checks, production HTTP smoke checks, and a clean npm ci passed. HTTP checks verified fresh CSP nonces matching rendered scripts, five demo picks, and rejection of unsigned clip requests.

Remaining dependency limitation: braces 3.0.3 has no published patched release for GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm. A reproducible postinstall depth-limit mitigation and regression checks are included. npm audit reports zero critical findings but still reports five high affected package entries in the braces dependency chain. Live Redis/provider behavior was not tested with production credentials.

author: danielhanchen
body:
## Problem

On ROCm, PyTorch only runs its fused SDPA kernels (AOTriton flash and memory-efficient) on GPUs it lists as "experimentally supported" when `TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL=1` is set. gfx1151 (Strix Halo) is one of them. Without the variable, `scaled_dot_product_attention` refuses flash and efficient ("No available kernel") and every call runs the math backend, which builds the full score matrix.

Studio sets the variable in two places, `unsloth/__init__.py` and `studio/backend/main.py`, so the Studio server gets it. Code that imports Studio's inference package by any other route does not: in-process callers, workers and tests that never import `main.py` or `unsloth`. On those, image and video attention silently runs math.

PyTorch reads the variable once, at the first SDPA dispatch that needs it (a function-local `static const` in `aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/cuda/sdp_utils.cpp`), and only on ROCm builds. Setting it any time before the first attention call is therefore enough, and setting it is a no-op everywhere else.

## Change

`core/inference/__init__.py` sets `os.environ.setdefault("TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL", "1")`, the same opt-in as `main.py` and `unsloth/__init__.py`:

- It runs before any `core.inference.*` module loads, including the diffusion, video and attention modules.
- `setdefault` keeps an explicit user value, including `0`.
- No new import: the package stays torch-free to import.

## Results

Strix Halo CI runner, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), Linux, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0 from `install.sh --local`. Base (main) and head (main + this change) run in the same job, on the same runner, through Studio's in-process `DiffusionBackend`. This is the in-process route that does not import `main.py`. FLUX.2-klein-4B, 1024x1024, 4 steps, same prompts and seeds:

| cell | main s/image (s/step) | this PR s/image (s/step) | attention kernels |
|---|---|---|---|
| variable not set by the caller | 27.27 (6.50) | 8.70 (1.87) | main: SDPA math only; this PR: `_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention` (AOTriton) |
| variable set by the caller (reference, as the server sets it) | 8.64 (1.86) | 8.70 (1.86) | AOTriton on both |

- **Outputs:** with this change, the unset cell's render is pixel-identical to the reference's (LPIPS 0.000). On main the math path's render differs from it by LPIPS 0.114.
- **Attention microbenchmark** in the same environment (one call, bf16, 24 heads of 128, 4096 tokens): math 129 ms, AOTriton flash 11.8 ms. At 16384 tokens the math path runs out of memory and AOTriton takes 178 ms.

## Tests

New `tests/test_inference_aotriton_optin.py`. Each case runs a fresh interpreter, because the variable is process-wide:

- importing `core.inference` or a leaf like `core.inference.chat_eos` sets it to `1`;
- a preset `0`, `1` or `false` is kept;
- importing the package still does not import torch.

On main the two "sets it" tests fail and the other four pass; on this branch, 6 passed.

## Not covered

- **Other architectures:** only gfx1151 on Linux was measured. Architectures PyTorch already lists as fully supported ignore the variable, and non-ROCm builds never read it.
- **Server users:** no change for the server, which already set the variable in `main.py`.

author: leninworld
body: This PR fixes [issue #3096](https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/issues/3096). ## Description `weibull_adstock(..., type="CDF")` currently constructs one more weight than `l_max`, unlike the PDF, geometric, delayed, and binomial kernels and unlike the public adstock components that use it. For example, `lam=10`, `k=1`, and `l_max=4` produces nonzero weights at lags 0 through 4. This change makes the CDF branch construct its positive-lag grid from 1 through `l_max - 1`, then prepend the lag-zero weight before applying the cumulative product. The resulting kernel has exactly `l_max` weights. The PDF branch is unchanged. The regression coverage verifies: - exact CDF kernel length with and without normalization; - zero response from lag `l_max` onward; - normalized response mass of 1; - `l_max=1` as an identity transform; - unchanged behavior for the existing CDF oracle and unaffected kernels. ### Numerical compatibility This is an intentional numerical correction for Weibull CDF models: - unnormalized models drop only the former lag-`l_max` term; - normalized models rescale the retained weights (about +11.5% for the issue's `lam=10`, `k=1`, `l_max=4` example); - `Before` and `Overlap` support narrow by one period because their padding follows kernel length; - saved fits reloaded with this version can therefore produce different predictions. This prediction-changing fix warrants the `major` label under `.github/release.yml`; the author account cannot apply repository labels, so a maintainer must add it. No public signature, serialized field, dependency, or default changes. ### Validation The unchanged base reproduced the extra lag under both `PYTENSOR_FLAGS=linker=cvm` and `linker=numba`. The corrected revision passed the same fail-before/pass-after probe under both linkers. - focused CDF tests: 11 passed, 140 deselected; - complete affected set with `cvm`: 593 passed, 7 skipped, 1 pre-existing XPASS; - complete affected set with `numba`: 593 passed, 7 skipped, 1 pre-existing XPASS; - Ruff check and format passed on both changed files; - API documentation validation passed (22 documented, 4 excluded); - `git diff --check` passed. The full pinned pre-commit wrapper was not run locally because an unavailable third-party hook could not initialize offline. Upstream CI will be its first complete run. No repository-wide suite or green whole-project mypy result is claimed. ### Validation evidence ## Related Issue - [x] Closes #3096 - [ ] Related to # ## Checklist - [ ] Checked that [the pre-commit linting/style checks pass](https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/latest/contributing/index.html). Feel free to comment [`pre-commit.ci autofix` to auto-fix](https://pre-commit.ci/#configuration-autofix_prs). - [x] Included tests that prove the fix is effective or that the new feature works - [x] Added necessary documentation (docstrings and/or example notebooks) using [numpydoc format](https://numpydoc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format.html). - [x] If you are a pro: each commit corresponds to a [relevant logical change](https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/GitCommitMessages#Structural_split_of_changes) ---- 📚 Documentation preview 📚: https://pymc-marketing--3104.org.readthedocs.build/en/3104/

author: idorionicolau-star
body:
## Problema
O catálogo, o stock (por localização), as receitas e as encomendas ligam-se pelo **nome** do produto. Mudar o nome no Catálogo só alterava o catálogo. Mudar no Inventário só alterava uma localização. O resto ficava com o nome antigo e deixava de bater certo (stock "órfão").

## O que muda
- **Stock Rápido: botão "Mudar nome"** (lápis) no painel do produto escolhido. Aparece só para quem gere o inventário; se o produto estiver no catálogo, é preciso também permissão sobre o catálogo. Num produto com variações há duas opções:
  - **Só esta variação**;
  - **A família toda**: muda a base de todas, por exemplo "Pavê - Vermelho" passa a "Pavê Borbulha - Vermelho".
- **Uma só mudança de nome, usada em todo o lado** (Stock Rápido, formulário do Catálogo e formulário do Inventário). Muda de uma vez:
  - o catálogo;
  - o stock em **todas** as localizações;
  - as receitas;
  - as encomendas em aberto.
  
  Avisa se o nome já pertencer a outro produto. O que estava na lista do Stock Rápido por gravar segue com o nome novo.
- **O histórico não é reescrito.** Os movimentos são imutáveis e as facturas mostram o nome com que se vendeu. O produto guarda os nomes antigos (`formerNames`) e, ao ler, as vendas, os movimentos, as produções e as encomendas entregues aparecem com o nome actual em toda a app (relatórios, histórico, reservas). Um nome antigo reutilizado por outro produto deixa de contar como nome antigo.
- **Não é preciso mudar as regras do Firestore.**

## Testes
- 8 testes unitários novos (`src/lib/__tests__/rename.test.ts`); `vitest` passa todo (263), `tsc` sem erros.
- No emulador, em telemóvel, pelo Stock Rápido:
  - o nome repetido é bloqueado;
  - "Cimento" passou a "Cimento 32,5N" no catálogo, nas 2 localizações, na encomenda em aberto e na receita;
  - a encomenda entregue e a venda antiga ficam como foram gravadas, mas a venda aparece com o nome novo na página de Vendas;
  - a família "Pavê" passou a "Pavê Borbulha" no catálogo e no stock.
- No emulador, em computador, pelo formulário do Catálogo: o stock das 2 localizações seguiu o catálogo, e os nomes antigos acumulam-se.
- Regressões: a demonstração + catálogo e as variações no Stock Rápido continuam a passar.

author: misko19
body:
Closes #2570.

## Problem

A turn's **More Turn Actions** menu is a popover on desktop and a bottom sheet on phones. It and the dialogs it opens are portalled out of the transcript. React still delivers their wheel, pointer, touch and key events to the transcript's handlers. #2565 gated only the follow-state calls on `isReaderInput`. The earlier-history calls in the same handlers still saw every event.

At the head of loaded history, one upward wheel over an open turn menu requested the previous page of history, and the rows were prepended under the menu (the reproduction in the issue).

## Change

In `apps/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx`, the reader's `onWheel`, `onPointerDown`, `onPointerMove`, `onTouchStart`, `onTouchMove` and `onKeyDown` now return early when the event's target is outside the reader's own DOM (`isReaderInput`). Input inside a portalled menu, menu sheet or dialog therefore:

- marks no earlier-activity intent (single-scroll, mouse-press or touch traversal);
- requests no earlier history;
- does not move the follow state.

The follow-state part is what #2565 already did for wheel, press and pan.

**Keys, beyond the issue's list.** The issue names the wheel and touch handlers. Keys were an unlisted path to the same defect: **PageUp**, **Home**, **k** or **Shift+Space** pressed while focus is in the open desktop turn menu loaded earlier history. The issue's expected behavior covers any input in a portalled menu, sheet or dialog, so `onKeyDown` gets the same gate. Keys pressed on the transcript itself are unchanged.

**Unchanged:**

- wheel, touch, scrollbar-press and keyboard reading on the transcript itself;
- the floating tail control's drag relay (#2425), which dispatches on the reader itself and so passes the gate;
- `onScroll`, which does not bubble in React.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With the transcript at the top of its loaded history, a wheel over an open portalled turn menu requests no earlier history and does not move the transcript. e2e: `earlier-activity-desktop.spec.ts`, "an upward wheel over an open turn menu at the head loads no earlier activity". The request count stays `1`, `scrollTop` stays `0` and the menu stays open.
- [x] A touch pan inside an open phone menu sheet requests no earlier history and records no earlier-activity intent. Two e2e tests in `earlier-activity-mobile.spec.ts` use a real CDP touch pan inside the sheet:
  - "a downward pan inside an open turn menu sheet at the head loads no earlier activity": no history is requested.
  - "a finger held on an open turn menu sheet arms no earlier activity for a reader that reaches the head": the reader starts 40px above its head and is carried to the head while the finger stays on the sheet. An intent armed by the sheet would read that scroll as reader traversal and request a page. It fails with only the `onPointerDown` and `onTouchStart` guards removed.
  - Dialogs use the same portal path through the same gate; no separate dialog e2e test.
- [x] Wheel, touch and keyboard reading on the transcript itself still load earlier history. The full `earlier-activity-desktop` and `earlier-activity-mobile` specs pass. The new desktop test also wheels the transcript after closing the menu and expects the next page.
- [x] An e2e test covers the desktop wheel case and fails before the change. On the old handlers both new tests fail (`data-tail-request-count` `Received: "2"`, expected `"1"`). With only the key gate removed, the desktop test fails on its key assertion.

## Tests

- New e2e tests: the three above, all passing.
- Updated: `reading-mode-architecture.test.ts` matches the new `onKeyDown` guard and asserts the reader-input gate.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` passes.
- Web unit and DOM suite: 4,214 tests. The one failure before the update was the source-shape test above; it passes now.
- Related e2e specs, 82 passed: `earlier-activity-desktop`, `earlier-activity-mobile`, `checkpoint-rewind` (the #2526 phone menu block), `session-usage`.
- Broader reader e2e specs, 169 passed: `keycap`, `focus-zones`, `timeline-reflow`, `recovery-notice`, `transcript-states`, `command-inbox-projects`, `status-popover-escape`, `shortcut-reference`, `pinned-summary-rows`, `pinned-summary-dock`.

## Security and Compatibility

None.

## UI Evidence

Captured with Playwright against the Vite dev server's paged-history harness (`/recovery-notice-e2e.html?pagination=resolve&pagination-delay=300`). Base handlers are from `1f14313c6`; the head is `9a090b005`. Each capture is taken 1.2s after the input. Images are attached to the session as artifacts.

| Flow | Before (`1f14313c6`) | After (`9a090b005`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop 1280×900: open More Turn Actions at the head, wheel up once over the menu | 2 requests, `scrollTop` 372, boundary gone, menu open | 1 request, `scrollTop` 0, Load Earlier Activity boundary in view, menu open |
| Phone (Pixel 7): open the More Turn Actions sheet at the head, pan down inside it | 2 requests, `scrollTop` 470, boundary gone, sheet open | 1 request, `scrollTop` 0, boundary in view, sheet open |

The visual difference is that the transcript no longer moves under the open menu: after the change, the **Load Earlier Activity** boundary stays at the top.

## Cross-Model Review

Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, high effort, read-only.

- **Round 1** (head `ee26ae0bb`): UPVOTE, one minor finding.
  - CR-1.1: the sheet test's scroll at an unchanged head could not prove that no intent was armed.
  - Agreed and fixed in `9a090b005` with the companion test above, mutation-checked.
- **Round 2** (head `9a090b005`): UPVOTE, no findings.
- **Round 3** (head `9a090b005`, canonical `codex exec review`, approval `never`, connectors disabled): UPVOTE, no findings. Rounds 1–2 ran with a non-canonical invocation (approval `on-request`, connectors enabled), so round 3 is the authoritative vote. It confirmed CR-1.1 resolved, that the tail-control relay, per-finger release bookkeeping and text-node targets are intact, and that the keyboard gate keeps preview, typing-context and global-shortcut behavior.

Accepted, intended behavior change: End or Shift+G pressed inside a portalled menu or dialog no longer resumes following the transcript underneath it.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and includes relevant tests.
- [x] Public documentation reflects changed behavior or configuration. (No documented behavior changes.)
- [x] User-interface labels follow the project Title Case convention. (No labels change.)
- [x] Fixtures, screenshots, logs, and generated files contain no credentials or private information.
- [x] New documentation is product-focused and contains no competitor comparison material.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes.
- [x] Relevant tests and builds pass.

Depends on #26; its row-input and CI foundation is included until that PR merges. The additional change covers the JSON object-of-arrays path.

An empty first column currently disables equal-length validation: `{"a":[],"b":[1]}` is accepted even though its columns have different lengths. Recognize the first column using the existing column-name count so zero remains a valid initialized length.

An entirely null column also throws `UndefVarError` because the union method does not bind its type parameter for `Nothing`. Handle that exact type as `Missing`. Empty parsed arrays can have `Union{}` as their element type; use `Any` for those unknown column types so constructing a table schema and converting the empty table succeeds on current Julia. Populated and mixed-null column types retain their existing handling.

Validation:
- The preceding column-length probe has eight passes and four failures, including accepted unequal lengths after an empty first column. Two all-null schema checks separately error with the unbound type parameter. Current Julia also reproduces empty-column schema/row/column conversion errors before the empty-type fallback.
- All 46 new public checks pass: unequal lengths in both orders and after multiple empty columns, valid equal empty/populated columns, mixed nulls, all-null columns through text/byte/IO/parsed inputs, schema types, and row/column conversions.
- The full 140-check suite passes on Julia 1.6.7 and 1.13.0 with four threads and forced bounds checks. `git diff --check` passes.
- All six checks pass at `7d72b625be0d176313a65d913c3dedfb1291b03e`: all four native jobs in run [37186035745](https://github.com/JuliaData/JSONTables.jl/actions/runs/37186035745), including Julia 1.0, plus both Codecov checks. All four coverage sessions were accepted at the correct repository/commit destination; the stable job uploaded 893 bytes and the final report is 93.75%. Merge remains held for prerequisite #26 and the required independent approval.

Co-authored by Codex

author: osher15
body:
A teacher can now prepare a readable single-pupil progress document from a class or pupil period report. Class context requires an explicit pupil choice; pupil context is limited to that pupil. Review the isolated preview before printing/saving as PDF through the browser, or downloading an offline HTML copy. Period history is optional and off by default.

The allowlisted document includes pupil identity, class/period bounds, required test names/units, best/date and measured/missing/exempt status. Zero remains measured; missing/exempt values are blank. Other pupils, grades, private teacher notes, exemption reasons and measurement internals are omitted. Stale stored context or globally ambiguous stable IDs block output. No storage writes, public link, pupil account or external sending.

Escaped script-free HTML uses a restrictive CSP and a sandboxed preview without script permission. Print/download failures preserve data. Physical/native printer/PDF acceptance remains separate.

Validation: 622/622 units including four new model/HTML tests; seven new browser cases plus eight report/Excel regressions passed (15). Final table styling reran all seven new cases. Actual offline HTML download and real browser-generated PDF; PyMuPDF confirmed one selected-pupil page with correct best/dates/missing count and no other pupil/private/outside-period content. Optional history, zero, stale/duplicate IDs, injected print/download failures/retry, Back, hostile escaped text, five languages and phone/desktop checked. Repeated build deterministic; generated GitHub outputs match local tested files; temporary helper removed.

author: chardonnay
body:
## Summary

### File > Open Recent (UX-17)
- New *File > Open Recent* submenu in both menu bars, with three parts:
  - **Connections**: up to 10 saved connections, the one used last first. These are the same connections Quick Connect shows at the top. A connection opens through `connectSavedConnection`, so the server policy is checked before any question. It is looked up again by id when clicked.
  - **Projects**: up to 10 recent project files, then the other `.kortty` files in `~/.kortty/projects`. Missing files are left out. The list is looked up on a background thread.
  - **Clear List**: deletes nothing. It only hides the connections used and the project-folder files changed before it was chosen.
- The submenu is rebuilt each time the File menu opens, so it is kept out of the command-palette harvest, like Recently Closed.
- ClosedWindowMenuRouter: **Clear List** needs no window. A connection or project entry acts in the frontmost window, the default. Two new pins in ClosedWindowMenuRouterTest cover this.
- New `GlobalSettings.recentProjectPaths` and `openRecentClearedAt`. Both live in `global-settings.xml`, so they are part of configuration backups.

### Split layouts restored without reflection or FX-thread sleeps (UX-18)
- `TerminalSplitPane` gains `snapshotLayout()`, `applyDividerPositions()` and a `splitWidget(…, beforeStart)` overload. The reflective `rootCell`/`focusedWidget` access is gone, and `TerminalWidgetReflectionGuardTest` now forbids `getDeclaredField` in TerminalView.
- `Thread.sleep(1000)` is replaced by a one-shot `TerminalTab.addOnFirstConnected`. It runs once, never on a reconnect.
- The panes connect one after another on a daemon thread and are attached in one hop to the FX thread. The saved dividers are applied two pulses after the last split.
- Signing in, per pane:
  - A pane on the tab's own server reuses the tab's password and key. Its access-reason memory replays CyberArk-style reasons.
  - A pane on another saved connection signs in through `ConnectionAuthResolver` without prompts.
  - Every pane passes `SplitConnectionPolicy`.
  - An expired temporary key is never renewed.
- Panes that stay closed are reported in the status bar.
- Each leaf can now record the saved connection of a pane that runs on another server.
- `currentDirectory` and `scrollbackRef` are stripped from every project file that is loaded or saved. Only session snapshots may carry them.

### Every window, its geometry and the active tab (UX-19)
- Save Project keeps every open window: the window you save from first, then the others in the order they were opened.
- Opening a project puts the first saved window into the current window and opens each further window in a new window, up to 32.
- Geometry is sanitised through `MainWindowGeometrySupport.plan`. For a maximized window the normal bounds are saved, with the maximized flag.
- The active tab is selected by session id, with the saved index as a fallback for old files. It survives sorting into tab groups and remote tabs that arrive late.

### Tabs that need you go to one non-modal bar; local shells reopen (UX-20)
- Each saved tab is classified without asking anything (`TabRestoreTriage`): READY, NEEDS_UNLOCK, NEEDS_CREDENTIALS, BLOCKED or MISSING.
- READY tabs open. That now includes local shells, which used to be skipped silently.
- Everything else is listed in one restore bar above the status line, instead of one modal dialog per tab. The bar offers **Connect…**, **Unlock Vault…** (through `VaultUnlockSupport`), **Details** and **Dismiss**. Connect… asks once per connection.
- `onVaultUnlocked` retries the tabs waiting for the vault, in every window.

### Session autosave and File > Restore Previous Session (UX-42)
- **Where it is kept.** `SessionSnapshotStore` writes to `~/.kortty/session/`. Writes are owner-only and atomic. A corrupt file is quarantined through StoreFileGuard. A single-writer FileLock means a second korTTY neither moves the previous session aside nor writes. The last session becomes the previous one at the next start only when it had a tab.
- **When it is written.** The snapshot is written 2 s after a change, and at the latest 30 s after the first change while changes keep coming. It is never written while a restore is opening tabs. A capture with no tabs never overwrites a snapshot that has tabs.
- **Quitting.** On Quit, and when the last window closes on Windows or Linux, the snapshot is written and sealed before any tab closes. That keeps a quit with several windows intact. `performShutdown` covers every other way korTTY ends.
- **What it never holds.** No screen text, scrollback, timestamps, passwords or temporary keys. The Recently Closed list is persisted with ids only.
- **The menu item.** *File > Restore Previous Session* reuses the project restore and the restore bar. It works once per run.
- **Backups.** BackupCoverageTest classifies both snapshot files as excluded from backups.

### Offer or perform the restore at startup (UX-43)
- New *Settings > Window > Session Restore* setting with three modes:
  - **Ask** (the default, D6): a non-modal offer bar with Restore and Dismiss.
  - **Auto**: restores once no modal window is open, checking every 500 ms. If a dialog stays open for 60 s, it shows the offer bar instead.
  - **Off**: nothing at startup.
- **Crash-loop guard** (`SessionRestoreDecision`): if korTTY ended uncleanly within a minute of a restore, Auto turns into the offer, and the bar says why.
- **Startup order.** The coordinator is posted after the consent line. That line and the consent dialog are untouched.
- **Unanswered offers.** An offer you ignore in a run where you open nothing comes back at the next start. Dismiss stops that.

### Review fixes
- **Locked temporary key.** A start with the vault locked clears every encrypted temporary SSH key in memory. The connection then looked like key auth without a key, and the resolver called it READY, so the login could only fail on the server. It is now NEEDS_TEMP_KEY: restores list it in the bar, and interactive connects ask for a new key. The fix is the new `ConfigurationManager.hasLockedTemporaryKey` plus a vault-seam default method.
- **Split restore worker.** An unexpected exception while preparing one pane used to kill the restore thread. The remaining panes never opened, nothing was reported, and the tab waited for its layout for good. That pane is now skipped as failed, and the finish step always runs.
- **Wording.** The restore bar's tooltip now also names a restored previous session, in all 8 bundles. Two Javadoc blocks that had come loose from their methods are back in place.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew test` on macOS: 7832 tests, 0 failures
- [x] The same suite in a Linux container (eclipse-temurin 25, non-root): 7832 tests, 0 failures
- [x] Doc validators: `doc-links.py`, `doc-coverage.py --strict`, `sync-version.py --check`, `external-api-check.py --strict`, `validate-doc-svg.sh`
- [x] German pages generated (LM Studio gpt-oss-20b), proofread against the English pages and the German UI labels; line alignment and the strict German build checked; guide staged
- [x] Headed smokes on macOS: `splitLayoutRestoreSmoke`, `restoreAttentionBarSmoke`, `sessionRestoreOfferBarSmoke`
- [ ] macOS: quit with two windows and several tabs (one split across two servers), restart, and check the offer bar, then Restore: windows, geometry, active tab, panes and dividers come back
- [ ] macOS: close the last window (korTTY keeps running), quit from the Dock, restart: the last non-empty session is offered
- [ ] macOS: Auto mode on a first start with the consent dialog: nothing connects until the dialog is answered
- [ ] macOS: kill korTTY within 60 s of an Auto restore, restart: the offer bar says korTTY ended unexpectedly, and nothing restores by itself
- [ ] macOS: with the vault locked at startup, password tabs show "vault locked" in the bar and Unlock Vault… opens them; a temporary-key tab shows "needs a new tempora

## Summary
- **`.ctv` schema v3**: `assignment_analysis` (tier, words > 0) and `assignment.analysed_at`. **Immutable by trigger**: a payable that rests on it must not be movable by anyone holding the connection; a re-analysis is a new assignment.

`pnpm format:check`, `lint`, `build`, `typecheck`, `pnpm test` (116 files, 1692 tests) pass locally; `check-lists.test.ts` ties the new CHECK to `RATE_TIERS`. `test:gate` and `test:golden` not run: nothing under their trigger paths changed. The route test changes the project after the offer and asserts the frozen analysis does not move.

author: vbalashi
body:
The selected training overview counted reviews scheduled before the end of the study day, while ordinary session launch selected only reviews due at the current server time. This let Reviews only show a positive Due today count and switch to Review ahead only after an empty launch.

Migration 210 makes Due today the actionable backlog, including overdue cards. Future cards remain in Total reviews. Review ahead is therefore available before clicking when no reviews are due, and its redundant trailing arrow is removed. Scheduling and explicit early-review behavior are unchanged.

Validation: 127 focused tests passed, including real PostgreSQL availability versus start-plan checks, early-review tests, UI and cache/client tests, and deployment contract tests. Typecheck, targeted lint, migration/postflight guards and diff check passed. Migration tested in an isolated disposable local database. Manifest enabled contract 210 with exact migration checksum and versioned postflight. No production rollout performed.

Closes #580.


Release-Ready: yes

This PR deploys independently: migration 210 and its manifest/postflight ship with the UI action change; no pending PR is required.

## Summary

- Outcome: Established a unified 4-tier geometric radius system (`xs: 4, sm: 6, md: 8, lg: 12, pill: 999`), eradicated all legacy 2px radiuses across all admin workspaces, refined public feed and post detail typography (`text-wrap: balance`, `tabular-nums`), and harmonized modal dialogs with concentric geometry.

## Changes

- Unify geometric radius tokens across `src/design-system/tokens.ts` and `src/styles/variables.ts`.
- Replace 999px pills in mobile tag chips and feed load-more buttons with 6px squircle controls.
- Replace legacy 2px radiuses in Admin Shell (sidebar avatar 50% circle, nav links 6px), posts workspace, tools workspace, cloud workspace, and profile workspace.
- Enforce concentric radius geometry (`12px > 8px > 6px`) in ConfirmDialog and publish modals.
- Update feed search input to 6px squircle with 4px physical keycap shortcut (`⌘K`), eliminating 0px sharp box and direct rgba literals.
- Sync PostDetail header colors to semantic tokens (`var(--aq-...)`) and apply `text-wrap: balance; word-break: keep-all;`.

## Scope

### Included

- Public surfaces: Feed, Detail, Company
- Admin workspaces: Shell, Posts, Tools, Cloud, Profile, Dashboard, Hub
- Shared design system: Tokens, Variables, Primitives, ConfirmDialog

### Excluded

- Backend API and database schema changes
- Unrelated structural layout refactors

## Verification

| Check | Result / Evidence |
|---|---|
| Focused test | `yarn test:unit` 414 passed (13.3s) |
| Required CI | `yarn check:design-colors`, `yarn check:refactor-boundaries`, `yarn type-check` |
| Manual / runtime | Component isolation visual captures and side-by-side before/after comparisons |

### Not Run

- None

## Risk & Delivery

- Risk: Low
- Main risk: CSS visual regression on edge viewport sizes

author: desktopmachineshop
body:
## What and why

The maintainer decided (#379, [decisions](https://github.com/desktopmachineshop/OpenV/issues/379#issuecomment-5977476038)) to fix how notification emails carry member-supplied text rather than dismiss CodeQL's "Email content injection" alert at `internal/notify/email.go:97`, which blocks #470. This PR is that fix: two real protections, each with a test that fails without it.

- **Member text stays on its line.** A new `memberText` turns each run of control characters (Unicode Cc, plus U+2028 and U+2029) into one space and drops runs at either end. It is applied where member text enters a message:
  - the joined member's display name and the invited address;
  - the artifact title in the review request;
  - the workspace name in the three stable-release titles;
  - the workspace and inviter names in the invitation;
  - the greeting in the verification and password-reset emails.

  Before, a display name like "Ben\n\nYour account is locked" opened a paragraph of its own in the bell, phone alerts and emails, and read as OpenV's text. That is the content spoofing CWE-640 describes.
- **Every line break reaches the mail server as CRLF.** `buildMessage` used to turn only LF into CRLF, so a bare CR went out raw. A server that takes a bare CR for a line end reads `\r.\r` as the end of the message, and what follows as commands of its own (the "SMTP smuggling" class). Every CRLF, bare CR or bare LF now goes out as one CRLF.
- **Unchanged:** ordinary text is byte-for-byte identical on the wire, and no golden changed (S10's notification goldens and the tours are untouched).

## What this does not do: clear the CodeQL alert

CodeQL still reports the same alert with the same six sources after this change, run locally with CLI 2.27.1 and go-queries 1.6.11:
- **No sanitizer exists.** `go/email-injection` has no `isBarrier` and no Sanitizer class; it is `isSource`/`isSink` over `net/smtp.SendMail`'s message argument.
- **Honest encoding doesn't help.** It models every honest encoder or writer (`mime/quotedprintable`, `net/textproto`, `strings.Map`/`FieldsFunc`/`Join`, …) as passing data through.
- **Four of the six sources are the recipient's own address** in the `To` header. That address must be there, `headerLine` already keeps it on one line, and `net/smtp` refuses an address with CR/LF before sending anything.
- **Two are false positives:** the org id from a runner-session URL flows into a map that CodeQL assumes can reach a notification link.

The only ways to turn the check green are to dismiss the alert, or to route the data through something CodeQL doesn't model, which would hide the flow without protecting anything more. This PR does neither; the maintainer decides #470's path.

## Release notes

- [x] A bullet under `## Unreleased` in `RELEASE_NOTES.md`, in its group (*New features*, *Maintenance updates* or *Bug fixes*), written for a workspace member: one bullet under *Bug fixes*.
- [ ] Nothing a user can see changes: the pull request carries the `no-release-notes` label.

**Tests:**
- `TestMemberTextCannotReshapeTheEmail` sends hostile member text through seven entry points (joined, invited, review, stable release, invitation, verification, password reset). All seven fail on master and pass after the fix.
- `TestBodyLineBreaksReachTheServerAsCRLF` feeds `buildMessage` a bare CR, a bare LF and `\r.\r` directly.
- Mutations: reverting the CRLF conversion fails the second test; making `memberText` return its input fails the first.

**Checks:**
- `go test` of notify, api, archtest and cmd/server, with Postgres;
- `release_notes.py check`;
- the Refactor guard on a merge.

author: kazu-2020
body:
Closes #52.

## Summary

This PR does the 6 steps of issue #52. Each commit keeps `go test` and `api/e2e.sh` green.

1. **Name references.** The SQL function `app_rename(names, old, new)` is in `schema.sql`. The Go tables `memberRefs` and `metricRefs` list each place that keeps an engine name. EditMembers, RenameMetric and DeleteMetric use them, and the statements run in one transaction.
2. **Partial property updates.** The engine has a new write operation, `set_property_values(dim, prop, {member: value | null})`. `editOps` now sends only the changed values. The copy of the mapping and the imitation of rename and remove are deleted. TEXT values change with partial SQL. `editOps` keeps the values and sends them in one operation for each property, so an import of 2000 rows takes about 0.1 s, the same as on main. A rename or a removal first sends the kept values that name that member.
3. **One entry point.** All handlers that write to the engine use `PlanServer.change(ctx, app, planOf)`. It takes the lock, reads the model and the api data, makes the plan, and runs the SQL statements and the engine write in one transaction. `writeWithList`, `editMembers`, `refusePropertyMetric` and the AddProperty compensation are deleted.
4. **Limits and error codes.** `caller` keeps only the rules. `caller.limitsIn(em)` is the only caller of `through`. The tagged errors `errDenied`, `errExists` and `errPrecondition` get their codes from `connectError`. WriteCells now returns InvalidArgument for input errors. Import now returns PermissionDenied for permission errors. `dbError` lets a `*connect.Error` pass through, so the transaction callers do not repeat that check.
5. **Split by feature.** `plan.go` and `server.go` are now `server.go`, `engine.go`, `access.go`, `model.go`, `metric.go`, `data.go`, `import.go`, `snapshot.go` and `item.go`. Each file has the calculations first and the actions after them. The tests follow the same split. A declaration check (go/parser) shows that all 159 declarations are the same before and after the move. `api/CLAUDE.md` is updated.
6. **Small items.** CreateApplication does the database inserts first, then the engine steps, in one transaction. CreateSnapshot holds the application lock, so the engine reads and the api rows (properties, items) read one version. It also compares the `seq` of each read with the model `seq` for writes from a different api process. If they differ, it reads again. After 3 tries, it returns Aborted.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The PostgreSQL transaction in `change` stays open during the engine write, so it holds one pool connection for that time. This is not a deadlock risk. If many slow engine writes run at the same time, the other RPCs can wait for a connection.
- All model changes of one application now wait for the lock, and cell writes and snapshots do too. Issue #52 step 3 asks for this.
- New snapshots store `seq` in the cube JSON. Replay ignores it, and old snapshots still load.
- If the commit fails after the engine write, the engine and the api tables can disagree. On main, the same risk was in the other direction. A replay error in CreateApplication can leave an engine model without an application in the router, because the router has no delete.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd api && go vet ./... && go test ./...` with PostgreSQL. The PG tests ran.
- [x] `cd api && ./e2e.sh` with the real router and engines. It now also checks that a member rename reaches the access rule and the property values.
- [x] tessera `tests.parallel` with the reference engine and with the Rust engine: 708 tests pass. New tests are in `test_redefine` and `test_journal` (file and PG journals).
- [x] Import benchmark with 2000 rows: 0.10 s on main and 0.11 s on this branch. Before the batching fix it took 1.62 s.
- [x] An independent review read the diff and ran the SQL against PostgreSQL. It found one regression (a property on a list that points to itself), which is now fixed and tested.
- [x] A second review (code review, over-engineering, comments) found that CreateSnapshot read the api rows without the lock. The last 4 commits fix it, remove a repeated error check and correct the comments. `go test` (24 tests, PG tests ran) and `e2e.sh` pass after each commit.

author: webovignesh
body:
The voice room could miss the first utterance while recognition started, show inaccurate Tamil-first browser drafts, and stay recording after speech stopped. The transcript review form and Sage/voice branding also interrupted the requested clean call UI.

This replaces browser captions with a Gemini 3.8 Live input-transcription listener. An AudioWorklet streams 16 kHz PCM, buffers the first packets until setup completes, and warms the next connection during reply playback. Local silence and server speech-end detection flush the recording and wait for late transcript segments before submitting once. The listener's generated audio is never played: SageAI keeps website tools/history, and the selected TTS speaker remains the only audible voice. If Live/worklets are unavailable or capture starts late, the complete MediaRecorder audio is transcribed as a bounded fallback.

The review form, branding header, language-specific browser recognition and browser fallback button are removed. Unclear speech receives a spoken clarification without guessed actions. The selected speaker/rate stay fixed during a call, successful 3.8 TTS model selection persists across calls, legacy TTS-family fallbacks are removed, and the style prompt is empty to avoid unnecessary accent/identity directions. Explicit close-voice commands work locally; greetings and negations cannot close the room.

Sage now receives its actual capabilities and current voice state. A paginated read_documents tool sends real stored-file attachments, reports per-file failures and enforces a 10 MB batch cap. File contents remain untrusted data and existing confirmation/current-request guards still apply. Versioned assets and precaching include the new listener/worklet; README describes the current pipeline.

Google docs reviewed:
- [Live capabilities and Tamil support](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/capabilities)
- [WebSocket setup, input transcription and audioStreamEnd](https://ai.google.dev/api/live)
- [Gemini 3.5 Transcribe](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.5-transcribe): Tamil is absent from the documented language list, so it is not the primary bilingual route.
- [TTS streaming and voice-consistency guidance](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/speech-generation)

Validation:
- 87 deterministic regressions passed for voice lifecycle, controls, tool attachments, latency guards, chat activation and real worklet resampling.
- Browser UI audit passed on desktop, mobile and small screens, including removed UI and stale-cache upgrades.
- Real Chromium microphone + production AudioWorklet: delayed first setup, five automatic bilingual provider transcripts, one selected speaker, no browser recognition/batch upload, and cleanup passed.
- Real MediaRecorder/WAV fallback, outage retry and five-turn capture audit passed.
- Offline audio-clock continuity audit passed (maximum sample error 0.001935).
- Boot, reference integrity and git diff checks passed.

Provider responses are mocked in these tests. Live Gemini-key access, real Chennai/Theni recognition, end-to-end latency and audible timbre/accent still need testing on the user's device. Generated voice variation cannot be eliminated by client routing alone. This PR does not merge or deploy the change.

body:
The second A2UI round: Android-widget-style components and a visual redesign of the existing blocks. Design: Prism-Shadow/penguin-harness-design#264.

## Widgets (all read-only)
| type | what it shows | live? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `weather` | Conditions at a place (11 conditions plus night variants), high/low, feels like, humidity, wind. Optional next hours (a temperature line that draws in) and coming days (range bars). An animated line illustration per condition. | No: a snapshot with `asOf` and `source` |
| `clock` | 1–4 IANA zones or the local one, digital, analog or both, offset from local | Yes: ticks each second, pauses off-screen |
| `countdown` | Time left until one instant, with a done label | Yes |
| `metrics` | 1–8 tiles: `reading` / `used` / `remaining` / `progress`, ring or bar gauge, sparkline history, delta, `detail` ("resets in 3 days"). `worse: high \| low` sets the direction `warn`/`danger` read in, so one type covers a system snapshot, a quota or budget left, and a progress bar | No: a snapshot with `asOf` |

- **Core (`@prismshadow/penguin-core/a2ui`)**: the types, validation, new L1 codes (`invalid_datetime`, `invalid_timezone`, `duplicate_zone`) and L2 warnings (`no_as_of`, `weather_hourly_long`, `metrics_too_many`). Shared pure helpers live in `widgets.ts`: number and temperature formatting, `resolveMetric`, `countdownParts`, `formatAsOf`. There is a text fallback for each widget, with blank lines between sections so messaging renderers keep them apart. Rubric question 3 now names widgets, and a new question 8 asks "is every number real". Widgets don't count as interactive, so prose may follow them.
- **UI**:
  - **Surface**: `WidgetSurface` on a new `ui-widget` hook. Frost is a soft tile with white inner tiles. Console is a hairline box with mono figures and crisp art. Primer is the card. A widget holding one short reading (countdown, one zone) sizes to its content.
  - **Motion**: `a2ui-motion.css` holds the condition loops (rain falls, snow drifts, rays breathe, lightning flashes, wind streams) and the one-off hourly draw-in. Timing comes from `--ui-live-timing` (Console steps). Everything stills under reduced motion and pauses off-screen.
  - **Language**: widgets format numbers, dates and weekdays in the interface language, carried as `A2uiStrings.lang`. Traces and subagent panels therefore match the words around them.
- **Redesign**:
  - **Choice**: short answer sets are a row of chips; others are cards with a radio-style disc. Multi-select uses the same card around the real checkbox.
  - **Form**: `Segmented` for a short single-select, toggle chips for a short multi-select, and a −/+ `NumberField` stepper clamped to `min`/`max`.
  - **Steps**: a numbered timeline with a connector.
  - **Mermaid**: the box takes the surface fill.
  - Every drawn block arrives with the theme's `data-reveal`. The callout keeps its one-row tone note.
- **Skill** (`plugins/a2ui` → `2026.10.04.1`): when to use each widget (and when not), the catalog table, and a "Get real data" section. Two new dependency-free scripts:
  - `scripts/weather.mjs <place>` reads Open-Meteo (no key, zh place names) and prints a `weather` fence.
  - `scripts/sysinfo.mjs` reads CPU, memory, disk, load and uptime and prints a `metrics` fence.
  - The checker bundle is rebuilt.
- **Docs and gallery**: Chat docs ("Rich output blocks" / 「富输出组件」), skills one-liners, the plugin README, and gallery samples for all four widgets plus the redesigned blocks. Changelog: `changelog/unreleased/2026-10-04-a2ui-widgets.md` (+ `.zh.md`).

## Verification
Run on the remote test host (vps4), Node 24:
- `pnpm build` (core, server and ui closures), then `build:a2ui-check` after formatting. The bundle header hash matches, and `a2ui-skill.test.ts` passes.
- **Typecheck** clean for core, ui, web, cli, server, docs, ui-gallery and landing. `pnpm lint` reports 0. `pnpm format:check` is clean.
- **Tests** green:

  | package | test files |
  | --- | --- |
  | core | 70 (+1 platform-skipped) |
  | ui | 136 |
  | web | 250, including deslop, icon-registry and hooks |
  | cli | 35 |
  | docs | 8 |
  | ui-gallery | 19 |
  | landing | 14 |

- **Visual**: the gallery content board was captured at 2× in modern light/dark (zh), Primer light (zh) / dark (en) and Console light (zh) / dark (en). Every block was captured separately, plus hover on choice. Two fixes came out of this: the coming-days range bars moved from the accent to a muted ink, and countdown/single-zone surfaces fit their content. Animated loops were checked visually in the captures; there are no animation tests by design.

author: techupbusiness
body:
## What it does

`TranscribeRequest` gains `maxContext` (`int?`, null by default). When it is `>= 0`, the native layer sets `whisper_full_params.n_max_text_ctx` to it — the same knob as whisper.cpp's CLI `--max-context` / `-mc`. `0` decodes every 30-second window without the text decoded before it, which is the equivalent of Python whisper's `condition_on_previous_text=False`.

## Why `noContext` is not enough

`noContext` maps to `wparams.no_context`, which whisper.cpp only uses to clear history **once, at the start of `whisper_full`** (`src/whisper.cpp`, the `if (params.no_context)` block before the main loop). On a freshly loaded context there is nothing to clear. Inside a single request, each window still appends its tokens to the prompt history and the next window still consumes them, gated only by `n_max_text_ctx` (the `if (params.n_max_text_ctx > 0 && ...)` block where the prompt is assembled). No shim set that field — the `int32_t max_context = -1` member in each shim's params struct was never parsed or applied — so it always stayed at whisper.cpp's default of 16384.

On long recordings this carry-over is what lets one hallucinated phrase repeat window after window. Measured with the whisper.cpp 1.9.2 CLI and `ggml-base-q5_1` on a ~3 h German conversation recording: **49% of segments** sat inside runs of five or more identical consecutive segments with default decoding (one stretch over an hour long), and **3%** with `-mc 0`, at a comparable word count.

The `noContext` doc comment claimed equivalence to `condition_on_previous_text=False`; this PR corrects it and points to `maxContext`.

## Scope and safety

- **Off by default** — without `maxContext` the request JSON carries `null`, the shims' `is_number_integer()` guard leaves the field at `-1`, and `n_max_text_ctx` keeps whisper.cpp's default. Behaviour is byte-identical to 2.7.1.
- **All three native shims** carry the identical block — `android/src/whisper/main.cpp` (also compiled by the Windows and Linux builds), `ios/Classes/whisper_flutter_plus.cpp`, `macos/Classes/whisper_ggml.cpp`. Each was clang syntax/type-checked against its vendored headers.
- **Composes with `keepModelLoaded`** — the field is per request and does not touch the resident-model checkout.
- Worth knowing for callers: whisper.cpp applies `initialPrompt` through the same `n_max_text_ctx` budget, so `maxContext: 0` also disables `initialPrompt`. The new doc comment says so.
- Generated files were rebuilt and only the three request/DTO outputs that carry the new field were kept; unrelated generator churn was dropped.

## Verification

- New DTO serialization test: `max_context` is null by default and forwards `0` and a positive budget (suite 16/16 green).
- End-to-end numbers through the plugin on the same long recording will follow in a comment.

## Noticed while integrating (separate from this PR)

- The iOS podspec declares `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 15.6` in `s.xcconfig`, which CocoaPods also copies into the app target's `Pods-Runner` xcconfig, overriding a host app's higher floor. `pod_target_xcconfig` (or `s.ios.deployment_target` alone) would keep it scoped to the pod.
- `ffmpeg_kit_flutter_new_min: ^2.1.0` resolves to 2.1.0, which predates the CVE-2026-8461 FFmpeg fix (3.4.1), excludes arm64 for the iOS simulator, and ships arm64e device slices (ffmpeg_kit #164). 3.6.x keeps the API this package calls; raising the constraint to `^3.6.4` worked unchanged here.

Happy to split either into its own issue or PR if useful.

author: hyperlapse122
body:
## Summary

Claude Code no longer runs an advisor model on any host. The next rebuild deletes the `advisorModel` key that earlier rebuilds wrote into `~/.claude/settings.json`, so sessions go back to Claude Code's default of no advisor.

The key now sits in `retiredKeys` rather than simply leaving the declared set. The merge only ever assigns, so a plain deletion would have left `"fable"` on every machine that had already rebuilt. While the entry stays in `retiredKeys`, an advisor turned on through `/advisor` lasts only until the next rebuild that produces a new Home Manager generation. Drop the entry once every host has rebuilt past it, and the setting becomes the user's again.

The `claude` check now asserts the rendered `remove` list for the settings merge and an empty one for the global-config merge. Putting `advisorModel` back into the declared set turns the check red, and so does emptying `retiredKeys`.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: disable the advisor (user-directed, over keeping `advisorModel = "fable"` declared).

## Validation

- `nix fmt -- --ci`: clean.
- `checks.x86_64-linux.claude`: failed on all six user entries after the test change and before the module change, and passed after it. Both mutations above turn it red again.
- `nix flake check`: all checks passed.
- All four `nixosConfigurations` outputs build, production and bootstrap. `homeConfigurations` and `systemConfigs` are empty.
- `vmChecks.all`: built.
- Not exercised: a real rebuild on a host. That Claude Code leaves the advisor off when `advisorModel` is absent is an assumption carried from the plan that turned it on.

author: gbouteiller
body:
AuthKit 0.2.10's public `@convex-dev/workos-authkit/test` export fails typechecking in Keenko's canonical isolated Bun installation. This change gives that export a narrow declaration boundary while keeping its upstream runtime adapter unchanged.

## Root cause and upstream investigation

- Re-fetched GitHub main at `92b2abbe3f0eb3f61d14a11fc5039a865e89b6a8` and read Linear KEE-53 before implementation. Linear was not modified.
- Inspected the actual npm 0.2.10 archive, manifest, exports, test implementation, dependency/peer declarations, nested helpers and real installed resolution paths. npm latest remains 0.2.10; upstream main still exposes the affected source. No corrected compatible published release is available.
- `./test` exports `./src/test.ts`. That source imports the undeclared development-only `convex-test` type. Nested workflow/workpool/batch-worker test helpers expose undeclared `convex-test` types and `vite/client` references. Neither module is provided by their published dependency contracts. Backend already declares `convex-test`, but the real isolated AuthKit boundary cannot resolve it.
- Independently reproduced missing `convex-test`, `vite/client`, and `import.meta.glob` diagnostics in an OS temporary workspace using the exact rc.2 managed dependency-role snapshot. The snapshot was byte-compared against the actual published Keenko rc.2 artifact. Initial failure is required by the automated regression.

## Narrow correction and ownership

One native Bun patch is specific to `@convex-dev/workos-authkit@0.2.10`. It adds a `types` condition to only `./test` and a 13-line declaration using the already-declared Convex peer, the concrete upstream component schema, and the adapter's component-registration protocol. The default export still resolves to the original TypeScript implementation. Vitest/Vite transforms and executes that source, erasing its development-only type references.

This avoids introducing dependency edges for erased types or accidentally exposing backend dependencies inside upstream packages. Resolution probes prove backend owns `convex-test`, Vitest owns Vite, and both remain unavailable from AuthKit's real package path. Runtime source is byte-for-byte unchanged. No dependency versions or managed slots change, and isolated linking with `hoist=false` remains canonical.

Preset generation and the focused native `1.0.2-authkit-test` Nx migration share the same installer. Keenko owns only the exact `patchedDependencies` mapping and patch asset. Unrelated mappings, assets, dependencies and consumer state remain project-owned. Conflicts fail before writes, and canonical reruns do nothing. Nx discovers/orders migrations; migrations never edit `bun.lock`; Bun's unconditional second install applies the patch and reconciles the lock.

The npm artifact includes the migration factory, compatibility installer and patch asset. Tests use those packed files in real consumers. Generated guidance explains future removal when upstream fixes the package: stop generating the correction and use a focused native migration to remove only recognized owned state, preserving historical assets while direct supported upgrades need them. The regression removes the mapping/asset and runs ordinary Bun installation, restoring the original errors without manually editing the lock or cleaning `node_modules`.

## Verification

Canonical evidence uses Bun **1.4.2** and Node **24.21.0**.

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused AuthKit, migration and preset suites | 334 passed, 0 failed; 1,028 assertions |
| Strengthened isolated AuthKit regression | 1 passed, 0 failed; 29 assertions; includes initial failure, strict declaration check, runtime fixture typecheck, default/custom registration and actual component queries, frozen/ordinary reinstall and removal proof |
| `bun run check` | 400 passed, 0 failed; 1,724 assertions; format, lint, typecheck, build/pack check and release-version checks pass |
| `bun run test:product` | Fresh target plus all 6 historical upgrades completed; 27 AuthKit proof executions, each with 2 real component-query tests, totaling 54 passing AuthKit runtime tests |
| Fresh isolated target | Install, codegen, lint, typecheck, tests, build, strict AuthKit declarations, normal backend typecheck, frozen and ordinary idempotent reinstall passed; no phantom fallback directory |
| Actual released 1.0.1 forward upgrades | Untouched, divergent dependency slots, renamed application, and 3-app consumers all passed |
| Additional published RC upgrades | rc.0 and rc.1 consumers passed |
| Managed dependency convergence | 75 slot instances for 1 app, 107 for 2 apps, 139 for 3 apps; consumer-owned dependency state preserved |
| Migration reruns | Patch/manifests/linker/lock and resolution unchanged; real AuthKit queries pass again |
| Package artifact | Actual tarball inspected; required metadata, factory, installer and patch present, with matching patch bytes |
| Release calculation | Exactly `1.0.2-rc.2` + `prerelease` = `1.0.2-rc.3`; plan check passes |
| Diff checks | `git diff --check` and staged diff check pass |

The 1.0.1 consumers were created from the actual released package without pre-normalizing them. Each ran the canonical locally packed candidate lifecycle:

```sh
bun x nx migrate keenko@<local-candidate>
bun install
bun x nx migrate --run-migrations
bun install
bun x nx sync
bun run codegen
bun run check
```

The second install is unconditional. No manual dependency correction or `node_modules` cleanup was needed. Historical Confect generated files are regenerated by canonical codegen before the added full-backend AuthKit check, as required by that lifecycle.

The final product invocation used `BUN_CONFIG_MAX_HTTP_REQUESTS=16` to avoid intermittent registry-proxy 404s encountered during earlier historical installs. This is an invocation-only network concurrency setting; no repository or consumer installation policy changed. Expected scoped Verdaccio shutdown messages appear after the final completed phase. Existing lint/API and peer warnings remain non-failing.

There is exactly one KEE-53 version plan. It uses Nx's native `__default__: prerelease` key: the supplied unquoted `**default**` spelling is invalid YAML and cannot be consumed by Nx. The actual dry-run calculation is rc.3. Package version remains rc.2 until the normal release workflow consumes the plan.

## Final file classification

- **Compatibility baseline:** `src/compatibility/files/workos-authkit-0.2.10.patch`.
- **Generated-state ownership:** `src/compatibility/authkit-test.ts`, `src/generators/preset/preset.ts`.
- **Focused migration:** `migrations.json`, `src/migrations/authkit-test-1-0-2.ts`.
- **Regression proof:** migration/preset specs, `tests/authkit-test.spec.ts`, both AuthKit fixture templates, `tests/fixtures/product-resolution.mjs.template`, `tests/packed-product.ts`.
- **Version plan:** `.nx/version-plans/kee-53-authkit-test.md`.
- **Temporary ownership documentation:** generated `docs/core/dependencies.md` source and `docs/packed-product-test.md`.

No unrelated cleanup, Anoulà changes, or rejected ANO-27 implementation was used. Nearby multi-app, managed-slot, linker, Vitest exclusion, Effect lint, Confect guidance, registry convergence and release-note coverage remains passing.

Remaining maintenance risk is the version-specific declaration, which must be replaced by verified upstream support when available. This establishes local packed-consumer acceptance only. Nothing was merged or published; published-package acceptance and ANO-27 dogfood remain deferred.

Reference: KEE-53.

author: bumbumei
body:
> memory64 PR(#112) 위에 쌓은 PR입니다. 이 PR에서 리뷰하실 변경은 마지막 커밋(e57fb3f) 하나입니다. memory64 PR이 머지되면 rebase하겠습니다.

## 문제

큰 Gerber 파일을 열면 파싱이 끝날 때까지 로딩 창이 `Parsing · 0 / 1 · 0%`에 멈춰 있습니다. 진행 막대가 "다 읽은 파일 수 / 전체 파일 수"만 반영하기 때문입니다.

- flash 300만 개(57 MiB) 파일 하나를 열면 로딩 5.4초 가운데 4.5초 동안 화면이 바뀌지 않았습니다.
- 24M 패드 샘플은 wasm32 시도와 memory64 재파싱이 로딩 37초의 대부분을 차지하는데, 그동안 아무것도 바뀌지 않았습니다.

## 변경

- **파서 진행률 보고 (Rust)**
  - `GerberParser`에 `progress` callback을 추가했습니다. #111의 streaming parser 루프에서 파일을 1 MiB 읽을 때마다 보고합니다.
  - step-and-repeat처럼 명령 하나가 shape 수천 개를 만드는 경우에는 shape가 262,144개 늘 때마다 보고합니다.
  - 읽은 위치는 command slice의 시작 주소로 계산하므로, 미리 명령 수를 세지 않습니다.
  - `finish_layers`가 render buffer를 만드는 동안에는 shape 수 기준으로 보고합니다.
  - callback이 없으면 명령마다 `Option` 검사 하나, shape마다 나머지 연산 하나가 추가됩니다. 결과가 같은지는 테스트로 확인했습니다.
- **새 export**
  - `parse_gerber_layer_payload_with_progress(content, offset_x, offset_y, preserve_arc_regions, quality, collect_interactions, on_progress)`
  - 진행률을 `on_progress(stage, done, total)`로 전달하고, 결과를 JS로 복사하기 직전에 `packing` 단계를 알립니다.
  - 기존 export의 이름과 arity는 그대로입니다(`wasm-abi.test.mjs` 통과).
- **파싱 워커**
  - 새 export가 있으면 그것으로 파싱하고, `{ id, progress }` 메시지를 0.1초에 최대 한 번 보냅니다. 단계가 바뀔 때와 끝날 때는 항상 보냅니다.
  - picking을 끈 경우에도 같은 export를 씁니다.
- **로딩 창**
  - 파싱 중인 레이어의 진행률을 막대에 반영하고 퍼센트를 표시합니다. 여러 레이어를 병렬로 파싱하면 레이어별 진행률을 합칩니다.
  - 단계별 비율은 측정값으로 정했습니다. 명령 85%, render buffer 5%, 복사 10%이고, 레이어 하나에서 파싱이 95%, renderer 추가가 5%입니다.
  - memory64 워커가 다시 파싱하면 단계 이름이 `Parsing again with memory64`로 바뀌고, 진행률이 처음부터 다시 올라갑니다.
- **오래 걸리는 메인 스레드 작업 전 화면 갱신**
  - render data가 32 MiB 이상인 레이어를 renderer에 추가하기 전과 picking 인덱스를 만들기 전에, 브라우저가 실제로 그린 뒤 작업을 시작합니다. `requestAnimationFrame` 다음에 `setTimeout`을 한 번 더 기다립니다.
  - 기존처럼 `requestAnimationFrame`만 기다리면, 이어지는 코드가 그 프레임의 style·layout·paint보다 먼저 실행됩니다. Long Animation Frames API로 확인한 결과, 300 ms 동안 막는 코드 뒤에 style·layout이 시작됐습니다. 그래서 새 단계 이름이 작업이 끝난 뒤에야 보였습니다.
  - 숨겨진 탭에서는 프레임이 오지 않으므로 기다리지 않고 바로 진행합니다.

## 측정 (Intel Iris Xe, Chromium 151, 혼합 구성)

| 파일 | 첫 진행률 표시 | 단계별 시간 |
|-|-|-|
| flash 300만 개 (57 MiB) | 0.5초 | 명령 3.2초 / buffer 0.2초 / 복사 0.3초 |
| SR 패드 600만 개 (15 KiB) | 0.1초 | 0.2초 간격으로 갱신 |

callback이 없는 경로(`parse_gerber_layer_payload_with_options`, 파서 단독 측정)는 memory64 PR과 같은 시간입니다. flash 459 → 462 ms, track 345 → 344 ms, region 513 → 506 ms, pad 225 → 220 ms이고, 같은 실행에서 교대로 잰 7회 중앙값입니다. callback이 있으면 워커가 0.1초에 최대 한 번 메시지를 보냅니다.

## 남은 한계

- wasm32만 쓰는 브라우저(Safari, `?wasm=32`)에서 파일 하나만 열면, 지금처럼 메인 인스턴스에서 파싱합니다. 그동안 페이지가 멈추므로 진행률을 그릴 수 없습니다. 파일이 둘 이상이면 워커에서 파싱하므로 진행률이 나옵니다.
- renderer 추가와 picking 인덱스 생성은 단계 이름만 보이고, 그 안의 퍼센트는 없습니다.
- ODB++ 레이어는 명령 단계 보고가 없어서 render buffer 단계부터 올라갑니다.

## 테스트

- **Rust**: 진행 보고 테스트 3개를 추가했습니다. 바이트·shape 기준 보고, SR 블록, callback 유무에 따른 결과 동일을 확인합니다. `cargo test` 230개와 clippy를 통과했습니다.
- **Playwright**
  - `loading-progress.spec.mjs`: 파싱 중 5%에서 90% 사이 값이 3번 이상 표시되는지, 진행률이 거꾸로 가지 않는지 확인합니다.
  - `memory64.spec.mjs`: memory64 재파싱 때 단계 이름이 바뀌는지 확인합니다.
  - 전체 결과(`wasm32`, `memory64`, `memory64-binary` 프로젝트, 245개): 225개 통과, heavy 1개 건너뜀, 19개 실패.
    - 17개: main에서도 실패하는 composite-viewer 9종입니다.
    - 2개: odb-import 80행과 anti-aliasing-composition 140행입니다. 여러 worker로 동시에 실행할 때만 실패했고, 단독 실행에서 3회씩 통과했습니다.
