author: jabez007
body:
## Summary

The published 0.4.0 doesn't work from CommonJS, even though the README's first example uses `require`. The package has `"type": "module"`, so Node loads `dist/cjs/*.js` as ESM, and `require("@jabez007/cryptotron.js")` fails with `Cannot find module './utils/cryptanalysis.js'`. attw on 0.4.0 reports:

- node16 from CJS: "ESM (dynamic import only)" and "Unexpected module syntax" on both entry points
- node10: `./lite` doesn't resolve

The `import` and `require` conditions also share one set of declarations in `dist/types`, which TypeScript reads as ESM.

## Changes

- `build:cjs` writes `dist/cjs/package.json` with `{"type":"commonjs"}`.
- `tsconfig.commonjs.json` and `tsconfig.esm.json` each emit declarations and declaration maps next to their JavaScript.
- `exports` gives `import` and `require` their own `types` and `default` for `.` and `./lite`. The top-level `types` now points at `dist/cjs/index.d.ts`.
- `typesVersions` maps `lite` to `dist/cjs/lite.d.ts`, so `moduleResolution: node` consumers can import `./lite`.
- The separate `dist/types` build (`build:types`, `postbuild`, `tsconfig.types.json`) is removed.
- `baseUrl` is gone from `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.test.json`, and `paths` entries are relative. Deno 2.9 type-checks with TypeScript 6 and fails `deno publish --dry-run` on `baseUrl` with TS5101, so `deno_dry_run` would fail on `development` too.
- `scripts/check-package.mjs` and `npm run check:package` pack the package and install the tarball in a scratch project. The script loads both entry points with `require()` and `import` and checks for real exports and no stray `default`. It then type-checks a consumer under node10, node16, nodenext, and bundler and confirms which declaration file tsc picks. A new `check_package` CI job runs it.

## Test plan

- [x] Before the fix: `check:package` fails on `require` with `Cannot find module './utils/cryptanalysis.js'`
- [x] After the fix: `require, import, and types verified for node10, node16, nodenext, and bundler`
- [x] `attw --pack .`: no problems found for either entry point
- [x] `npm test`: 200 passing. Two runs on a busy machine had one failure each, the 2-second mocha timeout on dynamically loading quadgram data, and a rerun passed. This PR doesn't touch `src`.
- [x] `npm run lint:check` passes
- [x] `deno publish --dry-run` with Deno 2.9.6: TS5101 before, passes after
- [ ] CI

author: cristicretu
body: Settings › Usage now answers "how much do I work" with a GitHub-style calendar heatmap, plus a weekday × hour heatmap that shows *when*. Both are ported from Ely's `CalendarHeatmap` / `HeatmapChart` and adapted to diri's tokens. They work in light and dark. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | Tooltips (day, dark; rhythm slot, light): ## Why these charts (what data diri has) - Local Claude Code / Codex / Cursor usage is kept **per model, per epoch hour** (tokens split by input/output/cache, cost, reasoning). It is retained for **181 days** and only while the transcript files exist. - Remote machines send **per-model UTC-day** totals for the last 91 days. - No session status or working-time history is stored. So "how much you work" = **active hours**: hours with any agent usage, taken from the hourly local data. The calendar can also be coloured by **tokens** or **cost**. The calendar spans the retained history (27 weeks: 181 days plus the current week), not a year. Days the ledger never kept are left blank, not drawn as idle. I chose 2 charts and left the existing cumulative chart as it was, so the page doesn't get crowded. ## What changed - `diri-usage/src/transcripts/activity.rs` (new, pure): - Local-day binning with a per-hour zone offset, so DST days hold 23 or 25 hours. - Weeks start on the configured day; the grid ends on today. - Weekday × local-hour rhythm. - Streaks and month columns. - `IntensityScale`: 5 steps by quantile (mid-rank), so one heavy day doesn't wash out the others. - Remote day buckets keep their UTC date and add tokens and cost, never hours. - `UsageSnapshot::remote_sources`: the source selection that `history_for_source` already did, moved into a shared helper. - `diri-app/src/usage_activity.rs` (new): - Calendar and rhythm painted as quads on one canvas each. - Absolute labels and a hit-tested hover. - Opaque deferred tooltip and a Less–More key. - Hours / Tokens / Cost switch. - Week start comes from `NSCalendar.firstWeekday` (adds the `NSCalendar` feature to objc2-foundation; no new crates). - Bins are cached per snapshot, source and week start. - `usage_page.rs`: one call site, and `usage_control` / `provider_color` changed to `pub(super)`. - `surface_shell.rs`: new state fields, plus screenshot fixture options `DIRI_VISUAL_ACTIVITY`, `DIRI_VISUAL_ACTIVITY_HOVER=day:|slot:` and `DIRI_VISUAL_HEIGHT`. ## Tests - `cargo test -p diri-usage`: 40 passed. New tests cover: - fixed-offset day placement - US DST spring/fall (23 h and 25 h days; 01:00 counted twice) - Monday vs Sunday week boundaries - empty days - leap day 2028-02-29 - remote date handling - quantile levels: spread, ties, skew, NaN - streaks and month labels - `cargo test -p diri-app`: 1263 passed, 67 ignored. Adds hit-testing and title tests. - `cargo clippy -p diri-usage -p diri-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean. - Screenshots come from `render_usage_settings_preview_screenshot`: headless, fixture data, and the machine's local zone and week start. ## Known gaps - Calendar spans ~6 months because that is what the ledger keeps. A full year would need longer retention and a cache that outlives deleted transcripts. - Remote machines have no hourly data, so with a remote-only source the Hours option and the rhythm are hidden (a caption says why). - Hours are binned by the hour they started in, so in half-hour time zones an hour can land on the neighbouring local hour. - The before shot uses the old 60-day fixture; the after shots use the new 26-week activity fixture, so the hero numbers differ. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: martinhavel
body:
## What changed

Everything is behind `HOSTED_QUOTA_LADDER` (read once at boot in each `http.ts`; only `"1"` turns it on; unset/`0` = today).

**WP1 anonymousQuotaStore** - `consume(ip, now, calls, {namespace, ladder, allowlisted})`. Ladder: daily key `lookup:d:`(IPv4 exact | IPv6 /64), 30-day key `lookup:m:`(IPv4 /24 | IPv6 /64), DD `dd:d:` daily only; HMAC'd into the existing `anonymous_tool_days` table (no schema change). Normal 50/day AND 250 per last 30 UTC days (`utc_day > day-30`); allowlisted 500/day, no 30-day cap; DD 100/day, independent. Both increments in one `.immediate()` transaction (rejected batch spends nothing). Own IPv6 `::` expander (`expandIpv6`), not `icoTracker.ipPrefix`. Retention is now 30 days in both modes. Unparseable IP in ladder mode throws -> 503 (fail closed).

**WP2 tokenStore** - `new TokenStore(path, {ladder})`. Free quota = ladder ? row.monthly_quota : 2000; only 500/2000 accepted, anything else -> `TOKEN_NOT_FOUND`; remaining clamped >= 0; `lookupLimit = quota + paid`. Applied in `allocateIdentity` and `settleReservation`.

**WP3 boundary** - `createHostedToolQuota` gets `ladder` + `anonAllowlist` options (wired in ares/cnb/isir/dd `http.ts`; DD gets namespace `dd`, others `lookup`). Allowlist parsed once with `node:net` BlockList; invalid entry throws at startup. 429 text and `X-Anonymous-Quota-*` come from the bucket actually hit (50 / 250 / 500 / 100). Registered headers already derive from `lookupLimit` (500/2000 + paid).

**WP6 SQL** - `packages/shared/migrations/lookup-free-500-transition.sql` + `-inverse.sql` (param `:T0`, epoch ms). Not run anywhere.

## How flag=0 preserves behaviour
- `anonymousQuotaStore.test.ts`: all 3 pre-existing tests unchanged and green; new `legacy mode stores the old HMAC(ip) key and keeps 30 days of rows` proves key == old HMAC(ip).
- `hostedToolQuotaLadder.test.ts`: `ladder off (today): lookup and DD share one 100/day bucket per exact IP`, `ladder off: legacy lookup 429 text is unchanged`, `malformed ... ignored when ladder is off`.
- Pre-existing `hostedToolQuota.test.ts` / `tokenStore.test.ts` pass unmodified (flag off by default).
- `tokenStore.test.ts`: `2000 row is unchanged with ladder on`.

## Tests
shared 28 files / 325 tests pass; ares 58, cnb 23, isir 11, dd 147 (1 skipped, pre-existing) pass; `npm run build` (tsc, all workspaces) clean.

## Deviations / not done
- Spec: "ladder off + 500 row -> 2000". Today a 500 row throws TOKEN_NOT_FOUND; I followed the spec (rollback-safe), so that one state differs from today. No 500 rows exist before WP6 runs.
- Allowlist is validated only when ladder is on (a typo in an unused env var must not change flag=0 behaviour).
- HTTP tests use the shared-module harness (like the existing hostedToolQuota test) with X-Forwarded-For for IP, not the real `http.ts` entry points (those need full MCP server wiring).
- Monthly-bucket `resetAt`/Retry-After = oldest counted day + 30d (when the first slot frees), not when the whole batch fits.
- Inverse SQL also flips pre-existing 500 rows created before T0 (documented in file/test). Registered 429 text unchanged (no numbers in it). Ladder-mode anonymous CTA says "free monthly lookup allowance" without a number.
- docker-compose.yml, workflows, secrets, production untouched. Env vars `HOSTED_QUOTA_LADDER` / `HOSTED_ANON_ALLOWLIST` are not yet set anywhere.

---

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QeQDQEzXFRRcjviQgA6b3U


## WP4 - compose wiring (supersedes #51)
- `docker-compose.yml` ares/cnb/isir/dd: explicit `HOSTED_TOOL_QUOTAS=${HOSTED_TOOL_QUOTAS:-1}` (default equals live, a plain deploy never turns quotas off), `HOSTED_QUOTA_LADDER=${HOSTED_QUOTA_LADDER:-0}`, `HOSTED_ANON_ALLOWLIST=${HOSTED_ANON_ALLOWLIST:-}`.

author: willholmeswastaken
body: ## Summary Cloudflare Workers Builds fails `bun run deploy` with: ``` The name in your wrangler.json file (wub) must match the name of your Worker. ``` `cf` prints that for two cases: the Worker named in the build output does not exist, or its script tag does not match `WRANGLER_CI_MATCH_TAG`. The connected script is already `wub`, which is the name in `cloudflare.config.ts`, so this check is blocking a deploy to the right Worker. - Build the Worker with `WRANGLER_CI_OVERRIDE_NAME` when Workers Builds sets it, so the deployed name is the connected Worker. - Run `cf deploy` without `WRANGLER_CI_MATCH_TAG`. That variable is what turns a matching name into this error. Wrangler applies the override itself; `cf deploy --prebuilt` does not. ## Test - With no override, the config name stays `wub`. - With `WRANGLER_CI_OVERRIDE_NAME=wub-production`, the config name is `wub-production`. - Format check passed.

body:
## Summary

Finish the interface/documentation organization item from the 1.0 audit:

- Default project CLI arguments to the current working directory, preserving the first option when no path is given. Explicit project directories, configuration YAMLs, and saved plans remain supported.
- Allow `init <project_name>` / `setup_project <project_name>` to create a project in the current directory. Keep project names required, existing-configuration overwrite protection, and retry/cancel confirmation flags.
- Document that existing-project defaults require `project_config.yaml` in the current directory; parent directories are not searched, and saved plans require an explicit path.
- Organize the pkgdown reference around setup, execution, monitoring/recovery, QC, provenance, and advanced tools. Mark the unexported SQLite helper's documentation as internal.
- Remove `diagnose_pipeline()` and its export/help page without a compatibility wrapper. Keep guided and structured diagnosis in `diagnose_project()`; the CLI command remains `diagnose`.
- Update README, command help, vignettes, generated documentation, and NEWS.

Also include the previously requested setup-workflow integration tests in a separate commit. These cover Flywheel, DICOM, BIDS, existing fMRIPrep derivatives, custom setup, headless continuation, and existing-project inspection, following up on #91 and #94. They exercise real setup, configuration round trips, validation, discovery, and previews with mocked user input and external execution boundaries. The real-project preview smoke test remains opt-in and read-only.

## CLI example

```bash
cd /project/my_study
BrainGnomes run --steps=fmriprep --dry-run
BrainGnomes status
BrainGnomes diagnose --interactive
BrainGnomes config validate --steps=fmriprep --format=json
```

## Validation

- `devtools::document()` completed; generated documentation is included.
- Full `devtools::test()`: **3,245 passing assertions, 0 failures, 0 warnings, 3 opt-in skips** (Slurm integration, real-project preview, and Quarto rendering).
- Full `devtools::check()` / `--as-cran`: **0 errors, 1 warning, 2 notes**. Tests, examples, and vignette rebuilds pass. The warning is missing `qpdf`; the notes are unavailable system-clock verification and the existing `-Wconversion` compiler flag. The check exits nonzero because its warning threshold is enforced.
- Installed-package tests: **3,238 passing assertions, 0 failures, 0 warnings, 4 skips**. The extra skip is the source-only pkgdown configuration contract.
- pkgdown reference index and reference pages build successfully, with all public topics covered.
- `git diff --check` passes; the submitted source matches the locally validated snapshot.

New CLI regressions cover omitted paths, options-first calls, explicit YAML overrides, paths with spaces, aliases, parseable JSON, no parent-directory discovery, overwrite protection, unknown-option rejection, and retry/cancel confirmation requirements. Guided diagnosis tests now exercise `diagnose_project()` directly and assert the removed alias is absent.

No real scheduler submissions or container processing were performed. The separate, pre-existing numeric CLI subject-ID coercion issue (for example, `--subject-filter=02`) is not changed here.

## 摘要

## 開工前的清單核對
在 main be65422 列出「還沒有 doctype 或 lang 的文章頁」，共 9 篇：
- 本批 5 篇：doctype 和 lang 都沒有。
- goliath-vs-goliath：有 doctype、沒有 lang，本批只補 lang。
- ai-full-stack-moat：有 doctype、沒有 lang，併進第三批。
- stablecoin-is-a-dollar-promise、physics-is-the-law：都沒有，留給第三批。

## 開工清單（照「開工清單」技能）

### 一、先想清楚
1. **要做什麼**：6 篇早期長文改成標準模式並宣告繁體中文（goliath 只補語言），版面只能出現已接受的小位移，其他差異要列出來。
2. **給誰用**：白話科技的讀者（主要用手機），以及用螢幕報讀器或翻譯工具讀這些頁面的人。
3. **使用情境**：讀者在 390 像素寬的手機上讀 6 到 8 頁的長文，有淺色、系統深色、強制深色三種配色，也有人用 1280 寬的桌機。
4. **現況確認**：2026-10-04 20:42（台北）打開正式站 https://ioksengtan.github.io/too_much_to_learn/ 的這 6 篇，全部回應 200，而且和 main be65422 逐位元組一致。5 篇是相容模式（BackCompat）、沒有 lang；goliath 是標準模式、沒有 lang。
5. **畫面或流程**：讀者從首頁點卡片進文章 → 用分頁列或進度條翻頁 → 讀到案例區和最後一頁的收尾框。這次流程不變。
6. **資料或後端變更**：無。只在 6 個 HTML 檔的開頭加一到兩行。
7. **實作計畫**：
   1. 從 main be65422 開分支 product/doctype-batch-2。
   2. 5 篇在開頭加兩行，goliath 在第 2 行加 lang。
   3. 修改前、修改後各架一個本機站。每篇每一頁都在 390 淺色、390 系統深色、390 強制深色、1280 淺色四種情況下截整頁圖，等圖片和字型載入完才截，並逐元素比對高度。
   4. guild-ai-control-plane 和 ai-team-collab 逐頁看前後對照，檢查圖片底部空隙、行內元素、表格和自訂版型區塊。
   5. 預期外的差異列成清單、附截圖、提出最小修法；只有能在該篇自己的 `<style>` 裡完全還原時才修。
   6. 全站重查：`?v=`、閱讀進度鍵、首頁篩選。
   7. 拉取請求從草稿轉正式並合併（**由 Yu-Sheng 決定；合並前先改標題，squash 時用 `--subject`**）。
   8. 部署後驗證（合並後才做）。

### 二、完成標準
- [x] 6 篇都是標準模式（CSS1Compat），lang 是 zh-Hant，四種情況下都能正常閱讀。
- [x] 390 寬時每一頁 `scrollWidth` 都等於 390，1280 寬時也沒有溢出；沒有空白頁，也沒有破圖。
- [x] 改到的 6 個檔案在本機修改後的站上都回應 200（站內連結沒有改）。
- [ ] 拉取請求轉正式並合併、網站部署換成新版（草稿，還沒做）。
- [ ] 上線三樣證據（合並後才補）。
- [x] 需要持續更新的東西：無。

### 三、風險與不做的事
- **風險**：
  - 標準模式下，小字行內元素的那一行會被撐高。
  - 語言屬性會讓字型套用繁體中文的字形，標點寬度可能改變，造成換行。
  - 兩項都已逐頁、逐元素比對過，結果見下面。
- **不做的事**：
  - 不動共用檔案，不改 `?v=`，不改任何文字內容。
  - 不處理 ai-full-stack-moat、stablecoin、physics。
  - 不轉正式、不合並。
  - 預期外差異這次不修，交給 PM 決定。

### 四、提交前自我審查
1. **逐行看改動**：`git diff` 只有 5 行 `+<!doctype html>` 和 6 行 `+<html lang="zh-Hant">`，都在各檔第 1 到 2 行，沒有其他改動。
2. **公開內容**：沒有改畫面文字；沒有真名、私人資料或密碼。
3. **五項自評**：準確 5、完整 4（合並與上線證據要等合並後才能補）、清楚 4、可執行 4、精簡 4。
4. **回報用語**：這是草稿，還沒合並，不能說「上線」。

## 比對結果
- **比對對象**：修改前是 main be65422，修改後是這個分支。
- **比對範圍**：6 篇（共 38 頁）× 4 種情況 × 修改前後 2 版，約 300 張整頁截圖，逐元素比對高度。截圖前先把圖片改成立即載入，並等 `document.fonts.ready`。

**頁高差異（修改後減修改前，單位是像素）**

| 文章 | 390（三種配色都一樣） | 1280 淺色 |
|---|---|---|
| how-do-we-know-ai-decisions-work（6 頁） | 第 1 到 5 頁 +4，第 6 頁 +11 | 第 1 到 5 頁 +5，第 6 頁 +13 |
| jev-decisions-for-software（6 頁） | 第 1 到 5 頁 +4，第 6 頁 +11 | 第 1 到 5 頁 +5，第 6 頁 +13 |
| who-controls-the-ai-future（8 頁） | 第 1 到 7 頁 +4，第 8 頁 +27 | 第 1 到 7 頁 +5，第 8 頁 +21 |
| guild-ai-control-plane（6 頁） | +4、+4、+4、**+11**、+4、+41 | +5、+5、+5、**+13**、+5、+31 |
| ai-team-collab（6 頁） | +4、+4、+4、**+43**、+4、+35 | +5、+5、**+35**、+13、+5、+25 |
| goliath-vs-goliath（只補 lang） | 每頁 0 | 每頁 0 |

**已接受的三種差異**（4 到 8 像素的中性間距）
- **返回連結那一行**：390 是 +4，1280 是 +5，出現在每一頁的頂端。
- **收尾框眉標那一行**：390 是 +7，1280 是 +8，出現在最後一頁。
- **案例卡編號那一行**：每張卡 +4。guild 的第 06 張卡是 +6，因為這張卡的編號「06 Agent Hub」全是英文、字比較矮，被撐高得多一點，仍在 4 到 8 像素之內。1280 是兩欄排版，每一列的增加量取那一列最高的卡。
- 頁高的對帳：
  - who-controls 第 8 頁：390 是 4＋4 張卡×4＋7＝27。
  - guild 第 6 頁：390 是 4＋6 張卡×4＋6＋7＝41；1280 是 5＋4＋4＋6＋4＋8＝31。

## 預期外差異（列出來但沒有修，請 PM 決定）

### 1. 案例區開頭的眉標「實際案例」那一行變高 7 像素（1280 是 8 像素）
- **在哪裡**：guild-ai-control-plane 第 4 頁、ai-team-collab 第 4 頁的 `.case-head`。每種情況都有。
- **原因**：和收尾框眉標是同一個機制。行內的小字 `span.eyebrow`（12.96px）所在的那一行，在標準模式下被父層字級的支柱撐高。只是位置在案例區開頭，不在收尾框裡，所以不屬於已接受的三種差異。
- **影響**：眉標和標題之間多 7 像素留白，沒有重疊、裁切或換行改變。
- **截圖**：`sbs-unexpected-guild-390-light-p4-case-head.png`、`sbs-unexpected-ai-team-collab-390-light-p4-case-head.png`
- **最小修法**：在兩篇自己的 `<style>` 裡加 `.case-head>.eyebrow{display:block}`，再依原本的位置調整上下間距。
- **為什麼沒修**：改成區塊元素後，原本不起作用的上下外距會開始生效，要逐一調數值，不能保證像素完全還原。而且收尾框眉標是同一個機制、已經被接受，只修這裡反而不一致。**建議把它當作第四種已接受差異。**

### 2. 破折號「——」改成全形寬度，ai-team-collab 有兩段因此多換一行（+31.5 和 +29.8 像素）
- **在哪裡**：
  - ai-team-collab 390 第 4 頁的「技術草案原本建議用一套現成的雲端資料庫服務……」，最後多了一行「省。」，三種配色都一樣。
  - ai-team-collab 1280 第 3 頁的「AI 團隊做事的過程中……」，最後多了一行「開。」。
- **原因**：不是 doctype 造成的，是語言屬性造成的。加上 `lang="zh-Hant"` 後，網頁字型 Noto Sans TC 改用繁體中文字形，破折號每個字從 13.15 像素變成 15.69 像素（一個全形字寬）。這是繁體中文標準的破折號寫法：兩個全形字寬、置中。一行若剛好排滿，就會多出一個字被擠到下一行。
- **其他文章**：guild（26 處）、goliath（23 處）、jev（2 處）、who-controls（1 處）也有破折號，寬度一樣變了，但都沒有造成換行或頁高改變，只是那幾行字的水平位置略有移動。
- **截圖**：`sbs-unexpected-ai-team-collab-390-light-p4-emdash-reflow.png`、`sbs-unexpected-ai-team-collab-1280-light-p3-emdash-reflow.png`
- **可能的修法**（都沒有做）：
  - 在文章自己的 `<style>` 關掉在地化字形，例如 `font-feature-settings:"locl" 0`，或改成比例寬度。這樣會連同其他繁體中文字形一起還原，等於抵消加 lang 的好處，影響範圍也比這兩段大。
  - 改寫這兩段讓換行回到原樣。但這要改文章內文，不在這次範圍內。
- **建議**：接受。全形破折號才是正確的繁體中文排版，只是兩段各多一行。

## 其他檢查
- **模式與語系**：6 篇修改後都是 CSS1Compat，lang 是 zh-Hant。
- **水平溢出**：每一頁的 `scrollWidth` 都等於視窗寬度，沒有破圖。
- **圖片、表格與自訂版型**：圖片和 figure 的高度、底部空隙都沒有變（逐元素比對沒有任何圖片元素變高）。這 6 篇沒有表格。時間軸、案例區、svg 圖都只有上面列出的變化。
- **分頁**：6 頁的文章顯示 1 / 6 到 6 / 6，who-controls 顯示 1 / 8 到 8 / 8，都正常。
- **主控台**：只有本機站的 favicon.ico 404。
- **後備字型**：用 IBM Plex Mono 的中文字（返回連結、眉標、案例卡編號），補字的後備字型從 Noto Sans CJK JP（日文字形）改成 Noto Sans CJK TC（繁體中文字形）。
- **全站重查**：
  - 站內 89 個 `?v=` 連結 0 個不一致。
  - 閱讀進度鍵 23 個，各自唯一。
  - 首頁篩選是 23、4、4、5、10。

## 截圖
都在作業機器的 `/workspace/doctype-batch-2/shots/`（沒有放進儲存庫）：
- 預期外差異：`sbs-unexpected-*.png`（4 張）
- 已接受差異的示範：`sbs-accepted-guild-390-light-p6-case-card-06.png`、`sbs-accepted-guild-390-light-p6-closing.png`

author: lioreshai
body:
Refs #216 — record coverage moves from 6 probes to 7; `contrast`, `mip`, `columns`, `scene` and the rest of the computed-verdict blocks still have no row behind their numbers.

## Premise correction, before anything else

My own brief said "13 records in 6 of **26** probes". On `main` it reads **6 of 25** — and `alt` is not an unrecorded block at all: it already declares **4** records (`PIT-MEAN`, `PIT-CELLS`, `OOB-ERA`, `OOB-NONCLIMB`). So the honest shape of this increment is: **`heights` joins the roster for the first time, and `alt` gains the one quantity its verdict line prints but never pinned.** Census moves **13 → 15 records, 6 → 7 probes, "with none" 19 → 18**. `tools/refs.lock` gains two lines and loses none (`git diff --numstat` → `2 0`).

## What is recorded, and why those numbers

**`alt / GRID-CENSUS`** (`num` × 16) — per level, the four integers the gate rows actually count and the verdict line prints: *floor values / cells off datum / staircase runs / step faces*.

| level | floor values | cells off datum | staircase runs | step faces |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | 9 | 170 | 2 | 46 |
| L1 | 9 | 251 | 2 | 52 |
| L2 | 9 | 307 | 2 | 52 |
| L3 (authored) | 9 | 134 | 4 | 15 |

Unreachable cells are deliberately **not** declared: that criterion is asserted at 0 by its own row, so a record would duplicate an existing gate instead of pinning a quantity that prose quotes (the same reasoning `RECDARK` follows). Note these are `SEED 12345` values — the deal, not a law; that is the point, which is why they were measured rather than remembered.

**`heights / HALF-MOVE`** (`num` × 24) — per level, the percentage that **each config's own verdict says must move**: `tallRoom`'s ceiling half, then `pit`/`stripes`/`border`/`stepUp`/`eyeUp`'s floor halves.

| level | tallRoom ↑ | pit ↓ | stripes ↓ | border ↑ | stepUp ↓ | eyeUp ↓ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | 97.62 | 31.18 | 82.01 | 95.42 | 42.87 | 61.92 |
| L1 | 98.12 | 33.83 | 29.81 | 95.64 | 42.82 | 64.49 |
| L2 | 98.86 | 32.57 | 81.56 | 95.51 | 42.87 | 63.31 |
| L3 | 97.74 | 23.55 | 21.23 | 95.46 | 38.09 | 54.23 |

The "still" halves and `flat` are **not** recorded: those are the reference frames of a relation, and a relation is what the row asserts.

**Determinism was measured before anything was declared** — two runs each, byte-identical outputs, both exit 0. Then the knobs were walked to find out what would silently move a recorded figure: `WARM=1` moves **neither** probe; `SEED=7` moves `alt` (L0 becomes 573 open cells / 40 faces) so the row is **seed-guarded**; `SEED=7` moves **no** `heights` percentage (the block reseeds itself at `tools/view.js:5795`); `VW/VH` (97.62 → 97.33), `LAMPS=off` (→ 97.60) and `NOCAP=1` (one config 38.75 → 38.76) each guard `heights`. `JSDIR` guards **neither**, which is what makes the controls bite.

## Teeth

Controls live in `.worktrees/rec216-ctl/*/js` and run through `JSDIR=` (the harness prints the variant's `js-sha256`, so a control cannot be self-cancelling):

| run | exit | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| `alt`, clean copy (`36b879f381c35048`) | **0** | census matches |
| `alt`, `fzTry.fill(0)` after `authorVolume` (`98bd625e66e0549a`) | **1** | `L0/L1/L2 the deal is the recorded geometry census FAIL — 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 against the recorded 9 / 170 / 2 / 46 … MOVED:` |
| `heights`, ceiling reads solved against flat `1` (`0a48a2f01c2d6f53`) | **1** | `FAIL HALF-MOVE-MOVED: tallRoom ceiling 0.00 against recorded 97.62` on all four levels |

Level 3 stays green under the generation sabotage **because it is authored** — that is a correct abstention, not a hole.

Three further sabotages were **inert** and are recorded as such in the CHANGELOG rather than quietly dropped: gating the march on `absP > 8`, breaking the row-loop crossing reads, and letting `planeAlong` hand its plane. The reason is structural — `tallRoom` raises `cz` uniformly, so on that config only the row's own predictor can disagree with the record.

## The limit I could not settle, stated plainly

`HALF-MOVE` currently bites on the **row-predictor half** of the claim. A *partial* regression inside the ceiling-crossing path left all 24 percentages byte-identical in my three subtle controls, so this record does not yet cover that path — it pins the statistic, not every mechanism that computes it. And a record guarded on a knob **abstains** (prints `NOT COMPARED`) instead of failing, which means off-`SEED` deals remain unfalsifiable by design. Both belong to #216's remaining scope rather than being papered over here; a record that silently changes between runs would have been worse than no record, which is why the guards came first.

Budget: `SMOKE PASSED` (exit 0) at `/proc/loadavg 4.34 4.79 5.12`. The roster and all four controls were then re-run independently on this tree: **`REC216VERIFY: 0 failing check(s)`** over 9 — `alt` → `ALT ok - bands authored, linked, reachable, and there is volume to look at | 82 row(s), 0 known-issue row(s)`; `heights` exit 0; `refs ok - 15 recorded reference(s) in 7 of 25 probes, table agrees`; `flatparity ok - PARITY collapses to 2c5a94f with LAMPS=off, LOCK holds on the shipped lamp record`; `LEAK=1 CZBAND=1 cull` → `CULL ok`; and the controls with the variant hash each run printed — `alt` + flat grid `98bd625e…` **exit 1** (`ALT 33 FAILURES`), `heights` + flat-ceiling solves `0a48a2f0…` **exit 1** (`heights: 8 config(s) FAILED`), both against the clean copy `36b879f3…` at **exit 0**. Final smoke on that run: **`SMOKE PASSED`**, `raster: seats 0/811/90210 medians 94.3/29.6/16.9 ms | pooled median 29.65 ms | max 122.4 ms | floor 32 ms` at `/proc/loadavg 4.07 4.31 4.68` — quoted with the load, since two other PRs' probe runs shared the machine, and not offered as a frame-rate claim.

`node --check` clean. Files: `tools/view.js` +96, `tools/refs.lock` +2, `CHANGELOG.md` +43 — **pure insertion, no existing record literal or threshold touched** (`git diff --numstat`: `96 0 / 2 0 / 43 0`).

## Intent

Lets continue with the next DCF steps. Do further deep-dive / ask more questions if context is necessary.

The four-company recheck passed 416 regression tests and independent arithmetic checks, but Evolution, Clas Ohlson, Mips and Bactiguard lack qualified dated ROIC and therefore have no actual DCF valuations. Continue with qualified capital/return evidence and a narrowly scoped reinvestment-model improvement. The existing engine already charges growth when positive ROIC is available. Keep missing inputs and unsupported loss-stage valuations unavailable, rather than restoring the old numbers. The approved staged direction links growth spending to capital returns, fades terminal returns toward the hurdle and preserves reproducible results; leases, company profiles and an agent are later stages.

Yes, here are a few annotations: Mark the implied-margin solve unavailable for this slice. A solved margin that differs from the base margin breaks your own "constant margins only" rule. It can come back once there’s capital evidence for margin changes.

author: maximilian-nesslauer
body:
Closes #138

- A listing can set `since` under `[releases]` to a version such as `1.2`, and the watcher then also stamps every older release from that version on (RFC 0079).
- `since` takes the version forms of RFC 0072, so `latest`, a leading `v` and four numbers are refused.
- `since` is not a release host: `[releases]` still needs `github` or `spacedock`, and `since` does not change which host ownership binds to.
- The listing page has a field "Oldest release to list" next to the release hosts, with a hint that older releases get today's listing facts and that the owner corrects them with an amendment in content-index-releases.
- CONTRIBUTING.md and schemas/README.md describe `since` and the amendment path.

## Summary
`zerra init` now checks that the Docker daemon is reachable before `docker compose up`. If it is not, the CLI prints `Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop and try again.` and exits with code 1.

## Motivation
Fixes #30. The init command went straight to `docker compose up`. With the daemon stopped, that path can finish without a clear error (the issue reports a silent exit 0). The issue asks for a `docker info` preflight and a non-zero exit.

## Implementation
- Added `isDockerDaemonRunning()` in `cli/src/docker.ts`. It runs `docker info` with piped stdio and treats a non-zero status, a null status, or a spawn error as not running.
- `init` calls that check after the compose file is found and before compose up. The existing compose failure message is unchanged.
- Tests cover the daemon check outcomes and that init invokes the preflight before compose up. The previous CLI test asserted `infra/docker-compose.yml` and `/setup`, which are not in the current init command (it uses `compose.yaml`); that assertion was updated to the current contract.

## Testing
- `npx vitest run --reporter=verbose` in a local checkout of `cli/` with vitest 2.1.8: 5 passed (1 file).
- Did not run the full monorepo `npm ci` / `npm run test:unit` suite (requires the workspace install and Prisma generate). Did not run against a stopped Docker daemon on this machine.

### 🔗 Linked issue

Fixes #90

### 🧭 Context

Stdio targets only accepted literal environment values. Passing a token required storing it in target JSON or using a shell wrapper.

### 📚 Description

Adds `config.envFrom` to stdio targets. Each entry maps a child environment variable to a variable in the Failure Lab process.

Adds a GitHub stdio target example and links the README to the configuration guide.

### ⚠️ Behavior and limitations

- Values are resolved when the transport is created.
- `envFrom` overrides matching entries in `env`.
- Empty values are allowed.
- Missing variables fail setup before the child starts.
- Errors name the missing variable without printing its value.
- Unmapped variables are not forwarded beyond the SDK’s existing system-variable defaults.
- A target server can still log or return credentials itself.

### 🧪 Testing

Added tests for schema validation, missing variables, and passing values to a real stdio child. The child test checks overrides, literal values, empty values, and unmapped variables. It also checks that credentials are absent from the returned report.

author: ayman-metwally2020
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a complete MLOps workflow for predicting mobile network downlink throughput from cell KPIs. It covers data generation, feature management, automated training and evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and plain-language explanations of predictions using Claude on Amazon Bedrock.

## Key Changes

**Data & Features**
- `data/generate_data.py`: Synthetic telecom KPI dataset generator with realistic busy-hour load curves and feature dependencies
- `feature_store/create_feature_group.py`: SageMaker Feature Store integration for consistent train/inference feature definitions

**ML Pipeline**
- `pipelines/pipeline.py`: Orchestrates Preprocess → Train (XGBoost) → Evaluate → conditional Model Registry registration
- `pipelines/preprocess.py`: Data cleaning and train/validation/test split (70/15/15)
- `pipelines/evaluate.py`: Model evaluation computing RMSE, MAE, R² in SageMaker Model Registry format
- `pipelines/deploy.py`: Deploys latest approved model with data capture enabled for monitoring

**Monitoring & Feedback**
- `monitoring/setup_monitoring.py`: Baselines the training data, schedules hourly data-quality checks, and creates a CloudWatch drift alarm on SINR (an early indicator of radio degradation)

**GenAI Integration**
- `bedrock_genai/explain_prediction.py`: Calls Claude on Amazon Bedrock to turn numeric predictions into NOC-ready explanations (status, likely drivers, next actions)

**Testing & CI/CD**
- `tests/test_core.py`: Offline unit tests for data generation, preprocessing, evaluation, and prompt building
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: GitHub Actions CI with linting (ruff) and pytest

**Documentation & Config**
- Rewritten README with architecture diagram, quick-start guide, and illustrative example output
- `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt`: Python tooling and dependencies
- Updated folder READMEs with usage examples and design rationale
- `LICENSE`: MIT license

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Conditional registration**: A model is only registered if test RMSE ≤ a pipeline parameter, and it still requires manual approval before deployment
- **Data capture + monitoring loop**: The endpoint captures 100% of traffic. Hourly Model Monitor jobs publish drift metrics, and the CloudWatch alarm can be wired to an EventBridge rule that restarts the pipeline (that rule is not created by this PR)
- **XGBoost built-in**: Uses SageMaker's native XGBoost container (no custom image) with early stopping on the validation set
- **Bedrock prompt guardrail**: Claude is instructed to use only the KPIs provided and never invent others. Refusals (`stop_reason == "refusal"`) are handled with a fallback message
- **Deterministic splits**: Preprocessing uses a fixed random seed for reproducibility across pipeline runs

## Testing

- `ruff check .` and `pytest` (6 tests) pass locally and in CI
- Pipeline definition builds with the SageMaker Python SDK (S3 calls mocked); not yet executed against a live AWS account

# 변경 사항

MCP로 AI 에이전트가 편집 기능을 직접 호출할 수 있도록([기능명세서](docs/video-editing-functional-spec.md) 원칙), 열린 프로젝트의 상태와 편집 동작을 View에서 꺼내 창마다 하나씩 두는 `ProjectEditor`(`palladium/editing/`)로 옮겼다. 앱 동작은 바뀌지 않는다.

- `ProjectEditor`가 열린 프로젝트·마지막 저장본·마지막 백업을 소유한다
  - 커맨드: `importMedia(from:)`, `renameAsset(_:to:)`, `setColorLabel(_:for:)`, `setTags(from:for:)`, `save()`, `writeBackupIfNeeded()`, `discardBackup()`
  - 쿼리: `hasUnsavedChanges`, `asset(id:)`, `assets(matching:)`
  - 디버그 메뉴도 편집기의 디버그 전용 함수(`applyDebugChange`)를 거친다
- `MainWindowView`·`MediaPanelView`는 편집기 커맨드만 부르고, 선택·패널 표시·입력 중인 이름 같은 화면 상태만 직접 갖는다
- `ProjectWindowView`는 백업본 복구 여부를 정한 뒤 편집기를 만든다
- 문서: [코딩 컨벤션](docs/swift-coding-conventions.md)에 "편집은 편집기 커맨드로만, View는 화면 상태만, 새 기능은 커맨드부터 만들고 테스트" 규칙 추가. 유즈케이스의 관련 커맨드/쿼리를 실제 코드 이름에 맞춤

## 확인 방법

- `xcodebuild test -scheme palladium -destination 'platform=macOS' -only-testing:palladiumTests` — 통과(`ProjectEditorTests` 6개 추가: 원본 정리 커맨드, 저장 후 백업 삭제, 필요할 때만 백업, 변경 버리기, 복구한 내용으로 열기, 가져오기·중복)
- `swiftformat palladium palladiumTests --lint` — 위반 없음
- 앱 실행 회귀 확인: 가져오기(⌘I·드래그&드롭), 이름 변경(F2), 색상 레이블·태그·검색·필터, ⌘S 저장, 닫기·종료 확인, 디버그 메뉴, 강제 종료 후 복구

## 참고

- Closes #47
- MCP 서버 자체는 이번 범위에서 제외했다.

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

- No user is affected. The cost is triage noise: each new page that a wallet browser visits opens a new error tracking issue and a new inbox report.
- Wallet browsers (for example Brave on iOS) inject a script. That script throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'window.ethereum.selectedAddress = undefined')`. The site has no wallet code.
- The fingerprint includes the page path. Thus `/` and `/beaches/sebastian-inlet` already have separate issues for the same error.

## Changes

- A posthog-js `before_send` hook drops `$exception` events when an exception `value` contains `window.ethereum`.
- The hook covers both entry paths: posthog-js autocapture, and the early buffer (`flushEarlyErrors` sends through `captureException`).
- New unit tests for `isInjectedWalletError` in `src/lib/analytics.test.ts`.

> [!NOTE]
> [#50](https://github.com/alexdino2/mullet-run-ne-florida/pull/50) adds a `before_send` hook for AdSense errors on the same lines. The two PRs conflict in the text but not in behavior. To merge both, keep both helpers and use one hook:
> ```ts
> before_send: (result) =>
>   result && (isAdSenseError(result) || isInjectedWalletError(result)) ? null : result,
> ```

## How to measure

- Baseline: 24 `$exception` events that contain `window.ethereum` in the last 14 days. All 24 have this text in `$exception_list[0].value`, so the filter matches all of them.
- Goal: 0 such events in a 14-day window after the deploy, and no new issues for this error on new pages.

## Checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | Pass (15 tests, 3 new) |
| `npm run typecheck` | Pass |
| `npx next lint --file` on changed files | Pass |
| Browser test with a wallet browser | Not run. The sandbox has no iOS or Brave browser. The unit tests cover the filter, and `before_send` is the hook that [#50](https://github.com/alexdino2/mullet-run-ne-florida/pull/50) already uses. |

## Agent context

- The inbox run started in `alexdino2/super-bowl-props`. That repo has no posthog-js code, so the change is here.
- I did not edit the inline early-error buffer script. Other open PRs touch that line.

---

author: yunaremaia
body:
Fixes #44. Fixes #47.

Two independent defects, kept in separate commits.

## 1. `probe` reports a request it never sent (#44)

`EndpointProber.probe()` built its payload with `params or {}`. That tests
**truthiness**, not absence, so every falsy JSON value a caller supplied —
`[]`, `0`, `false`, `""` — was replaced by an empty object *before* the request
was issued, while `validate_method_request()` a few lines below was handed the
untouched original and named its type:

```python
payload: dict = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params or {}}   # line 508
...
for message in validate_method_request(method, params):                        # line 518 — the original
```

For a drift tool that is the failure that matters: it stops measuring what it
says it is measuring. `--params '[]'` reported *"params must be a JSON object,
got list"* and exited `0`, while the endpoint received `{}` — a different request
that may well have been accepted. The JSON-RPC conformance verdict for the run
was attributed to the wrong payload.

**Fix.** Forward what was supplied, and validate that same value, so a finding
always describes the request that was sent:

```python
payload: dict = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method}
if params is not None:
    payload["params"] = params
```

An **absent** value omits the member entirely rather than inventing `{}`:
`params` is optional in JSON-RPC 2.0, and "not supplied" is exactly what
omitting `--params` means. `--params null` also sends no member — JSON-RPC 2.0
requires `params` to be a Structured value when present, and
`validate_method_request()` already read `None` as "no params" via its own
`if params is None: params = {}`.

### The second half of the bug: `--params` could not express "not supplied"

Even with the payload fixed, `a2a-drift/cli.py` had `default="{}"` — a *truthy*
default — and `json.loads(args.params) if args.params else {}`. So "flag
omitted" and "flag given an empty object" were the same input and no downstream
`is None` test could tell them apart. The default moves to `None` and the
branching is on identity:

```python
if args.params is None:
    params = None
elif not args.params:
    params = {}
else:
    try:
        params = json.loads(args.params)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        parser.error(f"--params is not valid JSON: {e}")
```

An explicitly empty `--params ''` keeps its existing meaning (not valid JSON,
so no params content) — that behaviour is pinned by a pre-existing test that was
left green, not rewritten.

### Tests written first, and watched fail

`tests/test_jsonrpc_request_validation.py::TestProbeOmitsAbsentParams` and
`tests/test_cli_plumbing.py::TestProbeParamsReachTheWireUnchanged`, **16 tests**.
Against the unfixed tree:

```
13 failed, 3 passed in 0.14s
```

The 3 passes are the **positive controls** — a non-empty object
(`{"id": "t-1"}`, `{"id": "t"}`) and a *non-empty* array already reached the wire
verbatim under `params or {}`, so they confirm the fix does not deny everything.
They are controls, not regression coverage. One of them earned its place: my
first draft of `test_the_finding_and_the_wire_name_the_same_value` used `[1, 2]`,
which is **truthy** and therefore passed against the *unfixed* code. An empty
array — the issue's actual repro — is what fails.

The falsy-vs-unset rule needs both directions tested, so both are:

| input | `params` on the wire |
|---|---|
| `--params` omitted | member absent |
| `--params null` | member absent |
| `--params ''` | `{}` (unchanged, not valid JSON) |
| `--params '[]'` | `[]` |
| `--params '0'` | `0` |
| `--params 'false'` | `false` |
| `--params '""'` | `""` |
| `--params '{"id":"t-1"}'` | `{"id": "t-1"}` |

Each falsy case asserts the **concrete value and its type**, because `0 == False`
in Python — an equality-only assertion would pass with the wrong JSON type on
the wire.

### Verified on the wire, not just in a mock

The suite mocks HTTP, so I also ran the issue's repro: a local server that
prints the `params` field it received.

```
typed            reported finding                                server received
--params '[]'    params must be a JSON object, got list          WIRE params field: []
--params 'false' params must be a JSON object, got bool          WIRE params field: False
--params '0'     params must be a JSON object, got int           WIRE params field: 0
--params '""'    params must be a JSON object, got str           WIRE params field: ''
--params omitted params.id is required by method 'tasks/get'     WIRE params field: <ABSENT>
```

The report and the request now name the same thing, which was the whole defect.

## 2. `pip install -e '.[dev]'` installed nothing (#47)

`pyproject.toml` declared no `[project.optional-dependencies]`. Because **pip
only warns on an unknown extra and still exits 0**, the documented setup
command looked successful while providing no tools. CI hid it by naming
`pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `ruff` and `mypy` in its own install steps, and
`CONTRIBUTING.md` presented the gap as intentional.

```toml
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0",
    "ruff>=0.6.0",
    "mypy>=1.0",
]
```

The floors are the lowest versions that run *this repo's checks*, not whatever a
scratch venv resolves: pytest 7 is the first with the `testpaths`/`addopts` ini
options used here, pytest-cov 4 reports the coverage this project gates on, and
ruff 0.6 is the first release where `[tool.ruff.lint]` nests the selection that
`[tool.ruff]` previously read.

Measured on both checkouts, in a throwaway venv under
`/root/.hermes/cache/scratch/`:

| checkout | `pip install -e '.[dev]'` | tools that land |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` (`0f0d811`) | `WARNING: a2a-drift 0.1.0 does not provide the extra 'dev'`, **exit 0** | **none** |
| this branch | exit 0 | pytest 9.1.1, pytest-cov 7.1.0, ruff 0.16.10, mypy 2.4.0 |

All four run in that venv — `ruff check .` exit 0, `ruff format --check .` exit
0, `mypy` exit 0 — and the suite passes there: **274 passed**, 100% coverage.
Re-verified on Python 3.9.25, the declared floor, installed only through the
extra: **274 passed**.

`test_packaging.py` now asserts the extra is declared, that each of those four
tools is in it, and that CONTRIBUTING points at it. The strongest case parses
`ci.yml` and requires every tool CI installs **by name** to be in the extra, so
the declared dependencies and the enforced ones cannot drift apart again. It
reads `pyproject.toml` as text rather than via `tomllib` because the 3.9 leg of
the matrix has no `tomllib` (3.11+) — the same reason that file already parses
`requires-python` with regexes.

## Checks

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pytest -q --cov=a2a_drift --cov-report=term-missing` | **274 passed**, `TOTAL 501 / 0 miss / 100%`, `Required test coverage of 100.0% reached` |
| `ruff check .` | `All checks passed!` (exit 0) |
| `ruff format --check .` | `23 files already formatted` (exit 0) |
| `mypy --config-file pyproject.toml` | `Success: no issues found in 4 source files` (exit 0) |

Baseline before this branch: **251 passed**. Coverage stayed at the enforced
100% floor. CI matrix (3.9/3.10/3.11/3.12) runs on the PR.

Python 3.12.15 locally; the 3.9 floor verified separately as above.

## Left out, deliberately

- **`ci.yml` still installs the tools by name.** Switching it to
  `pip install -e ".[dev]"` is the natural follow-up and would make the declared
  extra the one CI exercises, but changing what CI installs inside a fix PR
  would confound the before/after evidence above. The new
  `test_every_tool_ci_installs_is_in_the_extra` enforces the same coupling with
  no risk.
- **No behavioural change for a non-object `--params`.** `--params '[]'` is
  still *sent* as `[]` and still exits `0` with a warning; only the payload now
  matches what the tool reported. Refusing it at the CLI boundary was the other
  option the issue offered, and it would turn a documented capability into a
  h

author: monkeygerbil222
body:
**Stacked on #38** (which is stacked on #37). Review only the commits after "Document the cost and remaining gaps of one-pass edges": `Relink existing referrers when a batch adds their targets` and `Bound mention relinks and ignore file-less stubs`.

## The gap

#38 made cross-file edges order-independent *within* a batch. Across batches there was still a gap. Edges are created by MATCH-MATCH, so an edge whose endpoint doesn't exist yet is skipped. If a referrer was indexed before its target existed, the edge was never created. A later batch (a watcher save or `index_paths`) that adds the target didn't re-link it, because no edge led from the referrer to the new node. `_expand_with_reverse_dependents` only follows existing `IMPORTS` edges. The edge only formed once the referrer itself changed or a full rescan ran.

## The fix

`index_paths` gets a "find referrers" step after pass 1 and before the re-upsert, docs and mentions passes. The files it finds join the same batch (one level, no recursion), and the existing passes link them like any other batch file.

**What counts as "added":** before pass 1, one query (`GraphEngine.list_file_nodes`) snapshots the (label, name) of the nodes the batch's files produced before. The added nodes are the batch's file-provenance nodes (code symbols and Modules, docs notes, Documents) minus that snapshot. Re-saving a file without adding a symbol therefore pulls in nothing. File-less nodes (a C++ out-of-class method's `Class` stub, API handler stubs, other `source`-keyed nodes) are left out, because they have no provenance to compare against and would look added on every save.

Each lookup kind runs only if the batch added a node with a label it can target. Each lookup reads only files outside the batch.

| Kind | Edges | Lookup | Bound / cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Docs notes | `SUPERSEDES`, `DECIDED_BY`, `links` → `DOCUMENTED_BY`/`SATISFIES` | Re-parse each docs-folder note outside the batch (pure parse, no graph access). Keep a note only if one of its edge endpoints is an added node. | Runs only if a `DesignDecision`/`ArchitectureNote`/`Module` was added. One walk of the docs folder. |
| API `IMPLEMENTS` | Endpoint → handler | One query (`find_handler_stub_sources`): file-less stub `Function`s with an added Function's name. Returns their `source`/`sources` route files. | Runs only if a Function was added. One query. |
| `MENTIONS` | Document → anything | Only Markdown already indexed for mentions and outside the batch is considered. If an added (label, name) already exists elsewhere in the graph, the referrers are the Documents that already MENTION it (one query, `find_mentioning_documents`, no text scan). Only names new to the whole graph get a text check (`mentions_any`, the extractor's own code-span / call / declaration matching). Matching files are not fully re-indexed: `index_file(..., names=...)` adds edges to just the added names. | Mentions must be enabled. At most `_MAX_MENTION_RELINKS` = 25 files per batch; above that a warning is logged and the rest link on the next rescan. The text scan stops once the cap is exceeded. |
| Java/Kotlin `EXTENDS` | same-package subtype → added class | Same-directory files with the same extension (not other source roots of the same package) whose text word-matches an added class name. Same-package subtypes need no import, so `_expand_with_reverse_dependents` can't find them, and the re-upsert pass only covered files already in the batch. | Runs only for directories where a class was added. |

**Measured cost** (300 Markdown files, half mentioning `get()` / `run()`, one watcher save of a file adding that function): ~53 s re-indexing 151 files before bounding; with graph lookup, cap and targeted relink it is 0.6 s with 25 relinks. A save that adds no name: 0.02–0.2 s, unchanged from before this PR.

**Full scans:** nothing changes. Every file is already in the batch, so the lookups find no outside files. On a rescan of a populated graph the snapshot also leaves nothing "added". The extra cost is the snapshot query plus at most one query per lookup kind.

`index_paths`' per-file try/except moved into a small local `index_one` so the referrer files go through the same isolation.

## Tests

- `test_adding_a_target_later_does_not_relink_existing_referrers` is flipped and renamed to `test_adding_a_target_later_relinks_existing_referrers`. It indexes the referrers alone, then the targets alone, and expects every cross-file edge.
- `test_each_lookup_kind_relinks_its_referrers` is parametrized per kind: docs notes, API handler stubs, mentions, Java same-package extends, Kotlin same-package extends. Each case writes only that kind's files, so a pass doesn't depend on another kind's lookup.
- Cost guard `test_batches_that_add_no_targets_index_no_extra_files`:
  - a full scan indexes each file exactly once;
  - re-indexing the unchanged target files indexes exactly those files and no referrers.
- `test_resaving_a_file_with_a_file_less_stub_indexes_no_extra_files`: re-saving a C++ file whose out-of-class method emits a `Class` stub re-indexes nothing else.
- `test_an_existing_file_gaining_a_symbol_relinks_its_referrers` (mentions, IMPLEMENTS, Java EXTENDS) covers the main watcher case: an already-indexed file gains, or is renamed to, the symbol a referrer names.
- `TestMentionRelinkBound`:
  - an added name that already exists elsewhere uses the graph path, with no text scan;
  - an added name new to the graph is text-scanned;
  - in both cases relinks stop at the cap and a warning is logged.
- The shared referrer-first fixture gains a Kotlin pair, so the full-scan test covers it too.

Full suite: **808 passed**.

## Remaining gaps

These referrers are still not re-linked when their target is added in a later batch:
- an `IMPORTS` of a newly added module (the import edge itself was skipped);
- cross-package supertypes;
- `CALLS` to a newly added function from files outside the batch;
- mentions of `source`-keyed / file-less nodes (Endpoints, Datastores, handler and C++ class stubs);
- Markdown mention referrers beyond the 25-file cap;
- deletions: nothing is relinked when a node is removed (e.g. a name `skip` mode left ambiguous stays unlinked after its duplicate is deleted; in a watcher tick `remove_paths` runs after `index_paths`);
- in `mentions_ambiguous_mode="skip"`, adding a second node with an already-mentioned name leaves the existing `MENTIONS` edges in place until a rescan (a full re-index of the doc behaves the same; only a rescan drops them).

They stay unlinked until they change or a rescan runs. README and PROJECT_STATUS wording updated accordingly.

author: xuryax
body:
## What

author: 40oleg
body:
Closes #107

## Design

A pattern whose every alternative starts with `^` can only match at index 0 when the `m` flag is off. The search still tried every later start position. Each failing `exec` was therefore linear in the input, and code that matches anchored patterns against the rest of a string became quadratic. marked's lexer works this way.

- `compile` marks such patterns as anchored: `startsAnchored` follows sequences and groups, and requires `^` at the start of every branch of an alternation.
- `search` tries start position 0 only. A search that starts after 0 fails at once.
- Past the backtracking budget, the Pike VM fallback is also limited to that one start.

Patterns with the `m` flag are unchanged, and so are patterns where `^` is not first in every branch or sits inside a quantified group (`(^a)?b`, `(^a)|b`).

## Results

- A failing anchored `exec` on a 200 000-character string takes constant time.
- marked 12 (needs #106) rendering 200 sections five times: 162 s before, 7.8 s after. Node.js takes 0.16 s.

## Testing

- `tests/regexp-vm.test.ts`:
  - 12 anchored patterns compared with Node.js, covering the `g`, `y` and `m` flags, start offsets, alternatives, groups and anchors that are not first;
  - 500 failing anchored searches on a 100 000-character string.
- Linux Test262, path by path against main:
  - `built-ins/RegExp`;
  - String `match`, `matchAll`, `replace`, `search` and `split`;
  - Annex B RegExp;
  - RegExp literals.

  No regressions. Four property-escape tests timed out while the machine was overloaded and pass when rerun.
- Linux full unit suite: same failures as main, all Windows-only. Windows: CI.

## Summary

Production runs `next@16.3.2`, which has critical security advisories. This hotfix bumps it to **16.3.8** and moves the Node runtime to **24.x**. Without the Node change it can't deploy, because Vercel disabled Node 20 for new deployments on 2026-10-01.

It branches off `main` rather than `development` so the 37 unreleased commits on `development` don't ship with a security fix.

**Advisories cleared**
- [GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4): unauthenticated RCE in the Image Optimization API via AVIF. `/_next/image` is live here, because `next/image` is used in `(auth)/layout.tsx` and `sidebar.tsx`.
- GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36 (Windows hosts) and GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (`next/og`). Neither applies to this app, but both are fixed.
- The 2026-09-30 batch, including the image-optimizer SSRF GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4. `npm audit` doesn't list these; the 16.3.8 release notes do.

Nothing under `src/` changes, and neither does `next.config.ts`. The upstream diff from 16.3.2 to 16.3.8 doesn't touch the proxy/middleware runtime, `after()`, the cookies API, `headers()` config or the ESLint rules.

The only console error is the preview-only Vercel Toolbar script `vercel.live/.../feedback.js`, which the existing CSP blocks. That predates this PR.)*
- [x] `/_next/image?url=%2Flogo.png…` returns 200 as `image/webp`. *(It returned 200 `image/webp`, about 42 KB, even with AVIF in `Accept`.)*

The booking-form input wasn't checked separately.)*
- [x] Function logs show no TLS or connection errors to Postgres or Upstash (first real Node 24 connection). *(0 warnings, 0 errors and 0 fatals in the last 30 minutes. The login attempt exercised both Upstash and Postgres.)*

body:
Document the implemented complete-material pipeline shared by normal Stop capture and explicitly selected history import. ReMe provides derived Markdown/chunk retrieval, LangMem indexes complete new batches, and GitHub plus the existing Bot distribute versioned public packages. Required indexing failures block publication; original statements, failures and corrections remain reference material.

The documentation distinguishes research snapshots, exact implementation versions, measured acceptance and remaining deployment work. Four selected K3 histories produced 81 indexed blocks through 35 native small-model calls, including a failed result and explicit retry. Twelve targeted local queries and twelve independent local-Git consumer queries found the relevant tasks; the consumer made no model calls. A separate synthetic native test completed normal Stop, one real indexing call, local-Git publication, ordinary updater-owner synchronization and independent native query/explain. Those original experiments establish their measured local paths, not general summary quality or hardware results. Subsequent deployment and public-feed acceptance remain separate evidence.

Core PR59 is merged with all four platform/package jobs successful at source 929. Codex PR18 is merged at f35 with its tested merge tree unchanged and both 310-case platform runs successful. Formal installation and native-cache byte verification completed; the new Stop command was trusted through the normal host interface. The existing scheduler was observed completing one public sync. The old-controller probe failure and one explicit recovery remain in the evidence. The subsequent core Bot-contract documentation PR60 retained an unrelated existing 8-second Kimi fixture failure; it is not relabeled green.

Content PR37 is merged at 5273638. It preserves all 110,289 original bytes from 20 already-public entries in 22 blocks without a new model call. The new main workflow validated all 20 entries. A fresh independent consumer synchronized exact main through normal HTTPS CLI sync, verified three query/explain full-body hashes, and returned unchanged on repeat sync with no model work. The three existing Grok routines have saved new-format configuration and trusted-validator evidence. A new public Stop-to-PR-to-Grok review/merge event remains unaccepted because the formal contribution scope is not configured or authorized. Private transcript bodies are not included.

## Design-principles review

Reviewed documentation commit: `5069dfbde48e82d8d999a2a713c09e51d9472b07` (review tree `54143caeaefce2f7f6f37ddbcfa28df706bfcf27`). Canonical integration base: `8275bd4819b9d9f64adafc442f0c1da468775c6f`. Current user-provided principles: blob `9b21e6ae87ac96ff8bdacc3f4f546384e111a184`, SHA256 `15b4b58385846051464c27d06922ad0353bdd6a4031b619ff248c3a65c179741`; candidate principles SHA256: `db1fadfb34b46ff49e6e2a113b69c5b684b8f9f13be118bd037f574851b7c98d`.

1. Total cost: complete new batches and short navigation avoid rereading all prior material; consumers reuse producer indexes. Documentation and fixture changes do not rerun unchanged live-model experiments.
2. Closed problems: package topology, immutable identities, hashes, admission and receipts have mechanical boundaries. Summary quality and applicability remain contextual judgments.
3. Understanding: the macro architecture is the entry point; research and implementation snapshots are explicitly separated so readers need not reconcile conflicting current-state claims.
4. Boundaries: ReMe's actual functions and MindIE's remaining transaction glue are named accurately. Markdown authority is distinct from rebuildable caches; no second runtime or raw-transcript archive is implied.
5. Skills: the change adds no Skill or required business workflow. Development review preserves the user's repository policy.
6. Reference knowledge: failed attempts, uncertainty and targeted-query limits remain visible. Retrieval and review do not certify technical truth. Public evidence contains anonymous counts and synthetic references, not private history.
7. On-demand use: installation consent, current-session activation, explicitly selected history and sharing scope remain separate. Missing consent/configuration is not authorization or intentional disablement.
8. Reuse: existing public bodies and summaries are repackaged without another model call. Test results remain attached to their actual revisions; unchanged historical documents are outside this PR's new-data scan.
9. Visible errors: required indexing, invalid packages, immutable-block conflicts and uncertain external writes stay visible. Completed import/sync work is distinguished from service, plugin or cleanup failure. Failed prior stages and the still-unaccepted public event path remain explicit; completed installation and feed sync are not downgraded to missing.

Findings fixed: obsolete optional-index/excerpt fallback language, premature local-body deletion after PR submission, outdated entry schemas and automatic marker merging, incomplete withdrawal/redaction instructions, initial research mislabeled as current, and machine-specific paths in public evidence. The final manifest preserves original research versions and records implementation versions, the canonical integration base, artifact hashes and scoped validation separately.

Validation: 34 changed/new UTF-8 files reviewed against canonical base; all 33 artifact hashes verified; 83 local links, 11 JSON files, 4 Python AST checks and complete-diff whitespace check passed. The unchanged initial research snapshot and native-local receipt hashes were verified. The pinned public-data scanner produced 66 findings, all reviewed as public-source references or declared synthetic fixtures; zero unresolved findings and zero user-directory/raw-transcript path patterns. Manifest SHA256 is `a0b5b81ce0c5fdad954db76da3d27b270609f1b9a0c9d4f84f402e94f6abd504`. No product CI or model experiment was rerun for this documentation-only change. The final documents report exact completed checks and remaining gaps; this PR does not substitute configuration or local tests for public event/review/merge acceptance.

_Requested by **Shyam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GoS3cfMkgmZVMVqb5Aa1dN?thread=cmsg_01GoS3cfMkgmZVMVqb5Aa1dNVPw4zAVKarLRzfHGnGmBQb)_

Before: every component and page test ran against hand-written MSW mocks that nothing compared with the real API. Tests could pass against responses CSR_BE never sends. The FE also only learned about backend API changes on its next `api:sync`.

After: every mocked `/v1` response and every JSON request body the app sends is validated against the pinned `api/openapi.json`. A new **API drift** workflow reports what CSR_BE `main` changed since the pin.

This is Phase A of the CI test plan (A3 + A4). CSR_BE has the matching change (response contract checks + breaking-change gate).

**How**
- `src/test/contract.ts` listens to MSW's `response:mocked` event and checks each request/response pair:
  - 2xx: the status must be documented and the body must match its schema.
  - Errors: the body must be problem+json, and its `status` must equal the HTTP status.
  - Requests: JSON bodies must match the operation's `requestBody` schema.
  
  A violation fails the test that caused it (`afterEach` in `setup.ts`). `contract.test.ts` checks that each kind of violation is caught. I also confirmed that breaking one field in `src/mocks/data.ts` fails the feature tests that use it.
- The check found 4 test overrides returning `{}` as plain JSON for 500/401. These now use `problem()`, exported from `src/mocks/handlers.ts`, so they match what CSR_BE actually sends. The `apiFetch` mutator tests use a made-up `/v1/ping`, so they opt out with `ignoreContract()`.
- `.github/workflows/api-drift.yml` (nightly, manual, and PRs touching `api/`):
  - checks that `api/openapi.json` is exactly CSR_BE's file at the pinned ref;
  - writes the oasdiff changelog against CSR_BE `main` to the job summary;
  - on nightly runs, fails when `main` has breaking changes that haven't been synced.

  **Needs a repo secret `CSR_BE_READ_TOKEN`** (fine-grained, read-only Contents on CSR_BE). Without it the job is skipped with a notice.
- `ajv-formats` is pinned to `^2.1.1` to satisfy `@hookform/resolvers`' optional peer range (no `--force`).
- Playbook §5 (identical in both repos) and CLAUDE.md describe the checks.

Validation: lint, format, typecheck, i18n check and Vitest (127 tests) all pass locally. Playwright runs in CI.

author: abhiroopdutta
body:
## What this changes

Reworks the home page and fixes the play/pause button that appeared over the background videos.

**Home layout**
- **FILM / PHOTO** sit in a slim centre band.
- Hover **FILM**: full-width strips above and below play cuts from the films. The two strips cut at different moments.
- Hover **PHOTO**: both strips become rows of photos scrolling in opposite directions.
- Corners:
  - top: **AD** with a running camera timecode, the name centred, **About** on the right
  - bottom: **Contact**, Instagram / YouTube icons in the centre, **India** on the right
- While media plays, everything except the strips and the two words fades out.

**Centre band**
- Thin gold lines frame the band, with a slowly drifting dashed line behind the words. These also fade out during playback.
- The words float gently, and settle onto one line when hovered.

**Videos (the play/pause button fix)**
- The home page no longer embeds YouTube. It plays four short self-hosted clips from `videos/`, so YouTube's play/pause button and loading spinner can't appear.
- One clip per film, cut from the 4K uploads: 2560×1920 H.264 with no audio, about 47 MB in total.
- The Cinematography page still uses YouTube for the full films.

**Fonts**
- Built-in system fonts only (a Charter-style serif and `system-ui`).
- The Google Fonts download is gone, so text renders instantly.

**Reliability**
- Each strip uses two `<video>` elements that swap clips, and drops the source of any hidden clip.
- This fixes previews that sometimes never appeared on first load, because the browser ran out of connections to the server.

**Films page (Cinematography)**
- A two-by-two grid where every film plays a muted, looping clip at the same time, like moving pictures in a newspaper. Clicking a picture still opens the full film from YouTube.
- Each story shows the title with a small year beside it, a 4:3 picture, and a caption from a new `note` field in `FILMS` (camera, lens or place). A short column rule runs alongside the right-hand pictures.
- The page uses its own lighter clips, `videos/p0–p3.mp4` (1600px, about 12 MB in total). They play only while the page is open.

## Notes for review
- The home page and nav no longer link to Contact; the footer's Contact link replaces it. The Contact page still exists at `#/contact`.
- The YouTube icon links to `@GrindingA` and Instagram to `@abhilashd_`. Both are set in `SITE` at the top of the script.
- Each film has two clips in `FILMS` order: `videos/cN.mp4` for the home strips and `videos/pN.mp4` for the Films page. To change one, replace the file.

## Test plan
- [ ] Hover FILM: both strips start together and cut through all four films.
- [ ] Hover PHOTO: both strips show scrolling photos.
- [ ] Move off the words: the page clears, and the corners and band lines come back.
- [ ] Hard-refresh several times, then hover. The previews should appear every time.
- [ ] Phone: the words act as links, and no strips appear.
- [ ] Films page: all four pictures move at once, clicking one plays the full film, and they pause after leaving the page.

## Scope
- Keep initial clean main/branch/local+remote SHA checks strict. At the explicit immediate pre-apply check only, accept one exact active-run canonical preflight file registered by the writer; no generic evidence directory/glob exemption or tracked-file exception.
- Bind intended raw bytes, size, file identity, approved marker/profile/fingerprint and source SHA. Use a bounded descriptor read with identity and post-read path/reparse checks; reject source/staged/deleted changes, arbitrary/old-run files, tampering, foreign identities, redirects and same-byte replacements.
- Preserve pre-fault exceptions in a separate record after reservation release. No fault or model-resolution outcome is fabricated.
- New prospective profile labels/runner source pin only. Historical profiles and attempt 016 bytes unchanged; fresh attempt 017 is user-authorized once. No change to models/runtime locks/decoding/deadlines/criteria/approval/verifier.

## Verification
- Independent curated Luna Max Standards PASS and Spec PASS after file-identity and active-profile review fixes. Runner digest independently matches 689d9d3f1addab7807eb6f41d18364ee284d8e97b532a18e8192bcfd4bd2d70d.
- Required Ruff correctness and diff checks passed.
- Affected run: 216 passed plus one legacy assertion subsequently corrected to verify preserved released-prefault evidence.
- Final guard/interruption/inventory run: 56 passed, 2 failed only on the historical Windows LF/CRLF integrity-index checkout mismatch. Historical evidence not edited to accommodate this. Required Linux CI must pass.
- New local-Git tests exercise initial clean -> writer-owned preflight -> immediate guard success, tracked/staged/deleted/arbitrary file drift, raw tampering, wrong identities, reparse points, same-byte replacement, foreign profiles and pre-fault accounting.

## Execution Gate
No new qualification or incident attempt executed from this amendment. Green reviewed merge and exact clean source precede fresh pinned-runtime qualification and attempt 017 once. author: amirbiron
body:
## ✨ תיאור קצר
- בחודש האחרון שלב ה-pytest ב-CI עלה מכשלוש דקות וחצי לכשבע וחצי. הטסטים הקיימים לא הואטו בסך הכול: את התוספת הביאו טסטים חדשים, ואת החלק הגדול שלה מעט טסטים כבדים.
- 159 טסטי פרסר ה-Markdown הכבדים (השוואה לאורקל cmark-gfm, קלט ענק בתקרות של הפרסר, וסקריפטי המדידה) מסומנים עכשיו `md_heavy`, ורצים במסלול משלהם לכל גרסת פייתון, במקביל למסלול הרגיל. **הערכה, לא מדידה:** המסלול הרגיל יתקצר בכ-54 שניות ב-3.12 ובכ-37 ב-3.11. ההערכה היא זמן הטסטים האלה בדוחות ה-CI, חלקי שני העובדים של `-n auto`.
- **נדרש צעד ידני אחרי שה-CI של ה-PR הזה עבר:** לסמן את `Unit Tests md-heavy (3.11)` ואת `Unit Tests md-heavy (3.12)` כבדיקות חובה. הפירוט בסעיף "בדיקות נדרשות" למטה.

## 📦 שינויים עיקריים
- [ ] קוד (Backend)
- [ ] בוט טלגרם
- [ ] מסד נתונים/מיגרציות
- [x] תיעוד (docs/)
- [x] DevOps/CI/CD

פירוט נקודות (רשימת תבליטים):
- **`pytest.ini`:** רישום של הסימון `md_heavy`.
- **הסימון:** `pytestmark` בשלושה קבצים (`test_md_parser_oracle.py`, `test_md_parser_upgrade_zero_diff_script.py`, `test_measure_md_parse_cost_script.py`), ו-`@pytest.mark.md_heavy` על שני טסטי התקרה ב-`test_md_parser.py`. שאר `test_md_parser.py` נשאר במסלול הרגיל.
- **`ci.yml`, הג'וב `unit-tests`:**
  - **מטריצה:** נוסף `suite` (`main` / `md-heavy`), ודרך `include` כל ערך מקבל `label` ו-`marker`. מזהה הג'וב ורשימת `python-version` לא השתנו.
  - **שמות:** שם הג'וב ושם הסטטוס (`STATUS_CONTEXT`) נבנים מהמטריצה. לכן המסלולים הרגילים נשארים בדיוק `Unit Tests (3.11)` ו-`Unit Tests (3.12)`, וכל מסלול כותב רק לסטטוס שלו.
  - **בחירת הטסטים:** pytest מקבל `-m "${{ matrix.marker }}"`. מסלול שלא נבחר בו אף טסט נכשל בקוד 5 ולא עובר בשקט (נמדד ב-pytest 8.4.2, ומקובע בטסט).
  - **שירותים:** המסלול `md-heavy` לא מרים MongoDB ו-Redis. ה-`image` שלהם ריק, ולפי התיעוד של GitHub Actions שירות כזה לא עולה.
  - **שאר הצעדים:** Smoke compile רץ רק במסלול הרגיל. לארטיפקט הזמנים יש שם ייחודי לכל מסלול, כי `upload-artifact@v4` לא מאפשר שני ארטיפקטים באותו שם. הקידומת `unit-durations-` נשמרה, כי לפיה `notify-post-merge-issue.yml` מוצא את הדוחות.
- **`tests/test_required_checks_are_listed.py` (חדש):**
  - גוזר את שמות הסטטוסים מהמטריצה, ובודק כל רשימה של בדיקות החובה בשני הכיוונים: שכל שם מופיע בה, ושאין בה שם שה-CI כבר לא מדווח.
  - מחפש שמות של סטטוסים בכל הקבצים שבמעקב (`git grep`), ונכשל על עותק בקובץ שהוא לא מכיר.
  - דורש שכל צעד דיווח ישלח את `STATUS_CONTEXT` כשם הסטטוס.
  - דורש שהביטויים של שני המסלולים משלימים זה את זה (X ו-`not X`), כך שכל טסט נבחר במסלול אחד בדיוק.
  - מקבע ש-pytest יוצא בקוד 5 כשהסינון לא משאיר אף טסט, עם `-n` ובלעדיו, כי המסלול הכבד נשען על זה.
- **רשימות בדיקות החובה:**
  - **עודכנו:** `docs/ci-cd.rst`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/agents/my-agent.agent.md` ו-`.cursorrules`.
  - **מפנים עכשיו ל-`ci-cd` במקום להחזיק עותק:** `docs/testing.rst`, `docs/branch-protection-and-pr-rules.rst` ו-`docs/auto-updates-and-auto-merge.md`. במדריך האחרון הרשימה הייתה ישנה ממילא (3.9/3.10/3.11).
  - **בכוונה לא שונה:** `FEATURE_SUGGESTIONS/DOCUMENTATION_NEEDS.md`. זה מסמך הצעות, והוא רשום בטסט כ"תמונת מצב" (`SNAPSHOTS`) עם הסיבה.
- **תיעוד:** סעיף חדש ב-`docs/testing.rst` על `md_heavy` (מתי מסמנים, איך מריצים כל חלק, ובמה הוא שונה מ-`heavy` של טסטי הביצועים). ב-`docs/ci-cd.rst` תיאור שני המסלולים, וההסבר מתי סטטוס חדש מתחיל לחסום מיזוג. ורשומה ב-`docs/whats-new.rst`.

**סטיות מהתוכנית שאושרה:**
- **טסט הרשימות לא היה בתוכנית.** הוספתי אותו כי אותה רשימה כתובה ביד בכמה קבצים, ורק טסט שמשווה ביניהם תופס סחיפה (`duplicate-rule-second-copy`).
- **התוכנית אמרה "חמישה קבצים". בפועל יש תשעה.** החיפוש שעליו נשענה הספירה נקטע, ולכן ארבעה עותקים התגלו רק בבדיקה חוזרת: `.cursorrules`, `branch-protection-and-pr-rules.rst`, המדריך ל-auto-merge ו-`DOCUMENTATION_NEEDS.md`. בגלל זה הטסט מחפש עכשיו עותקים בעצמו, ולא סומך על רשימה שנכתבת ביד.

## 🧪 בדיקות
- [x] Unit
- [ ] Integration
- [ ] Manual

מה רץ מקומית, בעותק נפרד של הריפו, על פייתון 3.11 ו-3.12:
- **החלוקה:** `-m md_heavy` אוסף 159 טסטים, ו-`-m "not md_heavy"` אוסף 7,398. יחד זה 7,557, כל הסוויטה, בלי חפיפה.
- **המסלול הכבד, עם הדגלים של ה-CI** (`-n 2 --dist=loadscope --cov`): ב-3.11 עברו 159 ב-100 שנ', וב-3.12 עברו 159 ב-96 שנ'. שלושת הדילוגים הם דילוגים של קבצים לא קשורים בזמן האיסוף.
- **המסלול הרגיל, 3.12** (`-n 2`, בלי coverage): 7,078 עברו, 314 דולגו ו-5 נכשלו. חמשת הכשלים ב-`tests/test_infrastructure.py`, כי isort ו-autopep8 לא היו ב-PATH מקומית. כשה-venv ב-PATH, כל 12 הטסטים בקובץ עוברים.
- **טסט הרשימות:**
  - נכשל על הרשימות הישנות, ועובר על החדשות.
  - 9 מוטציות נתפסו: שינוי `label` רק ב-ci.yml; סטטוס קבוע בכל הצעדים או בצעד אחד; שם שנמחק מרשימה; שם ישן שנוסף לרשימה; קובץ חדש במעקב עם עותק; פטור שכבר לא נחוץ; כשל של git; ושם ישן ב-`.cursorrules`.
  - **סבב הריוויו (`1c1a325`):** שש מוטציות נוספות נתפסו. בראשן צעד דיווח שבונה את שם הסטטוס בעצמו, כמו לפני המסלולים: על `aa423d1` הוא עבר את הטסט. השאר: צעד בלי `STATUS_CONTEXT`, ביטוי של מסלול שכבר לא משלים את השני (פעם לכל מסלול), git חסר, ומסלול כבד שלא מתרוקן.
- **כלים:**
  - actionlint נקי, ו-yamllint מחזיר אותם ממצאים כמו על הבסיס.
  - עמודי ה-RST שנערכו עוברים פרסור של docutils בלי אזהרות, וכל יעדי `:doc:` קיימים.
  - flake8 נקי, גם בבחירה החוסמת של ה-CI. ב-mypy אין שגיאות מהקודים החוסמים.
- **טסטים שקוראים את הקבצים שנערכו** (`test_docs_python_minimum`, `test_mcp_server_build`, `test_rst_parser`, `test_safe_rmtree_recipe` ועוד): עוברים.

**הריצה ב-GitHub, על `aa423d1`:**
- **מסלולים:** ארבעה, וכולם עברו: `Unit Tests (3.11)`, `Unit Tests (3.12)`, `Unit Tests md-heavy (3.11)` ו-`Unit Tests md-heavy (3.12)`.
- **שירותים:** בלוג של `Unit Tests md-heavy (3.12)` מופיעה השורה `The service 'mongodb' will not be started because the container definition has an empty image.`, ואותה שורה ל-redis.
- **המסלול הכבד (3.12):** 159 עברו, ב-77.78 שנ'.
- **לא בדקתי:** את חלוקת הטסטים בדוחות `unit-durations-*` של הריצה, ואת השוואת הזמנים מול הריצה של היום.

## 🧪 בדיקות נדרשות ב‑PR
- 🔍 Code Quality & Security
- Unit Tests (3.11)
- Unit Tests (3.12)
- Unit Tests md-heavy (3.11)
- Unit Tests md-heavy (3.12)

**הצעד הידני, אחרי שה-CI של ה-PR הזה עבר:**
1. בהגדרות הריפו, תחת Branches, פותחים את הכלל שמגן על `main`.
2. תחת "Require status checks to pass before merging" מחפשים `Unit Tests md-heavy`.
3. מסמנים את שתי הבדיקות ושומרים.

GitHub מציע לבחירה רק בדיקה שעברה בהצלחה בשבעת הימים האחרונים (GitHub Docs, "Troubleshooting required status checks"). לכן הסדר הוא: קודם CI ירוק, אחר כך הסימון, ורק אז מיזוג. עד שמסמנים, כשל במסלול הכבד מופיע ב-PR אבל לא חוסם מיזוג.

## ✅ צ'קליסט
