## Summary by Sourcery

Make verification tooling self-tests deterministic by removing internal wall-clock waits and ensuring early interruptions are forwarded to child process groups.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent interrupted verification runs from orphaning child process groups when signals arrive during process startup.

Enhancements:
- Remove wall-clock timeouts from verification tooling self-tests so they wait on actual process, connection, and readiness events.
- Reduce file verification self-tests to the essential process-group cleanup coverage.

Tests:

author: conorpbrennan
body:
## Summary

Two defects in the pre-commit review flow.

**1. Gap-patching could approve a commit without its own tests.**
- **What happened:** the gap-patcher wrote tests to the working tree, then ran the marker recipe. The marker hashes the index, so the retry approved a commit that left those tests out.
- **Root cause:** the gap-patcher's report ended in `TDD_GATE: PASS`, the trailer every "write the marker" instruction keys on.

Fix:
- The gap-patcher's report ends in `GAP_PATCH: PASS|FAIL`, never `TDD_GATE`.
- The gap block hands out no marker recipe and writes no review lock.
- `thresholds-met` approves only when `coverage.xml` was measured on the index. No Python file may differ from its staged copy, and no test file or `conftest.py` may be untracked. The check is one `git --no-optional-locks status` call, which does not write the index.
- Where coverage passed with drift, the review-required message names the files the index lacks.

**2. `code-reviewer-deep` could not find its criteria outside this repo.**
- **What happened:** it read `agents/code-reviewer.md` by a relative path. That path resolves against the repo under review, not the plugin.
- **Fix:** the skill now passes the absolute path. The agent falls back to the plugin cache. If it cannot read the file, it ends `TDD_GATE: FAIL`.

## Known gap

A gitignored test file is invisible to the drift check, so coverage measured with one can still approve on `thresholds-met`. Adding `--ignored` would pick up the test files inside `.venv` and turn the fast path off in most repos. Follow-up.

## Review

`code-reviewer-deep`: rounds 1-3 FAIL, round 4 PASS.
- The early rounds patched one approval path at a time, against an invariant the hook cannot enforce.
- Round 4 is the redesign around the root cause above.

## Test plan

- `node src/hooks/test-pre-commit-review.js`: 412 passed, 0 failed. Gap and drift scenarios run in scratch repos:
  - gap, then patch, then retry, for both all-Python and mixed diffs
  - retry after an unrelated file is staged
  - untracked `conftest.py`
  - unstaged edits
  - a parser case with a deleted file, a space in the path and an untracked directory
  - the drift read leaves the index untouched
- `node src/test-plugin-layout.js`: 122 passed, 0 failed. The 10 new doc checks fail on `main`.
- All other node and bash suites pass. `claude plugin validate .` passes.

author: srinivasan8888
body:
Fixes #1358.

## Overlap / attribution

Claimed on the issue on 2026-09-27 (the issue is the maintainer's filing of a gap I found in #1323); the maintainer's ruling there was the refusal, with wiring left to follow-ups, and asked for #1357 to land first because both touch the config-load checks. #1357 merged on 2026-09-29 as #1372. This branch is the 27 Sep work rebased onto today's `main` (`f98dac9d`) with every (task, backend) pair re-measured against the current trainers.

## Shape

`apply_vocab_expansion` (`utils/data_pipeline.py`) is the one helper that adds `data.add_new_tokens` / `data.new_special_tokens` to the tokenizer and resizes the embeddings. On `main` today it is called from exactly eleven transformers setups: `sft.py` (text, vision, audio), `dpo.py`, `kto.py`, `orpo.py`, `simpo.py`, `ipo.py`, `bco.py`, `grpo.py`, `online_dpo.py` (`grep apply_vocab_expansion src/`). `preference` reaches it through the trainers it delegates to and `tts` through SFT's text path. Everywhere else the two fields loaded and were dropped.

One check at config load, `_validate_vocab_expansion_is_applied` in `config/schema.py`, with the list `VOCAB_EXPANSION_TASKS` beside it. When either field is set:

1. a task not in the list is refused, naming the task (gap 2: `pretrain`, `embedding`, `ppo`, `reward_model`, `prm`, `classifier`, `reranker`, `cross_encoder`, `unlearn`, `moe_lora_routing`, `distill`, `asr`). The task check comes first and holds on every backend, so switching backend never meets a second refusal from this check;
2. `training.stream_layers: true` is refused: the streamed model is built without the step that adds tokens (found while mapping the call sites; not in the issue's list);
3. `backend: unsloth` is refused, naming the backend and why (its setup loads the model and attaches LoRA in one call); `backend: mlx` the same (gap 1, plus the MLX path found while mapping).

An empty list asks for nothing and loads everywhere, as before. Nothing in any trainer changes.

## Before / after (`load_config_from_string`, `main` `f98dac9d` vs this branch)

| config | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `task: sft`, `backend: unsloth`, `add_new_tokens: ["<x>"]` | loads, tokens never reach the tokenizer | `data.add_new_tokens is not applied on backend='unsloth': its setup loads the model and attaches LoRA in one call, with no step that adds tokens. Use backend: transformers, or remove it.` |
| `task: pretrain`, `new_special_tokens: ["<x>"]` | loads, dropped | `data.new_special_tokens is not applied by task='pretrain': that trainer never adds tokens to its tokenizer or resizes its embeddings. Remove it.` |
| `task: tts`, `modality: audio_out`, `backend: unsloth`, `new_special_tokens: ["<x>"]` (the #1323 case) | loads, dropped | refused on `backend='unsloth'` as above |
| `task: sft`, `backend: transformers`, `add_new_tokens: ["<x>"]` (control) | loads | loads, unchanged |

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `sft` / `dpo` / `tts` with `backend: unsloth` and either field are refused at load — `TestGap1Unsloth` (6 cases), fail on `main`.
- [x] Each gap-2 task refuses the fields at load, naming the task — `TestGap2TasksThatNeverAddThem` (12 tasks x 2 fields), fail on `main`.
- [x] The existing transformers paths are unchanged — `TestWhereTheyApplyTheyStillLoad` (11 tasks x 2 fields load; the empty list loads on every task).
- [x] A `fixed` changelog fragment.

Plus: `TestTheOtherPathsThatDropThem` (MLX SFT, `stream_layers`), and `TestTheSplitMatchesTheTrainers`, the ratchet: every `task` literal of the schema is classified; for each trainer wrapper the schema's list agrees with whether its `_setup_transformers` reaches the helper (following `super()` up the MRO, which is how `tts` inherits it, and the five delegates for `preference`); no `_setup_unsloth`, the streamed setup or an `mlx_*` trainer calls it yet, so wiring one later fails the test and lifts that refusal.

Whole file on unmodified `main`: 56 failed, 60 passed (the 60 are the controls and the ratchet, which describe `main` as it is).

## Mutation table

Each applied alone to the committed head, `pytest tests/test_issue1358_vocab_expansion_refused.py -q -o addopts=` (baseline 116 passed), restored with `__pycache__` cleared.

| # | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | validator returns early (the original) | 33 failed |
| M2 | task check dropped | 25 failed |
| M3 | `stream_layers` check dropped | 1 failed |
| M4 | backend check dropped | 7 failed |
| M5 | `tts` removed from the applying tasks | 5 failed |
| M6 | `preference` removed from the applying tasks | 3 failed |
| M7 | `pretrain` added to the applying tasks | 3 failed (the ratchet and the gap-2 refusal) |
| M8 | only `add_new_tokens` checked | 15 failed |
| M9 | the backend message does not name the backend | 7 failed |

No survivors.

## Verification

```
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check src/soup_cli/ scripts/ tests/            # All checks passed!
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_issue1358_vocab_expansion_refused.py -q -o addopts=   # 116 passed
```

Full suite (`pytest tests/ -m "not smoke"`, worktree src confirmed imported): on `ec5b4481`: `33300 passed, 200 skipped, 2 xfailed, 0 failed in 25:01` (and the same on the pre-amend head `946c4721`, 26:38).

CodeRabbit on `ec5b4481`: 0 findings; on `946c4721` it had 1 (the test used `importlib.resources` after a bare `import importlib`, which works only when something else has imported the submodule), fixed by the explicit import in the amend.

## Scope limits

- Refusal only, per the ruling. Wiring any path (splitting `utils/unsloth.load_model_and_tokenizer` so the helper can run between load and `get_peft_model`; the MLX and streamed setups; any gap-2 trainer) is its own follow-up, and the ratchet's `_setup_unsloth` / streaming / MLX tests are the ones that fail when it happens, pointing at the refusal to lift.
- unsloth is not installed here; the unsloth half is a config-load check and a source walk, which is what the issue's criterion allows.
- `docs/data.md` gains one paragraph saying where the two fields apply; `docs/training.md`'s TTS section says the codec tokens are registered on `backend: transformers` only.

author: jhut89
body:
**The risk.** This is the first contract migration. After it runs, 0.1.0 can no longer start against the database. It gets refused at start-up with both migration numbers named. 0.2.0, 0.3.0 and 0.3.1 still start.

**Why 0.1.0 has to go.** Until now, every revocation (logout, password change, deactivation, admin reset, the expiry sweep) also deleted the matching rows from the legacy `sessions` table. That kept a rollback to 0.1.0, the only release that reads the table, from bringing a revoked session back. This PR removes those deletes, so 0.1.0 would no longer be safe against the result.

**Why the table stays.** 0.2.0 to 0.3.1 never read `sessions`, but they still delete from it. Dropping it now would break logout after a rollback to 0.3.x. Review caught that on the first version of this PR. STOOP-409 drops the table in the release after this one, raising the floor to this release's last migration.

**What changes.**
- `00049_sessions_unkept.sql`: `schema_floor` goes to 37, the last migration of 0.2.0. No schema change.
- `db.Floor` = 37; `TestFloorMatchesSchema` keeps the constant and the table equal. `stoop migrate plan` and `stoop upgrade` will say "contract migration: floor rises from 0 to 37; 0.2.0 and later can start".
- `DeleteCredential`, `DeleteOtherSessions`, `DeleteUserCredentials` and `SweepCredentials` lose their `WITH legacy AS (DELETE FROM sessions …)` CTEs.
- `data.md` now says the floor goes to the oldest release that still works, not always the previous one. 0.2.0 still works here, so 42 would refuse it for no reason.

**Tests.** The deactivation test no longer checks legacy rows. `TestWriteReport` reads `db.Floor` instead of a literal 0. `go test ./internal/db/... ./internal/auth/...` passes locally.

Release note owed for 0.4.0: name 00049 as a contract migration, and say that rolling back below 0.2.0 needs the backup.

STOOP-404 (decided on STOOP-379), follow-up STOOP-409

author: bharathm03
body:
## Why

On phones the app often lands on **"the remote connection was rejected — ConnectionBlockedException(peerRejected)"**, and it stays there until you tap Retry.

**Root cause.** A phone drops its authorization lease all the time:
- every resume re-fetches it (`refreshFresh` invalidates the snapshot synchronously);
- a backgrounded network lets it expire (60 s at most);
- a policy push fences it.

The `authorized()` checks inside a native dial reported that drop as a **terminal** failure. A terminal failure becomes `PeerTerminalError`, which becomes `notePeerRejected()`, and that block only `retry()` clears. Any dial in flight when the app resumes could therefore strand the connection. This was found by reading the code; no device log captured it.

## What changes

1. **`9ecb5e8a` — the fix.** A lease that lapses or changes mid-dial now throws the retryable `AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED_DURING_CONNECT`. This covers the three checks in `NativeEndpointOwner.dial` and the post-dial check in `PeerRuntime.connect`.
   - A real revocation is still refused terminally on the next attempt by `prepare()` and the peer checks.
   - An endpoint or ALPN mismatch stays terminal, and outranks a lapsed lease (`classifyDialedConnection`).
   - Disposal stays terminal wherever it lands, and so does a rotated local endpoint.
   - A registration not yet visible right after `register` is now retryable instead of terminal.
2. **`75e2e77e` — phone logs.**
   - **Where logs go:** on Android/iOS, `hostDir()` resolves from HOME/USERPROFILE, so `app.log` went nowhere useful. Phones now log in the app sandbox: the support directory on Android and the caches directory on iOS, which keeps the files out of iCloud backups.
   - **Push isolate:** the headless push isolate writes its own `app-push.log` and flushes it before its engine is torn down.
   - **Share logs:** the error screen and Settings show **share logs** on phones, using `share_plus` 12. Desktop keeps "open log folder".
3. **`cd21e198` — Sentry.**
   - `PeerTerminalError` now carries its failure code.
   - Every connection block leaves a breadcrumb.
   - Stranding blocks (`peerRejected`, `handshakeFailing`, `deviceRevoked`) also send one warning event per (reason, code) per process.
   - Only the enum name and a code that passes `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` leave the device; anything else is sent as `UNRECOGNIZED`.
   - The telemetry opt-out and demo mode are read per block.
4. **`44505db3` — review fixes.**
   - The push isolate keeps `app-push.log` on a retried directory lookup.
   - No Sentry report for a block raised during teardown.
   - The demo-mode gate is pinned in `demo_isolation_test.dart`.
   - No log-line encoding when nothing receives the line.

## Testing

- `flutter analyze`: no issues.
- `cd app && flutter test -j 2`: 4679 passed, 3 skipped (full suite, before the review-fix commit). After that commit, the affected directories passed 777/777.
- `cd packages/antgrid_peer_transport && dart test`: 75/76. The failure is a pre-existing wall-clock flake in `authorization_test.dart`. `AuthorizationLease` reads `DateTime.now()` through `_wallMs`, which those tests never inject, so a value comes out 1–2 ms short (`59999` vs `60000`), and a different case fails each run. Neither file changes in this PR.
- `npm run check:font-tokens`: OK.
- **Not tried on a phone.** The three `NativeEndpointOwner.dial` sites have no unit coverage, because iroh's `Endpoint` and `Connection` are final classes. The pure classifier and `PeerRuntime.connect`, through a dial seam, are tested.

**Checking it on a device:** before the fix, app.log shows `payload attempt failed: PeerConnectionFailure(AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED_DURING_CONNECT | AUTHORIZATION_DENIED | AUTHENTICATED_ENDPOINT_MISMATCH, terminal: true)` next to `app resumed — re-evaluating machine ladders`. After it, the same lapse shows `terminal: false` and the ladder recovers on its own.

## Before merge

- [ ] `pod install` in `app/ios` and `app/macos` on a Mac. `share_plus` adds a native plugin, so both `Podfile.lock` files are stale.
- [ ] One Android build. `share_plus` 12 declares AGP 8.12.1 against the app's 8.11.1. `package_info_plus` already does the same and builds, but only a build proves it.
- [ ] If the Windows build misbehaves after the plugin registrant regenerates, delete `app/build/windows`.

## Open question

**Should `deviceRevoked` send a Sentry event?** It is currently treated as a stranding block, so `LICENSE_REVOKED` / `LICENSE_INVALID` send one warning per app run. That is an account state, not a defect, which is the same reason `licenseExpired` is breadcrumb-only. It is left on for now: the `connection.failure_code` tag lets triage filter it out. The alternative is to drop it from `capturesConnectionBlock` and keep the breadcrumb.

**Known remaining sticky-block sources, left alone on purpose:**
- `STALE_ENROLLMENT` (409) during `prepare()`'s register.
- A stale-policy answer from a lagging read after a relay push, which `AuthorizationLease` treats as a denial.

The new `connection.failure_code` tag will show whether either happens in practice.

author: teolupus
body:
Hermes runs tirith on every command the agent sends to its terminal. The official image does not include it, so Hermes downloads whatever release is latest onto its data volume at first start. It checks the archive only against that release's own checksums (and the signature only when cosign is installed, which the image does not have), and never updates it.

This change puts tirith in the Hermes image:

- A separate build stage fetches the pinned release (`TIRITH_VERSION=0.4.2`) and fails unless `checksums.txt` carries a keyless cosign signature from tirith's release workflow at exactly that tag and the archive matches its checksum. Only the binary reaches the image, at `/usr/local/bin/tirith`, root-owned and outside the data volume. Hermes finds it on PATH before it would download one.
- `scripts/test-hermes.sh` also runs `tirith --version`.
- Renovate tracks the `TIRITH_VERSION` build argument through a new regex manager for the Containerfiles and merges a new release after seven days. The cosign image used during the build is tracked the same way. The build-tools rule is limited to Docker images, so it no longer covers the tirith version.
- tirith's threat database is not pinned: tirith refreshes it in Hermes' data directory, at most once a day, and verifies its signature.
- README and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md describe tirith, which is under the AGPL-3.0.

author: goswami-vivek
body:
## What this adds

Dijkstra's algorithm on the road graph, using our own MinHeap. OPERA will
use this to find the fastest ambulance to an emergency and the fastest
hospital from the scene.

## Files

- `include/RoutingEngine.hpp` — `dijkstra()` and the `ShortestPaths` result
- `src/RoutingEngine.cpp` — the algorithm
- `tests/test_routing.cpp` — 44 checks

## Design

- One run from a source gives distances to every location, so OPERA can
  compare all ambulances/hospitals with a single run instead of one per pair.
- Routes are rebuilt from a parent array, not stored per location.
- Uses lazy deletion instead of decrease-key: improved distances push a new
  heap entry and stale entries are skipped when popped.
- Complexity: O((V + E) log V).

## How to test

    g++ -std=c++17 -Iinclude tests/test_routing.cpp src/Graph.cpp src/RoutingEngine.cpp -o test_routing
    ./test_routing

Expected: `test_routing: 44/44 checks passed`

author: loonghao
body:
## Summary

Core 0.20.40 renamed `INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_VERSION` to `INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_REVISION` and kept the old name as a deprecated alias. The shared adapter contract (rule A001) rejects any reference to the old name, and the nightly sweep flags this repository.

The old name read like a report's `schema_version` field while it actually carried the revision of the published schema *artifact* (`adapter-install-sop-vN.schema.json`). The two are independent counters.

## Change

`_installer.py` held `ARTIFACT_SCHEMA_VERSION = INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_VERSION` — the adapter's own copy of core's artifact revision, read by nothing but one test assertion. The reference is **removed rather than renamed**.

## Why not simply rename it

The rename is not available here without a core floor bump, for two independent reasons:

- **`tools/verify_wheel.py` forbids the optional import.** It fails the wheel when `_installer.py` contains an adapter-owned Install SOP compatibility fallback (`except ImportError`). So the new name cannot be imported defensively.
- **CI pins `dcc-mcp-core==0.20.15`** in four jobs, and `INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_REVISION` only exists from 0.20.40. A plain import would fail all four.

Raising the floor to `>=0.20.40` would resolve the second point, but it also changes `pyproject.toml`, `MIN_CORE_VERSION`, the `install.md` runbook, the pinned specifier set in `verify_wheel.py` and every CI pin. That is a dependency change with its own compatibility review, and it does not belong in a cleanup whose only requirement is that the deprecated reference is gone. **Follow-up if the org wants the constant back: raise the floor in a dedicated change.**

## What the test asserts now

Core owns the artifact revision; mirroring it locally was a second source of truth for a value only tests read — and the reason the adapter referenced a name core has since deprecated. `tests/test_install_hardening.py` now asserts the invariant that actually matters, against core directly:

- the report field equals the `const` the published schema pins, and is `1`;
- where core publishes the artifact revision, the adapter keeps the two counters apart (`SCHEMA_VERSION != artifact revision`);
- the deprecated name is gone from the adapter.

`SCHEMA_VERSION` — the report field, pinned at `properties.schema_version.const` — is unchanged and stays `1`. No core floor change.

## Verification

- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean.
- `python -m build --wheel` then `python tools/verify_wheel.py <wheel>` — passes (the job that failed on the previous revision of this branch).
- `pytest tests/test_install_hardening.py` — 40 passed, 2 pre-existing Windows-only failures (interpreter-probe subprocess tests); a pristine `HEAD` checkout produces exactly the same 2 failures.
- `scripts/check_repo_contract.py --rule A001` on the working tree: no findings; the same command on the pre-change tree reports the A001 error at `_installer.py` L32.

author: conorpbrennan
body:
Stacked on #4. Merge that first, or retarget this to `main` once it lands.

## Summary

Two defects in the `test-pre-commit-review.js` harness.

**1. A crashed run exited 0.**
- **What happened:** a test that threw printed a hook block decision and exited 0 with no `Results` line.
- **Cause:** the hook registered its crash-to-block handler at load time, and the suite requires the hook.
- **Fix:** the hook registers that handler only when it runs as the hook (`require.main === module`). It still registers before any other require, so a broken lib file still blocks.

**2. Running the suite changed the caller's index.**
- **What happened:** the suite unstaged your staged files, then re-added them from the working tree. An unstaged edit to a staged file ended up staged.
- **Fix:** the suite copies the index file before touching it and renames the copy back on exit or crash. A self-check compares the staged and unstaged diffs before and after, so a regression fails the run.
- **After a kill:** the copy can't be restored automatically, because the suite is synchronous and a signal handler would never run. So the copy stays, and the next run refuses to start and prints the restore command. It does not restore unasked over staging done since the kill.

## Review

`code-reviewer-deep` round 1 PASS. Its four items were folded in, then `code-reviewer` round 2 PASS.

## Test plan

- New checks:
  - requiring the hook adds no `uncaughtException` listener
  - a throw after the require exits non-zero
  - the caller's diffs are unchanged after the run

  All failed before the fix.
- With the old re-add step put back, the suite ends `415 passed, 1 failed`.
- Manual checks, each with a staged probe file that also had a different unstaged edit:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Full run | Both diffs identical afterwards |
| SIGKILL mid-run | Copy left on disk |
| Next run after the kill | Exit 2, printed the `mv` command |
| `mv` run as printed | Index identical to before |
| Injected crash | Exit 1, index restored |
| Crash with the copy missing | Restore command printed, exit 1 |

- `node src/hooks/test-pre-commit-review.js`: 416 passed, 0 failed. All other suites pass.

author: cotswoldsmaker
body:
The top ribbon now has an envelope showing how many things are waiting on the person signed in, and pressing it opens a new page, `/inbox`, listing them and what was lately completed.

This is the third unit of the [waiting on me inbox plan](https://github.com/bailey-medics/quillmedical/blob/main/docs/docs/plans/2026-10-04-waiting-on-me-inbox-plan.md), phase 4. Feedback is the only source so far.

## LLM decisions

- Departed from the plan: the envelope was planned to open a dropdown of counts, and that was built first. Mark asked for a page of messages and tasks, current and completed, so the dropdown went and `/inbox` came in. Phase 4 of the plan is rewritten to say so.
- A source is a feature's answer to "what is waiting on this person?", a function pair in `backend/app/inbox/sources.py`. The pull request below gave each a count. This gives each its lines too, through a new `GET /api/inbox/items`, with `done=true` for what was dealt with. At most fifty from each source of either.
- A line never carries what somebody wrote. For feedback it is "Feedback from" and the sender's username, the category and the status. The message stays on `/admin/feedback/{id}`, which the line opens.
- Nothing is dealt with on the inbox page, and opening a line does not clear it. Feedback leaves "Waiting on you" when its status stops being `new`.
- The page is called "Inbox", not "Messages", because `/messages` is already the patient messaging page.
- The envelope always shows, with or without a count. It is in `MainLayout` and in `TeachingLayout`. An exam's timer keeps the ribbon's right-hand slot to itself, so no envelope is drawn and nothing is fetched during an exam.
- The count is fetched when the layout mounts, on each change of page, and when a page calls `inboxChanged()`, as the feedback page does after a change of status. It is not polled.
- An answer of the wrong shape counts as nothing, and a source the client does not know is left out. The envelope is on every page, so it must not be what breaks one.

## Risks

- Every page in the main and teaching layouts now makes one more request, `GET /api/inbox`, on each change of page.
- An operator's lines show senders' usernames and feedback categories. Operators already see both on `/admin/feedback`. Anybody else gets no lines.
- The ribbon changed, so the four accessibility journeys need running again. Phase 7 of the plan records that; it is not done here.

## What has changed

- An envelope at the right of the top ribbon: white when idle, amber with a count when something waits.
- `/inbox`, with a "Waiting on you" table and a "Completed" table. A line opens the page where it is dealt with.
- A side menu link, "Inbox", that shows only while the page is open.
- `GET /api/inbox/items` is new.
- `InboxButton` gains an `onDark` look and passes its ref and other props to its button.

author: ybeshkarov
body:
## Summary

A module can keep the user from the routes of the app until a condition holds, such as a first run that is not finished. `RoutesData` takes `guards`: each `RouteGuard` names a function of the app that returns a `ValueListenable<bool>`, and a route of the module to show meanwhile.

In an app with guards, the template of the router role generates, next to `appRouter`: `RouteGuard`, `routeGuards`, `redirectOf()`, `guardChanges` and the class `GuardedNavigation`, which keeps what the guards make a router remember. The role says what every router does with them. An app without guards gets none of this code.

## Scope

- Affected areas:
  - [x] Contracts (`smf_contracts`)
  - [ ] Pipeline (`smf_pipeline`) or the contract harness
  - [ ] Modules and their bricks
  - [ ] CLI (`smf_flutter_cli`)
  - [x] Tooling or CI (banlist)
  - [x] Docs

## Motivation and Context

A first-run flow, and later a sign-in, must cover the routes of modules that know nothing of it, with any router. As data of the role, the guards have one order, rules can check them, and no router hardcodes them.

A guard is a gate over the whole app: while it does not allow, the router shows its target in place of every route outside its flow. What a router remembers meanwhile is written once, in `GuardedNavigation`, so that every router brings the user back to the same place: the latest location that the user or the platform asked for, or the location below the pages that were pushed; the screen that the app starts on when the user was in the flow itself. A router asks the class before it shows a location and each time a guard changes.

The rules: `router.guards` (the data of a module: the function, the target, the flow), `router.guard_functions` (the function in the generated app), `router.guards_asked` (the provider creates a `GuardedNavigation` and reads `guardChanges`), and the start route may not be in a flow.

The name `RouteGuard` leaves the banlist: it was banned as a name of the old module model, and the model has guards again.

The routers follow in the next pull requests: with this one alone, a module with a guard is reported by `router.guards_asked` in an app with a router that does not ask yet.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `melos run check`, `melos run test:coverage` and `melos run coverage:check` (every line and branch of `lib/`).
- The generated code is type-checked and run on the VM with stand-ins for Flutter: each branch of what the class answers and remembers, with one guard, with two, and with two guards on one target.
- Every problem of the three rules, the order and the flows of the guards, `--start` in a flow, and the banlist.
- Apps without guards render as before: no snapshot changes.
- Two independent reviews; the second drove a model router at random against the generated class and found no mismatch with the contract.

## Checklist

- [x] Code is clean and readable; comments/strings are in English only
- [x] `melos run check` passes: format, analyze, banlist and tests
- [x] Tests added/updated where appropriate
- [x] User-facing docs or READMEs updated where applicable
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits, from which `melos version` writes the changelogs (don't edit them by hand)
- [x] If bricks changed, ran `melos bootstrap` and committed the bundles
- [x] Modules stay independent: no module refers to another it does not depend on
- [x] Avoided module-level installation instructions; modules are integrated via the CLI

## Related Issues

Part of the app shell for 0.4.

body:
## Summary

The plugin half of `/workflow`, on the `/now` and `/uses` pattern. The theme half (`templates/page-workflow.html`, `workflow.css`, the `is_page('workflow')` branch) ships separately.

- **Data:** `sn_workflow_page` option (autoload no), `inc/workflow-page.php`. Page: Title, Dek. Sample: Label, Title, Intro, Body (verbatim, only NUL removed), Outcome. Map rows: Title, Line, Show on page. Rules: Rule, Explanation. Row order is display order.
- **The hidden-row wall:** `sn_workflow_public_data()` drops every map row whose flag is not exactly true (missing, `0`, malformed, a new row) before any markup exists. The generator reads nothing else, so the Page, core REST, the .json twin, llms.txt and provenance signing never see a hidden row. The option is read only by the two admin forms.
- **Generator and Page:** `inc/workflow-page-render.php`. One `wp:html` block around `div.sn-workflow-page`; empty sections render nothing; every field escaped with brackets encoded as `[` `]`; the body sits in `<pre tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label><code>`. Top-level Page, slug `workflow`, template `page-workflow`, title from Title, excerpt from Dek. No Page until a save has something public.
- **Admin:** Content > Workflow, classic form (`inc/admin-forms/workflow-page.php`, `sn_rsm_*` helpers, template repeaters) and native leaf (`content/workflow`, spare-card repeaters). Handler `sn_handle_workflow_save` in `inc/admin-post-actions/workflow.php`; edge purge of /workflow; five flash codes.
- **Contract:** `workflow` added to `inc/generated-page-contract.php` (marker `sn-workflow-page` only; the hero is optional).
- **Docs:** CHANGELOG `[Unreleased] > Added`, new `docs/CONTENT-PAGES.md`.

## Choices to review

- **Withdraw on empty.** When a save leaves nothing public (for example the last shown row is unchecked), an existing published /workflow Page is moved to draft (`workflow_withdrawn`) instead of keeping a body that shows a row no longer public. /uses keeps its old body in that case; here that would breach the wall.
- **Every update sets `post_status` to publish**, so a withdrawn page comes back on the next save with content. Side effect: a page the owner set to draft or private by hand is republished on the next save.
- **Body escaping uses `htmlspecialchars` with double encoding on**, not `esc_html`: core's `esc_html` passes entities through, so a typed `&` would render as `&`.
- `inc/seo-schema.php:451` (profile page slugs) does not list workflow; not part of this spec.

## Test plan

- [x] `php tests/workflow-page.php`: 39 passed. Hidden rows absent from post_content and the public data, escaping (`<script>`, `[gallery]`, `-->`, `<!-- wp:`), whitespace byte for byte, empty sections, page shape, withdraw.
- [x] Mutation: with the filter removed, 11 assertions go red; restored, green.
- [x] `php tests/os-leaf-content-workflow.php`: 13 passed (classic and native post the same names and action).
- [x] Full suite loop prints nothing; `php -l` on every changed file.
- [x] Pins updated: handler map 82 to 83, Content sub-tab order, contract pages 3 to 4, orphan-class baseline (+7 theme-styled classes).
- [ ] After the theme half lands: save on Content > Workflow, check /workflow renders and an unchecked row is absent from the page, `/wp-json/wp/v2/pages?slug=workflow` and the .json twin.

## Summary
These are the findings from #1252's single review pass. Under the one-review-per-PR rule they're fixed here rather than in #1252. None of this has shipped yet: the store path needs a 1.3.0 build.

**Security-adjacent (purchase flow), so no auto-merge. The owner approves the merge.**

### 1. Cancelling the store sheet showed an error (mobile-reviewer WARNING)
Cancelling the App Store sheet showed "Could not complete the upgrade" with a Try Again button.

The cause: expo-iap's `purchaseErrorListener` forwards the native event payload unchanged (`build/index.js`). That payload is a plain `{ code, message }` object, not an `Error`, even though the type says `PurchaseError`. `mapIAPError` began with `instanceof Error`, so `user-cancelled` fell through to `UNKNOWN`. #1252's adapter test built a real `Error`, a shape the store never sends, so the test missed it.

What changed:
- The adapter turns the listener payload, and a rejected request, into an `Error` that keeps the store's code (`toStoreError`).
- `mapIAPError` also reads plain `{ code, message }` payloads, as a backstop.
- Tests:
  - the adapter test now emits the plain payload;
  - a new `usePurchase` test asserts that a plain `user-cancelled` rejection ends in `cancelled`;
  - the error-mapping table gains 3 plain-payload rows.

### 2. Android trial copy could hide a paid intro phase (code-reviewer WARNING)
An offer with a free P3D phase, then a paid intro, then the recurring price, was treated as a plain trial: "Free for 3 days, then $29.99 per year."

Now a trial is only disclosed when the offer has exactly two phases: free, then recurring. Otherwise the base plan is used. Test: a three-phase offer yields no trial and the base-plan token.

### 3. A failed first price load disabled the paywall until restart (mobile-reviewer SUGGESTION)
- `UseIAPResult` gains `refreshProducts`, with a stable identity (`useCallback` in the adapter, module-level in the mock). `usePurchase` exposes it as `refreshProduct`.
- `UpgradeModal` asks the store again when it is shown without a product. Because the identity is stable, a failed fetch doesn't re-run the effect.
- Tests:
  - the adapter re-fetches on `refreshProducts`, and not before connecting;
  - the paywall calls it once when opened without a price, and not when the price has loaded.

### 4. Advisory mutation check
On #1252 the mutation-on-diff job pairs each source file with its same-named test file, so it only ran `upgrade-modal-utils.test.ts`. The price, trial and renewal helpers are tested in `UpgradeModal.test.ts`, so the job counted them as unprotected.

`UpgradeModal.test.ts` was a superset of the older file: all 14 of the older file's cases have equivalents there. So its content moves into `upgrade-modal-utils.test.ts`, and the duplicate is removed.

## Test plan
- [x] Each new test was RED before its fix.
- [x] `client/components/__tests__` + `client/lib/iap`: 762/762.
- [x] preflight:fast: type-aware lint, tsc, related tests.
- [ ] Owner, on a 1.3.0 build:
  - cancel the purchase sheet and confirm no error appears;
  - check the price, trial and terms text.

`session-expiry-integration.test.tsx` failed once in a full local batch. It passed alone and on a re-run of the same batch (762/762). It's timing-sensitive, and nothing in this PR touches it.

author: adedola12
body:
`POST /admin/releases/batch` is the normal way to prepare a batch and stays the normal way. It needs a signed-in staff session, which a script doesn't have and mustn't fake by handling anyone's password — so this writes the same document, supersedes the same batches, and records the same audit event via `recordGateEvent`. The same operation through the other door.

## What it deliberately cannot do

**It cannot approve.** Preparing a batch only *asks* the approver to test a commit; the gate still refuses every merge until he presses Approve on `/admin/releases`, pinned to that exact sha. Nothing here shortens that, and nothing here should be extended to.

## Two guards carried over, because both failures are silent

- **Full 40-character headSha required.** A short one would never match the commit the gate asks about — the batch would look prepared and do nothing.
- **An already-approved batch is left alone** when superseding. Withdrawing an approval a merge may be relying on right now isn't this script's business.

## Why the dry run is the default

It prints how many batches it would supersede *before* it does. That's the reason this was written: a batch was already in testing with **16 items and no verdicts yet**, and preparing a new one would have dropped it out of the approver's queue untested, with nothing to say it had happened.

Server-only, so the `approved batch` gate passes on its own.

author: donaldmurillo
body:
## Summary

`gofastr docs serve` serves the docs website offline from the CLI. The markdown docs were already offline (`gofastr docs`, `--grep`, the MCP `framework_docs_*` tools); this adds the rendered site.

- **Default:** download `gofastr-site-<tag>.tar.gz` for the binary's release, check it against its `.sha256`, extract it through `os.Root` into the user cache (regular files and dirs only, owner-only modes, no escaping names), and serve it from a GoFastr app on `127.0.0.1:8083`. `--refresh` replaces the cache only once the new copy is complete.
- **`--full`:** `go install .../examples/site@<tag>` into the cache and run the live site, so the server-backed demos work. It needs a fixed `--port`, refuses a taken one before installing, and serves v0.82.0 or later.
- **`--dir`** serves a local export; **`--release`** picks another release; a local or `@main` build must name one.
- **release.yml** builds the export after the publish gate and before the re-verify step, and attaches the archive and checksum.

Building it surfaced three framework gaps, fixed here with their own commits:

- **`core/static.Config.NotFoundFile`** serves the export's `404.html` with status 404. A conditional request cannot turn the miss into a 304.
- **Static export missed app-served rail scripts.** Every exported docs page (GitHub Pages included) 404'd on `/__site/livedash-reducers.js`. `static.Builder.Handler` now fetches each same-origin rail src the build has not written, through the app router. A stale copy in a reused output dir is replaced. CDN and relative srcs are left to the browser. A same-origin src that does not answer 200 fails the build.
- **`examples/site` banner** printed `http://localhost127.0.0.1:…` when `PORT` held a host:port.

One more fix came from the pre-commit hook. `TestSupervisor_CircuitOpensAndGenResets` failed twice under the hook's parallel load. The cause was in `isIntegrityFault`: a child that died mid-handshake (broken pipe) was quarantined as tampered instead of charging the restart circuit. A handshake call with no answer now counts as a crash; an RPC error reply stays an integrity fault.

## Review

Four rounds of Fable + Opus reviews. Each non-nit finding was fixed with a test that fails first, and each new guard was mutation-checked. The remaining items are nits:

- with `GOFASTR_DEV=1` set during an export, the livereload script ships and its stream 404s.
- a percent-encoded src case that nothing in the repo registers.

## Test plan

- [x] Targeted tests: `cmd/gofastr` (Docs, Release), `core/static`, `framework/static`, `framework/uihost`, `framework/docs`, `framework`, `framework/processmoduletest`, `examples/site -short`
- [x] Repo vettool over the touched packages; gofmt
- [x] `go run ./examples/site --export` (root and `--export-base /gofastr`), served with `docs serve --dir`, checked in a browser: pages, navigation, palette, 404 page, no script 404
- [x] `--full` against v0.86.0: serves on the requested port; Ctrl-C exits 0 with no orphan
- [x] Pre-commit and pre-push hooks
- [ ] CI

author: ryanjosephkamp
body:
Handoff 0081, item 3. **No version is changed**: all eight places say 0.3.0 before and after, and no file but the three below is touched.

## What changed

- **`scripts/version.mjs`**
  - with no argument, prints the version and the eight places it is written;
  - `--check` exits 1 when the places disagree, when one cannot be found, or when what they hold is not `x.y.z`;
  - `<x.y.z>` writes that version in all eight and nothing else: no commit, no tag, no publish.
- **`scripts/version.test.mjs`**: six tests, run against a copy of the eight files in a throwaway folder, so the real ones are never written.
- **CI**: one step in the `build` job runs the tests and `--check`.

The eight places are the ones the brief names: the root, core, CLI and web `package.json`, `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, `apps/web/src/doc/keep.ts`, `apps/web/e2e/keep.spec.ts`, `scripts/test-install-local.sh`.

## How it holds

- A place is found by the exact line around it, and must be found once. A file that was reshaped fails the check and stops a write before any file changes, so a release never goes out with seven of eight.
- A write replaces only the characters of the version. The test writes `97.98.99` into the copies and asserts that putting the old version back gives each file byte for byte.
- `packages/cli/package.json` (the agents lane's) is read here and not written: the script was run in this branch only without an argument and with `--check`.

## Not in the eight, for whoever cuts the next release

- `README.md` line 47 says "Early, version 0.3.0." in prose. The site lane holds the README now, so the script neither reads nor writes it. Once that lane's README is in, it can be a ninth place.
- `plugins/grooph/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` says `0.1.0`: the plugin's own version, left alone.

## What was run

```
node --test scripts/version.test.mjs         6 pass
node scripts/version.mjs --check             the version is 0.3.0 in all 8 places
node scripts/american-english.mjs --check    nothing British in 510 public-facing files
```

author: w1ne
body:
Ports the unlanded labwired-core motor work from labwired#2294 (branch `feat/agent-session-2026-08-14`) onto the current config modules and CLI. The H-bridge shape is reworked to fit the current product decision: the motor stays a two-terminal `dc-motor` and a driver chip is a separate part, so the plant takes its direction and speed from the driver's terminal drive instead of carrying PWM/DIRECTION/M+/M- pins.

## What changes

- **Terminal drive.** `dc-motor` gains `in1_pin` / `in2_pin`: `10` forward, `01` reverse, `11` brake, `00` coast. This is mutually exclusive with `direction_pin`, which is now optional. When `pwm_pin` names the same pad as an IN pin (DRV8833 / L9110 style), both PWM phases are averaged, so fast decay and slow decay both give the right drive. `brake_pin` and `enable_pin` are optional. A half-wired encoder is rejected when the config is loaded.
- **Timer PWM.** `timer_name` / `timer_channel` make the plant read the timer's duty while that channel is in PWM mode. Otherwise it falls back to the pad latch. `tim1` also resolves to `tim1_pwm`. General-purpose timers now report their main outputs as enabled, because only advanced timers have a MOE bit; only the motor plants read that snapshot. The F401 gains TIM3 and TIM4.
- **Evidence.** `MotorSnapshot` adds `speed_rpm_peak_abs`, `speed_rpm_max` and `speed_rpm_min`. `result.json` gets a `motors` block, which is left out when the manifest has no motor.
- **Assertions.** In `motor_speed_reached`, `max_abs_rpm` is now optional (unbounded) and there is an optional `direction: forward|reverse`. It is evaluated without allocating snapshots. A new `gpio_edges: {pin, min_edges}` assertion uses cumulative per-channel edge counts, arms its own watch, and stops the run early on batch boundaries.
- **Example.** `examples/f401-hbridge-dc-motor` runs bare-metal F401 firmware: IN1/IN2 on PA0/PA1, ENA as TIM3_CH1 PWM at 70 %, forward then reverse. It is gated by `crates/cli/tests/motors_hbridge.rs`.

Not ported:
- The H-bridge driver-hop canonicalizer and its composed gate (`e9e4c8e`): this is the rejected multi-pin model, and the Rust canonicalizer no longer exists.
- The declarative `dc_motor` primitive attach (`0768466`, `8947865`): main already builds `external_devices` motors through `resolved_motor_models`.
- The non-motor commits on that branch: they are already on main in other forms.

## Evidence

- Example run: PASS with `assertions_passed` at 6.94M of 20M steps. `speed_rpm_max` was 1000.8 and `speed_rpm_min` was -600.3. The same run without the timer keys fails, because the AF-mode latch reads a duty of 0.
- S3 `gpio_edges` stop: `assertions_passed` at 17.2M steps against a 200M budget, with no `--watch-gpio` flag.
- Tests:
  - `labwired-config` passes in full.
  - `labwired-cli` passes in full, except `demo_blinky`. That test needs a prebuilt demo-blinky ELF and fails the same way without these changes.
  - `labwired-core --lib`: 4028 tests pass.
  - `firmware_survival`: 87 tests pass.
  - `motor_models`: 37 tests pass.
  - `labwired-wasm --lib`: 101 tests pass.
- Lint and generated-file checks: clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` is clean, `regen-all.sh` leaves no diff, and `--check --drift` passes.
- Drift ack: renewed for the five boards that watch `timer.rs`. Only `output_snapshot` changed, and this is an ack, not a capture.
- Downcast ratchet: lowered by one each (`as_any` 198, `downcast_ref` 197), because the two timer downcasts in `motors.rs` were merged into one.

## Perf (board_perf, release + event-scheduler, against committed baselines)

| board | mode | Ir/step | baseline | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stm32f103 | step | 905.4 | 913.1 | -0.8% |
| stm32f103 | batch | 1.4 | 1.5 | -6.0% |
| rp2040 | step | 868.9 | 876.5 | -0.9% |
| rp2040 | batch | 1.4 | 1.3 | +8.0% (one-decimal rounding of ~1.35) |
| nrf52840 | step | 1375.2 | 1382.5 | -0.5% |
| nrf52840 | batch | 1.9 | 2.0 | -3.6% |

The per-instruction `service_motor_models` wrapper did not change; it still returns immediately when there are no motors.

author: tk87tech
body:
test: keep the env examples honest about what the code reads

#7 carries a checklist item reading ".env.example updated if any variable name
changed". Comparing the two files by hand finds nothing today, which is the
problem with the check: it is a one-time observation on an issue that will still
be open next quarter, and by then the schema has moved.

Replaced it with tests that run on every CI pass.

What it found on the way in: `VITE_SOCKET_URL` is read in
`src/realtime/socket.ts` and was in neither `frontend/.env.example` nor the
README's list. Documented it. It is optional and defaults to the API host with
the /api/v1 prefix stripped, so nothing was broken - but an undocumented
optional variable is the quiet kind of trap, since every read has a fallback and
the app starts either way.

Also corrected the README to say `.env` rather than `.env.local`; Vite reads
both, but `.env.example` itself, the backend, and the root README all say
`.env`, and three out of four is not a convention.

## Backend

`tests/env-example.test.ts` takes the schema's keys from a successful
`parseEnv` - so a field added with a default is covered automatically - and
compares them against `backend/.env.example` in both directions. Undocumented
means silently defaulted; stale means ignored.

A third case reads the example secrets out of the file and asserts the
production guard in `src/config/env.ts` still refuses them. Regenerating the
example values without updating `EXAMPLE_SECRETS` would otherwise leave the
guard protecting a file nobody ships any more.

## Frontend

`src/env-docs.test.ts` walks `src/` for `import.meta.env.X` and requires every
non-builtin to be documented, again both ways. This one matters most: an
`import.meta.env` miss is not a compile error, and `VITE_SOCKET_URL` is exactly
the case where it costs nothing today and something later.

## Proved they fail

author: alex-1974
body:
## Purpose

Research implementation for #140.

This branch tests a **hybrid** clipping architecture after global lazy parameterization was rejected in #139.

## Dispatch

The experiment reuses the existing develop dense classifier:

```d
const bool useEdgeBoundsPrefilter =
    candidateEdgeCount <= edgeCount / 4;

const bool prepareEventProvenance =
    !useEdgeBoundsPrefilter &&
    edgeCount >= 16;
```

Then:

```text
!prepareEventProvenance
    -> source-identical current develop clipping baseline

prepareEventProvenance
    -> final dense-optimized lazy parameter path from #139
```

No new threshold is introduced.

## Why this is materially different from #139

#139 globally replaced the event representation and ultimately failed because DMD crossing regressed even after dense-64 was recovered.

The hybrid leaves crossing/sparse on the established production algorithm and uses parameter events only for workloads that current develop already classifies as dense enough to allocate provenance workspace and use the dense equal-denominator sort.

## Research implementation

- `segment_polygon_clip_p1_baseline_research.d` is copied from current develop and only renames module/internal entry point.
- current `segment_polygon_clip_p1.d` retains the final dense parameter implementation;
- dispatch happens immediately after the existing dense classifier;
- sparse/crossing therefore exercise the develop source path after one research preflight dispatch.

## Caveat

The first research form repeats the cheap edge-count/query-bounds/event-capacity preflight when dispatching to the baseline helper. This overhead is intentional and will be measured. A production promotion, if justified, would factor the shared preflight instead of duplicating it.

## Gates

1. DMD/LDC correctness and canaries.
2. Verify fixture branch selection.
3. Controlled ABBA against develop.
4. Require crossing/sparse neutral and dense favorable on both baseline compilers.
5. Validate more than one dense size before production proposal.

Research only; do not merge this branch.

Refs #140 #139 #137 #82.

hermes-operator v0.2.0's validating webhook rejects UPDATEs to this field (`validateImmutable`), so Argo's in-place update will be rejected. The accepted path (issue option 2) is applied manually after merge, per CR:

No PVC is deleted, re-created, or resized; `storageClassName` never enters the pod template, so no pod restart is expected.

author: jchirayath
body:
Found while wiring a real board: the generated header diagram drew 38 pads where its own docstring promised forty.

## The miscount

`RIGHT` was one row short, and not merely short — it dropped the second `GND` at row 4, which pulled every row below the third up by one, and lost `G2`/`G15` off the end. The bottom pads were therefore labelled `3V3`/`GND` when the board has `CLK`/`3V3` there.

Wrong since the diagram was first generated, through four subsequent edits. It survived because both missing pins are strapping pins the docs tell you to avoid — nobody was ever going to wire to them, so nobody missed them. Their *absence* is what shifts the rows.

The recommended pins are unaffected: `G32`, `G25`, `G27` and `G33` are all on the left header, which was correct, and the LED on `G23` is right-header row 1, above the shift.

## The variant trap

This family ships 2-, 4-, 8- and 16-relay versions on one module and one header layout, and the larger boards drive their extra relays from **exactly the pins these docs recommend** — on the 8-relay version `G32`, `G25`, `G27` and `G33` are relays 1, 3, 5 and 4.

Its pin card therefore looks like the right reference for any board in the family, because the pad positions really are shared. The relay annotations are not. Following them puts a reed switch across a driven output.

On the 2-relay board only four GPIOs are committed: `16`/`17` for the relays, `23` for the on-board LED, `0` for the button. Both drawings now say so, and point at `s`, which prints the pins the firmware is actually driving.

Also: the LED on `G23` is already fitted, so the pin table no longer sends people off to solder one.

author: realhacker
body: ## Cause The orbs were never wrong. They hop from the shared event list, so they stay on the sounding note. The **notes on the sheet** were wrong because a recycled system plane kept a GPU texture allocated at the **previous system's pixel size**. Systems break on a barline, not at a fixed width, so the engraved canvas is a different size from one system to the next. Three.js r169 uploads canvas textures with `texStorage2D`, which freezes the GPU store at the first uploaded width×height. After that, `texture.needsUpdate = true` only `texSubImage2D`s into that immutable store: - a **wider** system is clipped, or the upload fails and the old system stays up - a **narrower** system is drawn in the corner of the old texture and stretched across the new plane The CPU canvas is correct either way. A fresh `drawSystem` compared pixel-identical, orb `y` matched the engraved head, and a parked frame at the reported times looked fine — none of those checks read the GPU texture. That is why earlier measurement missed it. ### Why the user timestamps line up | Piece | Report | What actually happens | |---|---|---| | **Greensleeves** | flicker at exactly 0:20, then wrong notes | First ribbon recycle (`x1 + VIEW_BACK`): 20.00s. Sys 0 is 1339px, sys 1 is 1346px. | | **Für Elise** | flicker around 0:20, then wrong notes | First recycle at ~18.7s (displayed as 0:19–0:20). Sys 0 is 44.22 units, sys 1 is 40.2. | | **Canon in D** | diverge at 1:17, converge at 2:22, wrong again at 2:50 | Those are system boundaries where the canvas width **changes**, then **returns** to the original 37.12-unit / 1142px size (sys 16 at 2:22), then changes again (sys 19 at 2:50). | The vertical bar is the left edge of the new system. After the orb passes it, that plane is the one whose texture was allocated for a different width. ## Fix When `drawSystem` resizes a slot's canvas, the ribbon now **disposes the old `CanvasTexture` and binds a new one** so `texStorage2D` allocates at the current size. The dummy 8×8 canvas is never used as the immutable allocation. ## Test `tools/cdp-check.mjs` already owns this class of bug. It now parks at system 0, then at the first system whose canvas is a different pixel size, and fails if any visible plane kept a GPU texture from the old size. Verified on the three reported scores (harness, including the new GPU-size assertion): - Für Elise: `gpu tex 0/4 stale @sys1 t=18.11s 1355→1234px` - Greensleeves: `gpu tex 0/4 stale @sys1 t=20.03s 1339→1346px` - Canon in D: `gpu tex 0/8 stale @sys8 t=81.82s 1142→1193px` Also allows the harness to find Chrome on Linux and create a WebGL context via SwiftShader (`--use-angle=swiftshader`).

author: lenmei233
body:
## 问题

#176 评审跟进的用户实测（#183 合并后的 dev 验证）：整合包安装出现两条**新失败面**，均为连接层单次请求零重试，一次网络波动即整单判死：

```
ERROR install: failed kind=modpack error=获取版本清单失败: HTTP 请求失败:
  error sending request for url (https://launchermeta.mojang.com/mc/game/version_manifest.json)
ERROR install: failed kind=modpack error=批量获取 CurseForge 文件信息失败: HTTP 请求失败:
  error sending request for url (https://api.curseforge.com/v1/mods/files)
```

仓库已有重试先例（`services/version/completer.rs` 的 `download_file_with_retry`：3 次、`1000*(retry+1)`ms 退避），但只覆盖文件下载，未覆盖元数据/批量接口——网络抖动下「最不该裸奔的两个元数据请求」反而没有防护。

## 修复（用户确认方案 A：重试 + 镜像兜底）

### 1. `VersionManifestService`（services/version/manifest.rs）

- 新增 `get_json_with_retry`：**仅连接层错误**重试 3 次、退避 1s/2s（与 `download_file_with_retry` 同节奏）；HTTP 状态码错误**不重试**——4xx 无意义，部分上游有各自降级语义
- `get_version_manifest`：官方源重试穷尽后**切换 BMCLAPI meta 镜像**（`https://bmclapi2.bangbang93.com/meta/{原始URL}`，形态与 `DefaultDownloadSourceManager::generate_mirror_urls` 的 bug-for-bug 约定一致）——**消除 launchermeta 国内网络的单点依赖**
- `get_version_metadata`（version.json 拉取，安装高频路径）同样接入重试
- 解析逻辑拆出 `parse_manifest` 供官方/镜像两路径复用（愚人节快照重命名等行为不变，测试守卫）

### 2. CurseForge 批量接口（services/expansion/curseforge/query.rs）

- 新增 `post_data_with_retry` 包装批次请求：仅连接层错误重试 3 次；**400 Bad Request 语义不变**（仍由调用方 `is_bad_request` 跳批——源行为：该批 id 非法，重发同样 400）
- `get_files_batch_inner` 批次循环改用重试包装：374 文件 ≈ 4 批，任一批单发失败即全盘皆输，重试收益直接

## 设计取舍

- **只重试连接层错误**（reqwest `is_connect | is_request | is_timeout`）：状态码错误重试无意义且放大请求量；两个负例测试守卫这一点
- **重试参数与仓库先例对齐**（3 次 / 1s·2s 退避），不引入新常量体系
- **镜像 URL 不引入新端点**：直接复用 BMCLAPI 既有 meta 改写约定

## 验证

- 新增测试 4 个：镜像 URL 形态（bug-for-bug 对齐）、状态码错误不重试（负例）、Params 错误不重试（负例）、愚人节快照重命名在拆分后的 `parse_manifest` 中保持不变
- `cargo test --lib`：**80 passed / 0 failed**，连跑 2 遍稳定
- `cargo fmt --check` 通过；clippy 改动文件 0 告警
- 递交过程实测佐证：本 PR 的 git push 本身就遭遇两次 `Connection was reset` / `Could not connect`（重试第 2、3 次成功）——网络抖动是常态而非异常

## 配套

- Qomicex.Tauri 主仓子模块指针推进（合并顺序：先本 PR）

## Sourcery 摘要

通过连接重试和 BMCLAPI 清单回退机制，增强版本和 CurseForge 元数据检索对临时网络故障的应对能力。

新功能：
- 当官方 Mojang 端点持续不可用时，为版本清单请求添加 BMCLAPI 回退支持。

错误修复：
- 通过重试符合条件的请求，避免临时连接故障导致版本清单、版本元数据和 CurseForge 批量文件查找中止。
- 保留现有的 HTTP 状态处理、无效批次跳过以及愚人节快照解析行为。

增强：
- 集中处理清单解析，并在各项元数据请求中应用一致的连接层重试机制和递增退避策略。

测试：
- 增加对镜像 URL 构建、不可重试错误以及清单解析兼容性的测试覆盖。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Harden version and CurseForge metadata retrieval against transient network failures with connection retries and a BMCLAPI manifest fallback.

New Features:
- Add BMCLAPI fallback support for version manifest requests when the official Mojang endpoint remains unavailable.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent transient connection failures from aborting version manifest, version metadata, and CurseForge batch file lookups by retrying eligible requests.
- Preserve existing HTTP-status handling, invalid-batch skipping, and April Fools snapshot parsing behavior.

Enhancements:
- Centralize manifest parsing and apply consistent connection-layer retry behavior with incremental backoff across metadata requests.

Tests:
- Add coverage for mirror URL construction, non-retryable errors, and manifest parsing compatibility.

</details>

author: drfxai
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"drfxai"} -->
_Requested by **DrFX** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01JRgrMbSKezNgQ4F6fhWg8x?thread=cmsg_01JRgrMbSKezNgQ4F6fhWg8xBfrkh43BMkFZb47X8JNsgH)_

Before: 3X-UI Quick Config could only create VLESS over WebSocket, xHTTP, REALITY or RAW. Configs without TLS (RAW/WebSocket "None") were refused by the app's own Xray when the server had a public address. Nothing in the app showed which protocols get through the user's network.

After: there is a new **Protocols** screen (Servers > Protocols chip). It tests every protocol family on the user's network, ranks the ones that work by quality, and creates and connects the chosen one in one tap. Quick Config also creates Hysteria2, WireGuard and HTTPUpgrade, and configs without TLS now carry VLESS Encryption so they connect to a real VPS.

How:
- **Protocols screen** (`ui/protocols/`): it follows the approved v2 design, uses bundled Inter (OFL), and works in light and dark.
  - With a 3X-UI server it creates one test inbound per family. Without one it tests the saved configs grouped by family.
  - Ranking can be weighted Balanced, Fastest or Most stable.
  - The setup sheet saves the pick plus up to two working backups for Smart failover, and removes the other test inbounds.
  - Test inbounds the user doesn't keep are deleted on retest and when they leave the screen.
  - The test is blocked while the VPN is on, because it has to measure the direct connection.
- **Hysteria2** uses the panel's certificate. The self-signed one the installer creates is pinned with `pinSHA256`. It can share port 443 (UDP) with REALITY (TCP), because used ports are now tracked per transport.
- **WireGuard** takes server and client keys from the panel's X25519 generator. It picks a tunnel address that no other WireGuard client on the server uses.
- **VLESS Encryption** keys come from the panel (`getNewVlessEnc`). `fallbacks` is left out next to them, because Xray refuses that combination.
- The installer opens UDP 443/8443/51820/2408 when ufw or firewalld is active.
- `ProtocolLab` is the engine behind the screen. It handles server runs and saved-config runs, does the weighting, and offers `keepOnly`.

Testing: JVM unit tests pass (generator 20, ProtocolLab 6, PinnedTls 5).
- **Real 3X-UI v3.9.0 with Xray 26.9.30:**
  - All 7 generated configs carried real traffic.
  - The no-TLS configs connect against a public-looking domain.
  - A full ProtocolLab run created 6 families, ranked them, and left only the kept inbound.
- **The screen's UI code** was compiled and rendered with Compose Desktop. The ViewModel was type-checked against stubs.

No Android build was possible here (Google Maven is blocked), so the final Android compile and an on-device run are still to do. The score covers reachability, latency and jitter, not download speed.

author: djhulme1
body:
This lets the author of a held submission withdraw it, so log entry 83 can be closed for good without anyone signing with the operator key.

The rejection half, which you merged as #41, is live: a rejected submission can never be released. Rejecting still needs the operator key, which is on your laptop. These two commits reached #41's branch after you merged it, so they are here instead.

**What it adds:** an author may withdraw its own submission while screening holds it.
- `POST /v2/submissions/withdraw` takes a `submission.withdraw` envelope with the held id (the 202 gives it) and a reason, signed with the main key of an agent of the submission's own operator.
- It is accepted only while the hold is undecided, and goes on the log with the reason.
- After that the submission is never published, and any R1 decision on it is refused, since nothing is left to decide.
- Resending the very same envelope is refused. To publish the work, the author submits it again and it is screened again.

**Not changed:** R1. Nothing reaches the record without the operator key, and you still decide every hold whose author stands by it. A withdrawal can only keep something out. Published papers and escalated items can't be withdrawn this way.

**Also:** the holds list and the stewards' page show "withdrawn by its author". The OpenAPI description and the agents' skill text are updated (merged with #40's new quota wording), and the mirrors are regenerated.

**Tests:**
- The author's other agent withdraws a held submission. Later decisions on it are refused, nothing is published, and resending the same envelope is refused.
- Adversarial: another operator's agent can't withdraw (403) and a check key can't sign a withdrawal (403). Published papers, escalated claims and rejected submissions can't be withdrawn. Forged withdrawal entries change nothing, and a release written to the log after a withdrawal lifts nothing.
- The fuzz test covers the new entry type.

566 tests pass. Typecheck and the Worker build pass, and both replay audits show no change.

**After you merge:** the Bombus lab sends the withdrawal of entry 83 it has already queued, as its author, Bombus-Gemma, with the reason on the log. Nothing needs signing.

author: rcbevans
body:
The docs review's L-tier item: the pages that tabulate the settings surface were the last **silent-drift** surfaces — nothing failed CI when the code's settings changed and the docs went stale. This PR converts the tables into an enforced contract.

## The pin

`tests/test_settings_tables_docs_contract.py` (static-guard style, per `test_suite_hygiene.py`) parses every docs settings table and enforces, in both directions:

1. **documented-but-doesn't-exist** — every `TASKQ_*` name a docs settings table tabulates must be a real field of the canonical settings classes (`TaskQSettings` / `WorkerSettings` / `OIDCSettings` / `SAMLSettings` in `taskq.settings`).
2. **documented defaults match code** — each row's `Default` cell must agree with the field's `FieldInfo` default through a documented rendering resolver.
3. **exists-but-undocumented** — every public settings field must appear (by env-var name) in at least one docs settings table, so a new knob cannot ship without a row.

Tables scanned (headers swept across all of `docs/`): `configuration.md`'s `Env Var` reference, `workers.md`'s `WorkerSettings` table, the per-guide `Variable` tables (`admin-ui.md`, `cli.md`, `deployment.md`, `observability.md`, `progress.md`), `timescaledb.md`'s `Setting` table, `ops.md`'s knob table, and `sso.md`'s `Env var` field tables.

**Default-matching semantics** (resolver documented in the test module docstring, one implementation, no vacuous skips):
- bool/int/float compare numerically (`1750.0` vs `1750`, `True` vs `true`)
- timedelta compare as durations across both docs spellings (`7d`/`24h` and ISO `PT24H`)
- `None` defaults pin the *unset* state via the docs' prose markers (`None`, `unset`, `_(none)_`, `(unbounded)`, `derived …`, `falls back …`) — the honest pinnable part of the genuinely dynamic defaults (`TASKQ_RELOAD_INTERVAL` derives from the lease, the split DSNs fall back to `TASKQ_PG_DSN`)
- empty-string defaults (`TASKQ_HEALTH_TOKEN`, SSO secrets) accept `"" (empty)` / `_(none)_` / `n/a`
- non-empty string defaults compare as exact backticked spans
- `TASKQ_PG_DSN` compares credential-masked (dotenvmodel masks the password in `str`; the docs print the real default DSN — masking both sides compares host/port/database honestly)
- `TASKQ_QUEUES` is the one factory default; its list literal compares quote-style-normalized

## Inventory tally

Reconciled **157** code env-var fields (35 `TaskQSettings` + 102 `WorkerSettings` + 9 `OIDCSettings` + 12 `SAMLSettings`) against **157** documented names across 11 settings tables (~160 tabulated rows). Drift found and fixed (docs corrected to code truth, never the reverse):

- **exists-but-undocumented (1):** `TASKQ_SAML_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` was only "*(same as OIDC)*" in `sso.md` — now spelled out.
- **documented default/type wrong (2):** `allowed_groups` was tabulated as `frozenset[str]` / `frozenset()` — that is the derived `allowed_groups_set` *property view*; the setting itself is a comma-separated `str` with an empty default. Both SSO tables corrected.
- **documented-but-doesn't-exist: 0.** Every other documented name and default matched the code exactly.

## Red-first proof

In-suite drills (same reconciliation the real assertions run, on mutated copies): a staled default (`max_concurrency` → 9), a new undocumented field (`TASKQ_BRAND_NEW_KNOB`), and a phantom documented name (`TASKQ_MAX_CONCURENCY`, the typo `taskq doctor` warns about) each turn the corresponding pin red and name the offender.

Real-file mutations (applied, observed red, reverted):
- docs default `TASKQ_MAX_CONCURRENCY` 8 → 9 in `configuration.md` → `test_every_documented_default_matches_the_code_default` red: `docs Default '`9`' != code default 8 (WorkerSettings.max_concurrency)`
- new `WorkerSettings.brand_new_knob` field in `settings.py` → `test_every_code_setting_is_documented_in_a_docs_table` red, naming `TASKQ_BRAND_NEW_KNOB (WorkerSettings.brand_new_knob)`

## Gates

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean
- `pyright` (strict): 0 errors
- `mkdocs build --strict`: 0 WARNINGs; INFO output byte-identical to the base commit except the build-time line
- pin: 7 passed (plus 219 passed in the neighbouring settings/extras-docs suites)

One incident worth noting for future table edits: several type cells contain markdown escaped pipes (`str \| None`); a naive `|` split misreads every later column. The parser splits escaped-pipe-aware — that bug was caught during this PR's own reconciliation.

author: jackreichert
body:
Reject inherited object keys where an argument or name is looked up in a plain object, so `constructor` or `toString` can no longer pass a lookup as if it were a real key.

- `pr-open`: unknown-argument check uses `Object.hasOwn`.
- `ledger-index`: unknown-query check uses `Object.hasOwn`.
- `journal` approvals: grant buckets are a `Map`, so an odd approval value is ignored instead of throwing.

Behaviour change worth a look: `streams add` used to compare the mutated entry with itself, so adding an alias to an existing stream was never saved and always reported "unchanged". It now saves and reports "updated". This falls out of the aliases fix.

Each fix has a test that fails on its parent commit.

body:
## Summary

0.25.0 doesn't load on OpenClaw 2026.9.1. I found this while installing it on Jarvis, where `openclaw plugins doctor` reports:

```
plugin-memoryrelay-ai [register]: Error: plugin register must be synchronous
```

OpenClaw 2026.9 now refuses a plugin whose register function returns a promise. Our default export was `async` because it awaited two startup calls: `client.health()` and the first-run onboarding check. Both only ever logged their result and never changed what got registered, so they now run in the background. Register returns synchronously, with every tool, hook and gateway method in place.

- `index.ts`: `export default function plugin(api): void`. The health check uses `.then(log, log)`, and onboarding runs in a `void (async () => …)()` with its existing catch.

author: artur-panek
body:
## Summary

Makes real-instance alpha testing reproducible by publishing the exact manual-install package that passed CI.

- uploads the deterministic candidate ZIP and checksum from every non-scheduled green Validate run
- names the artifact with the full source commit SHA
- retains candidate artifacts for 14 days
- disables secondary artifact recompression because the payload already contains the release ZIP
- fails CI if the expected package is missing
- documents downloading and verifying the exact candidate before real-instance testing
- adds the CI artifact name to the alpha test-report template
- requires the tested commit SHA to be recorded in the release checklist

## Why this matters

Testing a moving branch or rebuilding locally can accidentally validate different source from the source that passed CI.

The intended alpha flow becomes:

~~~text
source commit
→ validation
→ deterministic package
→ exact-SHA CI artifact
→ real Home Assistant test
→ recorded commit/version
→ release decision
~~~

## Artifact verification

This branch's successful CI run produced:

~~~text
ha-forensic-lab-candidate-80ba1bd88aa8a10f94c74789985b869eea0431fe
~~~

The GitHub Actions artifact is tied to the same source SHA and contains the deterministic manual ZIP plus its SHA-256 checksum.

The artifact remains a **test candidate**, not a release.

## Validation

- HACS ✅
- hassfest ✅
- Ruff ✅
- Python compile ✅
- frontend JavaScript syntax ✅
- trace projection tests ✅
- pytest ✅
- deterministic release archive ✅
- exact-SHA candidate artifact upload ✅

Stacked on #19 (`release/alpha-packaging`).

author: clawd20130
body:
## Problem
The desktop on the G100 S turned between portrait and landscape by itself. Android itself stayed portrait throughout.

- **Cause**: the `phone-turns-with-android` patch treated any output configuration that carried a quarter turn, or a mode across the current orientation, as a request to turn the phone. The turn was **relative**: upright became landscape and landscape became upright. Clients resend the whole output state, and a `Rotated270` saved in `kwinoutputconfig.json` (left over from 2026-10-01) kept coming back with it.
- **Reproduced**: each `kscreen-doctor output.WL-0.rotation.right` flipped Android's orientation once.
- **Impact**: both deployments of dev 20261005.1 failed `input.text` and rolled back, because the screen turned in the middle of the smoke acceptance.

## Change
Per the user's decision, the phone turns **only when the user sets an orientation**: the device panel's Screen orientation (portrait, landscape or follow the system; portrait by default).

- `phone-orientation-from-device-panel.patch` (kwin `+rungic10`):
  - A configuration that would turn the phone is ignored, along with any Android size or refresh change carried with it.
  - The phone output never takes a transform.
  - KDE display settings' rotation no longer applies to the phone screen.
- `docs/50`: cause, fix and device evidence.

## Verified on the G100 S
Tested with the KWin dev overlay, after a session restart.

- Refresh 60 → 90 → 120 Hz: no turn.
- Two configurations with `rotation.right`: no turn; Android stays portrait.
- Device panel → landscape: Android turns, and KWin follows at 800×360 with no transform. Changing refresh while in landscape: no turn.
- Device panel → portrait: back to 360×800.
- The saved WL-0 transform stays `Normal`.
- Acceptance: `display.geometry` and `input.text` pass.

## Tests
`tools/run-tests.sh`: 835 passed. One flaky failure, `test_contract_codec.py::test_an_app_before_channel_version_2…` ("Broken pipe" instead of the 10-bit error), passed 6/6 on rerun. It is unrelated to this change; follow-up to come.

After this merges, dev release 20261005.1 has to be rebuilt to include the fix.

author: cmungall
body:
PAINT-project review of human **ARL13A** (Q5H913), with the affinage deep-research record.

**Summary (8 GOA rows)**
- **KEEP_AS_NON_CORE:** the ciliary location rows (IBA non-motile cilium, motile cilium, ciliary membrane; IEA 9+0 cilium). Zebrafish Arl13a-mCherry localizes to about half of embryonic cilia (PMID:30009987).
- **UNDECIDED, with propagation_review root cause UNRESOLVED:** non-motile cilium assembly and receptor localization to non-motile cilium (IBA).
  - Node PTN000746458 is seeded only by ARL13B-type proteins (worm arl-13, mouse Arl13b).
  - ARL13A sits in a separate PANTHER subfamily (SF1 vs SF3), has never been tested for these roles, and the one ARL13A study concludes the paralogs have "evolved different roles".

body:
## Summary

`golem-gate-watch.sh` had reached **716 production LOC**, over the 700 `sh` warn budget. This PR extracts the pane-classifier cluster into a sourced fragment, `golem-gate-watch-classifiers.sh`: `pane_is_plan_gate` … `pane_api_error_class`, plus their consts `MULTI_Q_RE`, `OWN_WORK_RE`, `PROMPT_GLYPH` and `PROMPT_NBSP`. The issue named this cluster as the first cut.

| File | prod LOC |
| --- | --- |
| `golem-gate-watch.sh` | 716 → **532** |
| `golem-gate-watch-classifiers.sh` (new) | **188** |

One cut is enough for the AC, so the feed and liveness seams are deliberately **not** cut. Splitting them now would add sourced files with no budget gain.

## Seam design

- **Byte-identical move.** The fragment body is `cmp`-equal to `origin/main` lines 531–1193. `split-verify.sh` reports `split-verified`: non-lossy, all 33 top-level units preserved, no dangling references.
- **Sourced in place**, between `emit_transitions` and `panes_snapshot`, so the consts load in the same order as before. The path resolves from `$SCRIPT_DIR`, never `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.
- **The load fails loudly** (`return 2 2>/dev/null || exit 2`). This matters for the two callers that *source* gate-watch. `golem-handoff-relaunch.sh`'s `pane_has_gate` treats a load failure as "gate", which is the safe refusal. If the load failed silently, the matchers would be undefined and the caller would read **"no gate"**, the unsafe direction.

## Tests

- New `tests/gate-watch/70-classifiers-load.sh`. It removes the fragment from a copy of `scripts/` and asserts three things:
  - executed gate-watch exits 2 and names the missing file;
  - sourcing gate-watch fails;
  - `pane_has_gate`, sliced from the real caller, answers `gate`, with an intact-tree control that answers `no-gate`.
  - **Mutation-checked:** weakening the guard to a bare `.` flips the answer to `no-gate`, and the case FAILs.
- The case gets its own fragment because `30-helpers-and-modes.sh` sits at 687 prod LOC, and adding the case there would have pushed it to 709. That's the same remedy #1097 used.
- All existing gate-watch tests pass unchanged (102/102). No test assertion was modified, and no sed-slicer targets the moved code. `60-pane-registry.sh` mutates `panes_snapshot`, which stays in the parent.
- `lint-shellcheck`, `lint-shell-portability`, `lint-worktree-recipes`, `validate-golem-scripts` and `lint-suite-reporting` are all green.

## Other changes

- `.claude/pre-review.yml`: the fragment goes into `test_skip_patterns`, with the structural reason "sourced, no entry point" (same precedent as `golem-status-signals.sh`).
- `plugins/workflow/README.md`: the script table now names the fragment.

## Review

The adversarial pre-PR review harness (cycle 1, 5 dimensions) came back clean, with 0 findings. The pre-review pre-scan also had 0 rows.

## Note on the pre-push run

The first push was blocked by `validate-context-budget.sh` → "emits the documented defaults". This golem session exports a stale `CONTEXT_BUDGET_FLOOR=91000`, from before the default moved to 104k, and that test does not scrub inherited env. With the var unset the stage passes 41/41. It's unrelated to this diff and will be filed as a follow-up.

This PR makes the relative norm maps functorial in towers of number fields. ## Summary

Before this change, a content file at a path registered in code (e.g. `content/count.md`) made axum panic on the duplicate route at startup. Now **registered routes win** and the site keeps running.
