author: zaubermaerchen
body:
Unconfigured `SIGUSR1`/`SIGUSR2` do not necessarily terminate a Go process. README and repository guidance now distinguish dam's configured release subscriptions from the Go runtime's default caught/no-action handling, and explicitly avoid promising OS-default termination. Two comments that incorrectly described `signal.Stop` as restoring a fatal default have been corrected.

This changes documentation and comments only. Signal registration, process-lifetime consumption of configured signals, aliases, unsupported-platform rejection and existing tests remain unchanged; no `signal.Reset` or `signal.Ignore` was added. The help text and signal tests were audited: help had no incorrect default-termination claim, and existing tests correctly verify that unconfigured USR signals do not release the gate.

Closes #63.

Evidence and validation:
- Linux arm64 reproduction with Go 1.22.12 (the go.mod/CI version) and Go 1.26.0: a minimal program importing only `bufio`, `fmt`, and `os` announced readiness, received each USR signal, then successfully echoed input and exited 0. It did not import `os/signal` or register signals. Dam with duration/file conditions also survived both signals, held binary input, and released it byte-for-byte only on its configured condition.
- [Go's documented default signal behavior](https://pkg.go.dev/os/signal#hdr-Default_behavior_of_signals_in_Go_programs) identifies these signals as caught without action. [Darwin's Go 1.22.12 signal table](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.22.12/src/runtime/signal_darwin.go) also has notification-only entries for both USR signals.
- Existing configured/unconfigured subprocess and condition lifecycle tests passed before and after the wording changes.
- `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent review found no actionable issues.

The standalone reproduction ran on Linux; a separate minimal-program macOS reproduction was not available locally. The PR's macOS CI runs the existing dam subprocess signal tests. No new failing tests were added because executable behavior did not change.

CI passed: [Ubuntu/macOS/Windows tests and Ubuntu race](https://github.com/zaubermaerchen/dam/actions/runs/37220918322), including the Unix signal subprocess tests on macOS, and [all seven release build targets](https://github.com/zaubermaerchen/dam/actions/runs/37220918313). Release publication was skipped for this PR.

author: blarghmatey
body:
### What are the relevant tickets?

Follow-up from review of the staff dashboard's B2B section (#3994, #3997), part of https://github.com/mitodl/hq/discussions/12784.

### Description (What does it do?)

The provisioning audit trail (`OrganizationProvisioningAudit`) is written by the `b2b.provisioning` service functions, so it covers the API and the staff dashboard. `sso_organization_id` is also editable on the organization's Wagtail page, to link organizations that predate the dashboard, and an edit there left nothing in the organization's change history. Pointing a page at a different Keycloak organization changes who its members and identity providers are, so it belongs in the same record.

This writes an `organization_updated` audit row from `OrganizationPage.save()` whenever the stored `sso_organization_id` changes. I put it in `save()` and not in a Wagtail hook because `before_publish_page`/`after_publish_page` only run from the editor's create and edit views. Bulk publish, scheduled publish and a direct `revision.publish()` skip them. `save_revision()` saves with `update_fields`, with the edited value in memory and not yet written, so those saves are skipped.

Who gets recorded as the actor:

- Publishing saves the page without a user, so the published revision's author is recorded. If one person drafts the change and another publishes it, the row names the author. Wagtail's page history has the publisher.
- The editor saves an _unpublished_ page straight from the form, before any revision exists. `OrganizationPageForm` hands the editing user to `save()` for that case.
- Anything else that changes the field without going through `b2b.provisioning` (e.g. a shell session, or republishing the revision that is already live) is recorded with no actor. The dashboard shows those as "System".

`link_organization_to_keycloak` already writes its own record, including whether the Keycloak organization was created or adopted, so it passes `audit_sso_link=False`.

`org_key`, `name` and `description` are already read-only on the Wagtail page as of #3997, so `sso_organization_id` and the logo are the only fields still editable there.

Not fixed here: the provisioning API writes the page row without saving a Wagtail revision, so publishing a page whose latest revision predates an API write puts the old `sso_organization_id` back. With this PR that revert shows up in the change history, but it still happens. That needs its own decision (save a revision from the API, or keep the API-owned fields out of the revision round trip).

### How can this be tested?

`pytest b2b/models_test.py -k organization_page`. The `b2b` and `cms` suites pass locally (955 passed, 1 skipped).

In the Wagtail admin, change "Organization SSO ID" on an organization page and publish. The change shows up under the organization's change history in the staff dashboard (`/staff-dashboard/b2b_organizations/show/<org_key>`) with your user. I have not done this step by hand.

Closes SHARD-540.

**Why.** `test_negative_size_refused` built its archive with a raw GNU base-256 size of -1. A patched tarfile (3.13.6, 3.14.7) ends the archive at that header itself, so the fixture raised `KeyError: top/a` before any SDK code ran. CI passed only because uv 0.5.9 installs 3.13.1.

- Without the `member.size < 0` guard in `_archive.py`, the test fails on all four versions (DID NOT RAISE).

author: mathisarends
body:
huego previously exposed light control, room/zone lighting and scene activation. Agents can now inspect complete Hue resources and configure the bridge through native JSON, including creating rooms, scenes and smart-scene schedules.

For example, `huego room create --file office.json --dry-run --json` returns the exact POST path and payload without writing; the same command without `--dry-run` creates the room and returns its resource identifier.

## Changes

- Add a native resource registry for all 41 resource types in OpenHue revision `1ffc817857abf456d5ff2ae50400ef768dbce28e`, with offline operation discovery and embedded request schemas.
- Expose `resource types/schema/list/get/create/update/delete` and direct resource groups. JSON payloads support inline data, UTF-8 files and stdin, preserving unknown fields, explicit nulls, false, zero and large integer values.
- Add configuration helpers for device names/identification/usertest, sensor enablement and motion sensitivity, behavior enablement, smart scenes, entertainment areas, Zigbee discovery, device updates, geofencing, effects and power-up presets.
- Reject ambiguous names and unsupported documented operations. Report HTTP-200 bridge errors as failures, including partial failures, while retaining native error details in JSON output. Keep existing compact lighting/scene list output.
- Provide dry runs for all new writes and an explicit `--raw` option for firmware extensions or operations missing from the public specification.
- Add an agent guide, editable room/scene/smart-scene request templates, upstream attribution and license packaging, and Linux/Windows CI.

The work is split into four commits: API foundation, generic CLI, direct resource commands/helpers, and documentation/CI.

## Validation

- `go build ./...`
- `go test ./...` — fake HTTPS bridges verify every resource's collection/item operation contract, direct CLI paths, exact helper payloads, input rejection, name ambiguity, full JSON preservation and dry runs.
- `go vet ./...`
- `golangci-lint run` — no issues.
- `goreleaser check`
- GitHub CI with Go 1.25 passed build, vet and tests on both Linux and Windows.
- Executed the three checked-in creation templates and a smart-scene deactivation as dry runs.

Schemas describe the pinned public API and guide payload authoring; the bridge validates payload semantics and hardware support. Automated tests do not exercise a physical bridge. REST configuration is covered here; DTLS frame streaming and SSE subscriptions remain outside this change.

author: williebee615
body:
## Summary
Before any paid testing, the owner asked me to verify that budget reservations are atomic across simultaneous requests and cover every model call, tool round, retry and billable token category. The audit of #186 found four gaps, all fixed here:

| Requirement | Gap in #186 | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Atomic across simultaneous requests | Reservations were in one server's memory; two instances (for example, during a Render deploy) could both spend the remainder | Database functions `agent_model_reserve` / `agent_model_settle` under one per-month advisory lock. Committed + open reservations + new ≤ min(budget, $10), enforced inside the database. |
| Every call, tool round, retry | Calls that timed out or dropped were recorded at $0, though they may have been billed | Up to 3 calls per answer (tool rounds included) are reserved. SDK retries are off. Possibly-billed failures (timeout, connection, 5xx, unknown) are charged at the call's worst case; rejected requests (auth, 400, 429, spend limit) at $0. Real cost is recorded uncapped; a reservation is settled once. A server that stops mid-answer leaves its reservation counted in full. |
| Input bound | Characters ÷ 3 was an estimate | Hard ceiling: UTF-8 bytes + 1,000 tokens of provider overhead. A token covers at least one byte, so this is a guaranteed bound; requests over it are never sent. |
| Every billable category | 1-hour cache writes were priced at the 5-minute rate | Input, output, 5-minute and 1-hour cache writes (1-hour rate when the split isn't reported), cache reads and server-tool requests are each priced. The reservation uses the dearest input rate. Worst case per answer: **$0.1035**. |

## Production (already applied)
- **Migration `20261005010000`:** applied. Execute rights for `service_role` only, and no anon or authenticated access (verified).
- **Settings:** `agent_model_mode = off`. The test-account list is pre-set to the synthetic reviewer accounts but has no effect while the mode is off.

## Tests
- **Database:** 104 passed. The new `agent_model_budget` tests:
  - 30 concurrent sessions against $10 at $0.60 each grant exactly 16;
  - settle happens once;
  - committed spend plus open reservations block new ones;
  - the $10 cap holds even when a larger budget is passed in;
  - bad input is rejected;
  - only the server role can execute the functions.
- **Server:** 1,561 passed. The model tests add:
  - 5 simultaneous requests with room for one get exactly one model call;
  - a timeout is charged at the worst case and an auth error at $0;
  - requests carry no billable extras and stay under the ceiling;
  - the server fails closed when the database can't reserve.
- **Unit:** pricing for every category, worst-case math, the byte bound with multi-byte text, the 3-call cap, and over-ceiling requests never being sent.
- **Browser:** 75 passed.

## Docs
- `docs/ai-model.md`: budget enforcement table.
- `docs/privacy-ai-disclosure-draft.md`: complete draft, with Anthropic's retention terms and sources. Not published.

author: jilint777
body:
Submission path: `solutions/00000001090/jilint777_submission_20261004150344/`

**Claim.** The maximal order of the automorphism group (the stabilizer of the permutation equivalence class) of an MDS code over GF(3) of type [12,6] is 660, attained by an M₁₁ embedding. The orders for all other classes divide 132. The first clause asserts that some MDS [12,6] ternary code (a `[12,6,7]_3` code) has |Aut| = 660. We refute it.

**Literal reading: no such code exists.**

**Theorem.** For `k ≥ 2`, if every nonzero row combination of a `k×n` matrix over F₃ has weight `≥ n−k+1`, then `n ≤ k+2`.

1. By linear dependence, two independent messages give codewords `u, v` that vanish on `k−2` coordinates.
2. The 8 nonzero combinations `au+bv` are nonzero codewords, so their weights sum to at least `8(n−k+1)`.
3. Each remaining coordinate is nonzero in exactly 0 or 6 of them, so the sum is at most `6(n−k+2)`.
4. The two bounds force `n ≤ k+2`.

So no `[12,6,7]_3` code exists, and nothing attains 660, for any notion of automorphism group. We also cover:
- `d ≥ 7` as well as `d = 7`;
- "[12,6]" read as [n,d], which asks for a `[12,7,6]` code; none exists.

**Golay reading** (probably what was intended). Up to monomial equivalence the ternary Golay code is the unique `[12,6,6]_3` code (Pless; Delsarte–Goethals). The conjecture's group is the permutation automorphism group PAut.
- The Golay monomial class splits into exactly 5 permutation classes, with |PAut| = 108, 120, 432, 660 and 7920.
- `golay` = [I₆|A] has |PAut| = 660. Doubling its column 6 gives `golay'`, with |PAut| = 7920 = |M₁₁|.
- So the maximum is 7920, not 660. Since a subgroup of order 7920 in M₁₂ has index 12, it is ≅ M₁₁, so M₁₁ is attained as a full PAut. Also, 108, 120 and 432 do not divide 132. The orders are Python-verified.

**"MDS" dropped.** The repeated-pair `[12,6,2]` code has 2⁶·6! = 46080 > 660 permutation automorphisms.

- **Lean** (4.19.0, core only).
  - Defines generator matrices over `Fin 3`, `IsGenMatrix`, `wt`, `MinDistGe`, `HasMinDist`, `IsMDS`, `IsPAut`, `IsMAut`, `PAutOrder` and `MAutOrder`.
  - Literal reading: `dep` and `no_mds_ternary` (for all n, k); `conjecture_00000001090_false : ¬ Conjecture1090` and `conjecture_00000001090_monomial_false`; `no_mds_12_6`, `no_mds_12_6_with` (any property P) and `no_mds_12_7`.
  - Golay reading:
    - `golay'_12_6_6`: `golay'` is a [12,6] code with d exactly 6.
    - `golayAuts_aut` and `golayAuts_nodup`: 720 distinct permutation automorphisms h∘k. The 54 factors are checked by `decide +kernel`, and closure under composition is proved.
    - `golay_reading_witness`, `golay_reading_false : ¬ GolayMax660` and `golay'_order_ge`.
  - "MDS" dropped: `atMost660_false` and `pair_order_ge`.
  - Non-vacuity: `tetra_mds` ([4,2,3] MDS, so the bound is sharp) and `golay_12_6_6`.
  - No sorry, native_decide or added axioms.
- **verify.py** (stdlib only).
  - Exhaustive check that no `[8,2,7]_3` code exists, and the Griesmer bound.
  - All 46080 pair-code automorphisms.
  - The full five-class Golay PAut spectrum, via the M₁₂ action on the 2¹¹ column-scalings, with |PAut(golay)| = 660 and |PAut(golay')| = 7920.
  - A re-check of the 720 Lean automorphisms.
- **report.pdf** contains the complete proofs and the readings covered.

No previous submission exists for this conjecture.

author: adam-leitgeb
body:
## Problem
`NavigationManager.modalEntryStack` only shrinks on `Dismiss`. Android system back pops a destination directly, so the entry of a modal closed by back stays behind.

- One sheet over a root screen: harmless. The stale entry is still a valid place to pop back to.
- **A sheet over a sheet** (found in Guardian: Edit action → Add contact): the stale entry is the lower sheet itself. Its next `Dismiss` runs `popBackStack(route, inclusive = false)` on the destination that is already on top. Nothing happens, so ✕ and Save look dead. `isInModalContext` also stays true when no modal is open.

## Fix
`pruneStaleModalEntries(navController)` drops entries that are no longer on the back stack, plus trailing entries equal to the current destination. A modal is always presented *over* its entry, so a live entry is never the current destination. It runs before every navigation in `processNavigationState`, and inside `onModalPresented` / `onModalDismissed` for callers that use the manager directly.

The rule is a pure `internal fun liveModalEntries(...)`, covered by the module's first host tests (`./gradlew :navigation-compose:testAndroidHostTest`). The build file gains `withHostTestBuilder {}` and `kotlin("test")` for this.

## Verified
In Guardian on an emulator, without the app-side `BackHandler` workaround. Steps: Edit action → Add contact → system back → ✕ on the action form.
- 0.2.3: the form stays open.
- This branch, published locally as `0.2.4-local`: the form closes.

iOS is unaffected; this is about Android's hardware back.

Release as 0.2.4 in a separate `chore(release)` commit, as usual.

body:
Fixes the `tests/desktop-e2e/tests/daemon.rs` `an_admin_shutdown_stops_the_daemon` flake that rust-ui-dev reported (relay seq 12181: 1 failure in 12 runs, `.expect("asked")` with `ShuttingDown`).

**Cause.** `admin.shutdown` is what makes the server stop. By the time `stop` reaches the connection, its task has already finished. The connection loop's `select!` is unbiased, so it could take `stop.changed()` before `in_flight.join_next_with_id()`. `end()` then called `JoinSet::shutdown()`, which threw the finished answer away. The client read `close{ShuttingDown}` with no answer before it. The client is not involved: its reader hands a response to the waiting call before it handles a close.

**Fix** (`crates/local/ipc-server/src/connection.rs`, `end`): `abort_all()` and then join every task. A task that finished keeps its output under abort, so its answer is written ahead of the `close`, as `finished` already writes answers (a request a cancel or deadline already answered stays discarded). A task that was still running is aborted and answered only by the `close`, as before.

**Evidence.**
- `server::tests::an_admin_shutdown_is_answered_before_the_close`: the fake's `shutdown` stops the server, as the daemon's port does through its owner. The test runs 32 iterations on a **current_thread** runtime. The old `end()` fails it on the first iteration with the flake's own shape: a close where the response belongs. With the fix it passed 5 runs × 32 iterations.
- The same test on a multi-thread runtime passed **without** the fix. The connection woken by the join takes its worker's LIFO slot and runs before the serve task sets `stop`. That is why the flake is rare, and why the test pins the current-thread runtime (the comment says so).
- `cargo xtask ci` at this head: everything green except one `human_app` case (`retention::a_process_kill_…`: "the human lease never became held", 32 s inside the full run). Run alone, `human_app` passed 3/3 at 13 s each, and `--test daemon` passed 6/6. Not checked: whether `main` shows the same `human_app` case under a full run.

**Not changed.** LOCAL-IPC.md §Close says nothing about in-flight answers at shutdown, and this neither changes nor contradicts it.

## Two more commits, on architect-cto's #189 findings

**c2f362c6, conformance: the trust check asserts item 11's three remaining facts** (architect-cto's request, relay seq 12434). `trust_administration_revokes_as_policy` now asserts that the local peer is never among the allowed. It also asserts that revoking an unlisted peer is `Ok` and leaves the read-back unchanged, and so does allowing a listed one (both compared as sets). The revocation must reach **two** watchers, not one. All three runners pass: the fake, in-process and over IPC. Each assertion was mutated in the fake and failed on its own message: the self row listed, an unlisted revoke inserting, the notice told to one session only.

**b072d945, composition: a revocation forgets every session's route to the peer** (architect-cto's observation, relay seq 12437). `SessionNotices::revoked` drops the peer's routes and its pending path notice in every session, and `set_trust` calls it on a revocation that changed the policy. `MAX_ROUTED_PEERS`'s comment now says what the bound tracks under churn, and the one residual case: a message already queued from the peer can still make a route when the session drains it. Tests: `notices::tests::a_revoked_peers_route_frees_its_place` (unit) and `in_process::a_revocation_forgets_the_sessions_routes` (wiring, with the pre-revocation change as its control). Mutants that dropped the runtime hook, the route removal or the notice removal each failed.

`cargo xtask ci` at b072d945: green.

## Review rounds

- **Round 1** (blind review of b072d945): one P2 (F1) and four P3s, each judged by the review class before it was answered. The dispositions are in the PR comment. Fixes: afc7481a, 4cbd4111, 25b7a095. F1 is fixed in the contract by architect-cto's **c32367ac**, supplied on `develop-qzapp/architect-cto-01/for/p2p-network-dev-01/route-ends-at-revocation` and folded `--no-ff` (634d5101) after merging `origin/main` (3873ebac). Supplier-Review: the review class approved ac865d7b..95f2b11e with 0 P1 and 0 P2, and its P3s were applied in c32367ac. Re-review: clean.
- **The automated thread** (judged real, P3): answers written at the end could spend the control lane's last slots, so the client read EOF instead of `close{ShuttingDown}`. **09dc7633** reserves the close's slot before any answer. Pinned by `the_close_keeps_its_slot_ahead_of_the_answers`, which fails on the old tail. Re-review: clean.

Carried P3 for the next change to `connection.rs`: the `outbox` field's doc lists "a close" among what can join it, and no close is pushed there. This predates this branch.

Local `cargo xtask ci` at 09dc7633: everything green except `human_app` `retention::a_process_kill_…`, "the human lease never became held", one 30 s wait running out at 31.7 s. It is the same load-timed case seen at 2fe8c300, before any of the later commits existed. It passed alone (3/3), and GitHub's `rust` job passed at 634d5101. Reported to rust-ui-dev (relay seq 12443).

**Work commits: 3** (2fe8c300, c2f362c6, b072d945). Plus 4 review fixes, 1 supplied commit and 2 merges. Under the floor of eight, so arming waits for the owner's word.

author: pabloagn
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution -->
_Requested by **Joris**_

Before: a publisher's logo showed as it was uploaded. Logos came in different sizes, colours and backgrounds, so the cards looked uneven.

After: drop a logo (SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP) into an organization's media dialog, on the Logo tab, and you see the finished card. Switches adjust it. Save makes it the house's logo. Every card comes from one template: 3:2, black, the logo in one light ink, every logo at the same visual size and centred on its visual middle. The publisher card and header show it full-bleed. No generative model is used: this is plain image processing with sharp.

How:
- `src/lib/media/logo-card.ts` runs the pipeline:
  - It rasterizes the file. An SVG is never stored or served as SVG.
  - It reads the background from the border. A transparent logo is judged against white when it is dark, against black when it is light.
  - It builds a one-channel ink mask that keeps inner details as cut-outs: Penguin's belly, New Directions' drawing.
  - It trims, sizes by ink area (capped by a box) and centres on the ink's centre of mass.
- Switches: invert, keep colours, emblem only, smaller or bigger, and badge. Badge is for disc logos: it drops the disc with no faint ring.
- `POST /api/media/logo-card` has three modes:
  - preview: answers a PNG and stores nothing;
  - save: the original is kept beside the card as lossless WebP, and the switches go in `processing_params.logoCard`;
  - re-run: runs the switches again on a saved card's original (`mediaId`, the dialog's "Adjust").
- Docs: `docs/05_API_REFERENCE.md` and `docs/07_STORAGE.md`, Logo Cards. Changelog 0322.

Checks:
- Tests: `logo-card.test.ts` (12 tests) and `logo-cards.test.ts` (4, on PostgreSQL with S3 in memory). They cover the two faults found in the issue's first test: a resized mask that came back with three channels, and a transparent logo that lost its inner details.
- Typecheck and lint pass. `pnpm test:local` passes: 154 files, 1797 tests. Page weight: 17 of 17 routes within budget.
- Chrome, Safari and Firefox 157, at 1440, 768 and 390 px: dropping a logo shows the 1200×800 card, and a switch changes it. The alignment and design audits are clean in Chrome and Firefox.
- Safari findings that predate this change: the shared title controls sit 0.55 px off, and the audit flags the dialog's existing tab buttons as unnamed in Safari only.
- Saving needs S3, which the disposable preview does not have, so the DB test covers saving.

Limit: a logo photographed on a busy background, such as a book spine, needs a background-removal model. That is not part of this PR.

## Summary

Lighthouse (the PageSpeed Insights engine) measured **mobile 34 / desktop 65 / Best Practices 50** for https://mysoundkit.com from a datacenter client. Root causes and fixes for #366:

| Fix | Finding | Change |
|---|---|---|
| #2 Stripe eager load | `loadStripe()` ran at module scope in `live-tip-button.tsx`; the code splitter hoists that module into the shared entry chunk, so every visit downloaded + executed the full ~900KB Stripe suite and set its third-party cookies | Stripe now loads on first tip-dialog open |
| #4 geolocation-on-start | Explore homepage auto-called `getCurrentPosition()` on first visit (browser permission prompt before the user asked for anything) | Auto-request removed; explicit "use my location" button remains |
| #5 asset caching | Content-hashed `/assets/*` served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` (Workers Assets default) | `public/_headers`: `max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| #1 (zone config) | The zone challenges datacenter/"likely automated" traffic — every `api.mysoundkit.com` fetch from PageSpeed/Lighthouse gets a 403 challenge with no CORS headers, so the homepage renders empty and retries ~4x per endpoint | `scripts/fix-zone-challenges.mjs` (diagnose/`--apply`) disables free-plan Bot Fight Mode via API and adds idempotent WAF skip rules for public GET endpoints + `/assets/*` — needs a token with Zone Settings/Rulesets/Bot Management Edit |

## Implementation Notes

- **Fix #3 (route code-splitting) turned out to be a non-issue**: the `tanstackStart` plugin already runs `tanStackRouterCodeSplitter` unconditionally — the Oct 2 production build ships 98 route chunks dynamically imported from the entry. The committed static `routeTree.gen.ts` is only the dev artifact. Details in the issue comment. The remaining 505KB-gzipped entry is hoisted shared library + shared route modules (including the tip button); shrinking that further (vendor `manualChunks`, lazily-imported tip-dialog component) is follow-up work, noted in the issue.
- Route splitting discovery means the invalid `router.autoCodeSplitting` option (rejected by the start plugin's schema) was reverted — vite.config.ts is unchanged in this PR.
- Verified against the installed TanStack types (`Promise<Stripe | null>` state, `EmbeddedCheckoutProvider` accepts it when the tip dialog opens).

## Testing Notes

- `bun run verify`: check-types + react-hooks + unit/worker tests + production build — **all green** (the build's final task tree completed 5/5).
- `ultracite check` clean on all touched files.
- Build output inspected: `_headers` lands in `dist/client/`; per-route chunks present; Stripe's `dahlia` loader module remains bundled in the shared chunk (harmless dead code until a dialog opens) but no longer executes at import time.
- `scripts/fix-zone-challenges.mjs` exercised in diagnose mode against the live zone (Free Website plan, id 2b4980fd4e802700f76c46e47e0e1f83) — degrades gracefully with a read-only token and correctly distinguishes 403-unreadable from 404-absent rulesets.
- **Expected impact after the zone fix + deploy**: mobile FCP/LCP ~6s → ~2s (no challenge/retry storm), TBT down (no Stripe eval: ~620ms of scripting/parse on mobile), Best Practices 50 → 90+ (console CORS errors, third-party cookies, and geolocation-on-start all resolved).

Follow-ups (in the issue): re-run Lighthouse after deploy + zone fix; entry-chunk `manualChunks`; render-blocking 34KB globals CSS; SSR TTFB ~440ms; source maps.

Closes #366

## Intent

Do them all. Asked after this proposal: "Real interval structure: repeat blocks ('Rep 3 of 5'), distance reps like 6 x 800 m, warm-up and cool-down that end when you press Lap, strides at the end of easy runs, run-walk as a proper repeat. Targets that match your watch: easy and long runs use your Garmin heart-rate zones by number ('Zone 2') so the watch and the plan agree, tempo and intervals keep pace ranges, wide enough the watch doesn't nag." Roadmap issues #18 and #29.

Fold them in: (1) recovery steps between reps can end when heart rate drops below a set value, with a time cap as a fallback; (2) a secondary cadence target where it helps (for example easy runs or strides), only if the Garmin payload supports a secondary target; (3) skip the last rest in repeat groups, and repeat-until-Lap for strides; (4) short coaching cues in each step note, kept within Garmin's note length.

## What Changed

- Add persisted repeat groups, distance intervals, Lap-ended warm-ups and cool-downs, easy-run strides, and skipped final recoveries. Update adaptation, API schemas, and mobile workout graphs for structured steps.
- Use cached Garmin zone numbers with heart-rate fallbacks, wider pace bands, optional secondary cadence targets, and coaching notes capped at 200 characters.
- Document unsupported combinations: heart-rate recovery with a time cap and repeat-until-Lap remain unimplemented. Recoveries use time or distance, and strides use fixed repetitions.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: Required behaviors are omitted or conditionally replaced, and normal plan creation silently loses the cadence data needed for secondary targets.

## Testing

Real HTTP scenarios and focused backend/mobile tests passed; API artifacts were saved. No screenshots were possible because the native simulator is unavailable. Garmin execution remains untested.

author: ayshinko
body:
## What

Local inference servers (Strata: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata) already know their own throughput — `GET /metrics` reports the live decode rate, the decode mean, the prompt-processing rate and the timings of finished requests. This PR lets `pi-token-speed` read those numbers directly instead of estimating TPS from client-side stream deltas.

It is **strictly opt-in and per provider**, so nothing changes for anyone who does not configure it.

```json
{
  "tokenSpeed": {
    "providerOverrides": {
      "strata": {
        "nativeMetrics": {
          "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metrics",
          "intervalMs": 300,
          "timeoutMs": 500
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

While streaming the status bar shows the server's own numbers:

```
⚡ 68.4 tok/s · Mean 64.9 · PP 1180 tok/s
```

and at the end of the request:

```
⚡ Mean 64.7 tok/s · 1248 tok · 19.3s
```

## How it is wired in

- **`src/native/strata-metrics.ts`** (new): a dependency-free poller (`fetch` + `AbortController` timeout, one in-flight request at a time). It parses the `live` block, parses the newest completed request record, latches the prefill rate (Strata zeroes `prefill_tok_s_mean` once decode starts), and records a baseline request timestamp at stream start so a previous request's record never leaks into the current one.
- **`src/core/engine.ts`**: owns the poller lifecycle (`applyConfig` / `start` / `stop`) and exposes `nativeSnapshot`, `hasNativeMetrics` and `finalizeNativeMetrics()`.
- **`src/core/events.ts` + `index.ts`**: `agent_end` now awaits one bounded final fetch so the last status uses the server's completed record.
- **`src/ui/renderer.ts`**: `renderNative()` renders the compact native format; tier colors and the `display` suffix (TTFT/stats) still work.
- **`src/settings/items/override-validator.ts`**: sanitizes the block (url required, `intervalMs`/`timeoutMs` clamped to 100–5000 ms) with the same warning style as the other override keys.

## Safety / fallback

The adapter never throws. If the endpoint is unreachable, returns a non-200, hangs past the timeout, or returns an unexpected payload, `nativeSnapshot` stays `null` and the existing sliding-window counter path runs unchanged. No `/tps` UI changes — the feature is configured through `settings.json` only.

## Testing

- 31 new tests in `tests/strata-metrics.test.ts` (live/completed parsing, malformed payloads, idle state, prefill latching, baseline filtering, timeout abort, non-200, finalize fallback, engine integration, renderer formats, override validation).
- `npm test`: **209 passed** (178 baseline + 31 new). `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Verified live against a running Strata server (`qwen3.8-flash-next-q2_0`, engine 0.1.39): live snapshot `53.2 tok/s / mean 53.2 / PP 17.4`, final record `53.7 tok/s · 1200 tok · 22.3s`.

## Caveats

- The endpoint shape is Strata's (`live` + `requests`); the parser is deliberately tolerant of missing fields, but other servers with a different schema would need their own adapter.
- `nativeMetrics` is only read from `providerOverrides` blocks, not from the base config, since it is provider-specific.

author: iamnotshifu
body:
## Why
Capturing an image-heavy marketing site produced (1) 30s `load` timeouts with zero output and (2) full-page screenshots with large blank areas, because scroll-triggered sections never appeared. Auditing the code turned up related bugs.

## What changed
**Capture**
- Scrolls the page top-to-bottom before `full`/`sections` captures so scroll-reveal content and lazy images appear (`--no-scroll` to disable).
- If `--wait-until` times out but the document is usable, capture anyway, cancel stalled requests, record a warning (`--strict-load` to fail instead).
- Screenshots respect `--timeout`. One failing page no longer aborts the batch; Chromium is always closed.
- New flags: `--freeze-animations`, `--user-agent`, `--ignore-https-errors`, `--headers-all-origins`.
- Images cancelled by a `load` timeout are re-requested once; images that still don't load are reported as a warning, and stalled requests are cancelled so screenshots can't hang. New `--image-wait <ms>` flag.

**Inputs**
- URLs without a scheme get `https://` (`http://` for localhost); pasted Markdown links are unwrapped; all invalid URLs reported together up front.
- Folder slugs no longer collide for query strings, non-ASCII paths, long paths, or different localhost ports.
- Sitemap fetch has a timeout, cycle guard, depth limit, and `.xml.gz` support. CSV/URL files tolerate BOMs and comments.

**Auth / security**
- `--bearer` and `--header` now go only to the captured site and its subdomains, not third parties (`--headers-all-origins` restores old behavior).
- Credentials embedded in URLs are redacted from `run-record.json`. Malformed `--header`/`--cookie` values now error instead of being skipped.

**Manifest / diff / zip**
- Manifest entries are replaced per job (no stale-error pile-up), paths use `/`, writes are atomic, corrupt files are moved aside.
- `diff`: unreadable screenshots are reported as errors (fail closed) instead of crashing; matching tolerates trailing slashes, Windows/POSIX paths, and moved manifests.
- `--zip` with `--out .` no longer writes `..zip` or includes itself.
- Broken `shotsweep.config.json` now errors instead of being silently ignored; unknown keys warned about.

## Behavior changes worth noting
- Scrolling is on by default, so captures of pages with scroll-reveal content will differ from earlier baselines. Re-baseline before running `diff`.
- Bearer/header scoping (above) could affect anyone sending credentials to a different origin than the page.

author: nachx639
body:
## Summary
- A read-only **Changes** sheet: changed and untracked files with +/- counts, and a per-file diff wrapped to the screen. Reached from the compact session menu, with the changed-file count the git status watcher already has.
- An opt-in ship flow from that sheet: **Commit**, **Push** and **Create PR** (via `gh`), each with a confirmation that shows exactly what will run. Off unless `"gitShip": true` is in config.json.
- Shared helpers for full-screen sheets: focus handling (`sheet-a11y.ts`) and an iOS ghost-click guard (`ghost-click.ts`).

## Why
When an agent works in a session, the first thing you want on a phone is "what did it change?", and often the second is "commit and push it". Today that means typing git commands on a phone keyboard.

## What changes for existing users
- **Session menu (compact menu):** a new read-only **Changes** item; greyed out with the reason outside a git repository.
- **Commit / Push / Create PR: off.** Buttons are hidden and the routes answer `403 { code: "disabled" }`. To turn on: `~/.vibetunnel/config.json` `"gitShip": true` (read on every request, no restart). Not settable through `PUT /api/config`; no env var or CLI flag. It stays off in `upstream-pr/37-defaults`, which only adds a Settings row for it.
- `GET /api/config` gains `gitShip`.
- **Mac app:** without https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/717, a settings save from the Mac app drops unknown config.json keys, so `gitShip` falls back to off (fail-safe).

## How to test
```bash
cd web
pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck
pnpm vitest run --mode=server git-changes git-ship config
pnpm vitest run --mode=client changes-sheet ship-sheet commit-message ghost-click sheet-a11y
```
Manual: open a session in a git repository on a phone, menu > Changes: file list and diffs, no ship buttons. Add `"gitShip": true`, reopen: Commit / Push / Create PR appear. Commit a file, push a feature branch, try pushing `main` (needs an explicit tick). Remove the key: the routes answer 403 at once.

All git tests use temporary repositories with a local bare remote and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`; `gh` is a fake script. Tested with the client and server suites, Biome and typecheck (each commit on its own). Guard tests were checked to fail with the guard removed.

## Notes / risks
- Medium-High by nature (writes to the user's repositories from a phone). Guards: auth on every route; off unless config.json says otherwise; path traversal refused in any spelling, including a symlinked folder that leaves the repository; `execFile` arrays only (no shell), literal pathspecs after `--`; option-looking file names and branch names refused; no force push; `main`/`master` need explicit confirmation; commit hooks are honoured (no `--no-verify`); one operation per repo at a time, with timeouts.
- Every server error has a stable `code`, translated client-side in all 8 locales; the commit message draft is deterministic (no model) and always editable.
- `?path=` on the read-only changes routes accepts any folder the server user can read, like the existing `/api/git/status`.
- The PR URL is parsed as the last `https://` URL that `gh` prints.

## Stacking
Depends on: https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/724, https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/726; review only the commits after https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/726. Independent of 10-15. The first commit (sheet helpers) is identical to one in https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/732; drop it from whichever lands second.

## Known conflicts with other PRs
- https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/732: locale tails only (keep both).
- https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/734: locale tails and `utils/sheet-a11y.ts` (keep 13b's two extra lines).
- https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/737: locale tails, `config-service.ts` (keep both), and `types/config.ts` (keep both, then re-add the second field's `/**` opener).
- `upstream-pr/24-share-links`: config files as above, plus `session-view.ts`, `compact-menu.ts`, `session-header.ts`, `server-config-service.ts` (keep both menu entries/props).
- https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/717: `config-service.ts`, `types/config.ts`, `server-config-service.ts` and the config tests; https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/716: `server.ts` imports. Keep both.
- `upstream-pr/21-mac-sessions`: `ghost-click.ts` (21 appends a helper; take 21's) and config files. `upstream-pr/23-previews`, `upstream-pr/20-tmux-attach`: `compact-menu.ts` (keep both items).
- https://github.com/amantus-ai/vibetunnel/pull/736: clean.

author: ahmadsaeedzaidi
body:
The active YouTube extraction pipeline has outgrown the old ML-oriented main branch. This PR brings the review branch up to the running implementation, removes obsolete code and workflows, and adds a hosted operator UI, topic knowledge graph, reusable storage core and observed-cycle Discord reporting.

- Remove retired training/prediction code and registry bootstrap workflows; consolidate current documentation, skills and test tiers.
- Host a read-only dashboard for extraction, storage, tracking and graph exploration. The deployed route uses trusted TLS and password protection; credentials stay outside Git.
- Add Grapher as a registered Maia agent, scheduled every ten minutes with a dedicated one-key reserve excluded from dynamic main-pool allocation. With the current three keys, discovery and tracking retain one each, and the previously manual Archeologist reserve becomes Grapher capacity. Build the graph from YouTube's observed Wikipedia topic classifications, using durable owned leases, bounded video/channel backfill and browser-safe graph/detail/export APIs. These are classifications, not inferred transcript facts.
- Extract a Python 3.12 hot/cold handoff library with no runtime dependencies, immutable digest-addressed writes, readback verification, conditional finalization, and SQLite/filesystem adapters. Atlas keeps the project-specific PostgreSQL and vault adapters. Document in-memory payload limits, adapter requirements and application-owned scheduling, leases, backups and cleanup.
- Reduce SQL and local cache pressure through two-day metric retention, count/byte/time-bounded transcript reconciliation, temporary Hub downloads and targeted vacuum settings. Verified copies are required before releasing hot content; concurrent updates remain hot.
- Overhaul the 15-minute Discord heartbeat to show actual scheduled cycles, failed/late/slow work, extraction failures, tracking, verified storage progress, disk pressure and graph coverage. Independent SQL collectors run concurrently under deadlines. Missing metrics remain unavailable. Remove empty-audio API probes; distinguish provider configuration from credential health and optional Prefect telemetry from live scheduler health. Bound webhook delivery and protect private URLs in error logs. Quota observation does not rewrite shared state, and unreadable state cannot silence the rest of the report.
- Diagnose the failure backlog and fix disk-full/download errors being mislabeled as missing remote media. Confirmed absence remains distinct from retryable local/cache/auth/transport errors. Add bounded audio recovery that preserves artifacts, completed stages and legacy whole-video failures. Heartbeat reports overlapping failure cohorts and counts affected videos once in the same aggregate, eliminating a redundant database scan.
- Keep CI on locked installs, the canonical quality/unit gate, isolated PostgreSQL regressions and a production image build. Unit fixtures block unmocked network/DNS access and isolate agent state.

Validation: `make check` passed 513 unit tests, lint, types, JS syntax and links in 25 current guides. All 16 isolated real PostgreSQL regressions passed. A copied storage package built and installed as a wheel in a fresh virtual environment outside the repo; verified handoff and cold reads passed without Atlas/Maia/Prefect/Hugging Face, including a second process. Read-only live heartbeat data collection took 0.40 seconds; the scheduled report took 1.83 seconds during concurrent startup work. Earlier public browser checks verified trusted TLS, password protection for HTML/assets/APIs, live video/graph details, bounded JSON export and mobile layout.

Activation: the additive graph/maintenance migrations are live, and the password-protected UI is hosted at https://opencodeserver.duckdns.org:8443/pleiades/. Approved cleanup of unused Docker build cache and the pipeline's local Hub dataset cache reclaimed about 15 GB; remote vault contents and SQL data were preserved. Verified reconciliation and topic backfill continue gradually. Ordinary VACUUM completed; no full-table rewrite was used. The deployment requeued exactly 57 audio stages with explicit disk-full log evidence; other failure cohorts and their artifacts were preserved. The heartbeat keeps its 15-minute cadence, with process-local observation history explicitly reset on restart; whole-host silence still needs an external watchdog.

The review branch snapshots changes onto main while preserving the running checkout's original dirty index. Historical branches remain in place, and the PR is not merged automatically. Existing installations must apply reviewed additive migrations rather than rerun legacy provisioning.

Latest verification: GitHub CI is green at dc46abd6427974800d812ba1d1051c28d6327086, including the canonical gate, 16 PostgreSQL regressions and production image build: https://github.com/AhmadSaeedZaidi/pleiades/actions/runs/37241451159

Live activation: Grapher completed its first dedicated-key cycle with 189 observations and 11 unavailable resources. Exactly 57 audio stages were requeued after matching explicit ENOSPC evidence; remaining failed-stage videos are 497 (276 raw, 5 audio, 216 visuals), overlapping 493 of the unchanged 2,595 legacy failures. Discord accepted the new report; ingestion remains active with no automatic restarts.

- `shelf_lower_not_counted` and `unit_lower_not_counted` as flat lists.
- Offer kinds `autoship`, `bundle` and `bulk`.
- Check value `not-read`.

The example in `SIMILAR_OUTPUT.md` is a **new real answer, re-read live today** (log below).

## Design decisions: what I chose, what I rejected, and why

| # | Decision | Chosen | Rejected and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | How each fact was read | `read` on each fact: `shelf_price`, `size`, `availability` and each offer. Values: `page-text`, `reader-summary`, `listing-page`, `search-snippet`, plus `shopper` for your own size. Only `page-text` counts. A compared item needs its price and stock from page text, otherwise it is flagged and shown as a lead. A `search-snippet` price is refused outright (SKILL already said snippet prices never enter). Snippet offers must be `unverified`. Where raw HTML and the browser differ, the browser's visible text wins. | **One item-level field:** it cannot say "price confirmed, offer only from the summary", which is exactly the Burst case. **Raw HTML as the authority:** today's read found a `display:none` ITALY10 block on Seattle Coffee Gear that the page does not show. |
| 1b | Page budget | A verifying re-read of a link already counted is free. 404s and blocked pages still count. | **Charging re-reads:** the new rule requires verification, and charging for it pushes agents to skip it. **Free 404s:** a 404 is still a request to a store; the fix is "never build or guess a link", now in SKILL. |
| 2 | Times | Run `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` right after each read and copy it. The checker requires every `checked_at`/`seen_at` inside `[started_at, finished_at]`. `similar-check` passes its own clock, so a `finished_at` ahead of it fails; `validate()` stays pure (`now` is a parameter). The doc says what it cannot catch: a made-up time inside the window. | **One run-level time:** loses per-page freshness. **An "estimated" flag:** an escape hatch that reads as honest. |
| 3 | Packs | The parser reads `12.5 oz (Case of 12)`, `case of 12, 12.5 oz`, `12 Ounce (Pack of 6)`, `250 ml x 6` and count words (heads, sachets, tea bags, bags, pods, capsules, cans, cartridges, filters, refills, pieces, each, ea, pack, count). The lowest shelf line compares only counted items **the same size as yours** (within 1%); other sizes compete on the per-unit line. | **Multiplying "N ct" by a measure:** "24 ct, 9.4 oz" pods is a total weight, so it is still refused. **"Per can" for cases:** cans differ (12.5 vs 13 oz), so per printed oz is exact. |
| 4 | No unit | `"unit": "none"` once for the whole answer (shoes, earbuds): every `size` is null, no `unit_price`, and no size words in the render. If your size is unknown and the kind has a unit, the shelf line is `null` and the answer asks "What size is yours?". A shopper-given size is recorded as `read: shopper`. A candidate's unit price no longer needs your size. | **A per-item `no unit applies` literal:** it cannot tell shoes from a coffee bag whose size is not printed. **Keeping "unit price only when both sizes are printed":** that threw away Vertere's per-oz price in the Finca El Puente run. |
| 5 | Lowest lines | Computed by `render` from the numbers, with no JSON flags. Under 2% below your price reads "no meaningful saving found" with both prices; the same rule applies on the unit line. When every counted price is from one host: "Only X's price could be counted". A "Your product: …; it is not counted below." line comes first when yours is out of stock, has no price in page text, is in another currency or is described. Lower-but-not-counted lists name flagged **and excluded** cheaper items. When nothing at your size is counted, the bar is your own price. | **Flags the agent sets:** more first-try failures, and they could disagree with the numbers. **Keeping the list inside `shelf`:** the list must exist when the shelf line is empty (the Open Farm case). |
| 5b | Same product | `same_product: true` ranks first even when excluded, then most `same` checks, excluded last within each group. | **Same product first only among non-excluded items:** the Rishi tea at Vitacost (out of stock, $6.20) would still rank below a different tea. |
| 6 | Brand-locked consumables | "Fits the shopper's model" is always a must-have for refills, cartridges, filters and heads. When nothing qualifies, the render says "**Similar products:** none qualified" before the lowest lines, and the section is headed "Products looked at, none qualified". | **Dropping excluded items:** the shopper should still see why each one failed. |
| 7 | Offer kinds | Added `autoship`, `bundle` and `bulk`. `other` stays for anything else, and the error message says so. | **Folding them into `other`:** three runs reached for these words first. |
| 7b | Contract version | Bumped to `similar-v2`. | **Keeping v1 with new required fields:** an old answer would fail with confusing messages; the version says the rules changed. |
| 8 | Install | The recommended Claude Code install is a sparse clone: `--filter=blob:none --sparse` plus `sparse-checkout set deal_finder scripts`, about 1 MB, measured today, and the checker runs from it. The two-file install stays, with a plain "**nothing checks the answer**" warning. | **A standalone checker file:** it imports the package; a sparse clone keeps one source. |

## Defects found, and what this PR does with each

Report letter and number refer to `data/deal-finder-accept-<x>1/report.md`.

| Report | Defect | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| a1-1, b1-1, c1-12, d1-7, e1-1 | The page reader summarises and does not quote. Burst's $21.00 "Sale price" was a gated subscribe price; Driftaway showed "all sold out" | **Fixed** (decision 1). Test `test_the_burst_reader_summary_price_never_counts`. |
| e1-2 | A price read from a listing page was marked `observed-now` | **Fixed**: `read: listing-page` is never counted (`test_a_compared_item_needs_its_price_from_the_page_text`). |
| e1-14 | A static fetch can hide part of the price block | **Fixed**: the browser's visible text wins where it differs from raw HTML. |
| e1-10 | A shared browser showed another store's page | **Fixed**: SKILL says to check that the page shown is the link opened. |
| a1-2, c1-5, e1-8 | The budget did not say whether re-reads count, and stale links burned it | **Fixed** (decision 1b). |
| c1-4, d1-8 | 404s, closed stores, news sites and `*.it.com` look-alikes | **Fixed**: links only from results or the store's menu; news, review and look-alike sites are not stores. 404s still count (1b). |
| b1-12 | Walmart is unreadable | **Fixed**: named with Amazon in SKILL and README. |
| e1-9 | The fetch location picks the currency or region | **Fixed**: SKILL note; never convert. |
| a1-3, b1-2, c1-13, d1-9 (and c1-9, first half) | Per-page times were made up; `finished_at` was ahead of the clock | **Fixed** (decision 2). `TimesTest`, plus `test_the_command_holds_the_finish_time_to_its_clock`. |
| d1-1 | "12.5 oz (Case of 12)" was read as one can | **Fixed** (decision 3). `test_the_open_farm_case_of_12_is_twelve_cans`, plus parser tests. |
| d1-2 | A single $4.49 can was the "lowest shelf price" against a $55.88 case | **Fixed**: equal-quantity shelf line. `test_a_single_can_is_never_the_lowest_shelf_price_against_a_case`. |

body:
Playtest feedback: *get rid of the hook, add a grind button, incorporate grinds, add ramps to jump, make the city more skatable.*

## Removed
- The sling line, plus everything that came with it: anchors, masts, lamps, the bracket, the HOOK button and the hook perks.
- Unchanged: the stone sling.
- Kept: flat roofs as surfaces, the above-the-lens camera rule, and the never-stuck-in-a-wall collision fix.

## Grinds
- **GRIND** is `C`, gamepad RB, or a GRIND button in HOOK's old spot.
  - On the ground it pops the board.
  - In the air it catches the line under the board.
- **What's grindable**: rails, ledges, benches and the Channel wall tops (85 lines).
- **On a line**: ride it to the end, run out of speed, or ollie or flip out.
- **Readability**:
  - the line you're heading for is lit in your colour
  - on a line you get sparks and a scrape
  - grinds are named by the kind of line (50-50, 5-0, crooked, feeble, smith, slides)

## Ramps
- Kickers are now real slopes: you ride up and leave the lip with air from your speed and the slope, about 2.8 m off the Lot's at full speed.
- Ramps and rails are now drawn. The town's ramps were always in the data but never rendered.
- One kicker authored inside the cafe is removed.
- Ramps stay off the roadway, per the existing design test.

## More skatable: the Lot
- **The Lot**: a poured pad in the empty field between Commons Street and Ridgeline Road, with paths in from all sides. It has four kickers, flat bars, a handrail, a long centre rail and a ledge, and it's the quietest place in town.
- **The plaza** gets a kicker straight onto a flat bar, plus benches.

## Jobs and kit
- Roof objectives are replaced by **grind** and **air** objectives:
  - TAG grinds the plaza ledges
  - PHOTOGRAPH is taken at the top of a kicker
  - the final job grinds the Lot handrail and airs both kickers
- New perks: **WAX** (grinds keep their speed) and **BIG POP** (more air).

## Tests
- `traversal.test.ts` is rewritten for grinds and ramps.
- Jobs, kit and touch tests are updated.
- Full suite: 640 passing; typecheck and build clean.
- Checked in a real browser at desktop and phone sizes: grinding the Lot rail and 2.85 m of air off its kicker.

Design note: `docs/45-grinds-ramps-and-the-lot.md`.

author: cm-ai-ops-bot
body:
Submitter checklist
- [x] Issue is clearly tagged: no upstream work item; ported from the cmdemo1 demo system, https://github.com/clearmeasure-aisf-sample-apps/cmdemo1-workorders/pull/8
- [x] Narrate status of the branch: feature complete
- [x] You expect the approval checklist to be satisfied

## What and why
On Linux outside GitHub Actions, `Init` in `build.ps1` always set `NUGET_PACKAGES=/tmp/nuget-packages`, overriding a cache path the machine already sets. The restored packages take about 1.6 GB; where `/tmp` is a small in-memory disk (2 GB tmpfs on the cmdemo1 build machine) the restore fills it and fails. `Init` now keeps `NUGET_PACKAGES` when it is set and falls back to `/tmp/nuget-packages` otherwise. GitHub Actions and Windows are unchanged.

## AI-factory containers (second and third commits)
The agent images (`.bob/skills/ai-factory-executor/Dockerfile.agent`, `Dockerfile.agent.claude`) set `NUGET_PACKAGES=/home/bobagent/.nuget/packages`, and the Argo workflow template mounts its `nuget-cache` volume at that path, but `build.ps1` replaced it with `/tmp/nuget-packages`, so Argo builds bypassed that cache. The `docker run` scripts (`container-manager.ps1`, `run-dev.ps1`, `run-experiment.ps1`) mounted the `ai-factory-nuget` volume at `/tmp/nuget-packages` only to match `build.ps1`. With the first commit alone they would restore into the container's writable layer every run, so the second commit mounts that volume at `/home/bobagent/.nuget/packages` and points the entrypoints' ownership fix there; the third (from the review) changes that fix from a recursive `chown -R` to the mount root only, so Argo pods do not walk the whole shared PVC (already writable through `fsGroup`) on every start. The scripts parse; the containers were not run here (no Docker on the test machine). These are separate commits, so they can be dropped if maintainers prefer another layout.

This touches build scripts, which `CLAUDE.md` asks maintainers to approve.

## How it was tested
- `PrivateBuild.ps1` with `DATABASE_ENGINE=SQLite` and `NUGET_PACKAGES` set to a home-directory cache (Linux, .NET SDK 10.0.401): compile with warnings as errors 0 warnings, unit tests 938 passed, integration tests 326 passed (`Category!=SqlServerOnly`), CRAP gate passed (0 production methods over 6). Packages restored into the configured cache.
- `Init` with `NUGET_PACKAGES` set keeps it; with it unset it still sets `/tmp/nuget-packages` (that restore filled this machine's 2 GB `/tmp`, which is the original problem).

## CI
`build.yml` runs on `push` only, so it does not run for a pull request from a fork. A maintainer can run it by pushing this branch to the upstream repository.

author: bledonibishi
body:
Task 6. Targets `dev`. Independent of #9 (S3); docs/`.env.example` may need a trivial merge.

## What changed
- **Sessions can require a licence**: `requireDrivingLicence: true` on `POST /v1/sessions`. New upload kinds `LICENCE_FRONT` (read) and `LICENCE_BACK` (stored for reviewers only). Submit then also needs `ID_BACK` and `LICENCE_FRONT` (`400` otherwise); sessions that did not ask are unaffected and an uploaded licence is ignored for them.
- **Parser** (`src/documents/licence`): reads fields **1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 4d, 5 and 9** by their printed numbers from OCR text: any order or layout, `.`/`)` labels, `.`/`-`/`/` dates, `ë→E` via `normalizeName`, date lookalikes (`5.03.1990` is a date, not label 5) handled. Look-alike characters (O/0, I/1, S/5, B/8) are repaired in dates and numbers and reported as `LICENCE_OCR_REPAIRED`, which blocks auto-approval. Unreadable fields are "not found"; nothing is guessed. Fields 1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 4d and 5 must all be read; categories (9) are recorded, not required.
- **Checks**: not expired (expiring today is valid), issued in the past, expiry after issue, validity 6 months to 15 years, holder ≥ 15 at issue.
- **Cross-check against the ID's MRZ**: personal number (4d vs the ID's optional data 2), surname, given names (one may be the leading part of the other), date of birth. If the ID could not be read the result is `unavailable` (`LICENCE_CROSSCHECK_UNAVAILABLE`), never a match.
- **OCR modes**: `OcrProvider.readText(image, { mode: 'mrz' | 'text' })`. Tesseract's MRZ alphabet whitelist would destroy a licence, so `text` mode runs without it; `TESSERACT_TEXT_LANG` (e.g. `eng+sqi`).
- **Privacy**: only flags and field *numbers* are stored/returned (`verification.licence`: `found`, `fields`, `expired`, `datesValid`, `repaired`, `crossCheck`). No licence value is stored, logged or put in a webhook; the ID values used for comparison exist only in memory. A test searches the API response, DB rows, audit log and webhook events for the printed values.
- **Decision**: a session that required a licence is auto-approved only if the licence is completely clean on top of every existing check; otherwise review. Never auto-rejects.
- Review UI shows the licence images and each result, with readable issue labels. Retention, erasure and evidence export already handle documents generically (a test erases a five-document session).
- Docs: `docs/kosovo-documents.md` (how it works, codes, limits), README, `.env.example`.

## Testing
`pnpm typecheck && pnpm build && pnpm test`: 263 pass (14 consecutive runs). 24 parser/check unit tests, decision-rule unit tests (including "licence required but missing" and "unclean licence with codes dropped"), a Tesseract test that the two modes pass different arguments, and 14 e2e tests: flag validation, submit requirements, clean approve, auto-approve off, each cross-check mismatch, expired/implausible/partial/unreadable/repaired licences, unreadable ID, no OCR engine, transient failure and retry, licence ignored when not asked, erasure. Synthetic text for fictional people only.
Also fixed a flaky retention test (a zero-day window raced the Node/Postgres clock difference of a few ms).

## Not done / open
- **Provisional: never run on a real licence photo.** The parser follows the field numbering in `docs/kosovo-documents.md` and tests use synthetic text. Real Tesseract accuracy on the Albanian/Serbian text and the background pattern is unknown; expect many sessions to need review until it is tuned against local samples (`fixtures/private/`, git-ignored). If you share a few real OCR dumps (text only, no images) I can tune the label handling.
- **QR code on the back is not decoded**, by instruction.
- The licence portrait is not compared with the selfie (face match still uses the ID photo); categories are not returned to tenants. Both are easy follow-ups if wanted.
- Matching is against the ID card only. A licence-only session (no ID) is not supported yet.

author: mirkobozzetto
body:
## What changes for the user

- Chats tab: **New conversation** opens a menu (native on iOS 26, web popover elsewhere): **With your notes** or **With Hermes**.
- **With your notes** opens the notes chat, unchanged.
- **With Hermes** opens an empty conversation with Hermes' face. Questions go to the user's own Hermes; tool calls fold into an "N steps" row; user bubbles are ink.
- The Chats list shows who answers (FlowFlow icon or Hermes face). A Hermes conversation reopens with its full history.
- Leaving the app mid-answer: the turn keeps running on Hermes and the reply is there on return.
- Settings > Connections: a Hermes card (address, key, "Save and test", one-sentence result). Not configured, unreachable or key refused: one sentence and a link to Settings.

## How it works

FlowFlow is a Hermes channel through Hermes' built-in API server. A Hermes session holds the history; FlowFlow keeps a device-local pointer to it.

- `infrastructure/hermes.rs`: HTTP client (sessions, messages, `/v1/runs`, SSE events with `Last-Event-ID` resume, run status). Errors map to not configured / unreachable / key refused / not found.
- `application/hermes_chat.rs`: history folded into turns and steps, live reply, send (opens a `flowflow_` session on the first question), follow (re-attaches after a dropped stream, clears the pending run when it ends).
- Migration V32 `hermes_conversations` (device-local: out of sync and backups). `hermes_api_key` joins the sensitive settings.
- UI: `HermesChatView`, `HermesReply`, `ComposerRole::AskHermes` (no "+", no mentions), Chats list faces, settings card. The native glass bridge accepts an anchor in the side menu (`chats-plus`).

## Commits

- `feat(hermes): client and device-local conversations for Hermes chats`
- `feat(hermes): talk to Hermes from the Chats tab`

## Checks

- `tests/hermes_test.rs`: 10 integration tests (real captured payloads, scripted server: refused key, unreachable server, first question, dropped stream resumed, forgotten run). `space_schema_test` and `backup` updated, 40 green.
- `cargo clippy --features mobile` clean.
- Validated on iPhone: connection test, Hermes conversation, notes chat unchanged.

## Server

The Hermes API server was enabled on the VPS (loopback, exposed tailnet-only with `tailscale serve --https=8642`, key in Hermes' `.env`).

Closes #175

author: titaosahraoui
body:
Confidence Score: 0/5

This PR is not safe to merge until the migration and availability lifecycle failures are corrected.

Findings

1.  **Equal timestamps block migration** ▶ 2.  **Cleanup cancels valid windows** ▶ 3.  **Due windows remain editable** ▶ 4.  **Edits race with cancellation** ▶ 5.  **Messages cannot be cleared** ▶ 6.  **Expired windows still show editing** ▶ 7.  **Integration fixtures persist** ▶ 8.   **Unauthorised requests trigger global writes** ▶
Fix with agent prompt `````markdown ### Issue 1 apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261004220000_team_availability_no_overlap/migration.sql:13 Two existing overlapping OPEN windows can have the same millisecond-precision `createdAt`. Neither is strictly older than the other, so this update cancels neither and the new exclusion constraint fails to install. Use a deterministic tie-breaker when resolving existing overlaps. ### Issue 2 apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261004220000_team_availability_no_overlap/migration.sql:5-15 Suppose A overlaps B and B overlaps C, but A does not overlap C. This update cancels both B and C because C overlaps the earlier B, even though B is also being cancelled. The team unnecessarily loses C, which could coexist with A. ### Issue 3 apps/api/src/modules/matchmaking/matchmaking.service.ts:218 Expiry is applied lazily, so a window can still be stored as OPEN after its deadline. This check permits editing it; moving its start into the future also resets `expiresAt`, keeping a window that should have expired OPEN. Reject or expire due windows before allowing edits. ### Issue 4 apps/api/src/modules/matchmaking/matchmaking.service.ts:277 PATCH checks OPEN status before entering the transaction, but cancellation and expiry do not take this advisory lock. If either changes the status before this unconditional update, PATCH still succeeds and changes the times and preferences of a CANCELLED or EXPIRED window. Recheck the target's status as part of the locked write. ### Issue 5 apps/mobile/src/screens/LookingForMatchEditorScreen.tsx:253 When a captain erases an existing message, this expression sends `undefined`. PATCH interprets that as “leave unchanged,” so saving succeeds but the old message remains. Send `null` for an empty edited message. ### Issue 6 apps/mobile/src/screens/RecommendedOpponentsScreen.tsx:115-122 A window can arrive here marked OPEN but already be past its deadline. Fetching recommendations expires it, while this edit action remains available based on the earlier route state. The editor then offers “Save Adjustments,” but PATCH returns 409. Refresh the window state and offer creation of a new window instead. ### Issue 7 apps/api/src/modules/matchmaking/recommendation-eligibility.integration.test.ts:343-345 This suite creates users, teams, ratings, and future OPEN windows, but teardown only disconnects. Every run leaves those records in the shared test database, where they accumulate and can affect later recommendation tests. Delete the suite's fixtures before disconnecting. ### Issue 8 apps/api/src/modules/matchmaking/matchmaking.service.ts:379 Any authenticated user can request recommendations for an arbitrary ID and trigger expiry across all teams before the availability lookup or captain check returns 403 or 404. Authorize the request before performing this write, while still checking fresh status afterward. **How this was verified:** The authenticated route calls a global OPEN-availability update before checking the requested availability or its captain. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

Summary

The PR adds availability GET/PATCH endpoints, database-level overlap protection, batched recommendation lookups, and a mobile edit flow. - The overlap migration needs a safe resolution for existing conflicts. - PATCH lifecycle checks and the mobile edit flow need corrections. - The new integration fixtures need teardown.
Diagram ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR Mobile[Mobile edit flow] --> PATCH[PATCH availability] PATCH --> Service[Validate and lock team] Service --> DB[(Availability and overlap constraint)] DB --> Recs[Recommendations] Recs --> Batch[Batch teams and ratings] ```

author: andreymikhailovvv-sys
body:
### Motivation
- Заменить устаревшую ручную механику `paymentUrl` на серверную интеграцию с YooKassa, чтобы цена и объём кредитов были доверенными и задавались только на сервере.

author: karimelzoser
body:
## Purpose

Implement the post-reservation operational core on top of the buyer/EOI/queue/reservation workflow: secure documents and signatures, payment/cheque schedules, and broker commission readiness/countdown.

## Documents and object storage

- S3-compatible object storage abstraction; file bytes stay out of PostgreSQL
- server-generated object keys and presigned PUT uploads
- SHA-256, byte-size and MIME verification with object HEAD before finalization
- immutable storage keys/hashes stored with business records
- versioned document templates
- required signer roles per template
- late transaction document uploads after reservation
- verify/reject workflow
- drawn/uploaded/typed/provider-neutral signature records
- contract signing and stamping update transaction milestones automatically
- Buyer document read/upload/sign permissions are `.self` ownership-scoped rather than project-wide

## Finance

- one payment schedule per transaction
- schedule currency must match the frozen reservation currency
- schedule item values must reconcile exactly to the frozen reservation total
- at least one down-payment item is required
- payment verification automatically derives `DOWN_PAYMENT_RECEIVED`
- installment status supports upcoming / due / overdue / paid / waived / cancelled
- separate physical cheque schedule and lifecycle:
  - expected
  - received
  - deposited
  - cleared
  - returned
  - cancelled
- cheque number + bank required once a cheque is received
- `CHEQUES_RECEIVED` is derived automatically and can revert when a cheque is returned
- buyer finance reads use ownership-scoped `installment.read.self`

## Broker commissions

- versioned commission plans per project + broker company
- commission rate is snapshotted from the plan effective when the transaction opened; later plan changes cannot alter an earlier sale
- commission basis is the frozen reservation price
- eligibility requires all four exact completed milestones:
  - down payment received
  - cheques received
  - contract signed
  - contract stamped
- eligibility/due timestamps drive countdown and overdue state
- PostgreSQL trigger refreshes commission completion/eligibility in the same transaction as milestone changes
- if prerequisites regress:
  - ELIGIBLE returns to PENDING_PREREQUISITES
  - INVOICED/DUE becomes DISPUTED
- application hooks also refresh after finance/document changes and list reads reconcile cases
- Broker Agent is restricted to cases attributed to that agent
- Broker Agent receives commission status/countdown only; rate and amount are independently permission-gated and omitted from the response when unauthorized

## Access additions

- `documents.read.self`
- `documents.upload.self`
- `contract.read.self`
- `contract.sign.self`
- `contract.sign.company`
- `documents.templates.manage`
- `payment.schedule.manage`
- `commission.plan.manage`

## Operational groundwork

- provider-neutral notification jobs table
- project milestone SLA settings
- document template signer requirements
- transactional outbox events retained for live updates and notification dispatch

## Validation

Production CI passes on the final head:
1. strict TypeScript across the full platform workspace
2. PostgreSQL 18 migrations from an empty database
3. explicit assertions for catalog, buyer/EOI/queue/reservation, document/signature, payment, cheque, commission, notification and SLA indexes/tables
4. explicit verification of commission creation and milestone-refresh triggers

## Next stacked slice

Outbox/event dispatcher, notification/SLA scheduling and delivery adapters, real-time project updates, and worker/runtime reliability so the web applications can consume live inventory, queue, transaction and commission changes without polling.

- **The bulk "Who they are" picker opens blank.** It no longer carries over the last saved kind. It opens on "Choose who they are…" and Save stays disabled until a kind is picked. author: wils0ns
body:
Tests only. Each of these passed whether or not the property it names held; each now fails when that property is broken, which was checked by breaking the production code (or the property) and restoring it.

- **`TestARateLimitedScannerDoesNotHoldConcurrencySlots`** built its own semaphore, so swapping the two acquire blocks in `engine.go` kept it green. It now drives the real `Run` with a two-slot pool: four jobs wait behind a one-per-hour limit, and an unrelated scanner finishes only while it holds both slots. One processor (`GOMAXPROCS(1)`, restored on exit) removes a schedule on which the wrong order also passes; with it, the swap fails 20 of 20 runs.
- **`TestRateGateServesCallersInOrder`** collected the order and never compared it, and sequenced goroutines with sleeps. It now fixes arrival order through the gate's injectable clock and compares.
- **`pkg/config/edit_test.go`** discarded `Set`'s error, so a failing `Set` made the `Unset` checks pass; a `mustSet` helper fails instead, and the version check compares the loaded value, with a `1.10` case that loads back as `1.1` when written bare.
- **`test/integration/coverage_test.go`**: the licenses and kubernetes tests asserted console substrings that were always true (the project name contains "licenses"). They now read `report.json` and require the control's verdict, no scan errors and its scanner; `scanTo` passes `--no-gate` and fails on a non-zero exit. Run locally against real tools and a kind cluster.
- **Doctor goldens** stubbed the latest version as `v9.9.9`, so they pinned `vv9.9.9`, which the resolver cannot produce.
- **Git fixtures** in `mend_sca_test.go` and `sagafetch_test.go` skipped on any git failure, so a developer whose git signs commits silently skipped six end-to-end tests. They now ignore global and system git config and fail rather than skip.
- **`TestSingleflightGroupRunsOnce`** ordered callers with a 10ms sleep; a channel barrier holds the first call until every caller has started.

Written by a subagent in its own worktree from a test-suite audit, then read and rerun here after merging current `main`. `make gate` passed in that worktree.

body:
## What

- `scripts/perf/bench-browser.mjs`: the GPU harness (`gpu: true`, `ENGINE_GPU=1`, `bench --gpu`, `bench:ref`) only dropped the software-GL flags. Headless Chromium on Linux then fell back to SwiftShader anyway, so "gpu" runs measured a software rasteriser. On Linux it now adds `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl`; `ENGINE_GPU_ANGLE` picks another ANGLE backend (`vulkan` adds `--enable-features=Vulkan`) or `default` to add nothing. Exported helpers: `gpuAngleArgs()`, `isSoftwareRenderer()`.
- `scripts/perf/bench.mjs`: a `--gpu` run whose WebGL renderer string names a software rasteriser (SwiftShader, llvmpipe, softpipe) fails with a fix hint instead of being recorded as `gpu`.
- Docs: STD-PRF-14's reference-run row in `docs/APPLICATION.md`; CHANGELOG.

The software harness and its flags are unchanged.

## Why (found in lab work)

Measuring a crowded three.js character test game (a labs-style kit test with 20+ animated people, MSAA, GTAO, bloom), the "GPU" bench ran at ~1 fps: `UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL` was `ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero)), SwiftShader driver)`. With this change the same machine reports `ANGLE (NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080/PCIe/SSE2, OpenGL ES 3.2)`. Labs (#177) lean on `npm run lab -- <id> bench`, so the GPU harness needs to mean GPU.

## Evidence

- `launch({gpu: true})` on Linux / RTX 4080: NVIDIA renderer; `launch({gpu: false})`: SwiftShader (unchanged).
- `node --test scripts/perf/bench-browser.test.mjs`: 9/9 (new test covers Linux args, other platforms, `ENGINE_GPU_ANGLE` values and injection rejection, software-renderer detection).
- `npm run check`: PASS.
- `bench-browser.mjs` is hashed into the experiment descriptor: GPU-harness runs get a new descriptor (no GPU baselines are recorded in `perf/`); software-harness numbers are unaffected. Not verified: macOS and Windows GPU harness (no change there; `gpuAngleArgs` returns nothing off Linux).

author: guilu
body:
Antes: el control plane repartía órdenes `START`/`CANCEL` a los runners, pero no había daemon que las ejecutara; los agentes se quedaban en cola.

Después: `skynet-runner` se registra en el control plane, recoge las órdenes, crea un worktree por agente, lanza Claude Code (o fake-claude) y envía los eventos normalizados. Cancelar o agotar el tiempo mata el árbol de procesos, y un corte de red no pierde eventos.

Cada `START` termina con exactamente un `agent.process.exited`. Esto vale también si falla el worktree, si se cancela antes de arrancar, si se agota `limits.timeout` o si el runner se para o se reinicia. En esos casos el evento trae `error` y el control plane deja el agente en `FAILED` con ese mensaje, salvo que se hubiera pedido cancelarlo.

**How**
- `transport/ControlPlaneClient` (java.net.http) habla con el control plane. Si recibe un 401, el daemon vuelve a registrarse.
- `journal/Journal` es una base SQLite que guarda:
  - las credenciales;
  - los eventos pendientes, con `seq` por invocación;
  - las órdenes ya vistas, para que una orden reentregada no se ejecute dos veces;
  - las invocaciones terminadas y los PIDs.
- Un evento solo sale del journal cuando el control plane responde al lote.
- `supervisor/ProcessSupervisor`:
  - vacía el entorno y deja solo una lista permitida;
  - redirige stdin a `/dev/null`;
  - guarda el log NDJSON bruto y los últimos 8 KB de stderr;
  - para terminar, envía SIGTERM al árbol, espera la gracia y después envía SIGKILL;
  - al arrancar mata los huérfanos que dejó un runner anterior, comprobando el instante de arranque del proceso.
- `workspace/WorkspaceManager` ejecuta `git worktree add` en `workspaces/<ejecución>/<agente>`, sobre la rama `skynet/<trabajo>/<agente>`. Después emite el nuevo evento `agent.workspace.ready`.
- `provider/claude/ClaudeCodeProvider` construye el comando de `claude -p … --output-format stream-json`.
- `AgentExecutor` y `RunnerDaemon` unen las piezas.
- Configuración por variables de entorno, documentada en el README.
- Tests:
  - procesos reales y repositorios git temporales;
  - fake-claude como agente;
  - el daemon completo contra un control plane simulado con `HttpServer` (con 503 iniciales en `/events`, rotación de token, reentrega y recuperación tras reinicio);
  - 2 IT nuevos en `RunnerProtocolIT`.

**Pendiente**
- Presupuesto propio en el runner: necesita tabla de precios; por ahora solo se pasa `--max-budget-usd`, que no es estricto.
- Tabla `workspace` en el control plane: el evento ya se guarda.
- `setsid`/grupos de procesos: ahora se toma una instantánea de los descendientes.
- E2E con el control plane real: es el paso 5.
